reason: Revision tests should exercise the same side effects as production, avoid coupling to internal publish implementation or manual source-of-truth assignment, cover distinct save paths, and make assertions about revision-backed fields deterministic across databases.
scope: global / Wagtail revision save, publish, and latest_revision-backed tests
common_pattern: Deterministic Wagtail tests for revision-backed behavior: explicitly create and retain revisions via save_revision() instead of relying on implicit revision creation, database null-ordering, or hardcoded timestamps.

text: When adding or changing a model's search configuration (e.g., `search_fields` or `FilterField` registrations), add a regression test that actually performs the affected search/filter/sort operation—including ordered querysets with `order_by_relevance=False` where applicable—so the test fails if the configuration is missing.
reason: Search index declarations affect runtime query behavior; indexing-only tests or tests that do not exercise the field registration will still pass when the configuration is omitted or invalid.
scope: Wagtail model search configuration changes (e.g., wagtail/wagtailcore/models.py search_fields)
common_pattern: Tests for Wagtail search/filter features should exercise the actual filtering or query path and assert exact expected results, including excluded items and validation behavior; changes to search configuration require regression coverage.

text: Keep the shared cross-backend search test suite backend-agnostic: shared tests must pass without backend-specific workarounds, `@unittest.expectedFailure` markers, or assertions about semantics that differ between backends. Move or override backend-specific cases (e.g. a multi-word `Prefix` query on Elasticsearch) in that backend's own test subclass/file, and when a previously-unsupported feature can now be implemented, implement it and drop the expected-failure marker rather than preserving the gap. Regression tests whose bug reproduces with the default database/search backend or standard Django/admin views must not require optional external backends such as Elasticsearch; place them in backend-agnostic modules so they run in default CI rather than being skipped. Backend-specific tests stay in that backend's suite: keep Elasticsearch-specific overrides (e.g. overriding `test_search_all` to apply a slice) there, and when changing generated query payloads, add a test that executes the query against an Elasticsearch instance (a smoke test that it runs without error is sufficient) rather than only asserting the generated query dictionary. When adding coverage for a new Elasticsearch model field (mapping, serialization, or document retrieval), extend the relevant existing test (e.g. `TestElasticsearch7Mapping.test_get_document`, `test_get_mapping`, or the existing retrieval test) with additional assertions or parameterized cases rather than adding a separate field-specific or duplicate test.
reason: Keeps the shared suite valid and meaningful for all backends, prevents backend-specific limitations from masking behavior of other backends, maintains feature parity, and avoids losing coverage when external backends are unavailable or when tests only validate generated payload structures.
scope: wagtail/search/tests shared backend suite and backend-specific test modules
common_pattern: Conventions for testing Wagtail's pluggable search backends: shared cross-backend tests stay backend-agnostic, backend-specific behavior and setup live in backend-specific test subclasses, and backends are configured/obtained through the real WAGTAILSEARCH_BACKENDS configuration path.

text: In search backend tests, inherit the shared `BackendTests` mixin (via the common backend mixin, respecting MRO) rather than manually invoking `BackendTests.setUp(self)`, and obtain the backend through the real configuration path — `get_search_backend("<name>")` and a correct dotted `backend_name`/`WAGTAILSEARCH_BACKENDS` entry — instead of instantiating backend classes directly, mutating DB state with raw SQL, or comparing against a wrong backend path that silently skips the test.
reason: Exercises the same configuration path users control, keeps tests decoupled from concrete constructors, avoids MRO/setup duplication, and prevents tests from silently becoming no-ops via SkipTest.
common_pattern: Conventions for testing Wagtail's pluggable search backends: shared cross-backend tests stay backend-agnostic, backend-specific behavior and setup live in backend-specific test subclasses, and backends are configured/obtained through the real WAGTAILSEARCH_BACKENDS configuration path.

text: Keep accessibility test scopes and exclusions accurate and minimal: scope axe-core scans to the root `html` element (not just `body`) so head elements such as meta tags are covered; remove `include`/`exclude` selectors once the issues they were added for are fixed; and pass optional `include`/`exclude` selectors directly to `AxeBuilder` without defensive `if` guards, since Axe safely accepts `undefined`.
reason: Body-only scoping leaves head elements untested, stale exclusions hide regressions and reduce coverage, and redundant guards add noise where the library already handles undefined optional values.
scope: accessibility integration tests and page-level axe configuration
common_pattern: Centralized, consistent configuration of the Axe accessibility checker: custom rules/checks should live in shared configuration collections rather than duplicate or dedicated attributes; per-rule enablement and options follow a single pattern; and accessibility test scopes/exclusions should stay accurate.

text: When testing accessibility checker configuration with an experimental axe rule example, use an actually experimental rule (e.g., `focus-order-semantics`) rather than a non-experimental one (e.g., `color-contrast-enhanced`), and update the expected `options` object to match.
reason: Using a non-experimental rule in a test meant to demonstrate experimental-rule behavior makes the test scenario invalid.
common_pattern: Rules governing Wagtail's accessibility (axe-based) userbar item: its behavior, guards, class identity, and test fixtures must reflect accessibility-specific semantics rather than reusing edit-action assumptions or non-experimental axe rules.

text: In unittest-style tests, use specialized assertion methods that express the exact intent instead of generic ones: use `assertIsInstance(obj, Type)` for type checks (not `assertTrue(isinstance(obj, Type))` or `assertIs(obj.__class__, Type)`), `assertIsNone(x)` / `assertIsNotNone(x)` (not `assertEqual(x, None)`, `assertIs(x, None)`, or `assertFalse(x)`), and `assertEqual(actual, expected)` (not `assertTrue(actual == expected)`). Use canonical names — `assertEqual`, not the deprecated `assertEquals` alias. For boolean checks, use `assertTrue`/`assertFalse` for truthiness, but use `assertIs(value, True)`/`assertIs(value, False)` when the test specifically requires the exact boolean value; do not use `assertIs(value, True/False)` as a truthiness check, and do not use `assertTrue`/`assertFalse` when only an exact `True`/`False` is acceptable. When a test must verify that an object was passed through/retained unchanged, assert equality or identity to that exact object (`assertEqual`/`assertIs`) rather than only checking its type with `assertIsInstance`.
reason: Specialized assertions yield clearer failure messages, express intent directly, and avoid false positives from overly broad checks; deprecated aliases like `assertEquals` break on newer Python versions. Truthiness vs. exact boolean checks require different assertions, and identity/equality assertions are needed when verifying exact object pass-through rather than just type.
common_pattern: Use idiomatic unittest assertion methods that precisely express the intended check (type, None, equality, boolean) rather than generic assertions that pass/fail on the wrong condition and give poor diagnostics.

text: When testing Django system check errors, assert the check's `message` and `hint` text in addition to its count, type, and ID.
reason: The message and hint are user-facing diagnostic output; asserting them prevents regressions in the explanatory text and ensures the check continues to provide correct guidance.
common_pattern: Design and verify Django system-check diagnostics: separate the problem statement (`messages`) from actionable remediation (`hint`), phrase hints unambiguously and with modern/preferred APIs, and test the user-facing message and hint text.

text: When testing Wagtail admin menu visibility or hook-based registration (e.g., `modeladmin_register` / `add_to_admin_menu` in `wagtail_hooks.py`), load the admin home/dashboard view and assert against the server-provided menu JSON data rather than rendered HTML (menus are populated client-side in JS). Check that expected menu item URLs are present or absent, and assert the menu hierarchy/structure—parent/child relationships and ordering—rather than only checking labels with `assertContains`. Place these tests in the existing `Test*Menus` class of the feature-specific test module (e.g., `wagtail/tests/test_{feature}.py`) rather than creating a new file/class, and do not manually register menu items via `Menu`/`register_temporarily`, which bypasses the hook logic under test.
reason: Rendering the admin view exercises the `is_shown`/hook registration path end-to-end, and Wagtail menus are rendered client-side so HTML assertions are unreliable—the JSON data is the correct source. Structural assertions catch nesting/order regressions that label-presence checks miss. Consolidating in `Test*Menus` keeps related tests discoverable, and manual registration would let broken hook registration still pass.
common_pattern: How to author tests for Wagtail admin menu visibility and registration: exercise the real hook/render path (load the admin view, assert server-provided menu data/URLs) rather than bypassing it, and assert meaningful menu state (structure/hierarchy) with deterministic setup.

text: In locale-dependent tests, activate the intended locale using the mechanism that matches production: use `translation.override(...)` for translation-catalog/cached-property assertions and compute both actual and expected values inside the same `with` block (including cached properties and menu/attribute reads); for views that rely on `django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware`, set `request.LANGUAGE_CODE` to simulate it rather than passing locale via query params; clear cached properties such as `admin_menu.registered_menu_items` before reading them, following the existing reset pattern in `wagtail/admin/tests/test_menu.py`; and when changing translation imports or translation functions (e.g. `gettext_lazy`), manually verify the affected UI under a non-default admin language.
reason: Values or cached properties evaluated outside the override reflect the default locale, tests that omit `request.LANGUAGE_CODE` do not match production LocaleMiddleware behavior, and stale cached menu items make results non-deterministic.
scope: translation/locale override tests, Wagtail admin menu tests, and test code for locale-aware views
common_pattern: Tests that verify locale-dependent (translated) behavior must activate the target locale via translation.override(...) and evaluate all relevant values — both actual and expected, including cached properties — inside that same override context, so that missing or incorrect translations are actually detected.

text: When adding quality support for a new image format, add a dedicated Test{Format}QualityFilter test case in wagtail/images/tests/test_image_operations.py mirroring the existing per-format tests (e.g. TestJPEGQualityFilter, TestWebPQualityFilter), and assert the actual Wagtail/Willow default option values (quality, optimize, progressive) rather than invented ones.
reason: Per-format test coverage keeps format-specific quality behavior discoverable and prevents regressions; asserting real defaults keeps tests in sync with upstream library behavior.
common_pattern: Wagtail image output quality must be handled per-format: each lossy format gets its own quality setting/filter whose default mirrors the underlying Willow encoder default, and each format's quality behavior is covered by dedicated tests asserting the real defaults.

text: When updating expected breadcrumb markup in admin tests, reproduce the full set of current Tailwind `w-*` utility classes on the `<li>` (including `w-max-w-0` where the shared template applies it), the `data-breadcrumb-item` attribute, and render the arrow `<svg>` as a sibling of the breadcrumb link rather than nested inside it. Match the template's conditional classes (non-trailing items include `w-max-w-0`; the trailing item omits it) instead of trimming classes that seem irrelevant.
reason: Keeps test fixtures aligned with the shared template's actual conditional classes and current conventions, avoiding legacy class names and inaccurate assertions.
scope: wagtail/admin/tests/test_page_chooser.py and explorer view breadcrumb tests
common_pattern: All generalizations concern the Wagtail admin shared breadcrumb component (`wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/shared/breadcrumb-next.html`) — its Tailwind utility-class width behavior, current-item visibility/data-attribute contract, test fixture markup, and CSS color-selector coverage. The cluster is topically coherent (one component) but contains several genuinely distinct sub-patterns that cannot be collapsed into a single rule.

text: In view tests, verify breadcrumb behavior using dedicated breadcrumb test helpers (`assertBreadcrumbsItemsRendered` with a list of `{url, label[, sublabel]}` dicts when breadcrumbs should appear, `assertBreadcrumbsNotRendered` when they should not) instead of asserting template names or the absence of specific action-button strings.
reason: Directly asserting the rendered breadcrumb structure confirms the correct hierarchy, links, labels, and page-type sublabels, and avoids brittle template-name or string-absence assertions that break when shared base templates intentionally render extra fragments.
common_pattern: Breadcrumb-related behavior in frontend/view tests should be verified through dedicated breadcrumb test helpers that assert the rendered structure (or its absence), rather than through indirect proxies like template-name or string-absence assertions.

text: In tests, do not hardcode primary keys or manually assign PK fields to ORM-created objects; retrieve objects via stable semantic lookups (e.g. `Site.objects.get(is_default_site=True)`) and use the resulting public `obj.pk` for expected values. Reference an instance's primary key through the public `pk` attribute rather than the internal database-value representation (e.g. `obj.pk.db_value`).
reason: Hardcoded/manually-assigned PKs break under `--keepdb`, when database sequences or creation order differ, and on non-SQLite backends; the public `pk` API is stable and returns a normal Python value instead of coupling tests to implementation details.
common_pattern: Best practices for handling Django model primary keys — use Django's `pk`/`_meta.pk` abstractions instead of assuming an integer `id`, and in tests avoid hardcoded, manually-assigned, or internally-represented PK values (with test fixtures chosen to exercise non-default PKs).

text: When adding a test model specifically to exercise custom primary-key handling, use a non-integer primary-key type (e.g. `UUIDField` or `CharField`) rather than an integer `AutoField`, so tests cover edge cases beyond the default integer autoincrement PK.
reason: Integer PKs mirror default behavior and miss bugs that only surface with non-integer PKs in lookups, relations, serialization, and form handling.
common_pattern: Best practices for handling Django model primary keys — use Django's `pk`/`_meta.pk` abstractions instead of assuming an integer `id`, and in tests avoid hardcoded, manually-assigned, or internally-represented PK values (with test fixtures chosen to exercise non-default PKs).

text: Add tests for cancellable-event contracts: register a listener that calls `event.preventDefault()` and assert that subsequent custom events or side effects do not occur. If `preventDefault` is conditional, test both branches: condition satisfied calls it; condition not satisfied does not.
reason: Guards the `preventDefault` contract against regressions where consumers can no longer cancel the controller's follow-up behavior or where default behavior is blocked incorrectly.
scope: client/src/controllers/*.test.js and Stimulus controller event tests
common_pattern: Designing, centralizing, and testing cancelable custom-event behavior in Stimulus controllers: dispatch before side effects, honor event.defaultPrevented, centralize the dispatch/filter logic, and verify cancellation in tests.

text: When writing tests that involve ordering: (1) If production code defines an ordering (e.g., default ordering, explicit ordering on a field/widget, or sort logic), assert the exact expected sequence of results (or rendered order). Cover each ordering scenario (e.g., ascending and descending, different order fields) with separate, descriptively named test methods. (2) If ordering is not guaranteed by the production code (e.g., unordered querysets), use order-insensitive assertions that preserve duplicates, such as `assertCountEqual` or a custom helper like `assert_unsorted_results`. Avoid converting to `set(...)` in assertions, as this hides duplicate results.
reason: Ordering is part of the behavioral contract when defined, so exact-order assertions catch regressions that order-insensitive tests would miss; separate, well-named tests make coverage clear and failures unambiguous. For unordered results, non-deterministic ordering causes intermittent failures, and set comparisons lose duplicate information, weakening the test's ability to detect backend bugs.
common_pattern: Testing ordering behavior: ensure tests assert exact order when ordering is defined, and use order-insensitive assertions that preserve duplicates when ordering is not guaranteed.

text: When modifying shared listing CSS selectors, verify the change against all listing variants — universal listings (with/without bulk actions and with custom ordering), snippets/images/documents, ModelViewSet views, legacy listings, and chooser listings with and without checkboxes — before committing.
reason: Shared listing markup and styles affect many UI contexts; the full matrix surfaces regressions in variants that do not use the bulk-actions mechanism or reuse the same icon/markup classes.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Wagtail admin listing styles: keep listing/chooser CSS centralized in the shared `client/scss/components/_listing.scss` (not view-specific partials), scope selectors so they cover all relevant listing icon/markup variants, and verify changes against the full matrix of listing views before committing.

text: Place audit-log data tests in `wagtail/tests/test_audit_log.py` and audit-log admin history/view tests in `wagtail/admin/tests/test_audit_log.py`, exercising representative admin workflows there, rather than scattering audit-log assertions into page/revision test modules.
reason: Keeps coverage in the canonical modules for each layer and tests audit-log/admin-history behaviour through realistic admin actions.
common_pattern: Best practices for testing audit-log behavior: (1) locate audit-log tests in the canonical dedicated test modules for their layer, and (2) assert on the actual recorded/displayed log content (action, fields, timestamps) rather than on counts or incidental test state.

text: When testing audit-log entries, assert on the actual recorded/displayed content — each expected entry's action and relevant fields (including correct message and timestamps) — and, for history-view bugfixes, verify the entry appears on the affected object's history page; do not rely on entry counts or incidental test-only state.
reason: Count- or state-only assertions can pass while logging the wrong actions or messages, so explicit content assertions verify the real user-visible behavior required by the fix.
common_pattern: Best practices for testing audit-log behavior: (1) locate audit-log tests in the canonical dedicated test modules for their layer, and (2) assert on the actual recorded/displayed log content (action, fields, timestamps) rather than on counts or incidental test state.

text: When testing Django model system checks that depend on Meta options (e.g. `constraints`, `unique_together`), temporarily mutate only the specific `_meta` option relevant to the check under test, restore the previous value in a `finally` block, and keep each test focused on a single behavior. Add separate focused tests for additional configurations/missing-constraint (warning) cases rather than broadening an existing test.
reason: Preserves the model's real Meta configuration, avoids cross-test state leakage, keeps test names and assertions aligned with a single tested behavior, and ensures both passing and negative/warning paths are covered.
scope: Model system-check tests (e.g. Wagtail translatable-mixin tests)
common_pattern: Django model system-check logic and tests around Meta constraints/uniqueness declarations — how to correctly inspect constraints in check() code, and how to structure focused, isolated tests that mutate Meta options.

text: In form-submission tests, POST every field present in the rendered form, using empty strings for fields the user left blank rather than omitting them. For hidden or permission-restricted fields, add POST-step tests that submit tampered values and assert the server rejects or ignores the change; do not rely solely on widget-type or render-time assertions. An omitted field is equivalent to the field not existing in the form, whereas an empty string reproduces what a browser actually submits. If including blank fields causes a test to fail, treat that as a signal of a possible implementation bug rather than weakening the test.
reason: Tests that omit fields diverge from real browser behavior and can hide genuine defects; widget-type checks do not prove server-side validation, so POST tampering tests are needed to guard against permission and validation regressions from HTML manipulation.
common_pattern: Admin form submission tests should POST payloads that faithfully mirror real-world browser submissions — both by including every field the rendered form would submit (even empty ones) and by exercising adversarial cases (tampered values for hidden/permission-gated fields) to verify server-side validation.

text: When changing `RulesController` rule-matching semantics, update unit tests to cover the new sentinel values (`[]`, `['on']`) and edge cases such as a checkbox with `value=""`.
reason: Tests must reflect the new rule contract to prevent regressions in edge-case behavior.
common_pattern: RulesController / Stimulus `data-rule` matching should operate on the explicit values present in `FormData`, treating rule values as plain strings with no hidden special-casing of falsy or absent values; checkbox states are expressed explicitly as `[]` (unchecked) vs `['on']`/the checkbox `value` (checked).

text: Every bug fix must include a regression test that reproduces the reported bug and exercises the specific broken behaviour — not a broad or incidental operation — plus a control test case that is expected to pass even without the fix. Verify the regression test is meaningful by temporarily reverting the fix (or running the test-only branch): the regression test must fail on the unfixed code and pass once the fix is restored. The control test confirms the tested feature works in the common case and helps catch over-broad fixes that suppress valid behaviour.
reason: A test that passes regardless of the fix gives false confidence and does not guard against the bug returning; confirming fail-without-fix/pass-with-fix proves the test actually covers the fix. A passing control case additionally isolates the bug's conditions, confirms the feature works normally, and guards against fixes that suppress valid behaviour.
common_pattern: Regression testing discipline for bug fixes: a fix is incomplete unless a test reproduces the bug, fails without the fix, and passes with it — verified by temporarily reverting the fix or running the test-only branch.

text: When changing a tree model's ordering (e.g. adding or modifying `node_order_by`), update all tests that assert sibling/traversal order (e.g. `test_get_prev_siblings`, `TestCollectionTreeOperations`) to the new expected order, and call `refresh_from_db()` on node instances after any tree-modifying operation (add, move, delete) before asserting on order or paths, since treebeard may update database paths without updating in-memory objects.
reason: Ordering changes alter tree traversal sequences, so stale test expectations produce false failures, and unrefreshed in-memory nodes carry stale paths.
common_pattern: Ordering behavior of django-treebeard tree models: define ordering declaratively via `node_order_by` at the model level rather than per-query `.order_by()`, preserve the established ordering contract when broadening traversal scope, and keep ordering-dependent tests in sync.

text: In keyboard/interaction controller tests — including keyboard shortcut tests with compound shortcuts such as Mousetrap's `mod` — use a shared keyboard-simulation helper (e.g. `simulateKey`) that dispatches the full keydown/keypress/keyup sequence with consistent KeyboardEvent options instead of manually constructing and dispatching KeyboardEvent objects ad hoc. The helper should accept an optional target (defaulting to `document.body`), derive `which` from `keyCode` when not provided, and ensure simulated events include every property the shortcut library listens for (e.g. `key`, `keyCode`, `ctrlKey`/`metaKey`) and are dispatched to the correct element; otherwise a correct implementation may appear broken and regressions can be hidden.
reason: Covers all keyboard phases controllers may listen for, reduces duplication, makes event simulation more realistic and consistent across tests, and avoids shortcut-library/property mismatches that can fail to trigger bindings.
scope: test files for keyboard/interaction controllers and keyboard shortcut tests
common_pattern: All generalizations concern how to reliably test keyboard interactions: centralizing keyboard-event simulation in a shared helper, and ensuring simulated events match what the shortcut-handling code actually listens for. The remaining generalizations (test ordering, fixture DOM delegation) are secondary test-organization guidance rather than the core pattern.

text: When changing the behavior of a client-side JavaScript module (entrypoints, API clients, components such as Draftail sources), verify the change before merging: if the module has colocated Jest tests, add or update the sibling `{module}.test.js` file alongside the source file, covering new behavior and new branching paths; if the module has no automated tests, manually verify the full user flow and relevant edge cases (e.g., confirm/cancel paths, different selection and search scenarios).
reason: The project colocates tests next to their source modules; changes altering a module's contract or adding conditional logic must be covered where test infrastructure exists. Where tests are absent, explicit manual end-to-end verification is the only way to confirm behavior such as URL state preservation before merge.
scope: client/src/** JavaScript modules (with or without colocated Jest tests)
common_pattern: Changes to client-side JavaScript module behavior must be verified — normally via colocated Jest tests in the sibling `{module}.test.js` file, and via documented manual verification when the module has no test infrastructure.

text: In tests, invoke the code under test directly and let exceptions propagate rather than wrapping calls in try/except solely to convert exceptions into assertion failures or boolean success flags.
reason: An uncaught exception already fails the test with a full traceback; wrapping it adds noise, can obscure the original failure location, and risks masking unexpected exception types.
common_pattern: Proper use of Python assertions and assertion-based testing: reserving `assert` for internal invariants (never runtime/user-input validation), and structuring tests so that exceptions, their types, and their messages are verified precisely rather than loosely or redundantly.

text: When an admin feature relies on markup injected via templates, add targeted assertions in the existing test layer that renders the relevant context: for a feature-specific JS asset, extend the feature's view tests (in the test class already responsible for the feature) to assert the expected `<script>` tag — e.g. with `src` equal to `versioned_static(...)` — is present, avoiding new test files or broad assertions in unrelated tests; for a template tag that emits markup into the admin skeleton/document head (e.g. a meta tag), add a skeleton/base-template test that renders the full page and asserts the expected element with its full value is present in the output.
reason: Confirms that template-mediated markup is actually wired into the correct rendered admin context — feature views for feature assets and the full skeleton for head markup — without redundant or incorrect assertions elsewhere.
common_pattern: Verifying that a JS asset required by an admin UI feature or workflow is actually included via the correct template — both in tests (where and how to assert inclusion) and in documentation (ensuring claimed hooks match template reality).

text: In Django tests, access response bodies through the framework-provided APIs: parse JSON with `response.json()` rather than custom helpers or `json.loads(response.content.decode(...))`; read non-streaming bodies via `response.content`, and read `StreamingHttpResponse` bodies via `b"".join(response.streaming_content)` rather than manually iterating chunks into a buffer. Do not use `response.content` for streaming responses.
reason: Django's test `Response.json()` handles decoding and parsing idiomatically, while `response.content` and `streaming_content` already expose complete bodies without redundant manual buffer accumulation; `response.content` is invalid or empty for streaming responses.
common_pattern: In Django tests, access response bodies through the framework's built-in accessors (response.json(), response.content, b"".join(response.streaming_content)) instead of hand-rolled loops, buffers, or manual json.loads(content.decode(...)) decoding.

text: When testing code that responds to `beforeunload`, assert cancellation via the standard `event.defaultPrevented` flag rather than defining the deprecated `returnValue` property on synthesized events — but only when the production code actually handles the `defaultPrevented` path; if production still reads `returnValue`, the mock must emulate that legacy contract.
reason: A test mock must exercise the same event contract the production code consumes; aligning the assertion with `defaultPrevented` simplifies mocks but silently stops testing real behavior if production still relies on the deprecated `returnValue`.
common_pattern: Handling the browser `beforeunload` confirmation via the modern, spec-blessed API rather than deprecated legacy mechanisms — i.e., use `event.preventDefault()` / `defaultPrevented` and model confirmation as a boolean flag instead of assigning a (custom-message) `returnValue` string.

text: Locale-specific transliteration and locale-comparison tests must use linguistically accurate, controlled test data: characters must exist in the target locale's alphabet, example words should be realistic, and words spelled identically across compared locales should be used when isolating mapping behavior.
reason: Incorrect alphabet characters, unrealistic examples, or differently spelled comparison words conflate input differences with the transliteration mapping under test, producing misleading expectations and false assumptions about language rules.
common_pattern: Best practices for testing locale/language-dependent utilities: cover non-happy-path locale inputs and use linguistically accurate, controlled test data to avoid false assumptions.

text: For formset controller/component tests, exercise mixed existing and newly added inline panel children with invalid data across consecutive saves: fix, reorder, remove, and delete children while asserting that deleted children remain in the submitted HTML with `deleted=true`, and verify validation error counts in tabs and the mini-map, plus that mini-map links point to the correct items after each save. Include regression coverage for reordering rows that mix valid and invalid data, not only all-valid rows.
reason: These interactions are where validation error counts and mini-map links most often desynchronize, so testing add/remove/reorder/validation together is more valuable than testing them in isolation; deletion is not just DOM removal because `deleted=true` hidden state affects backend/formset error counts. Mixed-validity reorder scenarios exposed an ordering bug that all-valid reorder tests missed, so they must be covered explicitly.
common_pattern: Correct handling of formset reordering in Django formsets, covering behavior during validation, test coverage for mixed validity, and documentation of 1-based ORDER indexing.

text: When testing which ModelAdmin edit_handler/panels configuration is used, assert on the resolved form fields (e.g., response.context['form'].fields) or mock get_edit_handler() calls rather than on created-object state or rendered HTML; prefer unit-style handler-resolution tests, and add regression tests for ModelAdmin-over-model precedence.
reason: Resolved form fields and mocked handler calls directly reflect the configured handler/panels, while created-object state and rendered-content searches are indirect and brittle; unit/mock tests isolate handler resolution and precedence.
common_pattern: Tests for Wagtail/Django admin form, inline panel, and edit-handler behavior should exercise the actual admin view or handler-resolution path and assert on resolved form fields or handler invocation, not on indirect proxies such as plain ModelForms, created-object state, or rendered HTML.

text: Tests for recursive Django model-relationship traversal should use different field names on each model in the chain so that resolving against the wrong model fails instead of silently succeeding.
reason: Same-named fields can mask bugs by making incorrect lookups pass; distinct names ensure the recursive behavior is genuinely covered.
common_pattern: Recursive Django model-relationship traversal must resolve fields relative to the current related model, and tests should use distinct field names across the model chain so incorrect model resolution cannot silently pass.

text: Tests for the cancel-workflow action should cover both invalid-form causes — validation errors and a lock — including a moderator/admin submitting for moderation, hitting a validation error, then cancelling.
reason: This path enters form_invalid() for a different reason than a lock and needs explicit regression coverage to keep cancellation and message handling correct.
common_pattern: Consistency and accurate documentation of workflow-cancellation handling in Wagtail admin views: wherever a form can be invalid (validation errors OR lock), comments, tests, and cancellation code paths should reflect all reasons and reuse the same behavior as the normal submit/action flow.

text: In tests for action creators and reducers, invoke or construct actions with all required arguments, the current action `type`, and all required payload fields, matching the function/reducer contract rather than simplifying calls, omitting parameters, or reusing stale action objects.
reason: Keeps tests aligned with real signatures and current action contracts, catching missing parameters/fields and preventing false positives.
scope: action-creator and reducer test files, e.g. `actions.test.js` and `reducers/*.test.js`
common_pattern: Tests should exercise the real action-creator/reducer contract by supplying the required type, arguments, and payload fields rather than simplifying calls or using stale/minimal action objects.

text: Custom block-validation ValidationError subclasses that group errors (e.g. StreamBlockValidationError, ListBlockValidationError) should expose each error group as a named attribute on the exception (e.g. self.block_errors, self.non_block_errors) rather than packing them into ValidationError.params, and their constructors should default internal fields such as block_errors and non_block_errors (e.g. to ErrorList()) so callers and subclasses can raise them without knowing serialization conventions or breaking the telepath adapter.
reason: Named attributes make the exception's contract explicit and avoid pack/unpack indirection in render/catch code, while sensible defaults let subclasses of clean() construct errors safely without depending on internal serialization shape.
scope: wagtail/blocks custom validation error classes (and analogous block error types)
common_pattern: Design conventions for custom block-validation ValidationError subclasses in Wagtail: how their error groups are exposed, how their constructors default internal fields, whether they are publicly exported, and when they should exist at all.

text: When validating multiple items, collect all validation failures into an aggregated error structure that preserves each error's associated item (e.g., index-aligned entries or nested arrays built via `map`), then throw a single `Error` containing that aggregated data at the end instead of throwing on the first failure, emitting per-item warnings, or appending errors out of alignment.
reason: Surfaces all invalid configurations at once, gives callers complete diagnostic data, and prevents missing or misattributed validation failures.
common_pattern: Aggregate all validation failures across multiple items into a single error, while preserving the correspondence between each error and its item, rather than failing fast, warning per item, or appending misaligned errors.

text: When surfacing aggregated form validation errors as text in user-facing views (e.g., import/redirect views), do not render raw `form.errors.as_text()`; instead, strip leading `*` bullet markers, join messages with commas, and remove internal sentinel keys such as `__all__`.
reason: Raw `as_text()` output is cryptic and unreadable in a single line, making it hard for users to understand validation failures.
common_pattern: Proper handling and display of Django form validation errors (especially non-field errors) in Wagtail admin templates and views, covering error inclusion, conditional rendering, API usage, and user-friendly formatting.

text: When consuming payloads from external producers, treat non-essential fields as optional and provide defaults at the extraction point. For JS destructuring of event payloads such as `CustomEvent.detail`, supply defaults at every destructuring level — both for intermediate objects (`detail: { value = '' } = {}`) and optional leaf fields (`status = 'success'`, `text = ''`). Likewise, when Python rich-text handlers pass entity attributes to JS, JS-side entity handling must tolerate `undefined` and not assume every attribute is present. This keeps types stable, avoids `TypeError`s, and prevents repetitive `undefined` guards at each consumer.
reason: Payload producers may omit optional objects or fields; centralizing fallbacks and optional-attribute handling at extraction prevents runtime crashes and broken rendering without repetitive checks at every usage site.
common_pattern: Defensive destructuring of optional/untrusted event payload fields: supply defaults at every destructuring level (for intermediate objects and leaf values) at the point of extraction, so consumers receive resolved, type-stable values instead of having to guard against `undefined` at each usage site.

text: Do not add defensive error/fallback handling for empty or unreachable states. When copying a template's full `.content` as a `DocumentFragment`, treat an empty fragment as a valid value rather than an error or `null` condition: do not reject empty templates or require an `HTMLElement`, and let downstream append/reset logic (e.g. `resetValue=true` clearing a target) handle emptiness. Likewise, do not add user-facing error/fallback branches for UI states users cannot reach in normal operation. Before removing any such branch, confirm that no other data path (e.g. imported rich text or API-generated data) can produce the state.
reason: Unreachable or empty-state defensive branches add dead code, translation strings, and maintenance burden without user value; full-content copying removes the old `firstElementChild` null failure mode and enables useful emptiness handling, but alternative data paths must be checked before removing existing safety.
scope: global (specific example: TeleportController and template-based Stimulus controllers)
common_pattern: UI state-handling code should be disciplined: branches should exist only for states users can actually reach, and handling for each reachable state should be colocated in the branch that processes that state.

text: In `SnippetChooserBlock`, when resolving a target model's snippet viewset, wrap the access in `try/except AttributeError` and re-raise as `ImproperlyConfigured` with a message naming the offending non-snippet model. `SnippetChooserBlock` has never supported non-snippet models, so failing fast with a descriptive error is the intended behavior.
reason: SnippetChooserBlock has never supported non-snippet models; failing fast with a descriptive error is the intended behavior.
common_pattern: In Wagtail's snippet framework, the SnippetViewSet is the authoritative owner of snippet admin/view configuration: it should be declared declaratively on the viewset (not monkey-patched onto the snippet model or scattered across view classes), exposed to model code via `model.snippet_viewset`, and registered through the standard `register_snippet` flow from `wagtail_hooks.py` rather than ad-hoc hooks or model decorators.

text: In Wagtail's panel-list expansion utilities (e.g. `expand_panel_list`), validate the top-level `panels` argument before iterating: if it is a bare string, raise `ImproperlyConfigured` with a hint about a likely missing trailing comma (e.g. a single-element tuple written as `("my_field")`) instead of iterating over its characters. This turns the confusing downstream `FieldDoesNotExist: ... no field named 'm'` into an actionable configuration error.
reason: A single-element tuple without a trailing comma (`("field")`) is just a string, and strings are iterable, so iterating produces characters and leads to a cryptic `FieldDoesNotExist` error. An explicit guard gives a clear, actionable error pointing the developer at the real mistake.
common_pattern: Guard against the bare-string configuration gotcha when a helper expects a sequence (e.g. a single-element tuple written without a trailing comma): detect the string before iterating and raise a clear configuration error with an actionable hint rather than letting character-wise iteration produce a cryptic downstream error.

text: In Wagtail template tags (wagtail/templatetags/), use semantically appropriate exceptions: raise Django's ImproperlyConfigured for configuration errors (e.g., a named URL pattern cannot be reversed) rather than TemplateSyntaxError, and raise ValueError for invalid arguments (e.g., pageurl/fullpageurl expecting a Page object). Add tests that pass invalid input and assert the expected exception is raised.
reason: Merges complementary halves: proper exception selection and test coverage for error paths. Keeps project-specific framing (Wagtail template tags) and aligns with Wagtail's established practice.
common_pattern: Error handling in Wagtail template tags: using semantically correct exception types and testing error-raising branches.

text: Centralize cache backend retrieval in a dedicated helper/classmethod (e.g., `_get_cache()`) that encapsulates the `caches[...]` lookup and `InvalidCacheBackendError` handling, rather than repeating the try/except pattern at each cache access site.
reason: This concerns code organization of the cache backend lookup itself, not exception taxonomy or which backends to guard.
common_pattern: Handling Django cache backends robustly: centralize cache lookup, and prefer relying on Django's cache abstraction + documentation over backend-specific guards/warnings.

text: Catch the narrowest exception type that can be meaningfully handled rather than a broad `Exception` (and never a bare `except:`). For pluggable backend abstractions, define a shared domain-specific exception wrapper (e.g. `SearchBackendException`) and require backends to wrap provider-specific exceptions in it, so callers can catch known expected failures without broad exception handling.
reason: Narrow catches avoid swallowing unrelated errors, and a shared backend exception wrapper lets callers handle known backend failures without broad exception handling.
common_pattern: Exception-type discipline: use the most specific, semantically meaningful exception type at every raise/catch/define site — preferring stdlib built-ins over bare `Exception`, reusing the project's existing dedicated exception types instead of inventing generic ones, and catching the narrowest type that can be meaningfully handled.

text: Validate required configuration and fail loudly: do not silently swallow errors or substitute hard-coded/safe defaults. For required class attributes supplied via constructor argument or class-level fallback (e.g., `model=None` with a `model` class attribute), resolve the value in `__init__`, validate it for `None`, and raise `ImproperlyConfigured` before assigning or mutating any instance attributes. Do not add permissive guards for attributes required throughout the implementation, since such guards imply support for subclass configurations that would require overriding most of the class. Validate/parse configuration (e.g., `new URL(...)` for required endpoint/API key values, dotted-path `import_string` imports, or `ImproperlyConfigured` setup checks) inside error-handling paths so invalid or empty values throw or propagate rather than falling back to a default endpoint/API key or default behavior.
reason: Merges the general principle of failing loudly on misconfiguration with the specific pattern for resolving required class attributes and the anti-pattern of permissive guards.
common_pattern: Handling invalid/misconfigured pluggable values (custom classes, dotted-path settings, config attributes): don't hide the misconfiguration. The cluster converges on 'surface configuration errors instead of silently falling back to a default.' A sub-thread disputes the *mechanism* — one comment prefers runtime warnings/logging on fallback, another prefers documentation of required types over runtime warnings. Both agree silent/hidden fallback is bad; the residual disagreement is warning-vs-documentation, not whether errors should be visible.

text: Separate configuration validation from runtime input validation. Validate settings values that don't depend on requests at startup (a Django system check or `AppConfig.ready()`) and raise `ImproperlyConfigured`; default the errors list and return it early when the setting disables the feature being checked. Validate request/input-dependent values at runtime, raising a domain-specific exception at the point the input is processed. Do not weaken or blur this during refactoring: keep raising exceptions for invalid input rather than silently skipping/discarding it, and don't toggle between startup and runtime validation via a helper parameter.
reason: Preserves the distinct architectural concern of separating startup configuration validation from runtime input validation, including the specific Django hooks and the anti-pattern of toggling validation location.
common_pattern: Django configuration-driven checks: how to structure them (early-return when disabled, fail fast at startup) and how to test their behavior at the disabled-value boundary (e.g. None).

text: Do not silently swallow caught exceptions: when a catch block intentionally ignores an error and continues (or 'passes'), log it so the failure remains diagnosable — unless suppression is explicitly and knowingly intentional. In exception handlers, log caught exceptions with traceback-preserving calls (`logger.exception()` / `logging.exception()` or `exc_info=True`) at ERROR level rather than plain `logger.error()` or `logger.debug()`, and include contextual identifiers such as the operation, URL/status code, or model class/primary key. Log the caught error object/details instead of manually interpolating exception messages or fragile args like `e.args[0]`. For expected/handled exceptions whose traceback adds no diagnostic value, log a concise error with the salient details rather than a full traceback.
reason: Merges the cluster's shared guidance against silent failures and for diagnosable exception logging: preserve tracebacks for unexpected failures via logger.exception()/exc_info=True, include contextual identifiers and error details, while allowing concise logging for expected exceptions and explicitly intentional suppression.
common_pattern: Exception-handling discipline: make error handling explicit and minimal — never silently swallow caught exceptions, keep try/except scoped to only the operation that can raise the expected error, and remove handlers that do nothing (e.g., bare re-raise).

text: Scope `try`/`except` blocks to the smallest operation that can raise the expected exception. Do not wrap unrelated operations (e.g., model saves, loops, imports, warnings, conversion/iteration logic) inside the handler; do not nest later fallible operations inside the `except` clause; and do not wrap recursive processing so nested errors are swallowed. Remove no-op `try`/`except` blocks whose handler only re-raises the caught exception. When using a builtin exception such as `TypeError` as control flow in a fallback (e.g., to detect whether an object is iterable), do not raise that same exception type for the fallback's own failures; raise a distinct exception type (e.g., a `LookupError` subclass) so the real error is not caught and masked and is reported at the offending element rather than an outer level.
reason: An over-broad try/except can catch and mask legitimate errors from unrelated code, code inside an except block that raises causes a confusing chained traceback, and a no-op re-raise adds noise and falsely suggests special handling. Using the same exception type that a fallback catches causes the real error to be masked and reported at the wrong level.
common_pattern: Exception-handling discipline: make error handling explicit and minimal — never silently swallow caught exceptions, keep try/except scoped to only the operation that can raise the expected error, and remove handlers that do nothing (e.g., bare re-raise).

text: In backward-compatibility shims that call an overridden or third-party method whose signature may not accept a newly added argument, do not wrap the call in a broad `try/except TypeError`. Instead, detect signature mismatch explicitly (e.g., via `inspect.signature`) and re-raise any unrelated `TypeError` unchanged, so genuine errors raised inside the method are not masked.
reason: Broad `except TypeError` mistakes errors from correctly-signatured implementations (e.g., an invalid paginator page number) for signature incompatibilities, causing the method to run twice, swallowing real bugs, and producing misleading exceptions that are hard for third-party developers to debug.
common_pattern: Backward-compatibility shims must not use broad `try/except TypeError` around calls into overridden (or third-party) methods to detect signature/argument mismatches, because this masks genuine TypeErrors; use explicit signature introspection (e.g., `inspect.signature`) or re-raise unrelated TypeErrors unchanged.

text: Manage resource lifetimes explicitly: for resources confined to a single scope, use a `with` context manager (e.g., `with open(...) as file:` or `with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:`) and do not call `close()`/`shutdown()` on a resource already managed by that context manager. If a resource must remain open across multiple validation/processing stages or several independent error exit paths, prefer explicit open/close or ownership transfer over a scoped `with` block. For temporary files created with `mkstemp()`, create and consume the temp file inside the same `try` block whose `finally` deletes it, so cleanup runs if later I/O or copying raises.
reason: Context managers guarantee cleanup on success and error paths and avoid redundant or missed close/shutdown calls; explicit lifetime management is needed for long-lived resources. The `mkstemp()` `try`/`finally` pattern prevents leaking temporary files when opening, copying, or otherwise consuming the file fails after creation.
common_pattern: Resource lifecycle management: prefer context managers for scoped cleanup, avoid redundant explicit close/shutdown calls, but use explicit resource management when the resource lifetime spans multiple pipeline stages or error paths.

text: Treat values from raw/external, legacy, historical/serialized, backportable data, and data migrations that read nested JSON from existing rows as potentially missing or malformed. Add or retain explicit presence checks / `is not None` guards or normalization before indexing or attribute access; for nested JSON, guard `None`/JSON `null` at each access level (handle `TypeError` when subscripting `None`, in addition to `KeyError`/`ValueError`) and skip records that do not match the expected JSON shape. Do not assume current-version or UI invariants guarantee presence; comment any null/legacy guard plus when it can be removed. If an invariant or type guarantees valid values, omit the defensive filter rather than leaving it unexplained.
reason: Raw/external, legacy/historical/serialized, and migration-read structured records can omit or malform values that current-version invariants normally guarantee. Explicit guards and normalization prevent TypeError/undefined crashes and aborted migrations, while comments keep defensive code understandable and prevent it from being incorrectly removed later.
scope: global (including data migrations that read or transform legacy structured data)
common_pattern: Defensive handling of values that may be absent or malformed because they originate from legacy storage, historical/serialized data, older releases, or backportable paths; such guards should be retained or added, and their legacy rationale should be documented.

text: When constructing regex/search/tsquery patterns from dynamic values, escape each interpolated value individually using the documented escaping mechanism for that syntax instead of removing reserved characters or maintaining custom escaping helpers. For regex patterns, apply `re.escape()` (or equivalent) to each list element before joining with `|`, and consistently escape every value type including pk/id/model values (e.g. via `json.dumps()` with inline escaping). For PostgreSQL `tsquery`, preserve reserved characters via their documented escape sequences (e.g. `\` -> `\\\\`) rather than deleting them, and when interpolating a `%s` placeholder into a raw `to_tsquery(...)` SQL template, use a well-escaped quoting pattern such as `to_tsquery('''%s'':*')` so the substituted expression remains valid and distinct terms are not merged.
reason: Unescaped regex metacharacters, special values, or tsquery reserved characters can change pattern meaning, cause false matches, corrupt search, or merge distinct terms. Escaping each interpolated value individually and using syntax-appropriate documented escaping preserves separators and semantics across regex and PostgreSQL tsquery construction.
common_pattern: Escaping dynamic values before using them to construct regex/search patterns, and applying that escaping consistently across all interpolated value types.

text: Choose the Django ORM single-object retrieval method based on whether the record's existence is an invariant: use get() when the record must exist (fail fast), and use filter(...).first() with explicit None handling when zero or multiple matches are valid. Do not catch MultipleObjectsReturned for non-unique lookups. When a Locale instance is used as a reference in a save operation—especially when it was obtained via a cache or other non-standard retrieval path—re-fetch it with QuerySet.get() before saving so it is guaranteed to exist in the database, and document this re-fetch requirement for callers. For scalar-only lookups via values_list(..., flat=True)[0], catch IndexError and return the appropriate empty result.
reason: get() enforces required-record invariants, while first() avoids MultipleObjectsReturned and silently returns None for optional or potentially duplicated data. Cached or indirectly retrieved Locale instances may be stale, so forcing a get() lookup before save validates existence and prevents foreign-key constraint violations. Scalar-only lookups need analogous IndexError handling to preserve empty-result behavior.
scope: Django ORM queries, especially data migrations and Locale references in save operations
common_pattern: Defensive Django ORM data access: choose lookup and creation methods according to expected cardinality and invariants, and explicitly handle missing/multiple rows, race conditions, and migration edge cases instead of letting get(), create(), or None surprise downstream code.

text: Do not rely on hidden form fields for access control — hidden fields can be tampered with via HTML/request manipulation. Instead, validate submitted values server-side in the POST handler. In the Wagtail admin, when a permission-gated action (e.g., moving a collection) is disallowed for a user, omit the corresponding form field (the `parent` field) from the edit form and ignore any posted value for that field server-side; add a test that POSTs a different value and asserts the collection's parent is unchanged.
reason: Hidden fields can be modified by users via HTML/request tampering, so server-side validation is required to prevent unauthorized changes. This matches the Wagtail admin security model where unavailable actions are not exposed as hidden form fields, and the test ensures the server-side validation path is covered.
common_pattern: Permission-gated form actions must be enforced consistently: omit the field in the UI when the user lacks permission, ignore any submitted values server-side, and cover the server-side path with a test that posts a different value.

text: Use explicit `None` or sentinel checks instead of Python truthiness when testing for missing/absent values; valid values can be falsy (`0`, `False`, `''`), so truthiness checks misclassify data changes as additions/deletions. Prefer positive early-return guards for the non-`None` case rather than wrapping the main logic in an `if/else` or writing an explicit `if value is None: return None` branch. When a function returns `None` as a sentinel for an unavailable/invalid result, check that value explicitly before unpacking or using it rather than relying on `try/except` around the unpacking (which can mask unrelated `TypeError`s). Keep defensive `None` checks even when the current block type is not expected to produce `None`, since future block implementations, custom variants, or manually rewritten data may introduce it. This applies especially to StreamField block traversal and comparison code, including methods such as `is_new()` and `is_deleted()`.
reason: Explicit sentinel checks prevent misclassifying valid falsy values and avoid `try/except` handlers masking unrelated `TypeError`s; early returns reduce nesting and clarify the main path. Defensive `None` checks remain necessary because future or custom implementations may introduce `None`.
common_pattern: Explicit, defensive handling of missing vs. falsy values in Wagtail StreamField block processing and comparison: use None/sentinel checks rather than truthiness, and retain None guards even when current block types are not expected to produce None.

text: Before passing a potentially `None` (or falsy) value to a built-in function that validates its arguments—such as `getattr` for an attribute name or `issubclass`/`isinstance` for a class reference—resolve it to a valid value or guard with a truthiness/`is not None` check. For `getattr`, never pass `None` as the attribute name and do not rely on an outer `or` fallback, because `getattr(obj, None, default)` raises `TypeError` before the default is considered (the attribute-name argument is validated first). For `issubclass`/`isinstance`, order conditions as settings flag → model existence check → type check (e.g. `self.model_class and issubclass(self.model_class, Model)`) so the expression stays a boolean.
reason: Built-in functions like `getattr`, `issubclass`, and `isinstance` validate their arguments before considering defaults or short-circuit fallbacks, so passing `None` raises `TypeError`. Guarding with a truthiness/`is not None` check prevents this and preserves correct boolean logic.
common_pattern: Correct use of Python class-introspection predicates (`issubclass`/`isinstance`) in Django-style code: (a) they must be guarded against `None` inputs that raise `TypeError`, and (b) they should be preferred over manual MRO/parent-list inspection.

text: When an API, argument, serializer field, or setting accepts only a fixed/enum-like set of values—including a list of registered features such as rich text editor features—enforce the restriction explicitly at the API boundary (e.g., `ChoiceField` with `choices`, or an up-front check) instead of silently ignoring or accepting invalid inputs. On failure, raise a descriptive exception (or emit a warning when non-fatal) that names the offending value with `!r`, describes the actual value/type involved (e.g., 'empty list', not 'empty queryset'), and, where useful, points the caller to the appropriate alternative API or method. Do not duplicate the valid-option list when it comes from an enum/choices definition; otherwise include the allowed values if that improves diagnosability. Tests should assert this validation rather than silent acceptance.
reason: Merges the specific feature-name validation rule with the broader fixed/enum-value validation rule. Both express the same complementary principle: reject invalid allowed-value inputs explicitly at the API boundary, and report failures precisely enough to debug them, while deferring to an enum/choices source of truth when one exists.
common_pattern: Validate arguments, fields, and settings that accept only a fixed/enum-like set of values at the API boundary, and make validation failures diagnostic by naming the offending value precisely rather than emitting generic errors or duplicating the set of valid options when it has a dedicated source of truth.

text: Do not use `assert`/`AssertionError` for runtime validation of user input, public API contracts, OS/environment failures, or recoverable backend dependency/configuration issues. Reserve assertions for internal invariants that should never fail. For invalid external inputs, public API contracts, or OS/environment failures, raise explicit domain-appropriate exceptions (e.g., `BadRequestError`). For recoverable backend dependency/configuration issues, emit an actionable warning (e.g., `RuntimeWarning` with a hint) and document the warning behavior in project docs instead of raising or translating third-party exceptions into `AssertionError`; assertions are stripped under `python -O` and produce generic failures rather than reliable error handling.
reason: Assertions are intended only for developer invariant checks and are removed in optimized runs, so they cannot reliably enforce validation of external inputs or handle recoverable environment/configuration conditions. Explicit exceptions preserve correctness for invalid external conditions, while actionable, documented warnings help users self-resolve recoverable backend dependency/configuration issues without misclassifying them as internal invariant violations.
scope: global; backend integrations for recoverable dependency/configuration issues
common_pattern: Proper use of Python assertions and assertion-based testing: reserving `assert` for internal invariants (never runtime/user-input validation), and structuring tests so that exceptions, their types, and their messages are verified precisely rather than loosely or redundantly.

text: When coordinating or restoring state across multiple cross-frame windows/iframes, detect cross-origin status incompatibility upfront and fail fast: early-return rather than relying on long timeouts in catch blocks for paths that cannot succeed, and treat a cross-origin status mismatch between frames as an error. In particular, when restoring scroll position between an old and a replacement iframe, only proceed if both iframes have the same cross-origin status (both same-origin or both cross-origin); if origins are mixed, skip restoration and return early without waiting for a timeout. When checking same-origin access to more than one cross-frame window, wrap each window's `contentWindow`/property access in its own try/catch instead of a single combined try/catch, so the code can determine exactly which frame violated the same-origin policy and choose the correct recovery path.
reason: Merged complementary cross-frame same-origin guidance: fail-fast upfront origin-incompatibility detection avoids delaying errors for paths that cannot succeed, per-window try/catch preserves the information needed to identify the offending frame and select the correct recovery path, and the scroll-restoration case is an application of the same same-origin-status precondition.
scope: browser iframe/frame coordination and synchronization, including cross-origin checks and scroll restoration
common_pattern: Handling cross-origin iframe/cross-frame communication defensively: (a) isolating same-origin access checks per frame so the failing frame is identifiable, and (b) avoiding timeout-based fallbacks for paths that are known to be impossible, failing fast instead.

text: Wrap multi-step database write sequences (e.g., delete-then-create, copying a page along with its M2M relations, rebuilding a denormalized reference/index table) in `transaction.atomic()` so that a failure partway through cannot leave partially persisted or inconsistent data. Place the `transaction.atomic()` block at the top-level action entry point (e.g., `execute()`, a management command, a signal handler) rather than inside a per-item helper method (e.g., `_copy_page()` or a model method), to avoid creating a savepoint for every item processed and to avoid the two extra queries an atomic block runs even on no-op write paths. When you do not control the code path, clearly document the caller's responsibility to use an atomic block so the operations stay consistent.
reason: Successive database operations can fail partway through, producing inconsistent state, partial updates, race conditions, data loss, or audit states where a logged action never actually happened. A transaction guarantees atomicity; placing the atomic boundary at the top-level action avoids per-item savepoint overhead and avoids running extra queries on no-op write paths. If the atomic boundary is owned by the caller, that contract must be explicit.
common_pattern: The cluster consistently addresses when and where to apply Django's `transaction.atomic()` to multi-step database operations. Two complementary aspects appear: (a) the need for atomicity whenever a sequence of writes must not partially persist, and (b) the placement of the atomic block at the top-level entry point rather than inside per-item helpers to avoid savepoint and overhead penalties.

text: Validate required DOM/controller preconditions early — including required template elements, element attributes such as `id`, and global dependencies such as `window.telepath` — and throw a descriptive error when they are missing, rather than silently returning or accessing undefined values.
reason: Surfaces broken assumptions immediately and prevents confusing downstream errors in DOM-dependent or Stimulus controller code.
common_pattern: Fail-fast validation of required DOM/controller preconditions: when code assumes required elements, attributes, or dependencies exist, validate them early and throw a descriptive error instead of silently failing or accessing undefined values.

text: When accessing a pluggable storage backend (e.g. calling `.size` or other backend operations), catch a broad exception type (`Exception`) instead of only `OSError`, because non-local backends such as S3 may raise exception types unrelated to OSError; explicitly catch and re-raise `SystemExit` and `KeyboardInterrupt` so they are not swallowed.
reason: Narrow exception handling around storage-backend calls leaves non-local backends unhandled and breaks cross-backend support; the broad catch keeps logic working across all supported storage implementations while re-raising control-flow exceptions.
scope: Wagtail storage/file handling (global for pluggable backends)
common_pattern: Choosing the correct exception type/scope when working with OS- and storage-backend-related failures in Python: (a) preferring the modern OSError name over deprecated aliases, and (b) widening the catch clause for pluggable backends whose errors may not subclass OSError.

text: Use `OSError` rather than the legacy aliases `IOError`, `EnvironmentError`, and `WindowsError`, which have been aliases of `OSError` since Python 3.3.
reason: The legacy names are retained only for backward compatibility and are aliases of OSError starting in Python 3.3; using OSError avoids ambiguity and reflects the modern exception hierarchy.
common_pattern: Choosing the correct exception type/scope when working with OS- and storage-backend-related failures in Python: (a) preferring the modern OSError name over deprecated aliases, and (b) widening the catch clause for pluggable backends whose errors may not subclass OSError.

text: When splitting a structured string on a delimiter, always pass the separator explicitly and use a bounded `maxsplit` (e.g., `split(sep, maxsplit=n-1)` or `rsplit(sep, maxsplit=1)`) so that extra occurrences of the delimiter do not cause unpacking errors, silent truncation, or invalid parsing.
reason: Bounded splitting with explicit separators prevents crashes from tuple unpacking when delimiters appear more times than expected, avoids silent truncation when delimiter characters are part of component values, and ensures the parsing intent is clear and correct.
common_pattern: String splitting operations for parsing structured identifiers should use explicit separators and bounded maxsplit to avoid errors from unexpected delimiter occurrences.

text: Guard programmatic focus: before calling `.focus()` on an element obtained via `querySelector`/dynamic creation, verify the result is non-null, and skip focus setup entirely (early return) when the component/menu has no focusable items.
reason: Menus and dynamically rendered lists may contain no focusable children; calling `.focus()` on `null` throws a runtime error, and scattered emptiness checks are better replaced by one early-abort condition.
common_pattern: Programmatic focus management in UI components: how and where to trigger element focus, how to guard it, when in the lifecycle to run it, and how to centralize/test it.

text: Treat `invalid_revision` errors, including messages produced by `Revision.save_revision`, as user-facing: use translated, period-terminated error messages consistent with other error conventions.
reason: Generalization 4 identifies that invalid_revision can originate from revision save logic, so translation/termination conventions must be applied at the source of the message.
common_pattern: Cluster centers on how to write Wagtail tests around revision save/purge/publish flows so that tests exercise real revision logic and cover distinct revision states (protected vs. latest, initial save vs. overwrite, validation failure) without false positives from masking conditions.

text: In delete-confirmation messages, use separate translation blocks for each combination (descendants only, translations only, translations with descendants, etc.) and provide correct singular/plural forms, rather than a single combined blocktrans that produces grammatically wrong output for counts of 1.
reason: A single combined `{% blocktrans %}` cannot handle singular vs plural (e.g. '1 more child pages') correctly across all count combinations.
common_pattern: Reuse and correctness of shared Wagtail admin delete-confirmation templates/messages — preferring generic/shared partials over per-app duplication, and ensuring the confirmation strings handle singular/plural forms correctly.

text: In `TranslatableQuerySetMixin.localized()` with `preserve_order=True`, when `original_translation_keys` is empty, do not add the `original_order` annotation or call `.order_by("original_order")` — return the localized queryset (or return early when the original queryset is empty).
reason: The `original_order` annotation only exists when there is at least one translation key to order by; ordering by a non-existent annotation breaks on empty inputs.
common_pattern: Behavior of translatable/localized querysets in Wagtail should be explicit and defensively scoped: result-altering options must be opt-in parameters rather than inferred from unrelated filters, and ordering/annotation logic must be guarded against empty inputs. (Generalization 2 is a related but distinct queryset-cleanup concern from a different PR.)

text: When passing accessibility attributes (e.g., `aria-label`) to reusable template partials, ensure each instance receives a defined, non-empty value. Do not rely on undefined context variables, as Django renders them as empty strings, producing inaccessible controls.
reason: Undefined template variables silently render as empty values, resulting in controls like `<input aria-label="">` that are inaccessible to screen reader users.
common_pattern: Best practices for handling accessibility attributes (e.g., `aria-label`, `id` on labels) in HTML/Django templates, covering documentation of non-obvious attributes, ensuring valid (non-empty) values in reusable partials, and consistent attribute ordering.

text: Prefer idiomatic promise error handling: use `.then(onFulfilled).catch(onRejected)` rather than passing the rejection handler as the second argument to `.then()`. When an async operation has a precondition that can fail, wrap the precondition and the async call in a `new Promise` that rejects on failure, then handle success and failure through a single `.then/.catch` chain.
reason: The `.then().catch()` form is more idiomatic and also catches errors thrown by the fulfillment handler. Wrapping preconditions in a promise unifies control flow, avoids scattered early returns, and centralizes success/error handling so side effects are not duplicated.
common_pattern: Idiomatic promise error handling: prefer `.catch()` for rejection handling and, when a failing precondition exists, unify the precondition and async call in a single `.then/.catch` chain.

text: Confine Http404 and HTTP/request-response semantics to the view layer: model, generic, and reusable helper code must not raise Http404 or call get_object_or_404; instead return None (or an explicit sentinel) or use ORM queries. View code is responsible for translating missing/None results into Http404, using a lookup constrained to a single object such as get_object_or_404(Model, pk=...), resolving required URL parameters directly without redundant fallback branches, and including a descriptive message when raising Http404 manually.
reason: This merges the complementary halves of the cluster: reusable code should not leak view-specific 404 behavior, while views should correctly convert missing objects into 404 responses using safe, constrained lookups.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail not-found and 404 handling should respect layer boundaries: core/model/helper APIs use explicit sentinel returns or ORM lookups, while views own Http404 translation and use constrained single-object lookups.

text: In browser event listeners, report invalid data via console.error and an early return rather than throwing an Error; when using built-in validation events for custom error display, suppress the browser's default validation UI (e.g., by preventing default on invalid events) to avoid conflicts.
reason: Thrown errors in event listeners become unhandled errors and are hard to test, while console errors still inform developers. Suppressing default validation UI prevents conflicts with custom error presentation.
common_pattern: Handling invalid data in browser event listeners without causing unhandled errors or conflicting with default browser behavior

text: In shared client-side entrypoint scripts, guard optional global integrations and page-specific DOM containers before accessing or initializing them, and wrap one-time initialization in an idempotency guard (e.g. `if (!window.telepath) { window.telepath = new Telepath(); }`) so the script works standalone, on pages that omit that UI, or after multiple imports without runtime errors or overwriting shared globals.
reason: Optional values such as `window.telepath` may be absent, and shared scripts may run on pages with different DOM structures or be included more than once; explicit presence/idempotency guards prevent TypeErrors and duplicate initialization/side effects.
common_pattern: Shared client-side entrypoint scripts must defensively guard optional globals/DOM containers and repeated initialization so they can run in contexts where optional integrations or UI are missing and when the script is imported more than once.

text: In Wagtail's `ImageBlock`, when no alt text is supplied and `decorative` is false, this is an invalid state and must raise `StructBlockValidationError`. Do not substitute `""` for the missing alt text in the non-decorative case — only use `""` when `decorative` is true, and otherwise preserve the actual alt-text value (including `None`) so the invalid state remains detectable.
reason: Preserves the accessibility contract that non-decorative images require alternative text, and prevents a fallback value from masking the invalid case.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Wagtail's `ImageBlock` vs `ImageChooserBlock`: how `ImageBlock` should validate alt-text/decorative state, and when each block should be used in StreamField definitions and documentation examples.

text: When a page/resource is moved and its URL changes, frontend cache invalidation must purge both the new URL and the previous URL (not only the new location), so stale content is removed from the old location.
reason: The old URL may still be cached and would serve stale content after the move; purging only the new URL leaves the old cached entry behind.
