text: When rendering SearchPromotion editor's picks, handle both internal-page and external-link picks in every rendering path: frontend templates should read through the pick's recommendation relation (e.g. `searchpick.recommendation.page` for the target and the pick/recommendation title for the heading), and the admin listing must not omit external-only picks (render `searchpick.page.title` when an internal page exists, otherwise the external title field).
reason: The pick model no longer stores the page directly and a pick may point to an internal page or an external link; if templates only read the page, external picks render blank hrefs and silently disappear from the admin listing.
common_pattern: When SearchPromotion editor's picks can target either an internal page or an external link, every code path that renders or documents them (frontend templates, admin listing, docs) must be updated to handle both cases with the correct fields.

text: When implementing a Mapping-like helper, make `__iter__` yield keys, not values, so iteration matches ordinary `dict` semantics and the `collections.abc.Mapping` contract.
reason: Consumers expect `for item in mapping` to iterate keys, retrieving values via `mapping[key]`; yielding values breaks membership checks, unpacking, and other mapping operations.
common_pattern: Idiomatic iteration over collection types (dicts/mappings and sequences): iterate directly rather than making unnecessary copies, materialize a snapshot only when mutation during iteration must be tolerated, and honor the standard iteration contract (Mapping.__iter__ yields keys).

text: When a filter's null/clear value is exposed to users (e.g. it appears in URL query parameters), prefer a human-readable value such as "all" over falsey sentinel values like false, None, or "none" — prioritizing the editor/admin URL experience over backend conciseness. Only prefer falsey null values (which allow walrus-style `if value := filter_value:` checks) for filters whose sentinel never surfaces in user-visible URLs.
reason: URLs are visible to and shared by editors, so `?site=all` is clearer than `?site=false` or `?site=none`; readability for end users outweighs simpler backend filter conditions. Falsey null values remain a valid optimization when the sentinel is internal-only.
common_pattern: Conventions for defining and documenting query/filter parameters — specifically how to choose the filter's null/clear sentinel value and how to document its default behavior.

text: Always declare `related_name` explicitly on Django/Wagtail ForeignKey fields: use a descriptive name when the reverse relation is needed, or the string `"+"` when the reverse relation is deliberately unused, instead of omitting it.
reason: Explicit related_name avoids accidental or ambiguous reverse accessors: descriptive names make ORM relationships queryable and readable, while `"+"` cleanly disables an unused reverse API and keeps the related-model namespace free of unintended relations.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail ORM relationship design: how foreign-key relations should be declared (explicit related_name), modeled (concrete FKs and per-model subclasses rather than generic FKs or ad-hoc settings), and documented (precise field/model/cardinality language). All generalizations concern the design and exposition of model relationships in the ORM layer.

text: Model cross-model relationships with concrete foreign keys (or per-model concrete subclasses of a shared abstract base model / mixin) rather than generic foreign keys (content_type + object_id) or new configuration settings; derive related models from existing ORM relationships instead of introducing settings to point at them.
reason: Generic FKs force callers to filter on both content_type and object_id (easy to get wrong) and prevent the database from optimizing queries as subqueries, while a dedicated setting for a single narrow use case is redundant and can drift from the actual model definitions.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail ORM relationship design: how foreign-key relations should be declared (explicit related_name), modeled (concrete FKs and per-model subclasses rather than generic FKs or ad-hoc settings), and documented (precise field/model/cardinality language). All generalizations concern the design and exposition of model relationships in the ORM layer.

text: In django-filter FilterSet.Meta, only list model field names that should have filters auto-generated; never list explicitly declared filters or non-model field names (django-filter raises `TypeError` for non-model names). When all filters are explicitly declared, set `fields = []` rather than enumerating names, and add a brief comment explaining why `fields` is required/empty. Filtersets consumed by the generic `IndexView` must still define `Meta` with `model` (and `exclude`, even empty), since the view calls `self.filters.get_fields()`.
reason: `Meta.fields` drives auto-generation from model fields; listing declared filters is misleading, listing non-model fields errors, and `get_fields()` requires `model`/`exclude` metadata for the generic IndexView contract.
common_pattern: Conventions for authoring django-filter FilterSets in Wagtail/WagtailFilterSet: how Meta.fields is used, how conditional/optional filters are resolved, and how external query parameters are retained.

text: In a FilterSet's `filter_queryset`/filter methods, read optional filter values with `self.form.cleaned_data.get('field_name')` and apply filtering based on the returned value, rather than indexing directly or consulting separate `*_enabled` flags. Keep `filter_queryset` focused on applying values from cleaned_data — do not embed UI-level decisions (e.g., whether a filter is displayed). Conditional filter availability based on settings or runtime state should be resolved inside the filterset (e.g., deleting entries from `self.filters` in `__init__`), not by conditionally returning/gating the whole filterset class from the view.
reason: `.get()` makes absence of a value represent the disabled state, removing redundant state and avoiding `KeyError`; keeping conditional logic inside the filterset keeps the view simple and ensures the filterset class is always resolvable.
common_pattern: Conventions for authoring django-filter FilterSets in Wagtail/WagtailFilterSet: how Meta.fields is used, how conditional/optional filters are resolved, and how external query parameters are retained.

text: When a query parameter is handled outside the filterset but must survive filter-form submission, represent it in the filterset as a hidden field backed by a no-op filter (a method accepting `(self, qs, name, value)` that returns `qs` unchanged) instead of relying on the parameter remaining in the URL. Put the shared `noop_filter` method on the base `WagtailFilterSet` so subclasses can declare retain-only fields without duplicating it.
reason: Applying the filterset otherwise drops parameters not represented in the form; a hidden no-op field round-trips them through the filter UI, and centralizing `noop_filter` on the base class avoids duplication.
common_pattern: Conventions for authoring django-filter FilterSets in Wagtail/WagtailFilterSet: how Meta.fields is used, how conditional/optional filters are resolved, and how external query parameters are retained.

text: When mapping models to `ContentType` records, never filter by model name alone; match on both `app_label` and `model`. For general lookups, prefer `ContentType.objects.get_for_models()` because it encodes correct lookup semantics and caching. For filtering a known set of models, a single OR-combined `Q(app_label=..., model=...)` filter is also acceptable to avoid an extra query and a Python-side PK list.
reason: Model class names are not unique across apps, so model-name-only filters can return unrelated ContentTypes.
common_pattern: Correctly constructing Wagtail/Django querysets and ContentType lookups, especially around Page subclasses, proxy models, and stable model sets, plus documenting non-obvious queryset behavior.

text: In admin listing/chooser views, filter UI must stay consistent with the filter form and human-readable: render active-filter summaries with the same localized labels as the filter form (e.g., 'Yes'/'No'/'Any' for booleans, formatted dates/times, translated durations — never raw `True`/`False`/`None`), and when empty results are caused by active URL filters, indicate that filters are applied rather than showing the plain 'no objects exist' empty state.
reason: Empty or raw-valued filter feedback misleads users into thinking no data exists or into reading unlocalized values; matching the form's labels and surfacing active-filter state keeps behavior consistent and understandable.
scope: Wagtail admin listing/chooser views and filter adapters (e.g., `BaseListingView.active_filters`, generic chooser views)
common_pattern: All generalizations concern how admin/chooser listing views handle filter state: keeping filter UI consistent (empty states, active-filter labels), keeping filtering logic consistent across sibling views, and avoiding over-fetching/over-forwarding when the filter value is only used for display.

text: For generic listing views, expose empty-state/no-results messages as overridable view methods (e.g. `no_results_message`) instead of requiring template blocks or template forking, so subclasses can customize the message without duplicating templates.
reason: Keeps generic listing templates reusable, avoids template divergence for message-only differences, and makes subclass customization of the empty-state message straightforward.
common_pattern: Empty-state/no-results messaging in Wagtail generic chooser and listing UIs: keep user-facing copy consistent, neutral, and translatable, and expose message customization through overridable view methods rather than divergent templates or one-off filter-specific wording.

text: Do not rely on native `title` attributes for required UI hints or tooltips; implement a custom JS tooltip when tooltip behavior is required.
reason: Native `title` tooltips render inconsistently across browsers and are not a reliable accessibility mechanism, so tooltip behavior should be implemented in JavaScript rather than through the `title` attribute.
common_pattern: How tooltips should be implemented in Wagtail templates — standardized on the `w-tooltip` Stimulus controller with `data-w-tooltip-*-value` attributes, replacing legacy `data-tippy-*` attributes and avoiding redundant/default configuration.

text: When an admin widget exposes an overridable collection property (e.g. `dropdown_buttons`), apply any sorting/ordering in the shared base method (`get_context_data`) rather than inside the property getter, so that all subclasses and overridden properties inherit the same ordering.
reason: Centralizing sorting prevents overridden property implementations from bypassing the ordering and guarantees identical output for base and hook-derived variants.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern where and how a canonical ordering is enforced in Wagtail admin/collection code: ordering decisions should live in shared base code (shared `get_context_data` / `Index.get_queryset`) so that overrides (overridden getters, subclass hooks, alternate sort keys) cannot silently change or bypass the intended sequence.

text: In `wagtail/admin/views/collections.py::Index.get_queryset`, keep collection descendants ordered by name rather than by `'path'`, since ordering by `'path'` reverts the fix from #4874.
reason: Preserves the collection index ordering fix and avoids reintroducing the previously fixed regression.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern where and how a canonical ordering is enforced in Wagtail admin/collection code: ordering decisions should live in shared base code (shared `get_context_data` / `Index.get_queryset`) so that overrides (overridden getters, subclass hooks, alternate sort keys) cannot silently change or bypass the intended sequence.

text: When dynamically creating a class with `type()` and attaching an existing bound method (e.g., a viewset/view method), wrap it in a function that takes an explicit `self` parameter — e.g., `def get_buttons(self): return viewset.get_list_buttons(self)` — instead of putting the bound method directly into the class namespace.
reason: A bound method already has its first argument bound to its original instance, so inserting it into a new class's namespace permanently binds `self` to that instance and the method behaves like a static function tied to the wrong object. A wrapper with an explicit `self` signature preserves correct method binding, so the generated class's instances are passed as `self`.
common_pattern: Both generalizations describe the same Python correctness issue: when dynamically creating a class via `type()` and injecting behavior from an existing bound method, the bound method must be wrapped in a function with an explicit `self` parameter, because bound methods already close over their original instance and will not rebind correctly as methods on the generated class.

text: For hooks that provide a mutable list of default items (e.g., actions, menu items), pass the actual mutable list to the hook rather than a derived copy, and in documentation examples, demonstrate in-place mutation of that list (e.g., pop/append or modifying items) instead of rebuilding the list from scratch.
reason: Passing the mutable list preserves the ability for extensions to remove or replace defaults, and in-place mutation examples remain concise, avoid duplicating framework internals, and stay aligned with the hook’s intended in-place contract.
common_pattern: In-place mutation of hook-provided default lists: pass a mutable list to hook extensions and demonstrate in-place modifications in documentation examples.

text: In `wagtail/contrib/settings/views.py`, build the post-save edit redirect via `self.get_edit_url()`; when editing a site-scoped (`BaseSiteSetting`) setting, the `wagtailsettings:edit` URL must include the edited site's `pk`, while generic settings omit it. Do not rebuild this URL with ad-hoc `redirect(...)` logic.
reason: The edit-URL helper already encapsulates the intended destination, and omitting the site `pk` silently redirects to the default site's setting, losing the edited site context.
common_pattern: Correctly preserving site context when editing Wagtail site-scoped settings: reusing the canonical edit-URL helper (with the site pk) for post-save redirects, and showing the site name rather than a single-option site switcher.

text: In class-based views, read URL route parameters from `self.kwargs` by name rather than unpacking them positionally from `self.args`; declare parameters that are always required explicitly in the method signature instead of relying on `**kwargs`; and extract them into instance attributes in `setup()` so later methods reference stable attributes rather than repeatedly reading `self.kwargs`.
reason: Named URL parameters are keyword arguments (and `self.args` may be empty), so `self.kwargs` is reliable. Declaring required params self-documents the contract, and resolving kwargs once in `setup()` centralizes extraction and avoids repeated, error-prone lookups throughout the view.
common_pattern: Consistent handling of URL route parameters and view kwargs in class-based views/viewsets: making required inputs explicit, referencing them by name, and keeping helper naming aligned with framework conventions.

text: Capture model provenance/audit metadata (creation reason, timestamp, triggering object) using the project's standard audit-log facility rather than adding ad-hoc audit fields to individual models, and surface that metadata in the admin UI so users can audit and troubleshoot record creation.
reason: A standard audit log is reusable across models, avoids per-model duplication, keeps audit concerns separate from domain models, and makes the captured metadata actually discoverable to users in the admin.
common_pattern: Use Wagtail's audit-log infrastructure abstraction (log registry, base/generic log models, standard audit log facility) rather than hardcoding concrete log entry models or adding ad-hoc per-model audit fields.

text: Reuse module-level shared instances (e.g., singletons, stores) instead of re-instantiating them, and avoid passing shared context as arguments to methods when the callee can resolve it internally.
reason: Reduces duplication, coupling, and call-site noise; maintains a single source of truth for shared context.
common_pattern: Avoid redundant propagation of shared context: reuse existing module-level instances and avoid passing shared context as method arguments when it can be resolved internally.

text: Sortable column headers must toggle between ascending and descending order when clicked repeatedly — generating a leading `-` on the `ordering` query parameter for the reverse direction — and display an up/down arrow icon reflecting the current direction. Detect the active sort column with a single membership check (e.g. `{% if "field" in ordering %}`) rather than duplicating asc/desc conditionals, and guard ordering-specific accessibility instructions so they render only when the ordering column is active.
reason: Repeated-clicks-must-reverse is standard table UX; a single membership check handles both directions with less duplicated template logic; scoping ordering instructions prevents screen readers from announcing reorder behavior when the listing is not in ordering mode.
common_pattern: Conventions for sortable columns and ordering in Wagtail generic listing/index (IndexView) admin views: how `sort_key` maps columns to sortable fields, how sortable headers behave (toggle asc/desc, icons, active detection), and how the ordering interface is named and customized.

text: For Django views that serve both full-page and partial/HTML-fragment responses, prefer explicit response-mode separation over branching on X-Requested-With: use separate routes/views or a shared class-based view overriding `template_name`, or an explicit flag such as `self.results_only`. If a request-header check remains, keep it simple and local rather than abstracting it. In `get_context_data`, scope context to the current response mode by excluding full-page-only context from partials and gating fragment rendering (e.g., follow `render_*_fragment` conventions) so fragments are not re-rendered on initial full-page loads.
reason: Keeps AJAX/fragment responses lightweight, decouples view behavior from legacy request headers, avoids unnecessary fragment re-rendering, and maintains consistency with existing view conventions and tests.
common_pattern: Django views that serve both full-page and partial/HTML-fragment responses should make the response mode explicit and scope context/fragment rendering to that mode. The cluster shows a project convention moving away from X-Requested-With toward separate routes or flags like `self.results_only`, while keeping partial responses lightweight.

text: For configuration-driven conditional menu/plugin registration, perform the decision at registration time in the registry/entrypoint method (e.g. `WagtailRegisterable.register_with_wagtail`): select the appropriate hook from config flags (e.g. choose between `register_settings_menu_item` and `register_admin_menu_item` via `self.add_to_settings_menu`/`self.add_to_admin_menu`), set `menu_hook = None` when neither applies, and skip `hooks.register` entirely rather than registering an item that would always be filtered out by `is_shown()`. Likewise, gate optional entrypoint initialization on whether the corresponding menu item is configured.
reason: Registration-time decisions are clearer, avoid dead always-hidden entries and unconditional initialization of unconfigured features, and keep `is_shown()` focused on runtime visibility.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin menu/plugin visibility is governed in two complementary places with distinct responsibilities: (1) registration-time hook selection for configuration-driven decisions (whether an item should exist at all), and (2) runtime `is_shown()` for per-request/per-user visibility, which must use the flag and permissions relevant to that specific feature only. The unifying principle is that each layer should own its appropriate decision and not leak unrelated concerns.

text: Do not rely on `mouseleave` alone for dropdown/menu dismissal; expose accessible interactions such as Escape, focusout/blur, explicit close controls, or click-outside. Also, `pointer-events: none` only disables pointer input—it does not remove items from tab order or prevent keyboard focus, so manage focus/tab behavior separately.
reason: Pointer-only interaction is inaccessible to keyboard and assistive technology users, and `pointer-events` cannot substitute for focus management.
common_pattern: Dropdown/popover visibility behavior should preserve transitions and remain accessible, rather than using abrupt hiding mechanisms or pointer-only dismissal.

text: When defining unique constraints for translation models, include `locale` in the constraint fields and use a name that follows the template with `%(app_label)s` and `%(class)s` placeholders (e.g., `unique_translation_key_locale_%(app_label)s_%(class)s`).
reason: Including locale allows multiple translations per owner/parent, and using app_label/class placeholders ensures uniqueness across models and matches the project's future naming convention.
common_pattern: Defining unique constraints for translation models in Django: ensuring locale inclusion and proper naming with app_label/class placeholders

text: Use `wagtail.admin.forms.tags.TagField` for tag form fields (e.g., `field_classes = {"tags": TagField}`) instead of overriding tag widgets with `AdminTagWidget` or manually parsing tag strings with `parse_tags`/`split`. For taggit tag widgets (`AdminTagWidget`/`TagWidget`, a `TextInput`), serialize API tag lists in taggit’s edit-string format (comma-joined, with tags containing commas double-quoted) so round-trips match admin form input and avoid data corruption.
reason: Merges the converging TagField rules (G1, G2) with the complementary taggit serialization rule (G4): both rely on Wagtail/taggit-aware tag handling rather than generic widget overrides or manual string parsing.
scope: Wagtail admin tag fields, tag widgets, bulk actions, and API serialization
common_pattern: Centralize Wagtail/taggit tag handling through tag-aware form fields and serialization formats instead of ad-hoc widget overrides, manual parsing, or generic stringification.

text: Do not overload an existing prop with a new data shape or meaning; add a dedicated prop (e.g., a separate `svgPath` prop for raw path data instead of overloading `name`).
reason: Each prop should represent a single concept. Overloading forces consumers to pass different kinds of values and requires the component to guess intent, hurting readability and type safety. Encoding the distinction in the prop API makes intent explicit and self-documenting.
common_pattern: Do not infer a prop's type, shape, or behavior from its value or the presence/absence of another prop; instead encode the distinction explicitly via structural type guards or dedicated props/types. All generalizations reject 'value-sniffing' heuristics (startsWith, presence checks) in favor of explicit contracts.

text: Wagtail fields that store URL paths should use `models.TextField` with a `TextInput` form widget, matching `Page.url_path`, rather than a length-limited `CharField` with `TextArea`.
reason: Keeps equivalent URL-path fields consistent in storage type, validation behavior, and form UI, avoiding divergent behavior between related models.
common_pattern: Wagtail schema/data conventions: where and how to express model changes in migrations, and keeping equivalent model fields type-consistent within Wagtail.

text: When an SVG `<path>`'s `d` attribute is sourced from an array of path commands, join the array with spaces (e.g., `name.join(' ')`) before assigning it to `d`.
reason: DOM attributes expect string values, and SVG path data requires path commands to be separated by spaces or other valid separators.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns concern SVG `<path>` elements: one about correct data serialization for the `d` attribute, the other about compact markup formatting.

text: Do not add new constraints (e.g., max_length, validators) to existing unbounded core model fields unless strictly required to fix the issue; when aligning with another field, adjust the app-specific or dependent field to match the established field instead, or accept practical inconsistency.
reason: Adding limits to previously unbounded fields is a backward-incompatible change that can break existing installations holding longer values and is unnecessary when not required for the fix.
common_pattern: Avoid introducing backward-incompatible constraints on existing core model fields; when consistency with another field is desired, adjust the dependent/app-specific field instead or accept practical inconsistency.

text: For SVG icons, make accessibility semantics explicit: decorative icons must be hidden from assistive technologies (`aria-hidden="true"`, no `<title>`, and `focusable="false"` for IE11), while informative icons must expose a meaningful accessible label. If an SVG is the only content of a link, its `<title>` must describe the link destination or purpose, not just the graphic; and when an icon component receives a `title` prop, render the visually hidden title text in every icon rendering path (e.g., both sprite-backed and custom-path icons).
reason: Prevents screen readers from announcing presentational graphics, ensures informative icons are properly labeled, avoids redundant or confusing link announcements, and keeps accessible labels consistent across all icon implementation branches.
scope: Global for SVG icon markup; component-specific for icon components that accept a title prop.
common_pattern: SVG icon accessibility semantics: distinguishing decorative icons that should be hidden from assistive technologies from informative icons that need a meaningful accessible name, and ensuring labels are rendered/derived consistently across icon implementations.

text: Choose the email send helper by flow ownership: for Wagtail admin notification emails, use the shared `wagtail.admin.mail.send_mail` helper so the configured `WAGTAILADMIN_NOTIFICATION_FROM_EMAIL` sender is respected; for emails belonging to an existing Django auth flow (e.g., password reset confirmation), use Django's `send_mail` (or the same sender address as that flow) instead, since the Wagtail notification helper is intended for workflow notifications, not auth flows.
reason: Keeps sender addresses consistent within each user flow and avoids applying Wagtail's notification sender setting to Django auth emails.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns concern Wagtail admin notification emails: (a) which send helper to use depending on whether the email belongs to a Wagtail notification flow vs. an existing Django auth flow, and (b) cleaning up obsolete mail helpers/templates when a notification flow or URL route is removed. They share the notification-email theme but address distinct concerns (sender selection vs. dead-code cleanup).

text: When an operation performs multiple conceptually distinct user-visible actions (e.g. copying a page while keeping it live, or creating and publishing), emit a separate log entry for each action rather than a single combined state-change entry — including when reconstructing log entries from historical revisions.
reason: Log entries are a record of 'actions performed' (not 'state changes'), so distinct entries preserve a complete, queryable audit trail and allow actions to be filtered by type or recombined in views.
common_pattern: Design conventions for Wagtail's audit-log action taxonomy and logging behavior: how actions are named (hierarchical dotted identifiers reflecting the true operation), when to emit separate log entries, when to reuse existing action identifiers rather than spawn parallel variants, and keeping the action reference documentation in sync.

text: In `RulesController` `data-rule` matching, do not special-case falsy or absent rule/field values (no mapping of `false`, `null`, `undefined`, `0`, or missing FormData entries to `""`). Coerce rule values uniformly with `String(value)` (preserving `0` as `"0"`) and match against the actual values returned by `FormData.getAll(fieldName)`, requiring an explicit `""` to match a blank value.
reason: Special-casing falsey/absent values silently drops valid input (e.g. `0` becomes `""`) and injects ambiguous hidden defaults; plain string coercion plus matching on real FormData values keeps the matcher simple and rule semantics explicit.
common_pattern: RulesController / Stimulus `data-rule` matching should operate on the explicit values present in `FormData`, treating rule values as plain strings with no hidden special-casing of falsy or absent values; checkbox states are expressed explicitly as `[]` (unchecked) vs `['on']`/the checkbox `value` (checked).

text: For form fields that can accept multiple selected values under the same field name, use checkboxes with one shared `name` and each input's `value` set to its option/ID; retrieve selected values with the framework's multi-value accessor (e.g., `request.GET.getlist(name)`). Do not use radio buttons for multi-selection, and do not encode IDs into field names or parse prefixes.
reason: Checkboxes allow multiple checked inputs with the same name, matching repeated-parameter form serialization, while radio buttons enforce single-selection. Using a shared name and value avoids fragile custom field-name encoding and lets standard multi-value retrieval handle the submission.
common_pattern: Multi-value form fields should be modeled with checkboxes sharing a single name, not radio buttons or name-encoded identifiers, and selected values should be retrieved using multi-value accessors.

text: When a Stimulus form controller programmatically submits a form, call `form.requestSubmit()` rather than `form.submit()`, so the native `submit` event is dispatched and other event handlers / Stimulus actions can react. If browser constraint validation should be bypassed, add `novalidate` to the `<form>` element rather than using `submit()`. Do not silently return when `this.element.form` is absent — call the form API directly so unsupported/invalid usage surfaces as an error instead of a hidden no-op.
reason: `requestSubmit()` fires the submit event while `submit()` bypasses it, and `novalidate` lets the form opt out of built-in validation declaratively without losing submit-event behavior. Silent no-ops when the form is missing hide configuration mistakes.
common_pattern: Conventions for Stimulus controllers in the Django admin that programmatically manage form submission and per-field form behavior (how to attach the controller, how to submit, how to handle missing forms, and how to document the behavior).

text: When calling Django's `form.add_error()`, pass the field name and `ValidationError` as positional arguments rather than using the `error=` keyword.
reason: `error` is a positional parameter in Django's API; the keyword form is redundant and adds unnecessary noise.
common_pattern: Proper handling and display of Django form validation errors (especially non-field errors) in Wagtail admin templates and views, covering error inclusion, conditional rendering, API usage, and user-friendly formatting.

text: For Wagtail admin class-level configuration attributes that define generated UI items (e.g., in wagtail/admin/utils.py), keep each item minimal (only fields like name and heading, without presentation or behavior details such as classname) and accept any iterable, including enums, rather than requiring a concrete list.
reason: This keeps the configuration API simple and decoupled from presentation/behavior details while allowing callers to pass natural iterable containers such as enums.
common_pattern: Designing Wagtail admin class-level configuration attributes for generated UI items: keep entry data minimal and accept flexible iterable inputs rather than concrete lists.

text: When resolving a translation for a `TranslatableMixin` model or setting, use `TranslatableMixin.localized` rather than custom locale-lookup helpers, request/locale parameters threaded through public APIs, or logic that assumes a fixed/hardcoded `translation_key` formula. Translation keys may be generated arbitrarily (e.g. randomly during data migrations), so lookup must work with any stored key.
reason: `localized` is the existing request-independent way to select the correct translation, respects arbitrary migrated `translation_key` values a fixed formula would miss, and keeps the public API simple.
common_pattern: Resolving localized translations in Wagtail's TranslatableMixin-based models/settings: prefer the existing `localized` API over ad-hoc locale/translation-key plumbing, plus adjacent contracts around docstrings, caching, and singleton-settings request behavior.

text: For translatable singleton settings, distinguish admin writes from front-end reads: when a `locale` is explicitly supplied, get-or-create in that locale; when no `locale` is supplied, return an existing active-locale instance, otherwise fall back to an existing default-locale instance, and only create in the default locale.
reason: Prevents front-end requests from implicitly creating active-locale settings that were never intentionally created, while keeping the default language as a stable fallback.
common_pattern: Resolving localized translations in Wagtail's TranslatableMixin-based models/settings: prefer the existing `localized` API over ad-hoc locale/translation-key plumbing, plus adjacent contracts around docstrings, caching, and singleton-settings request behavior.

text: In registry-style APIs, treat explicit user registrations as authoritative: registration should follow last-registration-wins semantics so a later call can intentionally override an earlier one, and framework defaults or auto-registration must never silently override or ignore a user-registered value. Keep the read/lookup path transparent — retrieval methods (e.g. get_by_type()) should always resolve registered or fallback values without requiring callers to pass a flag; any strictness/fallback-control parameters belong in write/registration operations, not reads.
reason: Silently ignoring an explicit registration (first-wins setdefault behavior, or a framework default shadowing a user policy) is surprising and makes the registry behave unpredictably; forcing callers to opt in on the read path leaks internal registration state and complicates lookups.
common_pattern: Registry-style API semantics: registration writes must be predictable and let explicit user registrations take precedence (last-registration-wins, no silent ignores), while read/lookup methods resolve registered or fallback values transparently without opt-in flags.

text: When a search or filter is applied in a paginated listing view, reset the pagination query parameter (e.g., `p`) so results return to the first page instead of carrying over a stale page offset.
reason: A stale page number after a new search/filter can yield empty or incorrect results; resetting the page param keeps pagination behavior consistent across search and filter handlers.
common_pattern: Resetting the pagination query parameter (e.g., `p`) whenever a new search/filter submission occurs, so results always return to the first page and consistent query-parameter cleanup is applied across handlers.

text: When multiple state updates are always applied together for the same event, express them as a single atomic action/update (and route multiple triggers of the same update through one shared update method) instead of dispatching or running several updates sequentially. Only fall back to sequential updates when the ordering is genuinely unavoidable.
reason: A single atomic update prevents the store/component from briefly existing in a partially-updated inconsistent state, avoids duplicated dispatch/update logic, and reduces extra renders and middleware calls.
common_pattern: Consolidating multiple state updates that always occur together (sequential store actions, or multiple value-change callbacks) into a single atomic/shared update path, avoiding intermediate inconsistent state and duplicated dispatch logic.

text: In Wagtail index/list views, expose combined search/filter state (e.g. `is_searching or is_filtering`) as a dedicated view property rather than duplicating the combined condition in templates. If a narrower flag such as `is_filtering` is still needed for filters-only behavior, add a distinct combined property instead of overloading the existing flag.
reason: Keeps conditional logic in the view, provides a single override/change point for subclasses, reduces template duplication, and avoids losing the ability to distinguish narrower states such as filters applied without search.
scope: Wagtail admin generic listing/index views and templates
common_pattern: Centralize combined search/filter view state in the view class instead of duplicating compound flag checks in templates, while preserving narrower flag semantics when needed.

text: For Wagtail admin search/filter forms using the `w-swap` Stimulus controller (`SwapController`): use `submit`/`submitLazy` when the action must serialize the form (e.g. AJAX filtering that must preserve query parameters), and keep `search`/`searchLazy` for location-based query/update. For live search/filter forms, trigger lazy submission with `input` on text inputs and `change` on filter/select controls rather than attaching both events at the form level; omit form-level `change` to avoid duplicate lazy submissions. In `data-action` lists for live-update forms, place immediate navigation/replacement actions (e.g. `navigate->w-swap#replace`) before lazy/debounced actions (e.g. `input->w-swap#submitLazy`).
reason: Merged cluster rule covering the related `w-swap` configuration sub-patterns: action naming/selection for form serialization, event binding to avoid duplicate or parameter-losing submissions, and action ordering for immediate vs lazy handlers.
scope: Wagtail admin listing/chooser templates using the `w-swap` lazy-submit Stimulus controller
common_pattern: Correct configuration of Wagtail's `w-swap`/`SwapController` for lazy AJAX form search/filtering: choose the right Stimulus action for form serialization vs location-based query, bind lazy submission to the right DOM events/elements, and order immediate vs lazy actions to avoid lost query parameters or duplicate submissions.

text: When adding a request-parameter constant (e.g., `*_VAR`) to an `IndexView` to enable filtering, ensure it is actually applied in `get_queryset` (after existing filtering logic). Declaring the constant alone does not filter results.
reason: Prevents dead query parameters and ensures UI filters actually affect the displayed queryset.
common_pattern: Correct handling of query parameters in Wagtail views/templates: preserve existing parameters when modifying and ensure declared parameters are applied in filtering.

text: Resolve parent page locale contextually from the localized subtree: when assigning a parent/default locale to a child page in a localized tree, inherit the parent page's locale rather than the site-wide default; conversely, when i18n is disabled, the parent page chooser must ignore the `?locale=` filter and render the chooser template (even when parent pages exist in multiple locales) instead of redirecting.
reason: Localized content lives in its own subtree, so inheriting the parent locale keeps localized branches consistent and prevents children from being stamped with the global default; when i18n is off, locale-based redirects are meaningless and the chooser should fall through to normal rendering so users can still select a parent.
common_pattern: Locale-aware resolution of the parent page in a hierarchical page tree — how the parent page chooser/assignment should behave with respect to locales, both in the default (i18n-enabled) case and when i18n is disabled.

text: In `wagtail/images/__init__.py`, settings-backed helper functions should follow the existing `get_upload_to` / `get_rendition_upload_to` pattern: accept an optional `instance` argument; when an instance is provided, delegate to an instance method (e.g. `instance.get_storage()`), and otherwise read the global setting with a default fallback (e.g. `default_storage`). The instance method should allow per-instance subclass overrides.
reason: Mirrors the established Wagtail pattern, preserving backward-compatible module-level calls while enabling global configuration via settings and per-instance/subclass customization.
common_pattern: All generalizations anchor on the Wagtail images `get_upload_to` / `get_rendition_upload_to` design: a module-level helper that accepts an optional instance and delegates to an instance method (falling back to the global setting/default otherwise), plus the corresponding need to document each method's actual, distinct default behavior. Two sub-patterns emerge: (a) the module-level helper design pattern, and (b) accurate per-method documentation of the upload defaults.

text: When building Wagtail admin listing/report filter UIs, tailor filters to the content type and editor workflow: include only filters meaningful for that content type/report, add primary entity facets such as page type to reports in addition to date filters, use editor-friendly labels (e.g. 'Page types' instead of 'Content types'), expose small/boolean choices directly with RadioSelect, and visually distinguish filter actions (e.g. use a distinct clear-filter icon).
reason: These practices improve editor clarity, reduce unnecessary choices, and make filtering quicker and more intuitive in Wagtail admin interfaces.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin listing/report filter UIs should be editor-centric: filters must be relevant to the content/report, labeled in editor-friendly terms, and use clear, appropriate filter controls.

text: For link-like components used in menus (e.g. the page explorer), keep the `href = '#'` sentinel default so that plain clicks expand content and modifier-clicks open the target in a new window. The click handler inspects this value to block default navigation and permit modifier-click; don't change the default without updating the handler logic that checks for it.
reason: The sentinel value distinguishes 'no suitable link available' from a real navigable URL, enabling the intended dual behavior of plain click vs. modifier-click. Changing the default silently breaks the handler's logic.
common_pattern: Preserving a sentinel default value (e.g., `href = '#'`) for link-like components and keeping it synchronized with the click-handler logic that inspects it to distinguish 'no link' from a real navigable URL.

text: When using the History API to reflect in-page UI state changes (tabs, panels, filters), ensure back/forward navigation remains consistent: use history.replaceState for non-navigational state changes, or add a popstate listener that restores the UI from the current location.
reason: Distinct functional rule about History API correctness; single-PR support but clear, actionable, and separate from documentation guidance.
common_pattern: Non-obvious URL/browser-history side effects in UI code need explicit treatment: document them clearly, and when they affect in-page state, keep browser navigation consistent.

text: When building or parsing Django ORM lookup/ordering paths (including relational field traversal, `label_for_field`, and admin sort keys), use `django.db.models.constants.LOOKUP_SEP` (`"__"`) rather than a custom separator such as `.` with manual `_` conversion. Do not hand-roll relation traversal (e.g. `_meta.get_field(...).related_model`) that Django already supports via double-underscore lookups.
reason: Django's ORM, `label_for_field`, and admin helpers already understand `__` for relation traversal, so custom separators require extra conversion logic, risk invalid sort keys (e.g. `author_name` instead of `author__name`), and may drift out of sync with ORM behavior.
scope: Django ORM field-path handling (e.g. Wagtail admin generic view code resolving labels or sort keys)
common_pattern: Use Django ORM's canonical field-reference mechanisms instead of ad-hoc string manipulation: (1) reference related fields through Django's LOOKUP_SEP rather than custom dot/single-underscore separators, and (2) distinguish model field references from literal values in database function expressions.

text: In Django ORM database-function expressions (e.g. `Substr`, `Concat`), wrap literal constants in `Value()` and never pass a bare literal where a column reference is intended; ensure the expression contains at least one real model field reference, since fieldless expressions fail with `Cannot resolve expression type, unknown output_field`.
reason: A bare string argument to a DB function is interpreted as a field name, while `Value()` marks a literal — ambiguity between the two produces incorrect SQL or unresolvable output fields.
scope: Django ORM expressions using database functions
common_pattern: Use Django ORM's canonical field-reference mechanisms instead of ad-hoc string manipulation: (1) reference related fields through Django's LOOKUP_SEP rather than custom dot/single-underscore separators, and (2) distinguish model field references from literal values in database function expressions.

text: When replacing a global object or default with explicit props/optional overrides, resolve each value using a backward-compatible fallback: read from the new prop/override first, and fall back to the existing global value when it is absent.
reason: Allows callers to pass data explicitly during migration without breaking legacy callers, preventing undefined values or runtime errors.
common_pattern: Backward-compatible fallback when migrating from a global object/default to explicit props or optional overrides: prefer the new prop/override when present, otherwise use the existing global value.

text: Pass all inputs and initial state from the calling page to a chooser/modal through its opening URL (e.g. query parameters), not through attributes or data attached to the triggering button or relying on other DOM details. Test chooser modal initial state by requesting the chooser URL with the relevant parameters and asserting server-rendered control states, rather than simulating clicks or asserting JS/DOM behavior; when asserting a specific chooser URL, configure the test setup so only the relevant feature is enabled.
reason: URL-driven inputs give modal components explicit, independent inputs/outputs, avoid the modal needing to know how it was triggered, and make behavior testable via URL-driven integration tests without DOM coupling.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin chooser/modal API design and configuration: chooser modals should be decoupled from the built-in widget, driven by explicit URL-passed inputs, and configured via data (props with global fallback, entity options, dynamic URL resolution) rather than hard-coded or DOM-coupled values.

text: When extracting helper logic around Draftail/`EditorState` content, have the helper accept serialized raw content (the output of `serialiseEditorStateToRaw`) rather than `EditorState` objects, so unit tests can use plain data fixtures without constructing Draftail internals.
reason: Plain serialized data simplifies test setup and assertions and reduces coupling of helper logic to Draftail internals.
common_pattern: Wagtail rich text (Draftail) conversion behavior should be tested at the serialized-output / converter-path level, colocated in existing test_rich_text.py modules, with helper code shaped to enable plain-data fixtures.

text: Place model-specific helper logic (computed values, derived attributes, resolution helpers) on the model class itself — as static/class methods, cached methods, or properties — rather than as standalone functions in utils modules, ad-hoc instance attributes set by external helpers, or new dedicated settings. This keeps behavior co-located with the model state, improves discoverability, and enables per-instance caching.
reason: Encapsulating model behavior on the model makes changes easier to reason about, avoids duplicated/monkey-patched logic, centralizes caching semantics, and reduces unnecessary configuration surface area.
common_pattern: Model-specific behavior and helpers should live on (or be reused from) the model class itself — not as standalone utils functions, ad-hoc instance attributes, new settings, or inline reimplementations.

text: When exposing request-routing functionality, name each method according to what it actually returns (e.g., distinguish a method returning a low-level `RouteResult` from one returning the resolved `Page`). Expose the primitive routing result, and add a convenience wrapper that returns the resolved page only when a concrete caller needs that shape.
reason: Methods should not be misnamed relative to their return type, and convenience wrappers should be justified by actual use cases rather than speculative API surface. In this PR the convenience method was ultimately not added because no caller needed it, while the naming concern remained valid.
common_pattern: API design for request-routing methods: distinguish low-level result-returning methods from convenience page-returning methods, and only add convenience wrappers when a concrete caller justifies them.

text: For `reverse("wagtail_serve", ...)` in contexts without a concrete page/path (e.g. the admin chooser), pass an empty string as the reverse argument and tolerate `NoReverseMatch`; do not synthesize a real page path or copy `Page.get_url_parts()`-style i18n handling unless tests show it is required.
reason: There is no valid page path when probing for potential matches and the serve view may not be mounted at the domain root; the translation logic is unnecessary for this DB-probing use case and adds complexity.
common_pattern: Wagtail page/site resolution: reuse existing framework APIs and conventions for resolving URLs/requests to pages and sites, and keep low-level URL reverse calls in non-request contexts simple rather than reimplementing framework internals.

text: For wildcard redirect/path matching in request-handling code, use fnmatch (pure string matching) instead of glob.glob to avoid filesystem access; pass the original pattern including wildcards directly to fnmatch, query candidate rows with __contains for the wildcard character rather than __endswith, and order matches by pattern length so precedence is deterministic when multiple patterns match.
reason: Avoids filesystem side effects in request handlers, lets fnmatch handle wildcard semantics without duplicating stripping logic, includes patterns with internal wildcards, and provides stable precedence when multiple wildcard redirects match.
common_pattern: Wildcard redirect/path matching in request handling: prefer fnmatch-based pure string matching over filesystem-touching glob, use original wildcard patterns directly, filter candidates with __contains, and order matches by pattern length for deterministic precedence.

text: When resolving a request to a page, return the actual page that handles the request; page routing should take precedence over redirect resolution, so redirects are only checked as a fallback when no page matches. This also applies to `RoutablePageMixin` helpers, which should return the handling page rather than the internal route/subpage.
reason: Pages should win over redirects for duplicate paths, and callers should get the least unexpected result: the page that actually handles the request.
common_pattern: Page/request URL resolution should return the actual page that handles the request and should prefer page routing over redirects or internal routing artifacts.

text: In `wagtail/contrib/search_promotions/views.py`'s `IndexView`, define the editors' picks column with `name="editors_picks"` and pass the `.all` lookup through `accessor` (e.g. `accessor="editors_picks.all"`).
reason: Preserves the intended Column API usage for the specific search promotions view.
common_pattern: Project-specific configuration requirements for Wagtail's search_promotions IndexView, covering permission policy and column accessor usage.

text: Express optional parameters and fallback values as default parameter values in the function signature. Do not accept `null` for a parameter that already has a default, do not re-implement the fallback with `||`/manual coalescing in the body, and do not hide caller-overridable values as local constants inside the function.
reason: Default parameters make optionality and fallbacks explicit in the API, remove dead/misleading fallback logic, and let callers override values as intended data inputs.
common_pattern: The cluster is about how optional/fallback parameter values should be expressed and consumed. Two complementary sub-patterns emerge: (a) fallback and optional values should live as default parameter values in the function signature (rather than as null-accepting types, in-body `||` fallbacks, or local constants), and (b) at call sites, values should be handled explicitly when the default could change or is not obviously stable, while redundant re-statement of a known default is avoided.

text: When a control outside the AJAX response region must update after results reload, use a targeted update mechanism instead of replacing the whole component. Prefer an existing selective-update pattern such as a pub/sub controller or a w-teleport template included in the before_results block, and give the original control a stable wrapper/target ID so its state can be synchronized.
reason: Preserves UI state (open popups, form errors) and avoids unnecessary rerendering while keeping controls synchronized with reloaded AJAX results.
common_pattern: Selective updating of UI controls outside the AJAX-swapped results region, rather than rerendering or replacing the entire component

text: In `KeyboardController.shouldLoad`, return `true` unconditionally rather than gating on `WAGTAIL_CONFIG.KEYBOARD_SHORTCUTS_ENABLED`, so the `?` shortcut can still open `keyboard_shortcut_dialog.html`, which displays a warning when shortcuts are disabled and info when enabled.
reason: Preserves the use case where users can still open the shortcut dialog and understand that keyboard shortcuts are currently disabled.
common_pattern: Keyboard-shortcut declarations in this project's controller/component system should expose shortcuts through the standard ARIA attribute `aria-keyshortcuts` on the interactive element that triggers them (as the single source of truth), with conditional element targeting instead of global scoping, and consistent modifier conventions to avoid collisions.

text: In revision/history views, only expose actions that are actually applicable to the given revision and view context: gate per-revision action options on the revision having changed content, and hide workflow/moderation actions (e.g. submit for moderation, approve) on revert views, mirroring the equivalent page-level menu logic.
reason: Presenting actions that are not meaningful for a revision (no content change) or not valid in a revert context confuses users; the page-level action menu already filters these, so revision views should be consistent.
common_pattern: Correct behavior and implementation of admin history/revision views: these views must reflect the *current* context (current page state, applicability of actions) rather than stale or irrelevant revision data, and shared revision UI should be centralized rather than duplicated.

text: Wagtail generic admin model views (e.g. `EditView`, `DeleteView`) must resolve objects through a configurable lookup field / URL kwarg analogous to Django's `pk_url_kwarg`/`slug_url_kwarg`, instead of hard-coding `id` or `pk`. Default the lookup field to `id` (avoiding `_meta` resolution overhead), and let subclasses set a custom kwarg (e.g. a `CustomUser` with no `id`) rather than overriding `get_object()` or other URL-building methods.
reason: Hard-coding `id`/`pk` breaks for models with custom or missing primary keys and forces every subclass to duplicate workarounds; a configurable lookup field keeps the base view reusable and consistent across generic views, matching Django CBV conventions.
scope: wagtail/admin/views/generic/ (generic model views and their subclasses)
common_pattern: Wagtail generic admin model views should follow Django's SingleObjectMixin conventions: object lookup must be configurable (via a lookup field / `pk_url_kwarg`-style kwarg) rather than hard-coded to `id`/`pk`, and reusable lookup behaviour should live in composable mixins so sibling views stay consistent.

text: In Wagtail block rendering, represent the absence of errors in the serialized `error_json` payload as JSON `null` (e.g. `json.dumps(None)` or the literal `"null"`), not as an empty object `{}`.
reason: Preserves the established API shape expected by downstream clients and keeps 'no errors' distinguishable from an empty error object.
scope: project-specific: Wagtail block rendering error JSON (wagtail/blocks/base.py `render_with_errors`)
common_pattern: How to represent the absence of errors in the block-rendering error JSON payload (the serialized shape of 'no errors'). The cluster contains a contradiction: one generalization proposes `json.dumps({})` while two later ones argue for JSON `null` (`json.dumps(None)` / `"null"`) to match the established client contract.

text: Override `label_from_instance()` on a `ModelChoiceField` subclass to customize how model instances are displayed as options, and ensure any related data needed for labels is fetched in bulk (e.g., `select_related`/`prefetch_related` or a precomputed mapping) instead of issuing a query per choice.
reason: `label_from_instance()` is the standard extension point for option labels, so label logic belongs there rather than in widgets or forms; however, because it runs for every choice, per-instance queries become an N+1 problem that scales with the number of options.
common_pattern: Using Django's `label_from_instance()` hook on ModelChoiceField to customize option labels, while ensuring related data is fetched in bulk to avoid N+1 queries during label rendering.

text: Prefer a single structured argument over multiple positional parameters when a function or constructor takes several arguments (~3+): accept one options object (destructured, defaulting to `{}`) placed after the primary/required argument, or an explicit sequence parameter that callers spread, rather than listing each value positionally or using `*args`. Keep required primary arguments (e.g., DOM elements) positional and group only configuration values into the options object.
reason: Named/structured parameters make call sites self-documenting, eliminate fragile argument-order mistakes, and allow new options to be added without changing the function's positional signature; an explicit sequence also enables type annotations and avoids forcing callers to spread ad-hoc positional arguments.
common_pattern: Argument-passing design: avoid long positional parameter lists by passing a single structured argument (an options object or an explicit sequence that can be spread), keeping the call site self-documenting and the signature stable as parameters evolve.

text: Keep `is_valid()` free of side effects such as database writes, lock refreshes, or user-facing messages; perform those side effects in the appropriate lifecycle hooks (`form_valid()` / `form_invalid()` for class-based views).
reason: `is_valid()` should remain a pure validation predicate; side effects there are surprising, can execute unpredictably when validation runs multiple times, and make control flow harder to reason about and test.
common_pattern: Django form/class-based-view lifecycle conventions: how forms are bound, validated, saved, and how validated data is reused — keeping form state semantics explicit and free of side effects outside the appropriate lifecycle hooks.

text: Overrides of Django ModelForm `save(self, commit=True)` must honor the `commit` parameter: pass it through to `super().save()` (or mutate via `super().save(commit=False)` and only persist with `instance.save()` when `commit=True`). When all extra fields are already applied, prefer calling the instance's `.save()` directly instead of routing through `form.save(commit=False)`.
reason: Callers rely on `commit=False` to obtain an unsaved, modified instance without a database write; unconditionally saving breaks that contract. Conversely, extra indirection via `commit=False` when the instance is saved anyway obscures intent.
common_pattern: Django form/class-based-view lifecycle conventions: how forms are bound, validated, saved, and how validated data is reused — keeping form state semantics explicit and free of side effects outside the appropriate lifecycle hooks.

text: Reuse values already present in `form.cleaned_data` instead of re-fetching the same object from the database by primary key.
reason: Avoids a redundant database query and uses already-validated form data, reducing unnecessary DB access and potential inconsistency.
common_pattern: Django form/class-based-view lifecycle conventions: how forms are bound, validated, saved, and how validated data is reused — keeping form state semantics explicit and free of side effects outside the appropriate lifecycle hooks.

text: Choose the range filter class that matches the underlying field's granularity: use `DateTimeFromToRangeFilter` for `DateTimeField` fields and `DateFromToRangeFilter` for `DateField` fields.
reason: Using a date-only filter on a datetime field drops time precision and produces misleading filtering behavior (e.g., for scheduled actions that happen at a specific date and time).
common_pattern: Consistency rules for Wagtail admin range filters and their widgets/adapters: naming bounds to reflect inclusive/general range semantics, matching the filter class to the underlying field granularity, and rendering/labeling bounds explicitly rather than ambiguously.

text: When a page chooser is restricted to a specific page type, use the common path prefix of existing pages of that type to pre-open the relevant section of the page tree when one exists.
reason: Improves UX by starting users in the likely location of pages they need to select.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin page-chooser conventions: use the standard AdminPageChooser widget, configure it with page_models, resolve target page types to the most specific applicable Page class, and improve tree UX using common path prefixes.

text: In Wagtail StreamField blocks and documentation examples, prefer `ImageBlock` when content editors genuinely need to decide alt text or decorative status per image; use `ImageChooserBlock` when the alt text is already available from an existing field (e.g. a caption rendered as the image `alt` attribute) or is governed by a developer-wide rule. Document `ImageBlock` as the accessible default for routine image fields, reserving chooser blocks for examples that specifically demonstrate chooser behaviour.
reason: Guides developers toward built-in accessibility handling for common cases, avoids duplicated alt-text fields, and keeps alt text synchronized with visible content.
scope: Wagtail StreamField block definitions and docs/reference/streamfield/blocks.md
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Wagtail's `ImageBlock` vs `ImageChooserBlock`: how `ImageBlock` should validate alt-text/decorative state, and when each block should be used in StreamField definitions and documentation examples.

text: When preserving state across Wagtail admin navigation and form submissions, follow the established Wagtail query-parameter patterns for the context: for chooser/locale-switching view URLs, copy `request.GET` and remove unnecessary parameters, matching chooser templates; for redirect/return destinations, pass a dedicated `?next=` query parameter on GET and include it as a hidden form field on POST instead of forwarding all GET parameters or embedding state directly in URLs.
reason: Keeps Python views and admin templates consistent with existing Wagtail conventions, avoids query-parameter drift, and preserves useful return flows without leaking unrelated state into URLs or form submissions.
common_pattern: Preserving query-parameter/state information across Wagtail admin navigation and form submissions by following established Wagtail patterns rather than ad-hoc parameter forwarding or URL-embedded state.

text: In Wagtail block subclasses, only override `get_searchable_content` when the subclass changes searchable-content behavior; otherwise inherit the parent implementation. When overriding, return the block's relevant user-visible text (e.g., alt text, table captions, column headings) instead of an empty list.
reason: Avoiding empty or redundant overrides preserves the class hierarchy's searchable content and ensures useful visible text is included in search indexing rather than silently excluded.
scope: Wagtail block subclasses implementing or overriding `get_searchable_content`
common_pattern: Overrides of `get_searchable_content` in Wagtail block subclasses should be intentional: inherit the parent implementation when behavior is unchanged, and when overriding, return relevant user-visible textual metadata instead of an empty list.

text: Normalization must handle every accepted input representation (raw IDs mixed with model instances, lazy/serialized forms like list-of-dicts) and expand nested child values to a uniform fully-normalized form before invoking child bulk fetches or other downstream consumers.
reason: Bulk and child APIs require uniform input; if lazy or mixed raw representations bypass normalization, downstream code either falls back to per-item queries or violates the normalize contract.
common_pattern: Normalization routines must accept and convert every legitimate input representation — mixed raw/model instances, lazy/serialized list-of-dicts — into a uniform, fully-expanded form before any downstream bulk or child-block operation consumes them.

text: When changing the type consumed or returned by a subclass, base class, or shared helper, audit and update all downstream/base methods that still assume the previous type.
reason: Type changes can silently break inherited implementations and shared helpers that rely on attributes or behavior of the old type, so they must be overridden or updated to accept the new type.
common_pattern: When a subclass or component changes the type it consumes, produces, or exposes, all downstream helper methods and inherited/base implementations that still assume the old type must be audited and updated to accept or handle the new type.

text: Put shared bound-block render context logic (e.g. injecting `id`) in the base `BoundBlock.render_as_block` method so that `render` and `render_as_block` behave consistently, rather than requiring each block subclass to duplicate the override.
reason: Keeps rendering behavior consistent across `render` and `render_as_block` and avoids fragmented, duplicated context injection in subclasses.
common_pattern: Wagtail block-rendering consistency: when subclassing blocks, delegate rendering to the base implementation or to the wrapped child block, rather than relying on defaults or duplicating overrides across subclasses.

text: In `StructBlock`'s JavaScript, do not modify the `prefix` argument passed to `renderChild()` for block child defs; prefixing for block child defs is handled internally by `renderChildBlockDef` (using `this.prefix + '-' + childBlockDef.name`), and the `prefix` argument is only relevant when rendering a block group.
reason: Preserves behavior unchanged from the previous version; unnecessary changes to the prefix argument for child defs can introduce bugs.
common_pattern: Wagtail block-rendering consistency: when subclassing blocks, delegate rendering to the base implementation or to the wrapped child block, rather than relying on defaults or duplicating overrides across subclasses.

text: In API serialization code, the method that produces an API-facing representation must be named `get_api_representation(self, value, context=None)` (not `render_api`). Custom `StructBlock` subclasses that change their runtime value type (e.g., to a model instance instead of `StructValue`) or that override storage hooks such as `get_prep_value` must implement `get_api_representation`; when the API representation should match the stored/prep representation, delegate to `get_prep_value(value)`.
reason: Without an explicit `get_api_representation` override, default `StructBlock` serialization does not understand the custom value type and omits custom fields (e.g., contextual alt text, decorative state) from API output; delegating to `get_prep_value` keeps prep and API representations consistent. Standardizing the method name improves clarity and consistency with existing API representation naming conventions.
scope: Wagtail API serialization / custom StructBlock and ImageBlock implementations
common_pattern: The Wagtail API-facing representation hook for blocks/streamfields is `get_api_representation(self, value, context=None)`: it must be used (not `render_api`) for naming, and custom `StructBlock` subclasses that change their value type or override storage hooks (`get_prep_value`) must implement it, typically delegating to `get_prep_value(value)` so API output stays consistent with stored/prep data.

text: In Wagtail admin block comparison (`wagtail/admin/compare.py`), make comparison block-type-aware: recursively apply block-type-specific comparison to nested StructBlocks (including those with custom templates) rather than falling back to HTML/template rendering, and reflect the block hierarchy when rendering nested field labels. When a block subclasses `StructBlock` but overrides behavior so its value is not a standard StructBlock dict (e.g. an image), handle the block's actual value/child blocks in `StructBlockComparison` instead of assuming StructBlock internals.
reason: Prevents errors and incorrect or inconsistent revision diffs in the Wagtail admin (History view) when comparing nested StructBlocks, custom-templated blocks, or StructBlock subclasses whose value is not a standard StructValue.
scope: Wagtail admin block comparison; StructBlock subclasses and nested StreamField blocks
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Wagtail admin block comparison (`wagtail/admin/compare.py`): block diffs and comparisons must be **block-type-aware** — applying each block's own value/child semantics recursively — instead of assuming generic StructBlock dict semantics, falling back to template/HTML rendering, or over-specializing the generic fallback.

text: Treat `ParentalKey` as a single-parent-only relationship: do not define multiple `ParentalKey` fields on the same model (each implies the model is edited only as a child of that parent) — use a dedicated child model for additional parent-child links. Before relying on nested `ParentalKey` hierarchies, verify that copy/publish operations include all nested descendants; if they do not, use `ForeignKey` or custom copy handling and add a regression test.
reason: Multiple non-null `ParentalKey` fields create conflicting child-of-parent semantics and can fail when the linked key is non-null, while nested `ParentalKey` relationships may not be fully supported by copy operations, silently omitting deeper children.
common_pattern: Parent/child relationship modeling must have unambiguous, single-purpose semantics: parent references should not be duplicated, mixed-typed, or used where the ORM/copy pipeline does not fully support them.

text: When a helper/wrapper object models a parent/child relationship, its parent field should consistently hold the helper type rather than raw model instances; if the field cannot hold a consistent type, remove it instead of keeping mixed-type state.
reason: Mixed-type parent attributes make traversal and equality behavior unclear and are difficult to test or document.
common_pattern: Parent/child relationship modeling must have unambiguous, single-purpose semantics: parent references should not be duplicated, mixed-typed, or used where the ORM/copy pipeline does not fully support them.

text: Resolve document/image URLs through the object's serving-aware `url` property (`obj.url`), never the storage-level `file.url`, so that serve-method settings, filename serve routes, storage fallbacks, and collection-privacy hooks are honored.
reason: Using `file.url` bypasses serving and privacy logic and can leak URLs that the document serving configuration intended to restrict.
common_pattern: Wagtail's document/image serving layer hinges on a configurable 'serve method' (e.g. WAGTAILDOCS_SERVE_METHOD); all code that touches document URLs — serializers, tests, and docs — must resolve URLs through the serving-aware path and account for the configured serve method rather than bypassing it.

text: For polymorphic constructor or API arguments, validate against the required subtype/interface rather than a broad ancestor type; for internal callers, prefer stricter signatures that fail fast on contract violations, and add tests for invalid/unsupported argument types to document expected errors or fallbacks. Avoid combining a broad parameter type with an inner subtype check around the primary operation.
reason: A broad ancestor check accepts invalid types that may not implement the required subtype API, causing failures later, while invalid-input tests and strict signatures make the contract explicit and surface programming errors early.
common_pattern: Enforce subtype-specific type contracts for polymorphic constructor/API arguments at the boundary: validate against the required subtype/interface, prefer strict fail-fast signatures for internal callers, and test invalid/unsupported inputs to document expected behavior.

text: Expose `purge_all` only as a fallback path within site-based purging, not as a standalone public utility: when purging across all sites, iterate `Site.objects.all()` and call the per-site helper (`purge_site(site)`), reserving `purge_all()` for cases where the hostname is not representative (e.g. the default site) or the backend lacks hostname-level purging.
reason: Purging everything is destructive and should be exceptional, while the default site's hostname may not represent the real domain, so a purge-all escape hatch ensures correctness without making broad invalidation a normal API.
common_pattern: Design and correctness rules for Wagtail frontend-cache purge utilities: when and how to purge (new vs old URLs, empty batches, batch-size limits, purge_all fallback) and how to expose/document purge features.

text: Accessor methods that expose a collection should return the stored collection or a direct view/comprehension rather than recomposing values, wrapping the result in an unnecessary generator, or hand-rolling memoization, unless filtering or transformation is explicitly required.
reason: Keeps a single source of truth, avoids duplicated inclusion logic, and reduces boilerplate and indirection in simple collection-returning accessors.
common_pattern: Collection-returning accessor methods should be thin and direct: return the stored collection, its direct view, or a simple eager comprehension instead of recomposing values, adding unnecessary generator wrappers, or hand-rolling memoization.

text: When writing or overriding code that consumes Django field `choices` (normalization utilities in `wagtail/utils/utils.py`, `Select.optgroups` overrides, choice-value coercion in choice blocks), support all documented Django choices formats: flat `(key, label)` sequences, list/tuple-grouped optgroups, dict-grouped mappings, and nested optgroup structures (recursing into groups so keys/labels are normalized at every depth). If a nested/grouped format genuinely cannot be supported, document the unsupported case in a comment or docstring rather than leaving it as a silent limitation.
reason: Django treats all of these shapes as valid `choices` definitions, so handling only one format makes utilities incomplete and leaves optgroup keys un-normalized after (de)serialization; documenting any remaining gap keeps behavior consistent across grouped and ungrouped options and makes limitations findable when debugging.
common_pattern: Utility functions, widget overrides, and normalization code that consume Django field `choices` must handle the full range of documented choices formats — flat (key, label) sequences, list/tuple optgroups, dict-grouped mappings, and nested optgroup structures — rather than only one shape; where a format genuinely cannot be supported, the limitation must be documented explicitly.

text: Only support input formats/types in a utility that callers can actually produce or consume; do not add speculative handling for formats with no concrete use case — remove it rather than writing tests or workarounds to accommodate it.
reason: Unsupported-by-callers formats are dead code that adds complexity, maintenance burden, and test surface area without providing real value.
common_pattern: Both generalizations express the same principle: do not add speculative support for input formats or types that have no concrete, realizable use case from callers. Both cite YAGNI-style reasoning (dead code, complexity, maintenance burden) and both recommend removing rather than accommodating such functionality.

text: Register model/view permissions through the standard mechanism provided by the relevant abstraction — `ModelViewSet`'s built-in permission registration, the existing `create_extra_permissions` branch for model mixins, or `AppConfig.ready()` for app-level policies — rather than creating custom bulk registration hooks or separate registration paths.
reason: Keeps permission registration centralized, customizable per view/model, consistent with existing framework patterns, and avoids import-time/AppRegistryNotReady problems.
scope: Wagtail permission-registration code (viewsets, model mixins, and app configs); broadly applicable to Django permission registration.
common_pattern: Permission registration should use the standard/built-in mechanism for the relevant abstraction instead of ad-hoc bulk hooks or separate registration paths.

text: On Django responses, set HTTP headers explicitly via `response.headers[...]` and do not manually set transport-level headers such as `Content-Length`; let Django or the app server compute and set those.
reason: Using `response.headers[...]` makes header intent explicit and aligns with the modern Django response API. Transport-level headers like `Content-Length` are framed by the framework or server and should not be manually duplicated or conflicted with.
common_pattern: Correct manipulation of HTTP response headers on Django response objects: use the explicit headers API for application headers and leave transport-level header computation to Django or the app server.
