text: Declare `api_fields` explicitly at the appropriate level of the model hierarchy: define the common/default field list on the shared base (e.g. abstract) class so subclasses automatically inherit API exposure (as with `AbstractFormField` exposing `label`, `help_text`, `required`, `choices`), and have subclasses explicitly extend the inherited field definitions when they require additional fields — never leave an API subclass as a bare `pass` that only inherits an incomplete field set.
reason: Centralizing default `api_fields` on the base class removes boilerplate and makes the common API-exposure case work automatically, while requiring subclasses to explicitly extend the list prevents an empty subclass from silently exposing an incomplete set of fields that fails to meet its consumers' needs (e.g. admin UI list/detail requirements).
scope: Reusable/abstract model base classes and their concrete API subclasses
common_pattern: Placement and completeness of API field declarations (`api_fields`) across a model inheritance hierarchy — defaults belong on the reusable base/abstract class so subclasses inherit them, and subclasses that need more fields must explicitly extend the inherited list rather than leaving a bare `pass`.

text: Do not introduce `OrderedDict` merely to control property order in dicts that will be serialized to JSON (or otherwise treated as order-insensitive); a plain `dict` is sufficient. Keep a stable field order only when it materially aids human inspection, not as a semantic contract.
reason: JSON object property order is not guaranteed and carries no semantic meaning, so `OrderedDict` adds complexity without providing a real contract. Note: the source PR contains a direct tension between 'use OrderedDict for readable field order' and 'OrderedDict is unnecessary for JSON'; the resolved stance is that order is not a semantic guarantee, so prefer plain dict.
common_pattern: Python data-structure ordering: be deliberate about whether insertion/iteration order is preserved, and choose constructs (dict.fromkeys, list of tuples) that preserve order when it matters, rather than relying on set() or unordered iteration. A secondary, contradictory sub-pattern concerns whether OrderedDict is worth using for JSON-serialized dicts.

text: Keep Page.save() and Page.move() generic and simple: do not add optional URL-change branching or extra data plumbing to them. Put optional URL-change behavior in a separate extension point (a dedicated signal handler or method), reusing existing lifecycle signals (e.g. page_moved) or a narrower one (e.g. slug-change) before introducing a brand-new signal.
reason: Optional functionality should not increase the complexity of the always-executed core persistence/move paths; confining it to signals keeps the code simple, decoupled, and consistent with the existing event model.
scope: Wagtail Page model / page lifecycle signals
common_pattern: Designing Wagtail page lifecycle signals for URL/slug changes: keep core model mutation methods (save/move) generic so optional URL-change behavior lives in signal handlers or separate extension points, and shape signal emission/detection around correctness (site-aware, batched) and efficiency rather than expanding core methods or emitting redundantly.

text: Emit page URL-change signals in a site-aware and batched way: emit once per site (since a single internal url_path cannot represent all public URLs of a page mounted on multiple sites), and do not emit for descendant pages when an ancestor slug changes (descendant url_path values are updated in a single bulk update, so per-descendant emission would jeopardise that efficiency).
reason: Site-aware emission produces correct before/after public URLs, and batched emission preserves the efficiency of the bulk descendant url_path update.
common_pattern: Designing Wagtail page lifecycle signals for URL/slug changes: keep core model mutation methods (save/move) generic so optional URL-change behavior lives in signal handlers or separate extension points, and shape signal emission/detection around correctness (site-aware, batched) and efficiency rather than expanding core methods or emitting redundantly.

text: In edit handler classes, implement html_declarations by delegating to cls.get_child_edit_handler_class().html_declarations() instead of manually traversing related_model._meta.fields to collect stream_block declarations, and include tests verifying that declarations for related-model StreamFields are included.
reason: Reuses the child edit handler's existing declaration logic, avoids duplicated field introspection, keeps declaration generation consistent between parent and child handlers, and catches regressions in declaration inclusion for related models and StreamFields.
common_pattern: Edit handler html_declarations generation should reuse the child edit handler's declaration logic instead of manual field traversal, with tests covering related-model StreamField declarations.

text: Treat model fields as schema commitments justified by current concrete use and a single source of truth: do not add speculative, historical/derived, or denormalized fields, and only remove an existing field after its replacement is implemented or the logic that required it is gone.
reason: Merges the cluster's complementary add/remove guidance: fields should not be speculative or duplicate state, but existing fields should not be removed prematurely before their replacement exists.
common_pattern: Lifecycle management of model fields: add or keep fields only when justified by current concrete usage and a single source of truth; avoid speculative, historical, derived, or denormalized fields, and remove fields only after their replacement or copied-state purpose is gone.

text: When writing queryset filters or query logic against enum/discriminator-style fields, only reference values that are actually defined in the codebase and that the application's write path can persist. Do not filter on not-yet-implemented enum values (they silently return empty result sets and can remove expected UI behavior) and do not add branches for sentinel values the write path never stores (rely on the write-path invariant unless external/custom code may write them).
reason: Filtering on undefined or never-persisted enum values eliminates valid results, causing silent regressions, while handling impossible database states adds complexity and makes query behavior diverge from the actual data model.
common_pattern: Query/filter logic must only reference enum or discriminator values that actually exist in the codebase and can be persisted by the write path; filtering on undefined or never-persisted sentinel values silently yields empty results or adds dead branches.

text: In wagtail/contrib/modeladmin, for each configurable ModelAdmin attribute, provide a corresponding get_<attribute>() method that returns the attribute value by default and call the getter from views instead of reading the attribute directly. If the value may depend on the current request/user, the getter should accept request as a positional argument and be called with the active request.
reason: Follows the established ModelAdmin API pattern, allows developers to customize behavior beyond a static list/value, and enables per-request/user filtering of configuration.
common_pattern: ModelAdmin configuration getter API pattern: expose configurable attributes through get_<attribute>() methods, optionally accepting the active request when the value is request/user-dependent.

text: In `Page.__init__` (Django model), only assign creation-time defaults such as `content_type` and `show_in_menus` (e.g. `if 'show_in_menus' not in kwargs: self.show_in_menus = self.show_in_menus_default`) inside the `if self.pk is None:` guard, so existing database-loaded instances retain their stored values.
reason: Applying defaults unconditionally overwrites values on persisted instances, causing unexpected behavior and broken tests.
common_pattern: In a Django model's `__init__`, defaults for fields (e.g. `content_type`, `show_in_menus`) must only be applied when constructing a new instance, guarded by `if self.pk is None:`, so instances loaded from the database are not mutated.

text: For optional descriptive metadata, do not fall back to a different field's value; when composing display or fallback text from multiple optional metadata fields, omit missing/falsy values before formatting and joining them.
reason: Both generalizations address the same underlying concern: optional metadata fields such as help text, author name, or provider name should not produce misleading fallback text. They are complementary halves of one rule—avoid cross-field fallback, and safely omit absent values when composing from multiple optional fields.
common_pattern: Optional descriptive metadata should be handled semantically: missing metadata must not be replaced by an unrelated field, and when multiple optional fields are combined into display/fallback text, missing values should be omitted before formatting and joining.

text: In Wagtail forms, form-processing methods should return the created submission instance, and callers should pass it as an explicit keyword argument (e.g., `form_submission`) to the landing-page render hook so overrides and templates can access the submitted data.
reason: Merges three complementary halves from the same discussion: processing returns the created object, callers capture/thread it, and the landing-page render hook accepts it explicitly. This avoids relying on side-channel state and keeps the submission available for context or redirect logic.
common_pattern: Explicitly threading the created form-submission model instance from form processing into the landing-page render hook as a dedicated keyword parameter, so landing pages can expose submitted data without side-channel state or re-querying.

text: When altering term-splitting/tokenization in search query classes (e.g., Term, PlainText), keep multi-word parsing semantics aligned across query classes and backend adapters. Before adopting a shared Python-side splitting strategy, validate how each backend's parser (e.g., plainto_tsquery) handles the same input so tests and query behavior reflect actual backend semantics.
reason: Prevents divergent behavior between Python-side query classes and backend parsers, avoids incorrect assumptions from cross-backend uniformity, and keeps multi-word search tests accurate.
scope: search query classes, tokenization/term splitting, and backend adapters
common_pattern: Search term-splitting/tokenization semantics must be consistent across query classes and explicitly validated against backend-specific parser behavior before introducing a backend-agnostic Python-side splitting strategy.

text: For Django file-backed models and management commands that mutate them, route cleanup of replaced or derived files through model signals (`post_save`/`post_delete`) and the configured storage API rather than form `save()` hooks or manual `MEDIA_ROOT` deletion; perform irreversible deletions only after the DB save or transaction succeeds, and tolerate backing files that are already missing.
reason: Combines the cluster's complementary rules: cleanup must run on all mutation paths, use the storage abstraction, avoid inconsistent DB/file state when saves fail, and remain robust when files are missing or storage is remote.
common_pattern: Django file-backed model cleanup should be centralized through model signals and the configured storage backend, performed only after successful DB persistence, and made resilient to missing backing files and non-local storage.

text: Tooltip positioning, sizing, and constraint logic should live in the shared Tooltip component and account for available viewport/container space when choosing placement, rather than being reimplemented in consumer components or relying only on the target and requested direction.
reason: Centralizing tooltip behavior avoids duplicated positioning logic and keeps consumer components focused, while space-aware placement prevents tooltips from overflowing or being clipped.
common_pattern: Centralizing tooltip positioning and constraint logic in the shared Tooltip component, which must account for available space when choosing placement.

text: Inline entity handlers in rich-text converters should accept entity-specific metadata (such as `entity_type` and `mutability`) as constructor/configuration parameters rather than hard-coding them, so a single generic handler (e.g. `InlineEntityElementHandler`) can be reused across all inline entity types.
reason: Hard-coded metadata ties a handler to one entity type and prevents reuse for custom inline entities; parameterizing entity_type and mutability makes the handler genuinely generic without needing a new class per entity type.
common_pattern: Design of reusable inline-entity handlers in rich-text converters: keep handlers generic by parameterizing entity metadata, avoid magic entity-type strings via central constants, and keep the cross-language (Python↔JS) attribute contract tolerant of missing values.

text: Model mutable boolean state as a noun resource subpath (e.g. `/active/`) rather than a verb/action path (e.g. `/toggle/`), and expose idempotent state-setting operations: `PUT` to set the flag true and `DELETE` to clear it.
reason: Resource-oriented routes make the state being changed explicit and align with HTTP method semantics, while idempotent `PUT`/`DELETE` operations avoid the frontend/backend state desynchronization that non-idempotent toggle endpoints can cause under concurrency, failures, or retries.
common_pattern: RESTful modeling of mutable boolean flag state: use a noun resource subpath instead of a verb/action endpoint, and expose idempotent HTTP methods for setting and clearing the flag.

text: In rich-text link/model lookup handlers, do not associate a handler with a cache-backed model: `get_model()` should return `None` unless the link type is genuinely backed by a model whose record deletion affects the rich-text reference. Handlers used for garbage collection (e.g. `get_instance`) must be side-effect-free and return `None` for missing references rather than calling provider/fetch methods that create cache records. Do not catch `DoesNotExist` inside these lookups — let it propagate so callers decide how to handle a missing linked object.
reason: Cache models like `Embed` are not canonical targets of a rich-text reference, so returning them from `get_model` implies a referential relationship that does not exist. Fetching on lookup inverts garbage-collection semantics, and swallowing `DoesNotExist` hides missing objects.
common_pattern: Rich-text LinkHandler / link-model lookup handlers must transparently represent missing or inappropriate references: no model association for cache-backed links, no side effects, and clear not-found semantics — plus documentation of those semantics.

text: Do not perform embed lookups, HTML fetching, or template rendering inside value-object constructors (e.g. `EmbedValue.__init__`). Defer the work to the point of consumption: expose derived values such as `html` as a `cached_property` that calls `get_embed(url)` / `embed_to_frontend_html(self.url)` on first access (catching `EmbedException`), or resolve the embed explicitly where it is actually needed — during `{% embed %}` template tag rendering (so the lookup happens exactly once), or via an explicit `get_embed()` call in the block's `clean()`. Constructors should stay cheap and side-effect-free.
reason: Eager lookup in `__init__` makes construction expensive and raises/handles embed exceptions at construction time; a block that builds many values (e.g. 100 random-video URLs) but renders one would trigger up to 100 unnecessary embed queries. Lazy `cached_property` access and single-point resolution at the template tag / clean() hook keep construction cheap, cache the result, and match developer expectations about when the fetch occurs.
common_pattern: Embed resolution/HTML fetching must not happen inside value-object constructors; it should be deferred — computed lazily (cached_property) or performed explicitly at the point of consumption (template tag rendering, clean() validation hook).

text: Implement menu ordering and nesting in the menu item API itself (e.g. add `order`/`parent` parameters to `ModelAdminGroup.__init__()` and `ModelAdminGroup.get_menu_item()`) instead of branching in call sites like `get_submenu_items()`; an explicit `order` argument passed to `get_menu_item()` must take precedence over the class-level `menu_order` attribute.
reason: Keeps ordering logic encapsulated in the menu class, lets `items()` pass values through without duplicating conditionals, and ensures caller-supplied ordering is never silently ignored.
common_pattern: Menu/composition ordering in Wagtail admin constructs is a first-class API concern: ordering must be expressed through explicit API parameters rather than ad-hoc branching, explicit per-call ordering takes precedence over class-level defaults, and existing `order` values must be preserved to avoid breaking user customizations.

text: When removing an item from an ordered menu/registry, preserve the existing `order` values of the remaining items rather than renumbering them.
reason: Renumbering can change the relative order between built-in items and users' custom menu items, breaking user customizations and backward compatibility.
common_pattern: Menu/composition ordering in Wagtail admin constructs is a first-class API concern: ordering must be expressed through explicit API parameters rather than ad-hoc branching, explicit per-call ordering takes precedence over class-level defaults, and existing `order` values must be preserved to avoid breaking user customizations.

text: When indexing or extracting references, determine field capabilities from each field's own capabilities or interface (e.g. enabled rich-text features or presence of an `extract_references` method) rather than from a single global pattern or enumerated core field classes, and use the same capability criterion for both index eligibility (`model_is_indexable`) and reference extraction.
reason: This avoids false positives and unnecessary scanning for limited rich-text fields, allows third-party/custom field types to participate via a known interface, and prevents indexability/extraction mismatches where a model is marked indexable but its references are never extracted.
scope: Wagtail reference indexing; generally applicable to extensible field-capability detection.
common_pattern: Reference indexing/extraction should be driven by each field's actual capabilities or interface—not by global assumptions or hardcoded core field types—and all related stages should use the same capability criterion.

text: Keep the base Block API minimal: `prepare_for_react` should be a thin delegation to `prepare_value` with signature `(self, value, errors=None)` rather than taking extra parent/type parameters, and parallel methods with identical behavior should not be introduced.
reason: Avoids duplicate API surface and clarifies the Block contract for subclasses.
common_pattern: Design of the Wagtail Block contract: parent/container blocks should own wrapper (BlockData/StreamChild) translation so child blocks always receive unwrapped values, and the base Block API should stay minimal — a thin `prepare_for_react(value, errors=None)` delegating to `prepare_value`, with no duplicate parallel methods.

text: When enumerating StreamFields on a Wagtail model, use the model's `get_streamfield_names()` helper and resolve each field via `model._meta.get_field(name)` instead of manually filtering `model._meta.get_fields()` with `isinstance(field, StreamField)`.
reason: Reuses the project's canonical StreamField discovery logic, avoids duplicated field-detection behavior, and keeps StreamField enumeration consistent across the codebase.
common_pattern: Wagtail StreamField handling conventions — the cluster shares the StreamField/JSONField entity but splits into three distinct concerns: (a) when/how widgets are initialized client-side, (b) canonical discovery/serialization helpers for StreamFields, and (c) internal API-shape details of the StreamField class itself.

text: Client-side reusable packages must expose an explicit integration API (e.g., a React component or initialization function) and be side-effect-free to import; host applications are responsible for initialization and host-specific wiring rather than relying on a prebuilt side-effectful bundle entry.
reason: This makes dependency and context boundaries explicit, avoids hidden coupling to a specific host app, and prevents implicit initialization order or duplicate execution issues.
scope: global for Wagtail client-side library integrations
common_pattern: Client-side library/host boundary: reusable packages should expose an explicit integration API and be side-effect-free on import, while host applications own initialization and host-specific wiring.

text: Keep serialization/deserialization and persistence logic out of UI components. UI components should either accept callbacks (e.g. `onChange`) so the host application owns saving/serialization, or delegate to the data-storage/frontend layer module that owns entity serialization.
reason: Separating data storage/serialization concerns from UI and business logic keeps save behavior visible, centralizes serialization changes, and avoids maintainability problems when library or component behavior is hidden in UI code.
common_pattern: Serialization/persistence logic should not be owned by UI components; it belongs in the host application or data-storage/frontend layer, with components communicating via callbacks or consuming already-managed entities.

text: In `EditHandler.get_comparison_class`, select the comparison class based on field configuration (e.g. `choices`), not just field type: fields with `choices` must be routed to the dedicated `ChoiceFieldComparison` branch rather than falling through to `TextFieldComparison`. Do not duplicate the choices check inside the generic `CharField`/`TextField` branch, since the specialized branch already handles it earlier in the method.
reason: Choice-constrained fields need choice-aware comparison behavior, and the method already centralizes this in the earlier ChoiceFieldComparison branch; duplicating the check in the generic branch is redundant and risks divergent handling.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern the same method (`EditHandler.get_comparison_class`) and the same design question: how to select a comparison class for a field with `choices`. One proposes adding a choices check in the generic CharField/TextField branch; the other resolves it by pointing to the existing dedicated `ChoiceFieldComparison` branch. Together they form a complementary pair (proposal + resolution) converging on: choice-aware comparison is handled by the specialized branch, so generic type branches must not duplicate that check.

text: Keep core/model-level methods self-contained and free of admin-specific dependencies: compute needed context inside the model method, and move admin-only concerns (e.g. locale selection, object creation, edit flows) into the admin view rather than the model API.
reason: Core logic that only exists to support one admin component will misbehave at other call sites; separating front-end read paths from admin workflows reduces model API complexity and coupling and makes each path easier to reason about.
common_pattern: Keeping configuration and behavior decoupled from shared/reusable objects — admin-specific concerns should not leak into core model code, and reusable helpers should receive the owning context rather than be re-instantiated or mutated to change behavior.

text: When detecting a URL scheme with string prefix checks, include the trailing ':' in the prefix (e.g. use ('http:', 'https:')) so the check matches an actual protocol rather than any string starting with those characters.
reason: Prefix matching without the colon produces false positives, such as treating 'httpfoo' as an external link, while including the colon ensures a protocol delimiter is present.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern correct handling and testing of related URL schemes (http vs https), emphasizing scheme-level specificity in detection and test coverage.

text: When using the shared `Transition`/`CSSTransitionGroup` wrapper, pass landmark and accessible-label semantics to the wrapper itself, e.g. `component="nav"` and a `label` prop forwarded to `aria-label`. Do not render `<nav>`, headings, or elements with fixed `id`s or aria labels inside the transitioned children, because enter/leave transitions can render duplicate copies and create duplicate DOM IDs and headings.
reason: Prevents duplicate DOM IDs and duplicate headings during transitions while preserving navigation landmark semantics and accessible labels.
common_pattern: Landmark and accessible-label semantics should be attached to the stable Transition/CSSTransitionGroup wrapper via wrapper props such as `component` and `label` (forwarded to `aria-label`), rather than to transitioned child content, because transitions may render duplicate copies and create duplicate headings or fixed DOM IDs.

text: For Draftail embed/media blocks, render all states (including thumbnail-less fallbacks) through the shared `MediaBlock` component. Add optional props to `MediaBlock` for visual variants/overlays such as `providerName`/`authorName` instead of building separate fallback markup, and pass interactive controls (links, delete buttons) as children so they appear in the tooltip rather than inline in the block's visible content.
reason: Keeps embed presentations visually consistent, avoids duplicated/divergent markup between thumbnail and non-thumbnail states, and keeps the block UI unobtrusive while editing.
common_pattern: Draftail embed/media block variants and fallbacks should be composed through the shared `MediaBlock` component, extended with optional props for visual overlays, with interactive controls passed as children so they surface in the tooltip rather than inline.

text: When creating a new version-specific Elasticsearch backend class in wagtail/search/backends/ (for example an `Elasticsearch{N}SearchQueryCompiler`), override inherited class-level attributes that reference version-specific classes, such as `mapping_class`, so they point to the matching classes for that version (for example `Elasticsearch{N}Mapping`) instead of remaining bound to the parent version's classes.
reason: Leaving inherited version-specific class references on a version-specific subclass silently reuses the older version's behavior and defeats the purpose of the subclass.
common_pattern: Version-specific subclassing requires rebinding inherited class-level references to other version-specific classes so the subclass uses its own version's implementations.

text: For Wagtail page lock indicators and lock-state checks, use lock-specific fields/helpers such as `page.locked_by` or `page_perms.page_locked()` instead of page ownership (`page.owner`) or manual `get_lock()` checks. Render distinct, accessible titles/messages for each lock state (locked by current user vs. locked by another), and clear or update cached lock state when a page transitions into or out of a locked state. Keep the lock indicator visible independently of optional surrounding forms.
reason: Prevents incorrect lock ownership checks, stale cached lock state, and inaccessible or misleading lock indicators across Wagtail admin templates and views.
scope: Wagtail page lock state handling (admin templates, views, and models)
common_pattern: Wagtail page lock state must be tracked, checked, and rendered using lock-specific data and distinct, accessible UI indicators rather than page ownership or generic lock messaging.

text: In Explorer navigation components, determine root and parent/back navigation from permission-aware, user-relative indicators: compare the page `id` to the global root identifier (e.g. `1`) to detect the global root, and use `depth` relative to the user's starting level rather than the existence of `page.parent`. Only render or link to a parent page when it is within the user's accessible navigation; otherwise treat the current page as the root (non-interactive Home state).
reason: The admin API may return `parent` metadata for pages the user cannot access, and `'root'` denotes the user's explorable root rather than the global tree root; relying on these raw markers causes incorrect headings, broken parent links, and JavaScript errors.
common_pattern: Explorer navigation should derive root and parent/back state from permission-aware, user-relative indicators (global root id, navigation depth) rather than from raw markers like the `'root'` string or the existence of `page.parent`.

text: Do not HTML-escape string values in non-HTML responses (e.g. `text/plain` bodies); HTML escaping must only be applied when the output is actually rendered as HTML, since escaping corrupts plaintext output (e.g. `&` -> `&`).
reason: Escaping is only meaningful for HTML; applying it to plaintext responses changes literal text and misleads readers about the response format.
common_pattern: Output escaping/formatting must match the target render context: HTML escaping/formatting is only correct where the output is rendered as HTML, and dual-format helpers should default to the dominant (HTML) rendering path with explicit opt-in for plain text.

text: Formatting/display helpers that can emit either HTML or plain text should accept a flag (e.g. `html=True` / `plain_text`), default to the HTML form for the dominant rendering path, and have rare plain-text consumers (e.g. `<option>` labels) explicitly request plain text at the call site.
reason: Defaults should serve the common HTML-rendering path; forcing the default to change for rare plain-text callers reintroduces broken display everywhere HTML rendering occurs.
common_pattern: Output escaping/formatting must match the target render context: HTML escaping/formatting is only correct where the output is rendered as HTML, and dual-format helpers should default to the dominant (HTML) rendering path with explicit opt-in for plain text.

text: Use `None` (not a magic numeric sentinel such as `-1`) as the default for optional CLI arguments that mean 'no limit' / 'all rows', and explicitly handle `None` by skipping the restriction and processing all items.
reason: Negative sentinels like `-1` are ambiguous in slicing/limit logic, since negative indices have established meaning in Python sequences (e.g. `-1` selects the last element), making it unclear whether an omitted argument imports all rows, the first row, or the last row. `None` is unambiguous and improves type integrity.
common_pattern: Use `None` rather than a magic numeric sentinel (like `-1`) as the default for optional CLI arguments representing 'no limit'/'all rows', because negative integers carry established Python sequence-index semantics.

text: When refactoring the rich-text rewriter/handler API, update all internal call sites—not just the primary entry point—including secondary admin converters in `wagtail/admin/rich_text/converters/editor_html.py`; for public/subclassable APIs, follow the project deprecation policy and preserve compatibility shims (e.g., `convert_rule_to_bulk_rule`) until remaining callers are migrated.
reason: Secondary invocation paths and third-party subclasses can break or behave inconsistently if left on an old API; deprecation and compatibility shims provide a safe migration path.
scope: rich-text rewriter/handler refactors, including `wagtail.richtext` public APIs
common_pattern: Maintaining code quality and API compatibility while refactoring Wagtail's rich-text rewriter/handler internals: documenting behavior and avoiding breakage for internal and external callers.

text: Prefer plain, explicit data structures and conventional collection APIs over custom lazy wrappers (e.g. namedtuples, custom `Mapping` helpers, hidden/lazy properties) whose only purpose is to preserve an existing interface while deferring conversion or evaluation. If preserving the interface requires too much hidden behavior, make a documented breaking change instead.
reason: Custom lazy wrappers often unify only shape, not semantics; they add unused abstractions and make APIs harder to reason about. Explicit structures and documented breakage are easier to maintain and understand.
common_pattern: Avoid custom lazy/wrapper abstractions and hidden properties whose purpose is to preserve an existing interface while deferring evaluation or conversion; prefer plain, explicit data structures and conventional collection behavior.

text: In workflow action menus, use distinct, unambiguous labels for resubmit/resume versus restart actions: reserve wording like “Restart workflow” for actions that start the workflow over from the beginning, and label actions that return to an existing task with continuation wording that names the specific task (e.g., “Save and resume {task.name}” or “Resubmit to {task.name}”). Remove or consolidate actions that appear to perform the same restart/resume operation.
reason: Labels like “Restart workflow” and “Resubmit for moderation” both sound like they start the workflow over, so users cannot tell whether an action resumes at the rejected task or restarts from scratch; distinct, task-naming labels and removal of redundant actions make the behavior clear.
common_pattern: Workflow action menu labels and the set of offered actions must unambiguously distinguish resubmitting/resuming at an existing task from restarting the workflow from scratch; redundant or similarly-named actions should be consolidated and labels should name the target task.

text: In permission/access-control checks, including Wagtail editor-access checks such as `user_can_access_editor`, explicitly return True for superusers even when group-membership checks fail (for example, add `or user.is_superuser`).
reason: Superusers are expected to have unconditional access; group-membership-only checks can incorrectly block them.
common_pattern: Access-control/permission checks must explicitly allow superusers, even when group-membership or workflow restrictions would otherwise deny access.

text: When an accepted RFC or proposal specifies a distinct method or default behavior, implement exactly that method/default rather than approximating it with another method or changing it based on convenience or perceived user awareness.
reason: RFCs and proposals encode agreed design decisions; substituting nearby methods or altering defaults hides intended distinctions, undermines project governance, and can create unexpected behavior or compatibility issues.
common_pattern: Fidelity to accepted RFC/proposal specifications: implement the exact method or default behavior that was agreed, rather than approximating or deviating for perceived convenience.

text: For simple mutable state with no dependent updates, initialize and assign public attributes directly; when a property setter exists that updates dependent state, assign through that setter rather than mutating the private backing field.
reason: Avoids unnecessary indirection and boilerplate for simple state, while ensuring dependent state (e.g., widgets) stays in sync and side effects are centralized.
common_pattern: Select between direct attribute assignment and property/setter usage based on whether the state involves dependent updates: use direct attributes for simple state, and use property setters when they exist to centralize side effects.

text: Provide indented collection name rendering as a reusable method on the `Collection` model — `get_indented_name(indentation_start_depth=<int>, plain_text=False, html=False)` — rather than inlining the logic in callers; at call sites such as `CollectionChoiceField.label_from_instance`, pass the format flags explicitly (e.g. `plain_text=True` for plain-text labels, `html=True` when the value may contain HTML) instead of relying on the helper's non-plain-text/non-HTML defaults.
reason: Keeps indentation/display logic reusable across plain-text and HTML consumers, and makes each call site's output intent explicit so a reader doesn't have to look up the helper's defaults.
common_pattern: Consolidating reusable indented-name rendering onto the `Collection` model via a `get_indented_name(indentation_start_depth=..., plain_text=..., html=...)` helper, with call sites (e.g. `CollectionChoiceField.label_from_instance`) required to pass the format flags explicitly rather than relying on defaults.

text: For custom Django form fields that drive widget rendering, expose the underlying data source (e.g., `queryset`) through a property getter/setter pair following Django's `ModelChoiceField.queryset` precedent. In the setter, update the widget and derive dependent field/widget rendering attributes automatically instead of requiring callers or form code to configure them manually.
reason: This keeps the field API familiar to Django developers, encapsulates synchronization between field and widget state, makes the field reusable, and prevents stale, duplicated, or incorrectly configured widget attributes.
common_pattern: Django form-field/widget state synchronization: expose field data-source state through a Django-conventional property getter/setter and use that setter to keep dependent widget rendering attributes synchronized and automatically derived.

text: When an API resource nests its payload under a `data` property, access all fields via `resource.data.{field}` (e.g., `page.data.id`, `page.data.admin_display_title`) rather than mixing top-level properties with nested ones.
reason: Mixing access levels after a response-shape change can produce undefined values, broken links, missing display values, and components that are harder to reason about.
common_pattern: When an API resource wraps its payload under a `data` property, field access should consistently go through `resource.data.{field}` instead of mixing top-level and nested field access.

text: When replacing an underlying action type with a new generic action (e.g., `GOTO_PAGE`), keep existing component-facing action creators (e.g., `pushPage`, `popPage`) stable by reimplementing them as wrappers around the new action instead of migrating component call sites.
reason: Preserves the existing component contract, reduces refactoring churn, and centralizes navigation behavior in the underlying generic action.
common_pattern: When replacing an underlying action type, preserve the existing public/component-facing action creator API by redefining those creators as wrappers around the new generic action, rather than migrating all call sites.

text: When bulk-converting a list of mappings/structured values where keys may be absent, preserve the original list length and ordering by substituting a per-occurrence default or raw placeholder for missing keys instead of filtering entries out; use raw placeholders such as `None` in raw bulk-conversion APIs, and call `get_default()` per occurrence only when a native default object is appropriate rather than reusing a shared default instance.
reason: Filtering missing keys shifts result indexes relative to the input, causing bulk-converted values to be associated with the wrong inputs. Reusing a single returned default object can also alias mutable shared state. However, raw bulk-conversion APIs need raw values, so `get_default()` is not suitable there and a raw placeholder such as `None` should be used.
common_pattern: Bulk conversion of lists of mappings/structured values with possibly missing keys must preserve positional alignment and handle defaults per occurrence, using native defaults only where appropriate and raw placeholders in raw bulk APIs.

text: Thread the acting user explicitly through operations that create, modify, publish, or copy content. In request-handling code pass `user=request.user`; in scheduled/automatic publishing pass the revision author such as `user=revision.user`; and in bulk-action `execute_action` implementations treat `user` as meaningful execution context for audit logging. When a management command or other non-web caller cannot provide a user, do not fabricate a default/synthetic superuser; either require an explicit real user, support and document `user=None`, or otherwise keep the required-user behavior consistent across implementations.
reason: Permission checks and audit logs need to know the real actor. Omitting the user loses attribution, while defaulting to an arbitrary superuser creates misleading logs.
scope: Wagtail content operations: scheduled publishing, translation copying, and bulk-action `execute_action` implementations
common_pattern: Content-mutating operations should explicitly carry the acting user for audit/ownership attribution, rather than leaving the user unset, implicit, or fabricated. The cluster also exposes a sub-contradiction around fallback superusers for non-web callers, which should be resolved in favor of preserving real attribution or documenting explicit None/required-user behavior.

text: Keep reducer state minimal and stable: do not store derived/computed fields that can be derived from existing state or payload data—derive them at the point of use via existing selectors. Preserve the existing state shape unless additional namespacing is needed to avoid API/local state field collisions. Consumers should access reducer-guaranteed state directly through existing selectors rather than reading the raw store shape or adding defensive checks for properties the reducer controls.
reason: Avoids duplicated, stale, or denormalized state; maintains a single source of truth; and decouples consumers from the exact store shape.
scope: Redux/reducer state, selectors, and components consuming reducer-controlled state
common_pattern: Reducer state should remain minimal, stable, and canonical: do not denormalize derived data into it, and access it through selectors or reducer-guaranteed shape rather than raw store reads or defensive checks.

text: When updating a model instance from a mapping of field names to values (e.g., `update_attrs`), validate each key against the canonical allow-list of updatable fields (e.g., `data_dict`), ensuring foreign-key field names (e.g., `foo` vs `foo_id`) are represented consistently, and raise an exception for unrecognized keys rather than silently skipping them.
reason: Using the canonical allow-list centralizes update logic and avoids `setattr` failures on unsaved model instances (e.g., M2M fields). However, silently discarding unrecognized keys hides caller errors and can cause data loss, so raising an exception is preferred. Ensuring consistent FK naming prevents valid fields from being accidentally skipped by the allow-list check.
common_pattern: Validating field-name keys against a canonical allow-list when applying updates to model instances, with attention to foreign-key naming consistency and error handling for unrecognized keys.

text: Adapters for standard-library types that are commonly shared between Python and JS (such as dates) should be built into the base telepath module as built-in standard support, not registered through an external appconf-loaded adapter module. Before adding such a type, verify that its Python and JS representations are compatible enough to treat it as a core telepath primitive.
reason: Core serialization support should be available everywhere and not duplicated in application-level adapter registries, while representation differences between Python and JS can make some standard-library types unsafe to handle as built-in telepath primitives.
common_pattern: Policy for adding standard-library type adapters to the base telepath module: types commonly shared between Python and JS should be built-in core support rather than external appconf-loaded adapters, but only after verifying Python/JS representation compatibility.

text: In widget APIs, pass initial state through a `render`/`renderState` argument and initialize the widget from it. Treat `setState` (post-initialization mutation) as optional: only implement it where the underlying widget genuinely supports state changes, never as a fake or no-op. Container blocks may implement it recursively only when all descendant blocks support it.
reason: Not all widget libraries support changing state after initialization. Separating initial state from mutable state keeps the API permissive, avoids forcing fake `setState` implementations, and prevents latent failures when callers rely on the API.
scope: telepath widget API and widget integrations
common_pattern: Conventions for how widgets receive and mutate state through render/setState APIs: keep initial state separate from mutable state, make mutation optional/real rather than faked, and apply the same state-setting convention across all render paths.

text: Temporary/staging upload models should include a `created_at` timestamp field to support identifying and pruning stale or unused uploads.
reason: Enables cleanup of old uploaded files that were never converted into permanent records, preventing accumulation of orphaned temporary files/records.
common_pattern: Design guidelines for temporary/staging upload models: include a timestamp for cleanup and name by role rather than arrival mechanism.

text: In `wagtail/contrib/forms/forms.py`, `create_tel_field` should return a phone-number-aware form field (e.g., `PhoneNumberField` from `django-phonenumber-field`) or otherwise provide telephone validation/help text. Do not return only `django.forms.CharField(widget=TelephoneInput)`.
reason: A widget controls rendering/UX but does not enforce valid telephone formats; using a specialized phone field enables country-aware validation and clearer user guidance.
common_pattern: Telephone fields in Wagtail form builder should provide telephone-number-aware validation rather than only a rendering widget; preferably use a specialized phone field such as PhoneNumberField, or at minimum add validation/help text.

text: In interface/type definitions, keep closely related fields (e.g., variants of the same concept) grouped together rather than scattered, and add a comment explaining the distinction when multiple similar fields exist.
reason: Grouping related fields makes their relationship immediately obvious and prevents misuse of the wrong field; an explanatory comment clarifies why similar fields are needed when the distinction is not self-evident.
common_pattern: Both generalizations come from the same reviewer comment about grouping similar fields (text/originalText/newText) in an interface and documenting why multiple similar fields exist. They are complementary halves of one readability guideline for interface/type definitions.

text: When applying inline styles in `CommentableEditor`, route style types and comment style IDs through `filterInlineStyles(...)` and pass `editorState.getCurrentContent()` (rather than a precomputed `filteredContent`) so filtering stays consistent with the current editor content and is centralized.
reason: Using the current content at the point of filtering keeps style application consistent with the live editor state and consolidates filter logic.
common_pattern: Separation of concerns in the Draftail commentable editor: comment storage/serialisation logic and shared save/filtering behaviour should be centralized (in `wagtail-comment-frontend`) rather than duplicated or embedded inside editor components like `CommentableEditor`.

text: Set `action_priority` on bulk-action classes so rendered actions follow the standard page-listing order (move, copy, delete, publish, unpublish), placing destructive actions such as delete last (e.g. a high value like 100) rather than first.
reason: Consistent ordering makes the admin UI predictable and reduces the risk of accidentally activating destructive actions.
common_pattern: Conventions for Wagtail admin bulk-action classes: how they are named (after the concrete model they operate on) and how their ordering is controlled via `action_priority`.

text: Keep comments/annotations rendered and within the visible viewport even when their associated anchor or field is hidden or offscreen; do not use field/anchor visibility as a reason to hide comments—reserve hiding for explicit comment mode.
reason: Comments should remain discoverable, and focused UI should not be scrolled off-screen. Field or anchor visibility should not add extra hiding logic.
common_pattern: Comment/annotation visibility should be preserved and managed explicitly rather than implicitly through anchor or field visibility.

text: When validating or coercing a model field value, call the field's `get_prep_value(value)` instead of branching on an `isinstance()` allow-list of field classes; for relation fields, call `field.remote_field.get_prep_value(value)` so validation follows the related model's primary-key type. Rely on `ValueError` for invalid input.
reason: A field's actual stored value type can differ from its nominal class (for example, a `ForeignKey` may be backed by an integer, text, or UUID primary key), so `isinstance` checks are brittle. `get_prep_value` centralizes the correct per-field conversion and validation.
common_pattern: Use Django model-field coercion/validation API (`get_prep_value`) instead of `isinstance`-based type assumptions when validating or parsing field/filter values.

text: When dispatching comment notifications, include every kind of comment activity (new comments, replies, edits, deletions, resolutions) and notify thread participants independently of page-level subscriptions — joining a thread is a separate, stronger subscription channel than subscribing to a page.
reason: Users subscribed to a page or thread expect to be notified of all comment activity; silently dropping activity types (e.g. replies) or suppressing thread-reply notifications because page-level notifications are off loses notifications users legitimately asked for.
common_pattern: Notification dispatch must aggregate all relevant consent signals: include every kind of comment activity (not just top-level comments), treat thread participation as a distinct subscription channel, and require BOTH per-object subscription flags AND the user-profile notification preference before notifying a recipient.

text: When the same entity can be persisted from multiple flows, centralize its save-triggered side effects (e.g., logging, notifications) in a shared helper/method and invoke that helper from every save site, including alternate paths such as perform_workflow_action, cancel, and restart.
reason: Ensures consistent audit/notification behavior across all workflows that save the same logical entity, while avoiding duplicated side-effect logic in each save path.
common_pattern: Centralize save-triggered side effects across all persistence paths for the same entity so behavior stays consistent and logic is not duplicated.

text: When passing multiple CSS classes via a `classes` argument or field, use a list (not a set) to preserve class order and maintain API consistency.
common_pattern: Conventions for handling CSS classes in template code: ensuring order preservation when passing classes and clear variable naming tied to the styled DOM element.

text: Keep method-type conventions consistent within a related call chain: if an entry-point method is a `@classmethod` invokable without instantiation (e.g. `execute(cls, ...)`), any overridable hook it calls (e.g. `execute_action`) should also be a classmethod, and any extra data the hook needs should be passed via keyword arguments rather than converting the hook to an instance method.
reason: Mixed classmethod/instance-method semantics in the same call chain are confusing; when one method in the pair is invoked without instantiating, the other should follow the same contract, and required context can be threaded through via kwargs instead of changing the binding.
common_pattern: Enforcement of Python method convention consistency: `cls` must be reserved for genuine `@classmethod`s operating on the class, while `self` is required for instance methods, and the classmethod/instance-method choice must stay coherent across a related call chain.

text: In Wagtail, keep workflow-state querying and prefetching out of the Page model's public API: expose public workflow states via WorkflowMixin.workflow_states, place admin/optimization prefetch helpers (e.g., prefetch_workflow_states, annotate_approved_schedule, annotate_site_root_state) on PageQuerySet, use an internal _workflow_states GenericRelation for prefetching rather than redefining workflow_states with a backend-specific query, and guard workflow prefetches behind WAGTAIL_WORKFLOW_ENABLED.
reason: This captures the shared pattern across both PRs: workflow-state access should be portable and differentiate public model API from admin/queryset optimization logic, while avoiding unnecessary work when workflows are disabled.
common_pattern: Organization of Wagtail workflow-state querying/prefetching: keep public access portable via WorkflowMixin, place admin/optimization prefetch helpers on PageQuerySet rather than the Page model, use an internal GenericRelation for prefetching instead of backend-specific redefinitions, and respect WAGTAIL_WORKFLOW_ENABLED.

text: Class-based extension points (e.g. `LogFormatter` subclasses) should support module-level registration via a decorator, consistent with existing class-registration patterns such as modeladmin, rather than requiring registration inside a hook function; document this module-level usage in the hooks reference docs.
reason: Keeps extension APIs consistent and discoverable, and avoids unnecessary nesting and discoverability problems in user code.
common_pattern: Extension-point registration in Wagtail should be available at module level via a decorator, consistent with existing class-registration patterns like modeladmin.

text: In database search backends, compute relevance as separate match expressions per field and multiply each field-specific normalization factor (e.g., `title_norm`) into that field's score. Do not use a single unnormalized match expression across multiple fields. The MySQL backend should follow the Postgres backend pattern.
reason: This preserves intended ranking semantics, ensures normalization factors are actually used, and keeps MySQL consistent with the Postgres backend.
common_pattern: Search relevance scoring in database backends must apply field-specific normalization factors per field, mirroring the Postgres backend behavior.

text: In the TypedTableBlock (client/src/entrypoints/contrib/typed_table_block/typed_table_block.js), controls must be placed to produce a logical tab order and icon-only controls must expose an accessible, localizable label. Specifically: prepend the add-column button inside header cells so it precedes the heading input; add a leading control cell with the Insert Row button while keeping the trailing control cell for Delete Row; and give the icon-only delete-column button an aria-label sourced from blockDef.meta.strings.DELETE_COLUMN.
reason: Accessibility reviews confirmed that this ordering yields a better keyboard tab sequence and that bare icon controls (e.g., ×) are unusable to screen readers unless labeled from the component's string table.
common_pattern: Accessibility-driven DOM/UX conventions for the TypedTableBlock component (client/src/entrypoints/contrib/typed_table_block/typed_table_block.js): logical keyboard tab order across column-header and row control buttons, localizable aria-labels for icon-only controls, and role-based element naming that makes interactive semantics explicit.

text: When an API accepts paired dimensions such as width and height, pass them as a single `(width, height)` tuple parameter instead of separate scalar or named parameters, especially to match existing project/transform API conventions.
reason: This keeps coupled values together, reduces parameter count, avoids passing dimensions in the wrong order or only one dimension, and preserves consistency across related APIs.
common_pattern: Paired dimensions should be bundled into a single tuple parameter rather than separate scalar/named parameters, to keep coupled values together and maintain API consistency across related transform APIs.

text: Icons that are part of an interactive control must be rendered inside that control's element/component; if the icon is purely decorative, give it `pointer-events: none` so pointer events pass through to the parent control.
reason: Icons placed as siblings outside the control are not clickable and mislead users who expect them to behave like part of the button; decorative overlays that intercept clicks steal events from the intended parent element.
common_pattern: Managing pointer-event hit targets for interactive controls and the icons rendered inside/near them, so that clicks land on the intended element and adjacent controls are not accidentally triggered.

text: Confine the clickable area of item links/previews to the visible content (e.g., the thumbnail image) rather than including surrounding padding or whitespace, especially when adjacent interactive controls (checkboxes, action buttons) are nearby.
reason: Padding-inclusive hit areas overlap neighboring controls and cause users to trigger the item link when targeting the adjacent control.
common_pattern: Managing pointer-event hit targets for interactive controls and the icons rendered inside/near them, so that clicks land on the intended element and adjacent controls are not accidentally triggered.

text: Do not expose `update_locale` on the page-alias creation API action; cross-locale alias creation belongs to the `copy_for_translation` API via its `alias` flag. The alias-creation API only aliases within the same locale.
reason: `create_alias`/`copy_for_translation` already owns translation-aware aliasing; exposing `update_locale` on the alias API would permit an unsupported value. Removing the field eliminates the invalid combination at the source rather than merely validating it.
common_pattern: Page-alias creation must not silently ignore inputs that the page-tree save logic overrides. This surfaces in two complementary ways: (a) validating option combinations upfront and raising domain-specific integrity errors instead of letting save logic silently correct invalid values, and (b) not exposing options (like `update_locale`) that belong to a different API (`copy_for_translation`).

text: In the SQLite search backend's `normalize()`, add a `Boost` case that returns `normalize(search_query.subquery)`, since FTS5 does not support `Boost` and unwrapping keeps the query traversable.
reason: SQLite FTS5 does not support Boost, so unwrapping is safe and prevents normalization from failing on valid Wagtail query trees.
common_pattern: SQLite FTS5 query normalization must correctly handle query nodes that FTS5 does not natively support or that are neutral for boolean connectors (Boost and MatchAll), preserving logical equivalence when simplifying Or/And expressions.

text: In the SQLite search backend's `normalize()`, simplify `MatchAll()` operands according to their boolean connector: for `And`, remove non-negated `MatchAll()` and return `Not(MatchAll())` if any negated `MatchAll()` exists; for `Or`, remove negated `MatchAll()` and return `MatchAll()` if any non-negated `MatchAll()` exists. When computing negated and non-negated subquery lists, each conditional must test the list that semantically matches its purpose.
reason: FTS5 boolean semantics make `And(MatchAll, X) == X`, `Or(MatchAll, X) == MatchAll`, `And(Not(MatchAll), X) == Not(MatchAll)`, and `Or(Not(MatchAll), X) == X`. Mishandling `MatchAll()` changes whether a search matches everything, nothing, or the intended subset, and testing the wrong filtered list silently produces incorrect normalization.
common_pattern: SQLite FTS5 query normalization must correctly handle query nodes that FTS5 does not natively support or that are neutral for boolean connectors (Boost and MatchAll), preserving logical equivalence when simplifying Or/And expressions.

text: When an internal API or optimization only needs non-request context (e.g., site route paths), pass a dedicated lightweight context object rather than constructing a dummy HTTP request.
reason: Dummy requests add unnecessary complexity and can carry misleading request-derived information (such as host/domain), causing bugs especially in multi-site scenarios.
common_pattern: Avoid constructing dummy HTTP requests for internal APIs that only need non-request context (e.g., site route paths); pass a lightweight/dedicated context object instead.

text: In action classes under `wagtail/core/actions/`, the `check()` method must validate that related object arguments (e.g., `self.revision`) belong to the primary target object (e.g., `self.page`), raising the action-specific data error (e.g., `RevertToPageRevisionError`) when the relationship is invalid. For example, verify `self.revision` is in `self.page.revisions` rather than assuming the caller wired them together correctly.
reason: Actions can be instantiated from multiple entry points (API, internal code), so caller-provided relationships cannot be trusted; enforcing the invariant inside `check()` prevents applying one object's related data (e.g., a revision) to another object and surfaces invalid input before any mutation occurs.
common_pattern: Action/command classes in `wagtail/core/actions/` must validate in their `check()` method that related object arguments (like a revision) actually belong to the primary target object (like a page), since the action may be constructed from multiple entry points and cannot trust the caller.

text: In Wagtail admin upload flows, when an uploaded item is detected as a duplicate, notify the user with a direct action (e.g., a button/link) to a filtered listing of potential duplicates, and restrict the duplicate matches/listing to objects the current user has `choose` permission for.
reason: This merges the complementary halves from the cluster: duplicate notifications must be actionable, and duplicate matches are only meaningful when the user can select them.
scope: Wagtail admin upload/selection duplicate-detection views; applicable to similar permission-aware duplicate-detection flows.
common_pattern: Duplicate detection in Wagtail upload flows should surface actionable, permission-filtered duplicate matches rather than merely reporting that a duplicate exists or showing objects the user cannot act on.

text: Management commands that regenerate Wagtail image renditions (or similar derived assets) should default to purging/deleting existing derived records and files before regenerating, rather than only using the get-or-create regeneration path. Accessors such as get_rendition() reuse an existing database row even when the underlying file is missing, so the command must delete/recreate the row to force the file to be regenerated.
reason: Database records can outlive deleted files; get-or-create regeneration will see the existing record and not recreate the missing file. Purging by default makes the command repair inconsistent state.
common_pattern: Derived-asset regeneration commands must purge existing database records/files before regenerating, because get-or-create accessors reuse stale records and silently skip recreating missing files.

text: For dismissible UI components (panels, dialogs, popovers, closeable sections), manage keyboard focus: place the close/dismiss control first in DOM order so it is the first focusable item in the tab order, and when the component closes, return focus to the control that opened it.
reason: Prevents keyboard focus from being lost, gives keyboard users a predictable next location, and matches user expectations for closeable sections.
common_pattern: Keyboard focus management for dismissible UI components: ensure predictable tab order and restore focus when the component closes.

text: For the preview side panel, use `alt+p` (`option+p` on macOS) as the keyboard shortcut rather than `mod+p`.
reason: `mod+p` overrides the browser print shortcut, which is undesirable; `alt+p` provides a non-conflicting shortcut.
common_pattern: UI conventions for the preview side panel (BasePreviewSidePanel)

text: For overridable helper classes, avoid adding optional constructor parameters; instantiate helpers through their factory, apply optional configuration through set_* methods only when a non-empty value is provided, and initialize defaults in __init__ by calling the same setter so default and overridden paths share one implementation.
reason: Prevents breaking subclass constructors, avoids compatibility warnings for missing constructor parameters, and centralizes default-configuration logic.
common_pattern: Optional helper configuration should be applied through set_* methods rather than constructor parameters, with defaults initialized via the same setter to preserve subclass compatibility and centralize configuration logic.

text: When a visual state, ownership, or context distinction is shown in the UI—such as current user vs. another user, or selected/owned via color—also provide equivalent non-visual and non-color cues: a distinct accessible label/title for each state, and a border, ring, icon, or shape so the distinction is perceivable by screen readers and users who cannot rely on color alone.
reason: Visual-only and color-only distinctions are unavailable to assistive technology and users with color-vision differences; the accessible name and secondary visual cue must mirror the same state information.
common_pattern: Accessibility redundancy for visual state indicators: any state distinction conveyed visually (via color or context-dependent UI) must also be conveyed non-visually and, where color is used, through a non-color visual cue.

text: In `client/src/components/StreamField/blocks/`, treat `parentCapabilities` as the interface between parent and child blocks: child block constructors and `render` methods should accept only `parentCapabilities` (not a `parent` block instance), all call sites must pass capabilities in that parameter slot rather than a parent object such as `this`, and optional parent-provided behavior should be exposed as an event in the capabilities dict (e.g. `onEnableDuplicate`) for the child to subscribe to, not invoked as a direct parent-to-child method call.
reason: Passing parent instances couples children to parent internals, while a capabilities dict/event interface lets children opt into parent-provided features without tight coupling.
common_pattern: StreamField parent-child block communication should be mediated by the capabilities interface rather than by parent block instances or direct parent-to-child imperative calls.

text: In `wagtail/contrib/forms/models.py`, split discrete page/form capabilities into dedicated mixins (e.g., `FormPageMixin`, `EmailFormMixin`) and compose abstract page classes from those mixins instead of embedding all behavior directly in a single abstract page class (e.g., `AbstractEmailForm` should inherit from an email-form mixin that encapsulates email handling).
reason: Improves reuse, separation of concerns, and consistency with the existing mixin-based form page design, keeping abstract page classes thin and allowing capabilities such as form rendering and email handling to be composed by page types that do not need or cannot use `AbstractEmailForm`.
common_pattern: Two distinct sub-patterns within `wagtail/contrib/forms`: (a) naming must match the established Wagtail forms terminology/model (submission = 'entry' / 'FormSubmission'), and (b) page/form capabilities should be factored into composable mixins rather than being inlined into abstract page classes. Both concern keeping the forms contrib app self-consistent with its existing conventions, but they are different kinds of rule (naming vs. structural composition).

text: In modeladmin primary-action helpers such as `get_primary_button_for_obj`, order permission checks by expected precedence: check edit permission before inspect permission so users with both permissions are routed to the edit view rather than the read-only inspect view.
reason: Users who can both edit and inspect generally expect the more actionable edit view to take precedence.
scope: module-specific: modeladmin button helpers such as `get_primary_button_for_obj`
common_pattern: Order permission checks for primary-action selection by expected precedence, so higher-capability actions take priority over lower-capability/read-only actions.

text: When a component reads a CSS selector from a data attribute, resolve it with `Element.closest(selector)` and bind related listeners (e.g., hover/mouseleave) to that nearest matching ancestor, so any valid CSS selector works and behavior targets the element the consumer chose rather than an assumed fixed parent.
reason: The selector should work for any valid CSS selector, and behavior should be bound to the element the consumer targets rather than an assumed fixed parent.
common_pattern: Resolving a consumer-supplied CSS selector from a data attribute via `Element.closest()` — covering both the implementation pattern and how to test it without a tag-name false pass.

text: For reusable dialog components, place configuration data attributes (e.g., data-url) on the dialog root element, not on the toggle; and populate the dialog body once when using one-time data, keeping the show handler limited to calling show().
reason: Decouples dialog content and configuration from the element that opens it, avoids redundant DOM rebuilding, and separates one-time rendering from visibility toggling.
common_pattern: Guidelines for dialog/modal component implementation: decouple dialog content and configuration from the toggle/trigger element, document required invariants between toggle and dialog.

text: Keep `description` as a distinct parameter/element for dialog/header description or body text, rendered outside the heading/header block (e.g., `div`/`p`), and do not rename it to `subtitle` or overload it for title-adjacent secondary text.
reason: Subtitle and description serve different semantic and visual roles; preserving `description` avoids breaking callers and keeps non-heading content out of the title block.
scope: Wagtail admin shared dialog/header component API
common_pattern: Wagtail admin shared header/dialog components must preserve a semantic distinction between title-adjacent subtitles (part of the heading) and descriptions/body text (separate non-heading content), and must not conflate or rename the corresponding slots/props.

text: In data migrations, when casting a JSON/JSONB subfield to a scalar type, extract the subfield as text first (Django `KeyTextTransform` / PostgreSQL `->>`) and then apply `Cast`; do not use a plain JSON key transform (`content__field`, `KeyTransform`, or `->`) that returns a JSON value directly.
reason: PostgreSQL cannot cast `jsonb` directly to scalar types like `integer`; text extraction makes the cast valid and remains portable across backends.
common_pattern: Database-layer handling of JSON/JSONB fields in Django/Wagtail data migrations and ORM queries: use JSON-aware database transforms/lookups instead of plain key transforms or Python-side iteration, and make migration reads null-safe.

text: When data is stored in a `JSONField`, prefer database-level JSON lookups/aggregations for filtering or counting rather than loading all records into Python and iterating over them.
reason: Database-level JSON queries avoid transferring and processing entire tables in Python, improving performance and scalability.
common_pattern: Database-layer handling of JSON/JSONB fields in Django/Wagtail data migrations and ORM queries: use JSON-aware database transforms/lookups instead of plain key transforms or Python-side iteration, and make migration reads null-safe.

text: Design APIs around the primary use-case and expose only one canonical path for supplying data; defer support for secondary datasources, alternative query styles, or redundant parameter paths until there is a concrete need.
reason: Avoids overcomplicated abstractions that arise from accommodating multiple query styles or ambiguous precedence between redundant data sources, and makes it clear where to find and change data.
common_pattern: API design should favor a single canonical, primary use-case-driven path and defer support for alternative query styles or redundant data sources until genuinely needed.

text: When a view/endpoint performs the same content state-changing operation (publish, schedule, release) as an existing management command, extract the shared behavior into a common helper (a utility function or a method on the relevant model, e.g. Page/revision) that both code paths call, rather than reimplementing the logic in the view.
reason: Duplicated publish/state-change logic between admin views and management commands drifts over time (e.g. one saves a new revision and the other publishes the scheduled revision), producing inconsistent behaviour depending on whether the operation is triggered from the UI or the CLI and making future changes error-prone.
common_pattern: Avoid duplicating content-state-change logic (publish/schedule/release) between an admin view and an existing management command; extract the shared behavior into a common helper so both code paths stay consistent.

text: In `wagtail/blocks/stream_block.py`, StreamBlock mapping-like accessors should behave like conventional dicts: use `child_blocks.keys()` when enumerating block names, and perform ordinary dict lookups for keyed access such as `blocks_by_name` rather than list comprehensions or custom lazy wrappers.
reason: This keeps the StreamBlock API idiomatic, avoids unnecessary iterator/allocation overhead, and makes keyed access predictable and simpler for callers.
common_pattern: StreamBlock mapping-like accessors should follow conventional Python dict semantics and idioms.

text: When defining an `InlinePanel`, explicitly set both `heading` and `label`: `heading` should be the plural section/group label, and `label` should be the singular item type (also used for the Add button). Do not rely on `heading` defaulting to `label`.
reason: Prevents duplicate page-region labels that fail accessibility checks, ensures inline panel sections are labelled, and avoids ambiguity because `label` now applies to each repeated item as well as the Add button.
common_pattern: InlinePanel usage should explicitly set both `heading` and `label`, using `heading` for the plural section/group label and `label` for the singular item type, to ensure distinct accessible region headings and avoid ambiguity now that `label` also labels each item and the Add button.

text: When mixins cooperate via super(), the base-class list order (MRO) is significant: place mixins so their intended super() chain executes (e.g. a mixin overriding a cooperative method goes before the mixin that also implements it), preserve and document the intended order, and reserve system checks for critical interactions while documenting less-critical ordering in the model reference docs. Inheritance-check error messages (E006, E007, etc.) must describe required ordering using explicit base-class list / MRO position wording (e.g. 'listed before/after', 'to the right of') consistently across all checks, not ambiguous 'applied before/after' phrasing.
reason: Cooperative multiple inheritance relies on a well-defined MRO; wrong order silently changes which implementation runs. Ambiguous 'applied before/after' wording can be read as construction order, MRO order, or inheritance direction, so users may place base classes incorrectly.
common_pattern: Python mixin composition discipline: mixins must remain independently composable (no cross-mixin isinstance checks/imports; cooperate via super() and overridable hooks), and because cooperative multiple inheritance depends on the MRO, base-class ordering must be preserved/documented and inheritance-error wording must unambiguously express base-class list / MRO position.

text: Keep the logic that determines which UI components to render in the view layer, not inside the UI component or side-panel classes; component classes should focus on rendering the components they represent.
reason: Separates rendering concerns from selection/orchestration so UI components do not need to know about page/view-specific rendering decisions.
scope: Wagtail admin UI (e.g., `wagtail/admin/ui/side_panels.py` and corresponding views)
common_pattern: Organizing and naming panel rendering logic in Wagtail admin: keep selection logic in views, and use clear, behavior-based, non-duplicative predicates for visibility/rendering state.

text: For `getDuplicatedState()` in container blocks (e.g. `TypedTableBlock`), reuse the same state extraction for simple metadata (e.g. columns) as `getState()`/`getValue()`; do not add column-specific duplication logic. Apply duplication-specific recursion only to child blocks whose types may contain nested ID-bearing blocks (e.g. row cells with `StreamBlock`/`ListBlock`).
reason: Simple metadata IDs such as column indices do not participate in uniqueness constraints/contentpaths, while complex cell block types can contain nested child IDs that must be regenerated during duplication. This avoids unnecessary duplication logic and prevents duplicate nested IDs.
common_pattern: Guidelines for implementing and testing `getDuplicatedState()` for block duplication in Wagtail (PR #9108).

text: Centralize locale/i18n default-resolution behaviour: expose locale-related behaviours (e.g. determining the default locale via `Locale.get_default()`) as cached methods/properties on the `Locale` model in `wagtail/models/i18n.py`, and reuse existing implementations (such as `LocaleMixin` logic) rather than re-deriving the default via settings or copying logic into new modules. Generally useful locale helpers that do not belong on the model should live in a shared core/utils location, not inside a specific contrib app.
reason: Generalizations 1-4 all push locale logic into a single reusable home (the Locale model or shared core utils) and forbid duplication/re-derivation, keeping callers decoupled from settings and preventing divergence.
common_pattern: Centralizing i18n/locale resolution logic in a single authoritative location (the Locale model or a shared core utils module) and reusing existing implementations instead of duplicating logic — with one outlier about test-side i18n fallbacks mimicking real runtime behaviour.

text: When implementing read-only field display, preserve user-facing information: format values using the field type's existing read-only/diff representation instead of redacted placeholders (e.g. rich text `readOnly={true}`, StreamField `read_only`, diff view representation without diff markings), and render `help_text` visibly rather than only through `aria-describedby`.
reason: Read-only display should not discard useful value information or leave sighted users without descriptive context; reuse UI components designed for safely displaying non-editable field values.
common_pattern: Read-only field rendering should preserve and expose useful information to users by reusing existing read-only display mechanisms and making supporting help text visible, rather than redacting values or hiding context behind accessibility-only attributes.
