text: Keep the public registration function a thin, timing-independent entry point. Extract the actual registration work into a private helper (e.g. `_register_{x}_actual()` / `_register_{x}_immediate()`) and call that helper from both the public function and the deferred-processing handler (e.g. `register_deferred_snippets()`), rather than re-invoking the public function. Avoid global flags (such as `DEFER_REGISTRATION`) that make the public function behave differently based on when it is called. When registrations are deferred until app loading completes, the public function must still detect calls made after `ready()` has run and register them immediately, since no later handler will flush newly queued items (e.g. from `wagtail_hooks`).
reason: In `wagtail/snippets/models.py`, `register_snippet()` was gated by a `DEFER_REGISTRATION` flag so its behaviour depended on call timing; deferred registration then re-entered the public function (re-running the defer check). Extracting the registration body into a private helper shared by both paths removes the global state, avoids circular re-entry and duplicate guard checks, and keeps the public API consistent across call sites. Because deferred queues are only flushed once during app loading, late calls (e.g. from `wagtail_hooks`) must bypass the queue and register immediately or they are silently dropped.
common_pattern: Refactoring deferred registration so the public registration function stays a thin, consistent entry point: extract the real registration work into a private helper (e.g. `_register_{x}_actual()`/`_register_{x}_immediate()`) shared by both the immediate path and the deferred-processing handler, eliminate timing-dependent global flags, and have the public function detect post-`ready()` calls so they register immediately rather than being queued.

text: When rendering tool-generated selector paths to users, e.g. in Wagtail userbar accessibility results, filter out internal/dynamic attributes such as `data-block-key` from the selector before assigning it to UI text content.
reason: Tool-generated selectors can contain implementation-specific attributes that are noisy, unstable, or meaningless to users; removing them keeps the displayed selector readable and avoids exposing internal StreamField block keys.
scope: Admin/user-facing selector rendering, especially `userbar.js` accessibility results
common_pattern: Filter internal or tool-generated attributes such as data-block-key from selector strings before displaying them in user-facing UI.

text: When copying a Wagtail object for translation, first resolve it to the latest revision if it implements `DraftStateMixin` via `get_latest_revision_as_object()`, then perform the copy using the internal `_copy(object, exclude_fields=exclude_fields)` helper rather than manually copying and updating child locales.
reason: Ensures translation copies include unpublished/latest revision content while centralizing copy behavior, preserving exclusion handling, and avoiding duplicated locale-propagation logic.
scope: wagtail/models translation-copy flows, especially DraftStateMixin models and i18n copy actions
common_pattern: Correct implementation of Wagtail translation copies: ensure revision-aware source resolution and reuse the centralized internal copy helper.

text: Keep methods focused on a single responsibility: decompose long or unwieldy methods along clear responsibility boundaries into purpose-named helper methods, but avoid premature fragmentation of cohesive logic. Do not overload a method with a concern that its name or docstring does not convey; introduce a separate purpose-named method for the new concern, sharing common logic via private helpers when needed. When a helper method is decoupled from the collection or parent method that previously defined its context, rename it to describe its standalone responsibility rather than retaining its former-context name.
reason: Focused, purpose-named methods improve readability, reviewability, testability, and API predictability. Avoiding hidden responsibilities and legacy-context names keeps intent explicit and discoverable, while avoiding over-fragmentation lets interfaces settle before being split.
common_pattern: Method APIs should be explicit and single-purpose: avoid overloading an existing method with new or unrelated semantics, introduce purpose-named siblings when semantics differ, and document the relationship or delegation between closely related methods.

text: When a cache such as `wagtail_site_root_paths` (used by `Site.get_site_root_paths()` / site-for-hostname lookups) gains a new data dependency (e.g. translations, page root data), connect invalidation to that dependency: clear the cache when the data changes and subscribe to the relevant signals (e.g. `Page` post_save/post_delete in addition to `Site`). Detect stale/legacy cached records via the cache-validity condition (e.g. tuple length) rather than relying on redundant `cache.delete` calls.
reason: The cached value depends on more than the Site model; without explicit invalidation on translation creation or page changes, stale site root paths / root pages are served.
common_pattern: Cache lifecycle management for Wagtail's site root paths / site-for-hostname caches: what invalidates them, how to keep them consistent in tests, and how to warm them to avoid repeated queries.

text: Design page-level cache invalidation around the URL-visible location, not the internal tree structure: build `Page.cache_key` from `url_path` rather than `path`, since sibling reordering mutates `path` and would spuriously invalidate unrelated entries. Attach cache-purge logic to publication-specific signals (`page_published`/`page_unpublished`) rather than generic pre-save/post-save signals so it only runs on publish/republish. When an operation invalidates caches at multiple locations, include enough context in the signal payload to identify both the previous and current locations (e.g. `old_url_path` alongside the current URL). Prefer documenting/bypassing via cache-key components over adding explicit cache-purge APIs, whose ordering relative to the update and final cache key is ambiguous.
reason: Scoping invalidation to URL-visible state and publish events avoids over-broad invalidation and unreliable purge timing, keeping cache behavior correct and predictable.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Wagtail's frontend cache (signal-based purge and `Page.cache_key`) — specifically, the semantics of what invalidates a cached page and how that behavior must be documented or implemented. The cluster splits into two complementary halves: (a) documenting cache-invalidation behavior so users understand when a cache miss will/won't occur, and (b) designing the cache key / purge signals so invalidation is scoped correctly.

text: Expose frontend-cache extension points (e.g. custom fixed paths/URLs or purge-time data) as Wagtail hooks rather than hard-coded `WAGTAILFRONTENDCACHE_*` settings.
reason: Hooks are Wagtail's standard extension mechanism, can derive values dynamically from site/page context, and avoid stale manually-maintained settings.
common_pattern: Design and correctness rules for Wagtail frontend-cache purge utilities: when and how to purge (new vs old URLs, empty batches, batch-size limits, purge_all fallback) and how to expose/document purge features.

text: In client-side JavaScript, prefer native DOM selection APIs (getElementById, querySelector, querySelectorAll) over jQuery selectors ($('#id'), $(selector, element), .find(), .children()) for element lookup; reserve jQuery selectors only for cases that require jQuery-specific behavior.
reason: Native DOM methods are standards-based, fast/direct, and reduce unnecessary jQuery dependency for basic element selection.
common_pattern: JavaScript DOM selection best practices: prefer native DOM APIs over jQuery, choose the correct native lookup method for the task, avoid redundant re-queries by reusing cached results, and avoid CSS-class-based selection.

text: In `StreamField.__init__`, accept only `BaseStreamBlock` (or explicitly validate that the passed block has the required stream-block attributes) as a pre-built top-level block rather than any arbitrary `Block`, and pass `block_opts` into the top-level block constructor (`StreamBlock(block_types, **block_opts)` / `block_types(**block_opts)`) instead of calling `self.stream_block.set_meta_options(block_opts)` afterwards, so unsupported options raise `TypeError` immediately.
reason: PRs #11830 and #6718 both tighten the `StreamField` constructor contract: enforce the expected block type and fail fast on invalid options rather than silently accepting them.
common_pattern: Guidelines for developing and documenting Wagtail's StreamField — covering documentation quality/accuracy, required tests for component and field behavior, and constructor-level validation. The dominant sub-theme (11 of 16 generalizations) is StreamField documentation standards; the rest split into StreamField testing and StreamField.__init__ validation.

text: In StreamField traversal, collection, and helper methods that expose child blocks (e.g. `collectors.py`, `blocks_by_type`, `blocks_of_type`, `first_block_of_type`), decide leaf/rich-text processing by the runtime value type rather than solely on declared block definitions, and return block objects (not their `.value`) from helpers so block-specific behavior such as custom templates is preserved; use block-definition checks only for structural recursion through the block tree. Additionally, prepopulate the returned mapping of aggregation methods with an empty collection for every child block type declared in `stream_block.child_blocks`, even when the stream contains no blocks of that type, so the result shape is consistent and missing-key handling is avoided.
reason: Custom or future block types may produce the expected runtime value type without being instances of a specific block class, and returning block objects preserves template metadata used by `{% include_block %}`; the mapping prepopulation is another aspect of the same collector-helper contract (PR #7266) ensuring a consistent result shape for declared-but-absent child block types.
scope: StreamField introspection and StreamValue aggregation helpers (e.g. collectors.py, `blocks_by_type`, `blocks_of_type`, `first_block_of_type`)
common_pattern: Wagtail StreamField/Block API value handling: consistently distinguish block objects from raw values, use runtime value types for leaf decisions, and keep wrapped/unwrapped value contracts explicit.

text: In Wagtail StreamField block collector recursion (e.g. `StreamFieldCollector.find_values` in `wagtail/core/collectors.py`), enforce a single `block_path` consumption invariant: each logical block level consumes exactly one path entry in total. Do not let both `StreamValue` and `StreamChild` wrappers representing the same `StreamBlock` advance/pop `block_path`; keep the current value consistently mapped either to `block_path[0]` or to the block already consumed by the previous recursive call.
reason: Multiple wrapper objects can represent the same logical StreamBlock. Popping a path entry for each wrapper misaligns `block_path` and breaks nested StreamBlock traversal.
scope: wagtail/core/collectors.py and similar StreamField traversal logic
common_pattern: Wagtail StreamField block collector recursion has two linked requirements: maintain a single path-consumption invariant so wrapper objects do not double-consume `block_path`, and test nested block paths because flat cases do not expose this bug.

text: Prefer native, visible accessible names over `aria-label`: use the element's visible text or an associated `<label for="...">` for form controls, and never use `placeholder` as the accessible label. When an `aria-label` (or `title`) is used, place it on the focusable interactive element itself (e.g., `<a>`, `<button>`), not on a non-interactive wrapper, make it name the entity actually being acted on in that template's context, and begin its text with the element's visible label so screen-reader/voice-control output matches what is displayed (WCAG 2.5.3 'Label in Name'). Do not add redundant sr-only/visually-hidden text inside an element that already has an accessible name via `aria-label` or a real `<label>`.
reason: Assistive technology and voice-control users navigate by the visible label; mismatched or redundant accessible names are confusing and break WCAG 'Label in Name'. Labels on wrapper elements may not be announced for the control, and a label referring to the wrong entity is misleading.
common_pattern: Web accessibility naming: how to provide correct accessible names for interactive elements and form controls (prefer native/visible labels, ensure the accessible name matches the visible label, and attach it to the right element).

text: Do not introduce a separate boolean attribute when an existing field already encodes the condition; use the existing field as the single source of truth for boolean state.
reason: Duplicate boolean state can diverge from the canonical field and forces extra maintenance of equality/hash behavior.
common_pattern: Naming conventions for boolean variables, flags, props, and parameters — choosing names that make the toggle's meaning self-evident at call sites and in state models.

text: In Stimulus controllers under `client/src/controllers/`, debounce methods/actions that can fire rapidly or overlap using the shared `utils/debounce` helper, and make the delay configurable rather than hard-coding it inside the controller — via the `.debounce` modifier at the data-action layer or a Stimulus value/param (e.g. `data-{identifier}-delay-param`), using per-path delays when appropriate (e.g. a longer deactivation delay to avoid flicker). Set up debounced handlers in `initialize()` rather than `connect()` for standard helpers, and name debounced variants with a `Lazy` suffix (e.g., `updateLocationLazy`) while keeping the immediate action name for the non-debounced variant when both are needed; if an action should always be debounced, the action itself may be replaced by a debounced bound version, otherwise expose separate immediate and debounced methods with explicit naming. Reference existing controllers such as `SwapController` and `AutosizeController` for convention.
reason: Prevents redundant event handling, fetches, and DOM writes from fast event bursts while keeping controller method intent clear and consistent with existing controllers; per-element/configurable delays avoid baking debounce policy into the controller and support triggers that need different timing or no debounce.
common_pattern: Stimulus controller debouncing conventions: use the shared debounce helper for high-frequency/overlapping actions, set up debounced handlers in the controller lifecycle with explicit naming, and keep delays configurable rather than hardcoded. The cluster also contains a lifecycle contradiction: some comments recommend `connect()`, while later/more specific guidance recommends `initialize()` for standard debounced helpers.

text: Expose timing/delay settings in Stimulus controllers as typed `static values` with sensible defaults instead of hard-coding them, and set a custom `data-*-value` attribute in HTML examples/docs so time-dependent behavior is easy to observe and test. Do not expose config values for behavior that isn't implemented yet.
reason: Consumers (and testers) can tune per-instance behavior via markup without editing controller code, while avoiding speculative config for unimplemented features.
common_pattern: Configurable timing/delay settings in Stimulus controllers should be exposed as typed `static values` with defaults (rather than hard-coded), and examples should exercise them via the matching `data-*-value` attribute for testability.

text: When adding new interactive behavior (placeholders, sync controllers, data-action hooks) to fields in parallel page admin forms, enable it only for the form variants where that behavior semantically belongs (e.g. create/edit); leave copy/duplicate forms using their existing field widgets unless the copy flow explicitly supports the behavior. Copy forms have different semantics, so introducing interactive sync behavior there should be a deliberate future enhancement rather than an incidental side effect of a shared change.
reason: Copy forms have different semantics, so interactive sync behavior should not be introduced there incidentally; it must be a deliberate, supported enhancement.
common_pattern: When a UI behavior is shared across parallel Wagtail admin widgets/forms (images vs documents upload, any consumer of a shared widget), the change must live in the shared widget/base class/mixin — not in per-template or per-model code — and be mirrored consistently across all parallel forms so the implementations don't drift.

text: Treat the `Revision` model as the single source of truth for revision-derived metadata. Prefer deriving page title and timestamps from `latest_revision` (e.g., `latest_revision.object_str`, `latest_revision.created_at`) instead of maintaining denormalized fields like `draft_title` and `latest_revision_created_at` on the primary model. After calling `save_revision()` on a Wagtail Page, do not call `page.save()` unconditionally — revision-backed fields such as `draft_title` and `latest_revision_created_at` are already persisted, and a later plain save can overwrite them with stale in-memory values, breaking page listings and ordering. Only call `save()` when persisting non-revision fields (e.g., custom subclass attributes), and scope it to the branch that actually needs it (e.g., `keep_live`). To publish, call `page.save_revision().publish()`. Documentation examples should demonstrate this distinction using a custom model field rather than a built-in field like `title`.
reason: Converges the source-of-truth design principle and the corresponding save-order API usage rule: denormalized or stale revision-derived fields cause listing/ordering bugs, so revision data should be read from the revision relation and plain saves must not overwrite revision-backed state.
scope: global / page & revision model architecture and save workflows
common_pattern: In Wagtail revision-based workflows, `save_revision()` already persists revision-backed fields; a subsequent plain `page.save()` can overwrite those fields with stale in-memory values and should only be used conditionally for non-revision fields or custom model attributes.

text: Use the project's canonical revision lookup helpers and managers rather than reimplementing revision queries. Use the model helper (e.g. `instance.get_latest_revision()`) for a model's latest revision, and choose the correctly-scoped manager — `Revision.page_revisions` for page-only queries, `Revision.objects` when non-page models (e.g. schedulable snippets) may apply — querying the `Revision` table directly instead of annotating the primary model with `Exists()` subqueries and re-fetching the latest revision per row.
reason: Reuses canonical revision-lookup logic, keeps revision semantics consistent, ensures reports/views cover all applicable revision-enabled models, and scales better than correlated subqueries with per-row lookups.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Wagtail's `Revision` model handling: which source of truth to read revision-derived data from, how to query revisions (helpers/managers), what to store in `Revision.title`, and how to document revision-related mixins/signals. The cluster is topically coherent around 'revisions' but contains several distinct sub-patterns rather than a single principle.

text: Store the canonical title in `Revision.title`, derived from `str(instance)` rather than the model's admin/display title or a duck-typed `title` attribute, so revision records remain stable when display-title logic changes and behave consistently across Pages and Snippets (respecting custom `__str__` overrides).
reason: Admin display-title logic is expected to evolve; using it in revisions makes historical revisions inconsistently formatted and prevents display tweaks from applying to older revisions. `str(instance)` keeps behavior consistent across model types.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Wagtail's `Revision` model handling: which source of truth to read revision-derived data from, how to query revisions (helpers/managers), what to store in `Revision.title`, and how to document revision-related mixins/signals. The cluster is topically coherent around 'revisions' but contains several distinct sub-patterns rather than a single principle.

text: In revision/revert views under `wagtail/admin/views/pages/`, derive page status and the 'Live' URL from the current `page.specific` object, not from the historical `revision_page`'s `live` / `has_unpublished_changes` flags; reuse the page object already fetched at the start of the view.
reason: A revision can be from the distant past, so its publication state does not reflect the current live page and can produce an incorrect Live URL.
common_pattern: Correct behavior and implementation of admin history/revision views: these views must reflect the *current* context (current page state, applicability of actions) rather than stale or irrelevant revision data, and shared revision UI should be centralized rather than duplicated.

text: When a Wagtail search backend needs backend-specific parameters, expose the common search/highlight parameters in the backend-agnostic API and accept backend-specific options through a `{backend}_extra` dict kwarg (e.g. `es_extra` for Elasticsearch), mirroring the `SearchFields` API pattern.
reason: Keeps backend-specific parameters from leaking into the generic API and makes it feasible to add highlighting support for more search backends without breaking the public API.
common_pattern: Wagtail search backends should keep backend-specific concerns isolated from generic APIs, and any related documentation (docstrings and user-facing docs) must be accurate, consistent, and concrete about backend capabilities.

text: In `wagtail/search`, backend-specific query implementations must build on the canonical query abstractions in `wagtail/search/query.py`: represent query variants as subclasses of the canonical query classes (not backend-local duplicates or helper base classes), and normalizers/compilers must handle every query node type — unwrapping unsupported nodes by compiling their subquery rather than leaving them unhandled. Backends must not expose query types or parameters they cannot faithfully honor, and high-level query classes should map to the engine's native query constructs (e.g. `PlainText` → Elasticsearch `match`) rather than being decomposed into primitives like `term` queries — so engine-level analyzers, language handling (e.g. CJK bigrams), and user settings continue to apply.
reason: Preserves a single shared query API across backends, prevents divergent parallel class hierarchies, allows unsupported features to degrade gracefully, and avoids bypassing engine features or exposing misleading public options.
common_pattern: All generalizations come from the Wagtail `wagtail/search` layer and converge on a single architectural principle: backend search implementations must conform to the canonical query abstraction layer (`wagtail/search/query.py`) and faithfully reflect the underlying engine's capabilities, rather than inventing parallel hierarchies, new public parameters, or advertising support (query types / operators) the backend cannot honor. Three distinct sub-patterns emerge: (1) canonical class hierarchy and complete node handling, (2) backend fidelity — delegate to native engine constructs and don't expose unsupported capabilities, (3) public API consistency with QuerySet search methods.

text: Keep public backend and search-handler APIs consistent and honest. Public backend search methods (e.g. `BaseSearch.search()`) must match the arguments of the corresponding QuerySet search methods; internal implementation details such as `query_compiler_class` must not appear in the public signature—when `search` and `autocomplete` need different compilation behavior, extract shared internal logic and pass the compiler class privately. Overridable search-handler methods (e.g. `search_queryset`) must keep a signature consistent with the base class and peer implementations, using a shared `**kwargs` catch-all instead of explicit internal parameters or ad-hoc names like `**extra_search_kwargs`; internal flags such as `distinct_applied` should flow through `**kwargs` rather than becoming part of the overridable signature. Do not interpret arbitrary `**kwargs` as implicit `queryset.filter()` arguments, and avoid exposing convenience options like `search_handler_extra_search_kwargs` unless the filtering semantics are clear; callers should pre-filter the queryset before passing it to `search_queryset`. If such extra-filter kwargs are supported, apply them before any early-return guards (e.g. `not search_term or not self.search_fields`) so results are constrained even when search is skipped.
reason: Consistent signatures make handler and backend implementations safely interchangeable, avoid surprising callers, keep internal compiler selection private, and prevent unclear or silently ignored filtering options.
scope: wagtail/search/backends/base.py and search handler interface, e.g. wagtail/contrib/modeladmin/helpers/search.py
common_pattern: All generalizations come from the Wagtail `wagtail/search` layer and converge on a single architectural principle: backend search implementations must conform to the canonical query abstraction layer (`wagtail/search/query.py`) and faithfully reflect the underlying engine's capabilities, rather than inventing parallel hierarchies, new public parameters, or advertising support (query types / operators) the backend cannot honor. Three distinct sub-patterns emerge: (1) canonical class hierarchy and complete node handling, (2) backend fidelity — delegate to native engine constructs and don't expose unsupported capabilities, (3) public API consistency with QuerySet search methods.

text: Declare shared or subclass-overridable defaults centrally—on the base class, its inner Meta, or a shared module-level mapping—rather than duplicating literals in concrete subclasses or passing them through custom constructor kwargs. Use declarative overrides (e.g., Meta or get_default hooks) for subclass/type-specific defaults, and do not encode type-specific fallbacks as sentinel Meta.default values on built-in blocks. For chooser classes/blocks, declare an overridable class attribute defaulting to None and resolve it in the accessor with `self.<attr> or <DefaultClass>` (or `BlanketPermissionPolicy(None)` when no model exists) instead of hardcoding the default at class scope.
reason: Centralizing defaults keeps behavior consistent across current and future subclasses, lets downstream code override or patch defaults at the base/configuration level, and avoids repeated literals or custom constructor plumbing. The chooser-specific None-plus-accessor pattern allows subclass overrides without duplicating imports or resolution logic.
scope: Wagtail block/base and chooser classes (wagtail/blocks/*.py and related generic chooser views)
common_pattern: Managing shared or overridable default values for Wagtail block/base classes: declare defaults centrally (base class, Meta, shared mapping, or get_default hook) and avoid sharing mutable default instances across instances.

text: Keep subclass-overridable class attributes (e.g. `model_fields`) as lists to avoid breaking downstream code that relies on list operations such as concatenation (`self.model_fields + [...]`); if a method needs set-based lookup performance, convert the attribute to a local set at the start of the method (`model_fields = set(self.model_fields)`) and use that local throughout, including helper calls.
reason: Changing an existing public class attribute from a list to a set is a breaking API change because sets do not support `+`, and the performance benefit is negligible for small collections. Local conversion preserves both backward compatibility and the optimization.
common_pattern: Preserving backward compatibility of subclass-overridable class-level collection attributes: don't change public list-typed attributes to sets; instead convert to a local set inside methods that need set semantics.

text: Keep app-specific setup/registration inside that app's own `AppConfig` (`apps.py`) rather than in core/central modules, and omit `AppConfig.label` unless a custom label is genuinely needed (e.g. resolving app-registry conflicts, preserving a legacy label, or controlling model table names/migrations).
reason: Self-contained apps give third-party apps parity with built-in ones and prevent hidden coupling between built-in apps and core. Django already derives a default label from `AppConfig.name`, so setting it without a specific need adds noise and can mislead readers.
common_pattern: Django AppConfig conventions: how apps are referenced (full dotted/config path vs. bare label) and where app-specific setup/label belongs (in the app's own AppConfig).

text: When exposing a third-party library's configuration in our public API, mirror the library's own option names and documentary concepts (do not invent local synonyms like `custom` for `spec`, or a generic `_config` suffix) and group the library's settings under a single nested spec/config object rather than adding one top-level key per option, so the interface matches upstream docs and can grow without changing shape. If the underlying library is an implementation detail that site authors should not need to know, name the public developer-facing setting in project-domain terms instead. If a local parameter, attribute, or config key intentionally diverges from the upstream name because the upstream name is misleading or accepts broader values than its name implies (e.g. an upstream `parentID` that actually accepts an arbitrary selector), add a brief code comment at the definition or mapping site explaining the naming rationale and the actual accepted values.
reason: Keeps the integration transparent and aligned with upstream documentation and semantics, avoids a hidden translation layer and unnecessary magic, prevents ad-hoc top-level keys that break the API shape as new options are added, and prevents future maintainers from 'fixing' an intentional divergence to match upstream or from assuming the upstream name fully describes the local behavior.
common_pattern: Two related patterns around how project code interacts with third-party library APIs: (a) naming/config-shape should mirror the upstream library's own terminology when exposing that library's configuration, and (b) when local names intentionally diverge from upstream terminology, the divergence must be documented in a code comment.

text: Encapsulate derived selection lists on bulk-toggle controllers as reusable accessors — e.g. implement `get activeItems()` as `this.itemTargets.filter(({ disabled }) => !disabled)` on `BulkController` and reuse it in selection-state calculations instead of repeating the filter inline.
reason: Centralizing the 'get me a list of non-disabled items' logic in a named accessor avoids duplication and keeps selection-state calculations consistent with the bulk-toggle controller's abstraction.
common_pattern: Reliable management of bulk-action selection state: track selected items by stable data identifiers (not cached DOM references or numeric-ID-derived ordering), and centralize derived selection lists (e.g. non-disabled items) in reusable controller helpers.

text: For bulk-selection checkboxes using the `w-bulk` Stimulus controller (including Wagtail admin chooser multi-select checkboxes), wire each item checkbox with `data-action="w-bulk#toggle"` and `data-w-bulk-target="item"` (and `data-multiple-choice-select` in chooser templates); use `data-action="w-bulk#toggleAll"` with `data-w-bulk-force-param="false"` for clear-all and `data-w-bulk-force-param="true"` for select-all instead of a dedicated clear action; store record identifiers on the checkbox `value` with a shared `name` rather than deriving them from DOM IDs. When applying a checkbox fix to one chooser template, propagate the same change to analogous chooser templates (e.g. `chooser/tables/page_checkbox_select_cell.html`).
reason: Keeps the bulk-selection controller API consistent: checkboxes are registered as controller targets, select-all/clear-all are expressed through toggleAll force params, selected values are collected from semantic form attributes instead of brittle ID scraping, and duplicated chooser templates stay in sync.
scope: client-side bulk-selection UIs using the `w-bulk` Stimulus controller, including Wagtail admin chooser templates
common_pattern: Stimulus w-bulk bulk-selection UI conventions and their test strategy

text: When adding request-method-dependent logic to a view, cover every method the view serves (not just the targeted one), and re-verify the chosen HTTP method still matches the handler's side effects as it evolves (e.g., switch away from GET once the handler writes to the database); document non-obvious method choices with an inline comment explaining the required edge cases.
reason: Partial method coverage silently skips protections on unhandled paths, and scope creep can invalidate an earlier method choice; documenting the rationale prevents accidental regressions during refactoring.
common_pattern: Correct and explicit handling of HTTP request methods in view/handler code: method choice must match the handler's side effects, method-specific logic must live in the corresponding handler and cover every method the view serves, and non-obvious method selections must be documented.

text: In admin chooser widgets, place generic instance-lookup behavior at the base layer that owns it (`BaseChooser.get_instance` or comparable widget lookup method). Resolve model instances using the ForeignKey's configured `to_field_name` (e.g. `self.model_class.objects.get(**{self.to_field_name: value})`) rather than scanning all unique fields. Handle invalid/unrecognized chosen IDs by catching `DoesNotExist` and returning no instance; keep form-specific validation in the calling form/view. Do not add subclass widget exception handling or per-form patches, and do not guard on `model_class` presence when it is assumed to exist throughout the class. When lookup logic changes, add tests covering both the configured `to_field_name` path and the default primary-key path, including missing-instance and invalid-value exceptions.
reason: Keeps chooser instance-lookup behavior consistent at the layer that owns it, supports non-PK unique ForeignKey targets without brute-force queries, preserves silent-drop behavior for invalid IDs, and protects both lookup paths with regression tests.
scope: global within admin chooser widgets/forms; chooser widgets / comparable admin widget model-instance lookup methods
common_pattern: Chooser class-hierarchy design in Wagtail: shared/generic chooser behavior should live at the base-class layer (BaseChooser / chooser block base), with subclass-specific concerns pushed to the caller, and overridable defaults expressed as None class attributes resolved via accessor fallbacks rather than hardcoded or guarded per-subclass.

text: Keep chooser modal APIs and chooser widget APIs separate. Expose modal-opening logic (e.g. a public API such as `Wagtail.openPageChooser(options)` or an `openChooserModal` method) so callers can open the modal independently of Wagtail's built-in chooser widget; non-widget consumers may continue to use `ModalWorkflow` directly. Factory functions for choosers should return an object exposing named action methods (e.g. `setImage`) rather than a bare callback, mirroring `buildExpandingFormset`. For client-side chooser modal implementations, avoid attaching global handler objects (e.g. `window.*_ONLOAD_HANDLERS`) to `window`; encapsulate onload handlers via a `ModalWorkflow` base class with per-modal subclasses or a factory-generated onload handler bundle, rather than switching to custom DOM events or a global handler registry.
reason: Chooser modals are consumed independently and should not be coupled to widget state/markup; modal-opening APIs and factory-returned named actions improve reusability, while encapsulating onload handlers avoids global mutable state and preserves API compatibility.
scope: client/src/entrypoints/ public APIs and Wagtail admin chooser JS modules; client-side chooser modal implementations under /client
common_pattern: Wagtail admin chooser/modal API design and configuration: chooser modals should be decoupled from the built-in widget, driven by explicit URL-passed inputs, and configured via data (props with global fallback, entity options, dynamic URL resolution) rather than hard-coded or DOM-coupled values.

text: Keep chooser-specific logic and value handling inside chooser components: chooser panels should use chooser APIs such as `chooserFieldName` and `chooserWidgetFactory` rather than scraping hidden inputs, and chooser widget HTML should be value-independent except for error states.
reason: Prevents chooser-specific concerns from leaking into generic `InlinePanel` behavior or value-dependent DOM/initialization; the chooser component/API should remain the stable abstraction.
common_pattern: Chooser-specific behavior, APIs, rendering, and styling should be owned by chooser components rather than generic panels, field/data-storage classes, or brittle DOM scraping.

text: In hooks that run after the framework has already sorted a list by an `order` attribute—notably `construct_page_action_menu`—list order is authoritative: the hook ignores each `ActionMenuItem`'s `order` field, and the last item in `menu_items` is the default action. Do not document or recommend mutating item `order` fields, constructing new menu items, or passing an explicit default flag. Instead, document that the `order` attribute is ignored at this stage and show the supported mechanism: reorder the existing `menu_items` list to move the desired action (e.g. Publish) to the end. In `docs/reference/hooks.rst`, note that redefining the whole list is unnecessary (it is done in the example only to make the resulting default obvious).
reason: The run-time behavior is that sorting has already occurred, so `order` is a no-op in this hook; default-action selection is derived from list position, not from `order` or a `default` flag. Documenting this contract prevents users from writing confusing, non-functional code and avoids popularizing fragile internal mutations.
common_pattern: Wagtail's `construct_page_action_menu` hook resolves action ordering and the default action from the list's ordering (last item = default, `order` field ignored), and this ordering semantics must be documented and tested consistently.

text: In Wagtail search indexes, store both the root and leaf content types on index entries and enforce uniqueness on `(root_content_type, object_id)`. The `Indexed` base class should index each object once by its root content type by default, and index rebuild management commands must prune entries for content types that are no longer registered. This prevents duplicate entries caused by multi-table inheritance and stale entries left behind after content types are removed or apps become standalone.
reason: Keeps the search index consistent across upgrades by avoiding duplicate entries from multi-table inheritance and stale entries after content types are removed or apps become standalone.
common_pattern: Search index lifecycle correctness: prevent duplicate entries via root-content-type uniqueness and prevent stale entries by pruning unregistered content types during index rebuilds.

text: Integrate with Wagtail search through its public API rather than reimplementing or maintaining internal abstractions: use `wagtailsearch.index.class_is_indexed` when checking whether a model is indexed (instead of testing `issubclass(model, Indexed)` directly), and integrate search into custom admin views via the public search API rather than internal mixins like `SearchableListMixin`. Remove unused, undocumented, untested code such as `SearchableListMixin` in `wagtail/admin/views/mixins.py` along with its now-unused imports (`SearchForm`, `get_search_backend`, `class_is_indexed`) rather than keeping it as a public convenience.
reason: Centralizes indexing eligibility logic across search backends so rules change consistently, and avoids maintaining unused internal abstractions that can drift out of sync with core views like `IndexView`.
scope: global within Wagtail search-related code, including wagtail/admin/views/mixins.py and legacy helper modules
common_pattern: Prefer Wagtail's public search API for indexed-model checks and custom view integration over inline duplication or internal mixin abstractions.

text: Implement locale filtering once in the shared Wagtail admin header (`wagtailadmin/shared/header.html`) alongside search, following the snippets/page-selector pattern: read the selected locale from the `locale` GET parameter, filter the queryset accordingly, and use the `_set_locale_query_param` helper to build locale query strings. Do not duplicate locale-filter UI in individual create/edit templates. Use `locale` (not `lang` or `local`) consistently as the query-parameter name, context key, and variable name (e.g. `locale_context`) for anything that filters or represents the selected locale in Wagtail admin/modeladmin/i18n views.
reason: A single shared locale-filter component serves pages, snippets, settings, and modeladmin, keeps behavior and the data contract uniform, avoids duplicated URL/UI construction, and prevents divergence from the established `locale` naming convention.
scope: wagtailadmin shared header and translatable admin views (modeladmin, snippets, settings); locale naming in Wagtail admin/modeladmin/i18n views and templates
common_pattern: Wagtail admin i18n/locale handling conventions: consistent locale naming (locale vs lang/local), reuse of shared locale-filter UI/helpers across admin views, and correct locale-resolution fallback semantics.

text: Do not determine the active locale solely from a `locale` GET parameter. When no valid explicit locale is supplied, fall back to `Locale.get_active()` so `LocaleMiddleware`/i18n language negotiation is honored. In docs, describe this dynamic behavior as resolving the 'most suitable locale' (target translation locale when i18n is enabled, otherwise the current admin user's language) rather than a predetermined 'determined model locale'.
reason: Front-end requests under LocaleMiddleware may set the active locale via middleware/language negotiation rather than a query parameter; relying only on the GET param can resolve the wrong locale or miss the active one. Accurate docs prevent misunderstanding of dynamic fallback.
scope: Wagtail i18n locale-resolution helpers and locale-aware widget/slug docs
common_pattern: Wagtail admin i18n/locale handling conventions: consistent locale naming (locale vs lang/local), reuse of shared locale-filter UI/helpers across admin views, and correct locale-resolution fallback semantics.

text: In Wagtail admin views that need locale/i18n behavior (including modeladmin views), reuse `wagtail.admin.views.generic.mixins.LocaleMixin` and gate translation-aware logic on the composite condition `getattr(settings, 'WAGTAIL_I18N_ENABLED', False) and issubclass(self.model, TranslatableMixin)` instead of checking only the mixin or relying on `self.locale`. Apply the same guard consistently across all related views (e.g. sibling `dispatch()` methods).
reason: The feature flag and the model-capability check are complementary halves of one condition; both are required to determine whether i18n is active for a model. Reusing LocaleMixin and the module-wide guard avoids divergent, narrower checks and reimplemented locale resolution.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin i18n/locale handling: gate translation-aware behavior on both the WAGTAIL_I18N_ENABLED feature flag and a model-locale capability check, reuse the platform's locale mixins/context rather than reimplementing locale resolution, and cover/display locale UI consistently (including for the disabled/non-translatable case).

text: For admin table columns that display one-to-many or multi-valued relations, do not use `annotate()`/`F()` over the relation, because it can duplicate parent rows and split related objects across rows. Instead use `prefetch_related()` for the relation and any nested rendering relations, and render the combined values through a custom `Column` subclass such as `RelatedObjectsColumn` or an `accessor` returning the related queryset.
reason: Preserves one-row-per-parent listing behavior, avoids N+1 queries, and correctly displays all related objects in a single cell.
scope: Wagtail admin listing querysets and multi-valued table columns
common_pattern: Use Wagtail's admin tables UI framework and its `IndexView`/`Column` abstractions consistently: define listings through Python table/column objects, keep cell templates coupled to column accessors rather than raw model fields, and localize column behavior to the app/viewset that needs it.

text: In report/listing views, build querysets from the primary model being rendered (e.g. Page) using its existing relations rather than from auxiliary log/audit or link tables; when decorating paginated results, maintain one primary-key-to-model-instance mapping and derive nested display fields from that instance instead of using parallel mappings or separate id-to-object conversion helpers.
reason: Keeps view data flow in one direction, removes id-to-instance conversion code, reduces duplicated conditional logic, and simplifies pagination decoration.
common_pattern: Simplifying Wagtail report/listing views by sourcing querysets from the primary rendered model (e.g. Page) and decorating results via a single primary-key-to-instance mapping, avoiding auxiliary-table joins, id-to-object conversion, and parallel field mappings.

text: Use bulk operations appropriately: follow Django's contract by using `bulk_create()` only for new/unsaved records (pk is None) and `bulk_update()` for existing records; do not mix create and update logic in a `bulk_create()` override, mutate caller-supplied fields (e.g. slugs), or replicate full `full_clean`/`save()` validation behavior inside it. Prefer `bulk_create`/`bulk_update` over repeated per-object `create()`/`save()` calls when writing many model instances, including in test setup, and do not make `save()` conditional merely to avoid per-object overhead. When a code path uses `bulk_create`, `bulk_update`, or `QuerySet.update()` and thereby bypasses model `save()` (and its signals/hooks), explicitly handle the resulting side effects (e.g. logging/audit signals), and in tests explicitly assert that fields normally populated by `save()` are populated.
reason: Bulk operations batch database work into fewer queries, but they insert/update only and skip save-time signals and field population, so callers and tests must handle those side effects explicitly.
common_pattern: Correct and efficient use of Django bulk ORM operations (bulk_create/bulk_update) versus per-object save()/create(), including respecting their contracts and compensating for the side effects they bypass.

text: For list/index views that render only a subset of a potentially unbounded reverse relation (e.g. Wagtail image renditions), use a filtered prefetch scoped to the exact subset needed, preferably via a reusable queryset helper such as `prefetch_renditions(relation_name="renditions", filters=None)` that accepts `Filter` objects or spec strings and filters by `filter_spec__in`. In Wagtail image views, prefer `prefetch_renditions()` over generic `prefetch_related("renditions")`, do not mix both approaches, and use `prefetch_renditions()` on `Image` querysets while `prefetch_related()` is still required when starting from a related-model queryset. Store the filtered subset under a dedicated attribute such as `prefetched_{relation}` using `Prefetch(..., to_attr=...)`; do not replace the relation's default manager/cache. Consuming code should check both the normal relation and the filtered attribute, and any code inserting newly generated related objects into the prefetch cache must key by the configured `to_attr` name; avoid generic/implicit `to_attr` support in favor of explicit named prefetch attributes. In documentation, show both image-rendition prefetch query shapes: direct `Image` querysets using `prefetch_renditions`, and related-model querysets using `prefetch_related` because `prefetch_renditions` is not available there.
reason: Prefetching all renditions can load unused or unbounded related rows into memory and increase query count for list/index views; a filtered `to_attr` keeps normal relation behavior intact and makes the optimization explicit. The docs must cover both query entry points because users query images directly and via related models.
scope: Wagtail image views/querysets and renditions docs
common_pattern: Scoped prefetching of image renditions in Wagtail list/index views: avoid loading all related renditions, use filtered/dedicated prefetch APIs, cache filtered results under a distinct to_attr, and document the direct-Image vs related-model query paths. The cluster is convergent/complementary, not contradictory.

text: Connect signal handlers inside the registration API (e.g., within a `register_model`-style function) rather than relying on `AppConfig.ready()` timing, so callers do not need to order apps in `INSTALLED_APPS`. This avoids hidden app-loading order dependencies and timing issues where another app's `ready()` inspects registered models before the registration function has run.
reason: Avoids hidden app-loading order dependencies and timing issues where another app's `ready()` inspects registered models before the registration function has run.
common_pattern: Django signal wiring location and timing: prefer connecting signals via the registration API to avoid hidden app-loading order dependencies, and treat any documented wiring location (including AppConfig.ready()) as a convention rather than a requirement.

text: For Wagtail widgets that need widget-specific assets (e.g. rich text editors using `versioned_static`), build `media` lazily in a `media` property decorated with `@cached_property` so URLs are generated on request and evaluated only once, and implement widget-specific media handling in the widget's adapter in `wagtail/core/widget_adapters.py` rather than in `FieldBlock`, delegating from block classes to the adapter.
reason: The inner `Media` class is what triggers conditional asset loading for a widget; constructing media lazily (and caching it) preserves dynamic/versioned asset URLs and avoids repeated evaluation, while routing widget-specific behavior through the adapter keeps concerns out of the block layer and avoids duplication across blocks.
common_pattern: Wagtail widget asset/media handling: the inner `Media` class is the mechanism that loads assets when a widget is used, so widget media should be constructed lazily and kept in the widget layer (adapter) rather than eagerly in blocks or __init__; documentation should explain the Media trigger and defer to upstream Django docs.

text: In Wagtail admin views, treat `media` as part of each rendered component's contract: when composing a view/page context from components (panels, forms, edit handlers, side panels, action menus, etc.), aggregate every rendered component's `media` into the context `media` (e.g. via `get_media`/media collector), even if the component currently declares none, and ensure every view/template that renders a shared media-exposing component includes that component's media.
reason: Components declare media as part of their interface. Omitting any component's media can silently drop required CSS/JS and break widgets, panels, forms, or admin views.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin views must honor the media contract of rendered components by aggregating their declared CSS/JS assets into the view/page context media, and by rendering that media wherever the component is used.

text: In Wagtail code, use Willow for all image handling (including tests, format conversions, and content type derivation) rather than importing or using Pillow (`PIL`) directly. When converting image format names to MIME types, use Willow's `mime_type` property instead of local helper functions or manual mappings.
reason: Wagtail standardizes image handling on Willow; direct Pillow usage bypasses the project's established image abstraction. Using Willow's native properties reduces redundancy and keeps behavior consistent across versions.
common_pattern: Wagtail standardizes image handling on Willow rather than Pillow (PIL) directly. This includes using Willow's built-in properties (e.g., `mime_type`) for format/MIME type conversion and validating image content via Willow in tests, avoiding local helpers or direct Pillow usage.

text: Normalize/sanitize inputs consistently at the boundary: perform normalization (e.g., trimming) at the caller/controller or at the point where content enters the system (e.g., paste handling), not inside a conditional branch of a shared utility or in rendering/decoration components, so it applies to all paths without changing utility behavior for other callers. Only add normalization or regex handling for edge-case input when there is demonstrated real-world input or a clear functional need. When the same normalization logic appears in multiple methods, extract it into a dedicated helper that takes the raw input and returns the normalized value.
reason: Merges both rules' complementary guidance on input normalization/sanitization: handle inputs at the boundary, avoid hidden/speculative handling in shared utilities or presentational components, and centralize duplicated normalization logic.
common_pattern: Normalization/edge-case handling in content processing: avoid ad hoc normalization unless justified, and when normalization is required, implement it consistently so downstream assumptions hold.

text: Default an optional output-format (or similar mode) parameter to the value actually required by current call sites, so existing callers need not pass a redundant argument; make alternate formats opt-in rather than defaulting to a speculative future use case.
reason: Defaults should reduce boilerplate for real usage; setting a default no current caller wants forces existing call sites to opt back into the needed behavior and bases the API on speculative future callers.
common_pattern: Choosing correct, format-specific default values when a function or option supports multiple output formats — (a) each format's parameters (quality, defaults) must be its own, not a copy of a sibling's, and (b) the default output format should match actual usage rather than being set speculatively.

text: In API documentation and schemas, use precise, implementation-aligned terminology: name entities by their correct type (e.g., Pydantic `Field` is a class, not a function), describe fields/classes by the specific domain concept they expose rather than a vague restatement of their name, distinguish endpoint parameters from response schema fields, name reused schemas after the base/entity resource rather than an endpoint-specific use case, and ensure example field meanings (such as `url` vs `full_url`) match the serializer's actual output.
reason: Merged from rules about precise API documentation terminology and implementation-aligned API schema terminology.
scope: API schema design, API reference documentation, and API examples
common_pattern: API schemas, fields, and documentation examples must use terminology and naming that accurately reflect their actual role, structure, and serializer behavior.

text: Expose interactive UI component behavior and state through documented namespaced DOM CustomEvents using a kebab-case `{app}:{component}-{action}` name, not generic or native-like names such as `hide` or `visibilityChange`. Wagtail admin uses the `wagtail:` prefix and names like `wagtail:tab-switch`, `wagtail:panel-collapse`, and `wagtail:images-upload`; use the full namespaced string as the identifier so it is greppable and unambiguous. Dispatch from the component root/container and allow the event to bubble; do not dispatch duplicate equivalent events on `document`. Always dispatch the component's custom event regardless of whether related DOM elements are present — do not guard dispatch on markup, and let listeners decide how to react. Verify that the dispatched event name exactly matches the string the receiving listener subscribes to, including spelling and pluralization (Wagtail admin message notifications use `w-messages:add`, plural, not `w-message:add`).
reason: Makes component behavior encapsulated, discoverable, collision-free, and reliably delivered to consumers, while avoiding duplicate handling and silent listener mismatches.
scope: client-side UI components (Wagtail admin client-side JavaScript)
common_pattern: Designing client-side UI component interactions around explicit custom DOM events: use CustomEvent, namespace and dispatch events from the component root, rely on bubbling rather than duplicate document-level events, and model state/lifecycle changes so external code can observe or intercept component behavior.

text: Custom component events should communicate domain-level state changes (e.g. 'form errors changed') rather than implementation-level DOM mutations such as 'custom DOM updated'. When a stateful component changes state, emit meaningful state-transition events rather than only a generic toggle without state information. Prefer a single event carrying the resulting state in `detail` (e.g. `detail: { opened: boolean }`), or use separate state/lifecycle events (such as open/close, or pre/post) when consumers need distinct semantics. If consumers must block or modify the change, provide a cancellable pre-change event plus a separate post-change event from the same component element, and dispatch state-change events from every code path that mutates the state.
reason: Consumers should be able to subscribe to meaningful domain state changes, optionally intercept them before they apply, and observe them consistently regardless of which code path caused the change.
common_pattern: Designing client-side UI component interactions around explicit custom DOM events: use CustomEvent, namespace and dispatch events from the component root, rely on bubbling rather than duplicate document-level events, and model state/lifecycle changes so external code can observe or intercept component behavior.

text: Do not add wrapper properties or methods that only forward to an already-exposed attribute or method; call the underlying attribute directly (e.g., `response.soup.select()` rather than `response.select()`, `image_file.mime_type` rather than a utility conversion function). Add indirection only when it provides meaningful abstraction, reuse, or an override point. Add a dedicated accessor when it removes value: (a) when a wrapper/delegating class repeatedly chains through the wrapped object (`self.wrapped_object.attribute`), expose the attribute directly on the wrapper; (b) when an existing attribute is being reused for a new semantic purpose, add a dedicated accessor instead of coupling the new use to that attribute.
reason: Redundant indirection enlarges the API surface, duplicates accessors for little ergonomic gain, and makes code harder to follow without adding functional value. Dedicated accessors are appropriate when they reduce repetitive chained access or couple callers to intent rather than an implementation detail whose original purpose was different, so the underlying representation can change without breaking consumers.
common_pattern: A single decision framework about accessor indirection: pass-through wrappers that merely forward to an already-exposed attribute add no value and should be avoided (direct access preferred), whereas a dedicated accessor IS warranted when it eliminates repeated chained access through a wrapped object or decouples a new semantic use from an attribute's original purpose.

text: For audit or log-entry foreign keys, use on_delete=models.DO_NOTHING so historical log records are preserved if the referenced object is deleted.
reason: Captures the model-design sub-pattern for audit/log foreign keys, which is distinct from documentation and testing guidance.
common_pattern: Correct use and documentation of Django ForeignKey.on_delete semantics across model design, management-command tests, and docs: being explicit about which FK fields are nulled/deleted, which parent records are preserved, and when to use PROTECT, SET_NULL, or DO_NOTHING.

text: Avoid introducing new component variants, sizes, or template variables unless there is a concrete reuse need. When a new variant is necessary, give it a descriptive variant qualifier that disambiguates it from the existing base name/case (e.g., rename `initButtonWithDropdown` to `initNewButtonWithDropdown` in `client/src/entrypoints/admin/tippy-tooltips.js`, since `button_with_dropdown` already names the existing component), and represent variant-specific differences in the type system (e.g., TypeScript).
reason: Prevents premature abstraction and design system bloat while ensuring variant-specific logic is distinguishable and self-documenting, and avoids naming collisions between an existing component and its new variant.
common_pattern: Managing component variants: avoid unnecessary proliferation and make necessary variants explicit in naming and type system.

text: Keep shared components minimal: remove code branches and parameters that are only needed for unsupported variants or page-specific cases, and move variant-specific logic to dedicated components.
reason: Reduces dead code and complexity, and keeps the shared component API clean and focused.
common_pattern: Keep shared components minimal by removing code paths and parameters that only serve unsupported variants or single-use cases, moving that logic to dedicated components.

text: In the breadcrumb component, the final/current breadcrumb `<li>` must remain visible (it is the current-location indicator) and must carry `data-breadcrumb-item` — the last item gets `data-breadcrumb-item` when `trailing_breadcrumb_title or not is_expanded`, and receives `hidden` only when `trailing_breadcrumb_title and not is_expanded`. Leading items may be collapsed, but the final item should not be conditionally hidden by collapse/expand state alone.
reason: The breadcrumb jQuery code relies on `data-breadcrumb-item` to locate the last item, or click/link behavior breaks; and hiding the current-location item removes the location indicator or leaves it permanently hidden in the expanded state.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern the Wagtail admin shared breadcrumb component (`wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/shared/breadcrumb-next.html`) — its Tailwind utility-class width behavior, current-item visibility/data-attribute contract, test fixture markup, and CSS color-selector coverage. The cluster is topically coherent (one component) but contains several genuinely distinct sub-patterns that cannot be collapsed into a single rule.

text: Implement ARIA tab widgets using the standard tabs pattern: a container with `role="tablist"` must have direct child elements with `role="tab"`; do not wrap tab controls in heading elements (`h1`-`h6`); do not use a tabs container when there is no tabbed content — use a plain, non-tabbed structure instead. Bind keyboard navigation to the `role="tablist"` container rather than individual tabs (horizontal Left/Right/Home/End only), auto-activate/reveal the corresponding panel when focus moves to a tab, and use roving tabindex so only the active `role="tab"` is tabbable (`tabindex="0"` or no attribute) while inactive tabs get `tabindex="-1"`; update tabindex for all tabs on initialization and selection changes, never set `tabindex="-1"` on non-tab triggers/standalone controls, and do not add `tabindex="0"` to natively focusable elements.
reason: Centralizes keyboard behavior, matches the ARIA tabs interaction model, ensures accessible and semantically correct tab widgets, prevents unreachable controls, avoids empty tab containers that confuse screen readers, and avoids redundant tab stops that break expected keyboard accessibility.
scope: global for ARIA tab widgets and composite tab controls, including Wagtail admin UI components
common_pattern: Keyboard navigation and tabindex management for ARIA tab widgets (the ARIA tabs pattern), covering centralized key handling, automatic panel activation, roving tabindex, and avoiding incorrect tabindex on non-tab/natively focusable elements.

text: For Django model field introspection, use the public `_meta` API — `Model._meta.get_fields()`, `Model._meta.fields_map`, `Model._meta.pk`, etc. — rather than legacy internals (`_meta.fields`), `hasattr`/`vars()` checks, or constructing field classes directly; avoid `_meta` APIs deprecated in the project's supported Django version, adding a compatibility fallback with a TODO when an older supported Django must still work. When you need a model's primary-key field object, use `Model._meta.pk` directly instead of resolving `Model._meta.pk.name` and passing it to `Model._meta.get_field()`; reserve `get_field(name)` for genuine dynamic field-name lookups, and if the same PK lookup is needed in multiple places (e.g. across chooser views), extract it into a shared utility method.
reason: The public `_meta` API is the canonical, forward-compatible source of truth for declared model fields, avoiding false positives, breakage from deprecated/legacy internals, and unnecessary intermediate string lookups while keeping custom primary-key handling consistent when reused.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern correct use of Django model field machinery — preferring canonical/built-in Django field APIs and metadata (`_meta`) over custom subclasses, legacy internals, manual introspection, or re-implemented behavior. Two coherent sub-patterns emerge: (a) `_meta` field-introspection API usage, and (b) preference for built-in model fields over custom code and framework-duplicating tests.

text: Prefer built-in Django model fields over custom field subclasses when no custom validation or behavior is needed, choosing the field type that matches the constraint (e.g. `CharField` for bounded lengths, `TextField` for unbounded text); do not write tests that merely assert Django's built-in field behavior (e.g. that a `URLField` is a `URLField`) — tests should verify project-specific logic instead.
reason: Built-in fields communicate intent at the schema/form level and avoid unnecessary custom code; Django already guarantees its field behavior, so testing it adds cost without catching project regressions.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern correct use of Django model field machinery — preferring canonical/built-in Django field APIs and metadata (`_meta`) over custom subclasses, legacy internals, manual introspection, or re-implemented behavior. Two coherent sub-patterns emerge: (a) `_meta` field-introspection API usage, and (b) preference for built-in model fields over custom code and framework-duplicating tests.

text: Do not hardcode bubbling for component/controller custom events: default them to non-bubbling (`bubbles: false`) and expose bubbling as an opt-in compatibility parameter (e.g. Stimulus `params.bubbles`) that shared dispatch helpers forward as `{ bubbles }`. When binding a Stimulus action to a bubbling event, add the `:self` action option (e.g. `event->controller#method:self`) if only events dispatched directly on the bound element should trigger the action.
reason: Keeps controller event handling scoped by default, avoids unexpected ancestor/descendant-controller interactions, and lets consumers opt into bubbling for delegation without changing default behavior. The `:self` action option prevents same-named events bubbling from descendant elements from unintentionally firing the action and duplicating handler execution.
common_pattern: Event dispatch semantics for synthetic and controller custom events — explicitly controlling bubbling behavior and delivery scope so delegated/ancestor listeners behave predictably.

text: For custom events from Stimulus controllers, make cancellation semantics explicit: dispatch events as cancelable when consumers may cancel them, capture the returned event, and skip DOM mutations or side effects when `event.defaultPrevented` is true. Check `event.defaultPrevented` rather than relying on `dispatchEvent`'s boolean return value. Set `cancelable: false` explicitly only for purely notification events whose consumers are not expected to call `preventDefault`; dispatches with `cancelable: false` otherwise make `preventDefault` throw.
reason: Honors `preventDefault` semantics, lets consumers reliably cancel controller behavior, keeps controller code compatible with Stimulus's `this.dispatch()`, and avoids runtime errors on non-cancelable events. The `cancelable: false` exception is valid only for notification events.
scope: client-side Stimulus controllers and custom event dispatch
common_pattern: Designing, centralizing, and testing cancelable custom-event behavior in Stimulus controllers: dispatch before side effects, honor event.defaultPrevented, centralize the dispatch/filter logic, and verify cancellation in tests.

text: Default values must not override user-supplied settings: in a create/save view, apply a default only when the user did not explicitly supply that value during creation (e.g. Wagtail's `set_default_privacy_setting` in `wagtail/admin/views/pages/create.py` must not replace an explicit `PageViewRestriction` supplied via the create form). Add tests covering the user-supplied case to confirm the default does not override it.
reason: Silent defaults override explicit user intent, causing data loss and surprising, often security/privacy-relevant behavior regressions; reapplying defaults on creation that already carries user input mixes create-only behavior into edit flows.
common_pattern: Correct handling of default values: defaults must not silently override explicit user-provided values, and default-application logic must be kept consistent (single-sourced) across the flows where the object is created, edited, or loaded.

text: Keep default-application logic for an object consistent across create, edit/publish, and load flows by reusing a shared source of truth (shared helper, controller static values, etc.) rather than duplicating the default or hardcoding divergent magic numbers; the create view should expose the option to override any configurable attribute so create-time and edit-time behavior do not diverge.
reason: Duplicating default logic in one flow (or a single view) makes behavior depend on which path the user takes and forces awkward draft-then-edit workflows because the applied default is hidden.
common_pattern: Correct handling of default values: defaults must not silently override explicit user-provided values, and default-application logic must be kept consistent (single-sourced) across the flows where the object is created, edited, or loaded.

text: Implement tooltips in Wagtail admin templates with the `w-tooltip` Stimulus controller: activate it via a static `data-controller="w-tooltip"` and pass configuration through namespaced Stimulus value attributes (e.g. `data-w-tooltip-content-value`, `data-w-tooltip-offset-value`, `data-w-tooltip-placement-value`). Omit any value attribute whose desired value matches the component default (e.g. omit `data-w-tooltip-placement-value` for `bottom` placement); only specify explicit configuration when a non-default value is actually needed. Do not use legacy `data-tippy-*` attributes (e.g. `data-tippy-content`, `data-tippy-offset`) and never place tooltip content or values in `data-controller`. Assert against `data-w-tooltip-content-value` in tests for rendered tooltip markup.
reason: Merges the `w-tooltip` Stimulus controller migration guidance with the convention to avoid redundant default configuration markup. Covers activation, namespaced value attributes, default-value omission, legacy `data-tippy-*` avoidance, prohibition on values in `data-controller`, and test assertion expectations.
common_pattern: How tooltips should be implemented in Wagtail templates — standardized on the `w-tooltip` Stimulus controller with `data-w-tooltip-*-value` attributes, replacing legacy `data-tippy-*` attributes and avoiding redundant/default configuration.

text: For context dictionaries, document guaranteed keys before the optional section and access them with direct indexing; document optional keys under `may also contain:` in the form `'key' = description` and access them with `.get()`.
reason: Context-dictionary API contract convention: guaranteed keys fail loudly if missing, optional keys are safely guarded, and docstrings match the actual implementation.
common_pattern: Maintaining a consistent contract for context dictionaries: distinguish guaranteed keys from optional keys, and reflect that distinction in both access patterns and documentation.

text: In Wagtail listing views, expose dedicated `register_{entity}_listing_more_buttons` hooks for 'more' dropdown buttons instead of reusing `register_{entity}_listing_buttons`; follow the `register_{entity}_listing_{context}_buttons` naming convention, add matching `construct_*` hooks, call construct hooks with `more_buttons`, and mirror the hook family between page and snippet listings.
reason: Reusing the top-level hook can break existing consumers that return `ButtonWithDropdownFromHook`, which is invalid inside dropdowns; a parallel hook family preserves backward compatibility and keeps page/snippet listing APIs consistent.
scope: Wagtail admin listing views and hooks
common_pattern: Wagtail admin listing views require separate, context-appropriate APIs for top-level listing buttons versus 'more' dropdown buttons: dedicated hooks, matching button classes, page/snippet parity, and documented contracts.

text: Buttons returned for listing dropdowns must be dropdown-compatible (`MenuItem`/`Button`), while top-level listing buttons must be top-level (`ListingButton`/`ButtonWithDropdown`); use generic `Button` for non-page-specific bulk actions and do not bake context-specific default CSS class names into shared/base listing button classes.
reason: The rendering context determines the valid button class; using incompatible types or baked-in default classes causes broken dropdown rendering, misrepresents action scope, and forces defensive normalization.
scope: Wagtail listing buttons and listing view hooks
common_pattern: Wagtail admin listing views require separate, context-appropriate APIs for top-level listing buttons versus 'more' dropdown buttons: dedicated hooks, matching button classes, page/snippet parity, and documented contracts.

text: Use Wagtail's log registry and base/generic log models instead of hardcoding concrete log entry models: resolve the log model via `log_registry.get_log_model_for_model(model)` (not `ModelLogEntry` directly), and derive user-facing log labels/messages from the base/generic model's metadata (e.g. base `Page` verbose name) rather than the concrete subclass, especially when the report UI already shows the concrete type.
reason: Wagtail supports custom log entry models; hardcoding a concrete model misses entries logged elsewhere and can leak internal subclass naming into user-facing text or duplicate type information already shown in a dedicated column.
scope: Wagtail audit log usage: model resolution and user-facing log message wording
common_pattern: Use Wagtail's audit-log infrastructure abstraction (log registry, base/generic log models, standard audit log facility) rather than hardcoding concrete log entry models or adding ad-hoc per-model audit fields.

text: In Wagtail admin report templates under `wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/reports/`, keep rendering generic over log-entry records: do not unpack model instances or branch on instance-specific properties/object types. If different log-entry types need distinct display, expose a single overridable extension point on the shared base record (e.g. a method returning a template component, or a property such as `display_label` defaulting to the existing behavior) and call that from the template.
reason: Report templates were deliberately made uniform by removing Page-specific special-casing; reintroducing instance digging or template-level type branching recreates brittle coupling. A base-record extension point keeps templates generic, testable, and scalable to future log-entry types.
common_pattern: Keep Wagtail admin report templates object-type-agnostic over log-entry records, and move any per-type display divergence into an overridable extension point on the shared base record rather than template conditionals.

text: Prefer explicit, component-supported contracts over inference: use structural type guards (e.g., `Array.isArray(prop)`) instead of inspecting string values or prefixes; derive conditional UI from an explicit structural/state prop rather than inferring from the presence/absence of another prop; expose and query opt-in values (e.g., in `BASE_ATTRS`) instead of inferring intent from DOM structure; and use existing third-party component props/configuration instead of creating custom wrappers.
reason: Value/prefix heuristics, prop-presence inference, DOM-structure inference, and custom wrappers are fragile, refactor-unsafe, and may silently diverge from the intended contract. Explicit structural/state/opt-in APIs and existing component-supported props match the documented contract and reduce maintenance burden.
common_pattern: Do not infer a prop's type, shape, or behavior from its value or the presence/absence of another prop; instead encode the distinction explicitly via structural type guards or dedicated props/types. All generalizations reject 'value-sniffing' heuristics (startsWith, presence checks) in favor of explicit contracts.

text: When multiple forms, models, or field subclasses need the same validation for a common field type, define the validation once on the shared form field/widget/base form or common field base class (e.g. BaseField.check(model)) and have callers delegate to it. Do not duplicate the logic with per-form clean_<field> overrides or per-subclass reimplementations.
reason: A duplicated validation only fixes the single form or subclass where it lives; centralizing it ensures the constraint is enforced everywhere the field is used and avoids drift between copies.
scope: Shared field validation across forms, models, and field subclasses; project-specific examples include common tag fields and wagtailsearch BaseField/check().
common_pattern: Validation that applies to multiple uses/subclasses/forms of the same field type should be centralized on the common field/form base class or shared widget, rather than duplicated per subclass or per-form.

text: Put model validation logic in the dedicated Django validation hooks instead of overriding clean() generically: single-field validation goes in clean_<field_name>(), cross-field validation goes in clean(), and uniqueness checks that exceed simple DB constraints go in validate_unique().
