reason: These hooks are called by full_clean() for their specific purpose, so using them integrates with Django's validation flow, receives the right parameters (e.g. exclude for validate_unique), and avoids reimplementing framework logic in clean().
common_pattern: Django model validation: which built-in hook to use for validation logic, and how/when validation must be invoked explicitly since full_clean() is not automatic outside of forms.

text: Since Django only runs full_clean() automatically for forms, invoke validation explicitly for programmatic model use: call full_clean() in save() when instances are created directly, call full_clean() directly on model instances in validation tests (rather than routing through a ModelForm), and do NOT rely on model validation during data migrations (avoid full_clean()/validation there and document that migration-time customization bypasses validation).
reason: Direct model creation and migrations do not go through Django's form validation, so validation silently does not run; calling full_clean() explicitly in save()/tests keeps validation consistent, while migrations should not call it because ValidationError is unhandled in that flow.
common_pattern: Django model validation: which built-in hook to use for validation logic, and how/when validation must be invoked explicitly since full_clean() is not automatic outside of forms.

text: In `wagtailsearch`, preserve existing default indexing behavior unless the user explicitly opts in: keep documented legacy configurations working until a formal deprecation cycle, and make new or costly indexing modes opt-in via explicit per-field options such as `SearchField(..., type='attachment')`. For the Elasticsearch backend this means retaining defaults like `FileField` mapping to `'string'` and indexing filenames only. Values sent to the backend must be JSON-serializable primitives; convert objects such as `FieldFile` to a filename string before indexing. When removing deprecated attributes, migrate all backend code paths consistently.
reason: Search indexing changes must preserve backward compatibility and documented defaults, avoid surprise cost/timeouts from expensive modes, and prevent inconsistent behavior or `SerializationError` across backend paths.
common_pattern: Backward-compatible evolution of search-field indexing behavior: preserve existing defaults, make new behavior opt-in, maintain legacy support until formal deprecation, and migrate all code paths consistently.

text: Do not add field-type-specific options (e.g., `search_index`) to field types that do not support them (e.g., `RichTextField`); keep such options scoped to the field type they belong to, such as StreamField. For other fields, search indexing is controlled by including or excluding the field in `search_fields`.
reason: Options like `search_index` are StreamField-specific concepts; adding them to unrelated field types creates unnecessary API surface and migration noise.
common_pattern: Wagtailsearch field/indexing API design: preserve existing default indexing behavior, make specialized (and costly) indexing modes explicit opt-in via a scoped per-field option, and don't leak field-type-specific options into unrelated field types.

text: When registering or configuring Draftail features in Wagtail, keep feature-specific options declarative in the feature's entity inner options in `wagtail_hooks.py` (e.g. `chooserUrls`, `allowlist.href`) rather than adding hard-coded per-entity-type branches (e.g. `type === 'LINK'`) or merging feature defaults into shared client-side code (`Draftail` base `get_options()` / `client/src/components/Draftail`); shared editor code should stay feature-agnostic and generic. At the same registration sites, use the shared Draft.js type constants (`BLOCK_TYPES.*`, `INLINE_STYLES.*`, `ENTITY_TYPES.*`) wherever a Draft.js type string is needed, rather than mixing constants with raw string literals.
reason: Python remains the single source of truth for Draftail feature configuration; JS-side special cases duplicate logic and drift from Python definitions, while raw Draft.js type strings cause typos and obscure handler/feature mapping.
scope: Wagtail Draftail feature configuration / `client/src/components/Draftail` and feature registration sites
common_pattern: Establishing a single, declarative source of truth for Draftail editor configuration and feature wiring, rather than special-casing entities in shared client-side JavaScript. A secondary pattern concerns consistency of type identifiers and client-side wiring. The cluster is topically bound (Wagtail Draftail) but splits into a dominant sub-pattern (declarative Python feature config over JS special-casing) plus loosely related sub-patterns (shared type constants, prop-name correctness, doc accuracy).

text: Wagtail rich text editor/field APIs must be editor-agnostic. Expose customization through a shared, backend-neutral `editor_config` parameter/attribute (and/or a standard Django form widget instance) that accepts the complete editor configuration object, rather than editor-specific options such as `hallo_config`. Nest editor-specific plugin settings under a `plugins` mapping (e.g. `{'plugins': {'halloheadings': {...}, 'halloformat': {...}}}`), not as top-level plugin names or a `plugin`/`plugins`-named API. Expose context-specific rich text behavior as a per-field/per-editor option rather than a global `WAGTAILADMIN_*` setting, and name resolution functions after what they return (e.g. `get_rich_text_editor_widget`, not `get_rich_text_editor`) to leave room for future setting extensions. Keep rich-text field-level `features` configuration limited to a list of feature identifiers describing the allowed data format (e.g. allowed HTML elements); do not add per-feature UI/editor options (toolbar configuration, nested-list depth, etc.) to model fields — editor behaviour belongs to the editor widget, and per-field options risk database-migration breakage and misuse.
reason: Keeps pluggable rich text editors interchangeable, prevents a specific editor's API from leaking into callers' configuration code, preserves a stable/extensible public API, and keeps the features system identifier-only and data-format focused.
scope: Wagtail rich text fields/widgets/blocks and editor configuration APIs (e.g. `wagtail/wagtailcore/fields.py`, `wagtail/wagtailadmin/rich_text.py`)
common_pattern: Editor customization APIs should use a generic, editor-agnostic configuration surface rather than plugin-specific or vendor-specific naming and shape.

text: In Wagtail rich text, store content using the existing editor's output tags (`<b>`/`<i>` for hallo.js) as the canonical storage format to avoid migrating legacy database content; perform semantic conversion to `<strong>`/`<em>` only at render time or in editor widgets.
reason: Most legacy rich-text data already uses hallo.js's `<b>`/`<i>`; aligning storage avoids unnecessary migration, while separating rendering allows future semantic improvements without changing stored data.
common_pattern: Separate rich-text storage format from rendering format: store using the legacy editor's tags (e.g., `<b>`/`<i>` for hallo.js) to avoid migrating existing data, and convert to semantic tags (e.g., `<strong>`/`<em>`) at render time or in editor widgets.

text: When calling String.prototype.replace, pass the search pattern (string or regex) as the first argument and the replacement as the second; never pass the source string as an argument.
reason: replace operates on the receiver string; passing the source string as the first argument replaces the wrong pattern and misuses the API, leading to incorrect results.
common_pattern: Correct usage and sequencing of String.prototype.replace to avoid silent string corruption

text: Do not introduce a new audit-log action identifier for a derived, scheduled, or wrapper variant of an operation that already has its own log action (e.g. no `wagtail.schedule.revert` when reverts are already logged as `wagtail.revert`); reuse the existing action identifier.
reason: Duplicating action identifiers fragments the audit log and makes it harder to query all occurrences of an operation under a single action; it also keeps the taxonomy simpler and less ambiguous.
common_pattern: Design conventions for Wagtail's audit-log action taxonomy and logging behavior: how actions are named (hierarchical dotted identifiers reflecting the true operation), when to emit separate log entries, when to reuse existing action identifiers rather than spawn parallel variants, and keeping the action reference documentation in sync.

text: Express checkbox conditions in `RulesController` rule definitions with explicit arrays: `[]` requires the checkbox to be unchecked (field absent from FormData) and `['on']` (or the checkbox's actual `value` attribute, e.g. `['']` for `value=""`) requires it to be checked.
reason: Using explicit array values instead of a magic empty-string default makes rule intent readable and correctly supports checkboxes with custom or empty `value` attributes.
common_pattern: RulesController / Stimulus `data-rule` matching should operate on the explicit values present in `FormData`, treating rule values as plain strings with no hidden special-casing of falsy or absent values; checkbox states are expressed explicitly as `[]` (unchecked) vs `['on']`/the checkbox `value` (checked).

text: When a translation-aware queryset method such as `TranslatableQuerySetMixin.localized()` changes result semantics (for example by including draft translations), do not infer that behavior from unrelated queryset filters like `live=True`; expose it as an explicit parameter with a conservative default.
reason: Translations are conceptually not pages, so silently replacing live translations with drafts based on an unrelated filter would surprise callers. An explicit, opt-in option keeps the API predictable.
common_pattern: Behavior of translatable/localized querysets in Wagtail should be explicit and defensively scoped: result-altering options must be opt-in parameters rather than inferred from unrelated filters, and ordering/annotation logic must be guarded against empty inputs. (Generalization 2 is a related but distinct queryset-cleanup concern from a different PR.)

text: Use CountController’s built-in conditional class states (`active`, `max`, `over`) and its label/count-output features for selection-count UI instead of ad-hoc class additions, custom rendering, or custom class-toggling JavaScript. For count-threshold behavior, configure CountController’s `min`/`offset` settings (e.g., `min = offset + 1` to activate only after at least one item beyond the initial offset), and ensure the class/state is removed when the count drops back to or below the threshold so stale classes or UI state do not persist.
reason: Reusing CountController keeps state handling consistent, reusable, and covered by existing unit tests, and using `min`/`offset` for thresholds avoids duplicated custom logic and stale `active`/`max`/`over` states when counts decrease.
common_pattern: Count-threshold state/class toggling in CountController should be driven by the controller’s threshold configuration and cleaned up in both directions.

text: In generic or reusable code operating on an unknown model (generic views, mixins, permission policies, library-level helpers), query via `self.model._default_manager` — or `_base_manager` when the base manager implementation is specifically required — instead of assuming the model defines a manager named `objects`.
reason: `objects` is only a naming convention and may be renamed, overridden, or absent, whereas `_default_manager` is guaranteed to resolve to the model's canonical default manager (respecting `Meta.default_manager_name`), making reusable code robust across models.
common_pattern: Use a Django model's Manager API — especially `_default_manager` in generic code — rather than assuming an `objects` manager or bypassing the manager with custom querysets or private instance methods.

text: Route collection- and manager-level operations through the model's Manager: delegate to the default manager API (e.g. `objects.get_or_create()`) instead of constructing custom querysets, prefer semantically named manager lookup helpers over generic `get(**kwargs)` filters, and place collection-level management operations on the Manager class rather than as private instance methods on the model.
reason: Keeps query logic centralized and semantically meaningful, avoids duplicating or subtly differing lookup logic at call sites, preserves default manager behavior, and keeps model instances focused on instance state/behavior.
common_pattern: Use a Django model's Manager API — especially `_default_manager` in generic code — rather than assuming an `objects` manager or bypassing the manager with custom querysets or private instance methods.

text: When a PR changes tree traversal or ordering behavior, include the required model-level ordering configuration (e.g. `node_order_by`) in the same PR; defer only data migration/backfill tooling to a follow-up.
reason: Prevents merging behavior that regresses ordering guarantees and avoids depending on a separate follow-up change for correctness.
common_pattern: Ordering behavior of django-treebeard tree models: define ordering declaratively via `node_order_by` at the model level rather than per-query `.order_by()`, preserve the established ordering contract when broadening traversal scope, and keep ordering-dependent tests in sync.

text: In Wagtail/django-treebeard tree code, use the existing tree queryset/model APIs for ancestry, descendants, children, and parent checks — e.g. `get_children()`, `get_ancestors()`, `descendant_of()`, `ancestor_of()`, `TreeQuerySet` helpers, or `path` when only parent existence is needed — instead of manually constructing path-prefix queries, looping over `get_parent()`, or adding caller-side `numchild`/leaf optimizations. Keep tree query optimizations centralized in the tree method that owns the query.
reason: Centralizes path/steplen arithmetic and ancestor/descendant semantics, avoids N+1 queries and duplicated query logic, and keeps callers simple and refactor-safe.
scope: Wagtail page/treebeard tree query and traversal code
common_pattern: Tree/hierarchical model queries in Wagtail and django-treebeard should use the existing tree queryset/model APIs and materialized-path semantics instead of reimplementing path-prefix logic, issuing per-node parent/ancestor queries, or adding caller-side tree optimizations.

text: Use Stimulus declarative keyboard actions: bind shortcuts with `data-action` key descriptors (e.g., `keyup.up->w-sortable#up:prevent`, `keydown.left->tabs#method`) and drive behavior from component-set `data-*-action-value`/`data-*-target` attributes (e.g., `data-w-kbd-action-value={slim ? 'click' : 'focus'}`, `data-w-kbd-target='element'`). Keep generic keyboard controllers generic by avoiding hardcoded key mappings or component-specific state checks, implement the referenced controller methods, and prefer a single event type (e.g., `keyup`) with `:prevent` when default browser behavior must be suppressed. For the `w-kbd` controller, conditionally bind a shortcut to a specific element with `data-w-kbd-target={shouldBeActive ? 'element' : undefined}` instead of `data-w-kbd-scope-value="global"`; omit the target attribute entirely when the shortcut should not be active (e.g., mobile view).
reason: Merges the general Stimulus declarative keyboard-binding convention with the w-kbd-specific conditional target/scope guidance, since the latter is a concrete instance of component-state-driven target toggling already described in the broader rule.
common_pattern: Declarative Stimulus keyboard interactions: bind keyboard shortcuts in markup with Stimulus action descriptors and data attributes, keep controllers generic, and implement the referenced controller behavior instead of hardcoding key/state logic in JavaScript.

text: Declare keyboard shortcuts via the standard `aria-keyshortcuts` attribute on the interactive element (e.g., the `<button>`) that triggers the shortcut, and treat it as the single source of truth — do not also duplicate the shortcut on the controller's private `data-w-kbd-key-value` attribute. If a controller supports both, fall back to reading `aria-keyshortcuts` when no explicit key value is configured.
reason: Addresses the distinct concern of shortcut declaration/accessibility and avoiding duplicated state; it is not subsumed by the general Stimulus binding convention.
common_pattern: Keyboard-shortcut declarations in this project's controller/component system should expose shortcuts through the standard ARIA attribute `aria-keyshortcuts` on the interactive element that triggers them (as the single source of truth), with conditional element targeting instead of global scoping, and consistent modifier conventions to avoid collisions.

text: Expose computed values through dedicated accessors instead of exposing internal collections for callers to inspect. For zero-argument methods that compute or return a value and are conceptually property access (e.g., methods named with a `get` prefix in JavaScript/TypeScript), declare them as class getters (`get <name>()`) and access them as properties (`this.name`) rather than invoking them as methods (`this.get<Name>()`). Prefer noun-named properties for cached attribute-like values and focused accessor methods when appropriate, rather than `get_*()` getter-style methods.
reason: Centralizes computation, preserves encapsulation, avoids leaking internal representation, makes computed values easier to reuse across call sites, expresses property-access semantics, and aligns with JavaScript/TypeScript class conventions.
common_pattern: Convergence: both generalizations express the same principle — argument-less value-returning methods with `get` naming should be declared as class getters and accessed as properties. One frames it globally, the other scopes it to `client/src/controllers/*.ts`; the scoped version is an entity-specific instance of the broader rule.

text: Keep form-related logic inside the form class: declare static fields as class attributes, configure dynamic fields in `__init__`, and place validation/permission-aware behavior in the form rather than in views or templates. When a form needs request-scoped context (the current user, a permission-filtered queryset), pass it explicitly through the constructor—at every construction site, for both bound and unbound cases—instead of having the form inspect `self.request.user` or having the view mutate the form after construction. Reuse existing form/formsets abstractions and extract complex `__init__` logic into named methods.
reason: Mutating a form from a view (e.g. setting `disabled`) only affects rendered HTML and is invisible to the form's clean/validation logic, silently breaking behavior; centralizing field config and user-scoped logic in the form keeps views simpler, avoids duplication, and makes permission-aware forms testable without hidden request state.
common_pattern: Django form logic placement: field configuration, validation, and request-scoped behavior belong in the form class (class attributes or __init__), with any required request-scoped context (user, permission-filtered querysets) passed explicitly through the constructor — rather than being manipulated from views, templates, or global/request state. A secondary sub-pattern concerns documenting non-obvious framework options.

text: In Django view handlers, use `request.method` to detect the HTTP method (e.g., `request.method == 'POST'`) rather than checking the truthiness of `request.POST`. Read request parameters from the collection that matches how the client sends them: `request.POST` for body-submitted values (e.g., ping/update payloads) and `request.GET` for query-string parameters. Keep bound and unbound form instantiations separate by branching explicitly on the request method (e.g., `if self.request.method == 'POST': form = Form(self.request.POST) else: form = Form()`); do not merge them with the `request.POST or None` idiom, which treats an empty POST payload as no submission and changes form-binding semantics.
reason: `request.POST` can be empty for a valid POST request (e.g., a confirmation form with no fields), so truthiness checks skip method-specific logic. `request.GET` only exposes query-string parameters; reading body-submitted data from it returns `None` and breaks revision/editing-session tracking. Separating bound (validating submitted data) from unbound (rendering initial UI) forms preserves distinct semantics, avoids losing validation errors, and makes view code easier to follow.
common_pattern: Django form/class-based-view lifecycle conventions: how forms are bound, validated, saved, and how validated data is reused — keeping form state semantics explicit and free of side effects outside the appropriate lifecycle hooks.

text: When filtering a queryset by the existence of related rows, prefer a boolean existence check (e.g. `Exists(OuterRef(...))` or an `__isnull` style check) over a `Subquery`/`values_list` that returns identifiers to be matched, because only presence matters and the boolean check expresses intent directly while avoiding unnecessary ID materialization/casting. When also aggregating over reverse relations (SUM/COUNT), do not use a direct relation filter such as `related__isnull=False`: that introduces a JOIN which duplicates parent rows and inflates aggregates even when `.distinct()` is present, since SQL applies the aggregate before DISTINCT. Instead, isolate the aggregate using `Exists` (preferred) or a subquery such as `pk__in=OtherModel.objects.values_list('fk_id', flat=True)`, and add regression tests with multiple related rows to assert that aggregates are not multiplied by the join.
reason: Boolean existence checks correctly express yes/no conditions and avoid unnecessary ID work; direct relation filters introduce joins that multiply rows and corrupt reverse-relation aggregates, and DISTINCT cannot fix this because aggregation happens first.
scope: Django ORM related-row existence filters and reverse-relation aggregation
common_pattern: Django ORM subquery/queryset patterns: constrain subquery-specific APIs explicitly, test flag interactions with queryset layering, and prefer boolean existence checks when only presence matters.

text: When resolving a Wagtail `Site` from a request, URL, or hostname, always reuse the existing framework resolution utilities instead of reimplementing URL parsing, site lookup, or direct `Page`/`Site` queries: use `Site.find_for_request` (or provide resolution methods that do not require a `request` object — name them `find_for_request` for consistency across Page/Site models) for request/URL resolution, and use the shared `get_site_for_hostname()` helper for hostname/optional-port resolution rather than manually parsing the host and calling `Site.objects.get()`/`filter(hostname=...)`. Because `get_site_for_hostname()` falls back to the default site when no hostname matches, when resolving a site for a specific URL or `?site=` value, validate that the returned site's hostname matches the requested one instead of blindly accepting the default-site fallback.
reason: Reuses tested framework logic and centralizes hostname/port semantics across the codebase, avoiding duplicated edge-case handling copied between views; keeps method naming consistent and prevents request-dependency in non-request contexts such as management commands; and prevents operations keyed to a URL from silently running against the default site when the URL's hostname belongs elsewhere or is unknown.
scope: Wagtail site lookup code (e.g. API viewsets resolving a `site` parameter, request/URL site resolution, hostname resolution)
common_pattern: Wagtail `Site` resolution from a hostname: prefer the shared helper, validate that the resolved site actually matches the requested hostname (rather than silently accepting the default-site fallback), and cache site lookups under a single host+port key.

text: Make page URL-generation and public page-URL APIs site-aware: let callers pass an explicit `Site` (for example a `site` kwarg on methods like `Page.get_url_parts`, or `request`/`current_site` on `get_url`/`get_full_url`) instead of inferring the site from an `HttpRequest` or fabricating a dummy request. This bypasses `Site.find_for_request`, avoids wrong-site resolution for pages on non-default sites, preserves existing method overrides rather than adding parallel methods, and exposes URLs using the existing site/path abstraction rather than the internal `url_path`.
reason: A dummy request always resolves to the same (default) domain, so redirects and URLs for pages on other sites are generated incorrectly. Passing the known site also lets callers skip redundant `Site.find_for_request` logic, avoids wrong-site resolution, and avoids leaking internal storage fields.
common_pattern: Wagtail page URL generation must be site-aware and correct for non-default sites: callers that know the target should pass an explicit `Site` (e.g. a `site` kwarg) instead of deriving the site from a request or fabricating a dummy request, and the URL output format (absolute domain-qualified vs path-only) must match what the consuming framework expects (Django sitemaps prepend the domain; API fields/serializers want absolute links via a shared helper).

text: When appending a new button to `header_more_buttons` in a view that inherits from a superclass, set its `priority` relative to the inherited buttons' priorities (lower values sort earlier). For example, to place a new button after an inherited button with `priority=80`, use a priority greater than 80; `priority=50` would place it first. In the redirects index view, choose the new button's priority relative to the inherited `Download XSLX` button, which has priority 80.
reason: Menu order is determined by button priorities, so ignoring inherited priorities causes unintended placement or reordering of existing admin actions.
common_pattern: Overriding Wagtail admin views' inherited `header_more_buttons` action lists: preserving inherited actions and controlling ordering via `priority`.

text: In Wagtail admin generic model views, `get_*_url` helpers (e.g. `get_add_url`, `get_edit_url`, `get_inspect_url`) must return `None` when the target view is disabled or the user lacks the required permission, so callers can safely chain fallbacks (e.g. `if edit_url := self.get_edit_url(instance): return edit_url; return self.get_inspect_url(instance)`). Preserve a `None` returned by `super()` rather than passing it to URL-modifying helpers (like query-string utilities) — only transform the URL when the parent URL exists. Raise `ImproperlyConfigured` only when the corresponding `*_url_name` configuration is missing and there is no meaningful fallback. When relying on this `None` return (e.g. for a fallback chain or a disabled view), add or update a test using a viewset where the relevant view is not enabled, and include a comment explaining the disabled-view context so the test's intent is clear.
reason: Returning `None` is the established contract for permission-/view-gated helpers and lets callers chain fallbacks without guarding each call; wrapping `None` in URL utilities can break or imply a nonexistent URL. Raising is reserved for genuine misconfiguration (missing `*_url_name` with no fallback), keeping behavior consistent across helpers. Tests using a disabled view verify the `None` return and document the edge case.
scope: Wagtail admin generic model views and their tests
common_pattern: Behavior contract for Wagtail admin generic-view URL helper methods (`get_add_url`, `get_edit_url`, `get_inspect_url`, and similar `get_*_url` helpers) when the underlying view or permission is unavailable — whether to return `None` (enabling safe fallback chaining) or raise a configuration error, plus how those None paths should be tested.

text: In modeladmin URL helpers, pass the owning `ModelAdmin` class/instance into the helper (e.g. `AdminURLHelper`) so URL behavior is derived from it — do not mutate helper instance state or add configuration arguments like `base_url_path` to change behavior.
reason: Instance mutation introduces additional breakage vectors, while passing the owning object gives the helper the context needed for more nuanced behavior and future extension.
scope: wagtail/contrib/modeladmin/helpers/url.py (modeladmin URL helper classes such as `AdminURLHelper`)
common_pattern: Keeping configuration and behavior decoupled from shared/reusable objects — admin-specific concerns should not leak into core model code, and reusable helpers should receive the owning context rather than be re-instantiated or mutated to change behavior.

text: Custom block types whose value is rendered by a wrapped child block (e.g. ImageBlock-style StructBlock subclasses) must implement `render_basic` by delegating to the child block's `render_basic` (e.g. `self.child_blocks["image"].render_basic(value)`) instead of relying on the base `StructBlock` rendering.
reason: Ensures correct rendering in contexts that call `render_basic` (StreamField rendering, previews, comparison) and avoids errors when the block value is not a StructBlock dict.
common_pattern: Wagtail block-rendering consistency: when subclassing blocks, delegate rendering to the base implementation or to the wrapped child block, rather than relying on defaults or duplicating overrides across subclasses.

text: When overriding `clean()` in a custom `StructBlock` (or block subclass), delegate to `super().clean(value)` or to the relevant child block's `clean()` after converting the value into the expected StructBlock value format, rather than reimplementing validation. The override must also respect the block's/child blocks' `required` setting (allowing `required=False` blocks to accept empty/None) and reuse the existing `ignore_required_constraints` mechanism (e.g. for deferred draft validation) instead of introducing parallel requirement-ignoring flags.
reason: Reuses inherited validation, child block cleaning, and standard error handling so custom blocks stay consistent with Wagtail's block contract and configuration instead of diverging from or breaking it.
common_pattern: Correctly and safely overriding Wagtail Block/StructBlock `clean()` validation — delegating to existing validation (`super().clean()`, child block `clean()`), respecting the existing `required`/`ignore_required_constraints` mechanisms, and safely extending the `clean()` signature — plus documenting the intended customization hooks.

text: When adding a new optional argument to `Block.clean()` and propagating it through `StructBlock.clean()`, ensure every child block implementation accepts the argument or only pass it when supported; unconditional propagation breaks basic blocks such as `FieldBlock` inside a `StructBlock` with a `TypeError`.
reason: Not all block types implement new keyword arguments, so unconditional polymorphic propagation breaks common existing block compositions.
common_pattern: Correctly and safely overriding Wagtail Block/StructBlock `clean()` validation — delegating to existing validation (`super().clean()`, child block `clean()`), respecting the existing `required`/`ignore_required_constraints` mechanisms, and safely extending the `clean()` signature — plus documenting the intended customization hooks.

text: Use the project's standard page chooser pattern for admin page selection: use `widgets.AdminPageChooser` with a `ModelChoiceField`, passing target page model classes via `page_models`, instead of custom `ModelChoiceField` subclasses, custom label-building, `RadioSelect` querysets, or manually resolving a `ContentType` for `content_type`. Resolve chooser target models to the most specific applicable `Page` class: `PageChooserPanel.target_models()` must return the target model for a `ForeignKey` pointing to a specific model even without a widget override, and lowest-common-ancestor logic should return a non-creatable intermediate `Page` subclass rather than falling back to base `Page`.
reason: Choosers are the standard, performant, and consistent way to select pages in Wagtail admin forms; using `page_models` uses the widget's supported API and avoids unnecessary `ContentType` lookups and custom label-building queries. Widget overrides are not generated for all `ForeignKey` fields, so relying only on widget overrides breaks existing behavior. Falling back to base `Page` lets users select invalid pages and defers errors to validation, while using the most specific common ancestor keeps chooser choices correctly scoped.
scope: Wagtail admin page-selection forms, `AdminPageChooser` widget usage, and `PageChooserPanel`/`AdminPageChooser` target-model resolution
common_pattern: Wagtail admin page-chooser conventions: use the standard AdminPageChooser widget, configure it with page_models, resolve target page types to the most specific applicable Page class, and improve tree UX using common path prefixes.

text: In block comparison implementations, route all diff rendering through the comparison class's `htmldiff()` method for every comparison state (added, deleted, changed, unchanged) rather than duplicating diff logic or calling `block.render_basic()` directly. Provide a base `htmldiff()` fallback that renders the block's current state so subclasses can override rendering only where needed. Keep the no-block-ID StreamField comparison fallback as a generic text/HTML diff—do not route it through a specialized comparison class such as `RichTextBlockComparison`—so rich-text-specific changes cannot unintentionally alter generic fallback behavior.
reason: Keeps comparison rendering centralized and extensible through `htmldiff()`, while preserving a stable generic fallback for non-rich-text StreamField comparisons.
scope: Block comparison implementations, including the StreamField comparison fallback in `wagtail/admin/compare.py`
common_pattern: Centralize block comparison rendering in the comparison class's `htmldiff()` method: avoid duplicating diff logic, avoid bypassing the comparison class with direct `render_basic()` calls, and provide a base-class `htmldiff()` fallback so subclasses only override where needed.

text: Treat model primary keys as opaque identifiers that may be integer or UUID. Do not cast PKs to `int`, validate chooser/widget IDs with `parseInt`, or use `typeof parseInt(...) === 'number'` (NaN is also a number) — only require the ID to be non-empty. Cast or assume integer PKs only for built-in models whose PK type is documented as integer (e.g. Wagtail's built-in `Document`). In Django/Wagtail URL routing, choose the path converter that matches the actual PK field type and the original URL/regex group (`UUIDField` -> `<uuid:...>`, integer PK -> `<int:...>`, `\d+` -> `<int:...>`, `\w+` -> `<slug:...>`) instead of falling back to the broad `<str:...>` converter, which greedily matches static segments like `add/` or `results/` and makes those routes unreachable. Do not default all non-UUID PKs to `int`, since that breaks string-based PKs; use an appropriate converter such as `<slug:...>` when the PK is genuinely string-based, rather than a plain `str` converter. Name such conversion attributes using Django's established terminology, e.g. `pk_path_converter`.
reason: Chooser widgets and custom models may use UUID primary keys or remote/non-numeric identifiers, so numeric validation and int-casting silently exclude valid data; built-in models like Document have guaranteed integer PKs, making int-casting acceptable there. In routing, a permissive `str` converter greedily shadows static routes, and mismatched converters break routing/reversal for non-integer PKs; type-specific converters preserve the original URL-matching semantics.
common_pattern: Correctly handling model primary keys in Django URL routing — (a) choosing an appropriate URL path converter rather than the greedily-matching default and (b) properly percent-encoding/decoding PKs when generating or consuming URLs. These are two related-but-distinct sub-patterns sharing the 'Django PK ↔ URL' theme.

text: When serving file-like content in Django (e.g. a `BytesIO` buffer or an open file), use `FileResponse` instead of `HttpResponse` and pass the open file object directly (e.g. `FileResponse(open(path, "rb"))`) without wrapping it in a `with` block — `FileResponse` streams the content and closes the file automatically after sending. Similarly, do not add redundant `seek(0)` or explicit `close()` calls on Django `File` objects: `File.open()` already seeks to the beginning, and lifecycle management (including closing) is handled by the framework. Only add explicit `seek`/`close` when there is demonstrated evidence they are required, since premature closing can raise 'file is not opened for reading' errors with custom storage backends or downstream consumers such as rendition generation.
reason: `FileResponse` streams content (lower memory overhead) and manages file headers and file closure correctly; wrapping the file in a context manager or pre-emptively closing it can close it at the wrong time and break the response. Likewise, Django's `File` semantics already reposition and close files; redundant operations cause unnecessary I/O and can regress storage-agnostic code where custom backends or shared file consumers do not expect early closure.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns advise relying on Django's built-in file/stream lifecycle semantics instead of manually compensating — use the appropriate response class for file-like content, and avoid redundant `seek(0)`/`close()` calls on Django `File` objects because Django already positions and closes them.

text: Distinguish genuinely absent values from deliberately blank ones: use `None` as the sentinel for 'not provided' and an empty string/collection only for values that are deliberately empty; never conflate the two via truthiness, a falsy default, or an empty-container fallback. Test absence with `is None` (or `hasattr(...) and getattr(...) is not None`), and when a fallback is needed return a meaningful default rather than an empty string. When blank and absent states produce different behavior, model them with an explicit flag (e.g. `decorative`) instead of overloading `''` versus `None`/undefined to distinguish output. For optional block/widget values that represent genuinely absent data (e.g. an optional `CharBlock`, or a widget's `value_from_datadict` input), preserve/default to `None` and do not pass `None` through value converters — reserve the empty string for string model fields where the field is non-nullable.
reason: Empty-string/collection values are semantically meaningful ('defined but blank'), so treating them as 'missing' silently changes behavior; an explicit `None` sentinel keeps the two states distinct. Where divergent output behavior is needed, an explicit flag is clearer than overloading `''` vs `None`. Optional block/widget inputs should preserve `None` for genuine absence and avoid passing `None` through converters.
common_pattern: Distinguishing 'absent/not provided' from 'defined but empty' — consistently use None (and `is None` checks) as the sentinel for absence, never conflate it with an empty string/empty collection via truthiness, defaults, or falsy fallbacks.

text: When a choice/chooser block needs to convert or coerce values (chooser lookups, non-string choice keys), reuse the appropriate existing field/block machinery — delegate to the wrapped chooser block's `to_python()`, or use Django's `TypedChoiceField` via a typed block wrapper (e.g. `TypedChoiceBlock`) — rather than reimplementing conversion logic or overriding `to_python` on a plain `ChoiceField`. Because form-field coercion (e.g. `TypedChoiceField(coerce=...)`) only applies during validation while JSON/StreamField serialization round-trips values as strings, choice blocks whose keys may be non-string Python types must normalize them in the block's `to_python` after deserialization — and the same normalization must be applied to multi-select blocks (e.g. `MultipleChoiceBlock`) for consistency.
reason: Reusing the underlying field/chooser conversion behavior avoids duplicated, brittle conversion logic and keeps validation/backward-compatibility consistent. Serialization stringifies non-string keys, so block-level normalization is required to restore the original key type, and applying it uniformly to single- and multi-select blocks avoids inconsistent behavior.
common_pattern: StreamField/block value conversion should reuse the built-in conversion and coercion machinery of the underlying field/chooser block (e.g. delegating to the wrapped chooser's `to_python`, or using `TypedChoiceField`/`TypedChoiceBlock`) instead of hand-rolling conversion logic — and where JSON/StreamField serialization strips type information, block-level `to_python` normalization must be added (consistently for single- and multi-select blocks).

text: When implementing or overriding block conversion methods (e.g. `bulk_to_python`, `to_python`) for StreamField/StructBlock, delegate to the child/top-level block conversion APIs and batch related lookups; do not duplicate conversion logic or call a batch parent method from inside a per-item branch. Bulk conversion must preserve input length and positional alignment, pass through `None` values, and, if mixed input types are supported, partition by type, bulk-convert each partition, and merge the results.
reason: The contract for block conversion overrides is to use canonical conversion/bulk APIs instead of ad-hoc reimplementation, while preserving expected bulk sequence semantics.
common_pattern: Block data conversion overrides should delegate to canonical conversion/bulk APIs rather than reimplementing them, and bulk conversion methods must preserve their input sequence contract: length, positional alignment, None pass-through, and type partitioning where mixed input is supported.

text: Keep block conversion hooks separated by input domain: `to_python()` accepts JSONish/serialized (database) values and returns normalized Pythonic values, while `normalize()` accepts only Pythonic block-native values and returns normalized Pythonic values. Handle string/JSON input (e.g. `page.body = "..."`) at the top-level boundary (`StreamField.to_python`), not inside per-block `normalize()`. In `normalize()`, canonicalize blank/falsy inputs to a single blank representation (the block's empty value instance or `None`) so downstream code (`clean()`, `get_prep_value()`, templates like `{% if block.value %}`) never sees empty wrapper objects such as `EmbedValue("")`; rely on this canonical value instead of adding sentinel comparisons in `clean()`. Keep the permissive empty-value handling in `to_python()`, which must still accept raw JSON/database values. If `normalize` would be functionally equivalent to `to_python` for a top-level block, alias one to the other rather than duplicating logic, and delegate to the block's dedicated value class (e.g. `StreamValue`) instead of re-implementing field parsing. Do not tighten `normalize()` to require permissive values while other entry points still supply them. When changing this behavior, add unit tests covering blank, non-blank, and already-wrapped values.
reason: The two methods operate on different input domains; collapsing them makes `normalize` a catch-all parser and causes logic divergence. Empty value wrappers often lack equality, so sentinel membership tests fail and `required=False` validation rejects valid blanks while templates treat blanks as truthy; centralizing blank handling in `normalize()` keeps validation logic focused and consistent.
scope: block-level conversion API across block types (wagtail/blocks)
common_pattern: The `normalize()`/`to_python()` conversion-hook contract for Wagtail block values: `normalize()` is responsible for canonicalizing block-native/Python values (including collapsing blanks to a canonical empty representation), while `to_python()` parses JSON/serialized/raw data at the field boundary — the two responsibilities must stay separate and neither should absorb the other.

text: When adding recursive serialization/prep behavior to a block-based field, implement it in the block-level method (e.g., `StreamBlock.get_prep_value`) and route the top-level field method through it, so nested/composite blocks cannot bypass the behavior by calling child block methods directly. Within that method, centralize shared normalization (e.g. missing ID assignment) after branching, and add comments explaining why the normalization is needed and why this location is appropriate.
reason: Ensures consistent behavior across nested blocks, avoids duplicated logic and unnecessary side effects, and clarifies intent for maintainers.
scope: global (e.g., applies to Wagtail StreamField/StreamBlock serialization)
common_pattern: Implementing recursive serialization/prep behavior in block-based fields by routing calls through block-level methods, centralizing shared normalization, and documenting non-obvious normalization.

text: In `Block` hierarchies, expose behavior that only some subclasses provide through an overridable hook (property, attribute, or method) on the base `Block` class with a sensible default, overriding it in subclasses that can supply a value. Do not have shared code/templates reference concrete implementation attributes such as `child.block.field`, and do not decide special-cased behavior by enumerating known subclasses. When introducing such a hook or refactor, apply it consistently to all sibling classes that share the behavior (e.g. `StructBlock`, `TypedTableBlock`).
reason: Not all blocks wrap a Django form field, and class lists are a perpetual source of bug reports because they miss some classes, especially user-created ones. A base-class hook gives a uniform interface and prevents sibling implementations from drifting.
common_pattern: Design against the base `Block` abstraction: expose standardized, overridable hooks on the base class (with sensible defaults) instead of reaching into concrete subclass attributes or enumerating known subclasses, and apply that pattern consistently across sibling block classes.

text: Base browser-compatibility decisions on the project's declared minimum supported browser baseline. Before adopting a newer JS/TS/platform API (e.g. `Promise.withResolvers`, `Object.hasOwn`, `Intl.Segmenter`, `URL.canParse`) or adding a legacy-browser polyfill, verify it is supported at that baseline — do not assume syntax transpilation also covers built-in runtime APIs. When the baseline supports it, use the API directly (no defensive polyfill-style conversion, and no deferral behind a future browser-support drop); when a still-supported browser may lack it, guard with feature detection and provide a fallback/polyfill. For legacy polyfills, match the polyfill to the API category and scope it to the browsers that need it: `@babel/polyfill` only covers ECMAScript language features and the JS stdlib, not host DOM APIs (e.g. `NodeList.prototype.forEach`), so DOM APIs require a dedicated DOM polyfill or a compatible fallback. Prefer a centralized/shared polyfill (e.g. `client/src/utils/polyfills.js`) over patching individual call sites, and conditionally invoke browser-specific polyfills behind a guard (e.g. `IS_IE11`) instead of running them unconditionally on every browser. Remove fallbacks/shims for browser versions the project no longer supports.
reason: Merged complementary rules 1787 and 1788: both govern browser compatibility around the declared support baseline, covering API adoption vs. guarded fallback/polyfill decisions and the specific legacy-polyfill management pattern.
scope: browser-facing / client-side JavaScript and TypeScript; frontend build configuration (`client/src/utils/polyfills.js`, admin bundle)
common_pattern: Browser-compatibility discipline: all decisions about using newer JS/TS/platform APIs and about polyfilling must be grounded in the project's declared minimum supported browser baseline, with polyfills matched to API category and scoped to the browsers that need them.

text: In widget initialization functions, accept configuration via an `options` parameter and forward the widget's configured options to shared factory constructors rather than relying on default arguments.
reason: Consistent naming improves API recognizability across widgets, and forwarding configured options prevents silent misconfiguration when non-default settings are used.
common_pattern: Conventions for handling configuration options in widget initialization functions: parameter naming and forwarding configured options to shared factory constructors.

text: In search backend implementations, route operations that write to or populate index tables through the existing write_connection property/write connection alias, and reserve read connection aliases for read-only queries. When a write connection is required, do not introduce a new read_connection accessor; if a read_connection accessor becomes unused after write operations move to write_connection, remove it instead of keeping dead or misleading connection API.
reason: Read replicas are intended for read-only queries, so using a read connection for writes can fail, target the wrong database, break read/write separation guarantees, or cause errors in replication setups. Additionally, avoiding unused or incorrect connection accessors keeps the connection API surface clear and prevents future code from accidentally using a read connection for write operations.
common_pattern: Routing index-modifying database operations in search backends to the write connection alias, reserving read connections for read-only queries.

text: For Django many-to-many relations, use the related manager methods to modify the relation (`set(iterable)` to replace/assign the whole collection, `add()` to add items) instead of manual assignment, and do not call `.save()` on the owner instance afterward; related manager methods already persist the relation and calling `.save()` causes redundant database writes and unnecessary save signals.
reason: Using related manager methods is concise and avoids redundant database writes and unnecessary save signals that occur when calling `.save()` after `add()`, `remove()`, `set()`, or `clear()`.
common_pattern: Django many-to-many relation handling through related managers, covering persistence semantics, save/PK ordering, and clone completeness.

text: Do not assign many-to-many fields on an unsaved Django model instance; defer M2M assignments until after the instance has been saved. When duplicating or cloning an instance, explicitly copy its many-to-many relations (e.g., `target.groups.set(original.groups.all())`) in addition to scalar fields.
reason: Django cannot assign a many-to-many relation before the owner has a primary key, so setting M2M fields on an unsaved instance fails. Cloning only scalar fields also loses group-based permissions or restrictions, producing incorrect access control on the copy.
common_pattern: Django many-to-many relation handling through related managers, covering persistence semantics, save/PK ordering, and clone completeness.

text: In Wagtail page serving, implement post-response modification or before/after response logic as a middleware-style serve-time hook (`on_serve_page`) rather than embedding response logic in `Page.serve` or duplicating `before_serve_page`/view-restriction queries. Build the serve chain from `serve_chain(page, request, args, kwargs)` calling `page.serve(...)`, wrap it with `reversed(hooks.get_hooks(...))` so the last-registered hook is outermost, and run `before_serve_page` hooks first, returning immediately if any returns an `HttpResponse`. Consolidate access-control/restriction lookups so they run once per request, preferably in a serve-time hook that executes before `serve` side effects and can still modify the response.
reason: Keeps feature logic out of core serving code, preserves extensibility, avoids duplicated queries on every page request, ensures hooks execute in expected middleware order, and prevents unauthorized requests from triggering `serve` side effects before access is checked.
common_pattern: Introduce a middleware-style page-serving hook when response must be modified after rendering or logic must run both before and after serving, with clear ordering between existing before_serve_page hooks and the wrapped serve chain.

text: For page request behavior that must apply across page types or survive `RoutablePageMixin` overrides, expose it as reusable `Page` methods and/or serve-time hooks rather than requiring subclasses to override `serve()` or relying only on standalone global hooks; keep `serve()` as unrestricted as a Django view function. HTTP-method-specific handling such as `OPTIONS` may belong in `Page.serve` rather than a global `before_serve_page` hook.
reason: Keeps serving behavior associated with the page class, avoids bypasses via overridden `serve()` paths, and preserves the documented ability to override `serve()` like a Django view.
common_pattern: Wagtail page request handling should centralize cross-cutting concerns (view/access restrictions, framework-level HTTP behavior) at the appropriate extension point, avoid duplicate database queries between `Page.serve()` and serve-time hooks, and keep the logic effective across page types such as `RoutablePageMixin`.

text: In `client/src/controllers/` event-handling methods, resolve configuration keys by destructuring from a merged object of the controller defaults, `event.params`, and `event.detail`, spreading sources in explicit precedence order: defaults first, then `event.params`, then `event.detail` last so runtime event detail overrides declarative params. Read the key from this merged object rather than only from a single source, and avoid error logging when a valid default already exists.
reason: Allows callers to override parameterized defaults per event invocation while keeping the remaining merged values available as data, and prevents silently ignoring valid overrides from params or event detail.
common_pattern: Resolving configuration keys in controller event handlers by merging multiple input sources (controller defaults, event.params, event.detail) with explicit precedence so more specific sources override broader ones, rather than reading from a single source.

text: When reading optional GET query parameters to drive behavior, use `request.GET.get('key')` and test the value rather than checking key presence (`'key' in request.GET`); treat empty strings such as `?q=` as absent. For boolean parameters, do not rely on Python truthiness or identity checks (`is True`); parse the raw string value explicitly, e.g. `request.GET.get('key', 'false') == 'true'`.
reason: GET parameters are strings; key presence is true even for `?q=`, which can incorrectly activate behavior, while relying on truthiness or identity breaks boolean parsing like `?flag=true`.
common_pattern: Idiomatic handling of HTTP GET query parameters: inspect the parameter's value (falsy/truthy) rather than key presence, and construct derived params/forms with a single falsy fallback instead of branching. A separate sub-pattern concerns boolean query params needing explicit string comparison. Two generalizations (2 and 3) directly contradict each other about whether the `querystring` tag should drop empty values.

text: Centralize redirect path normalization in the redirect creator class and its entry points: apply `Redirect.normalise_path()` consistently wherever redirects are created (batch creators, signal handlers, forms) instead of mutating `url_path` temporarily, and consume old/new paths already provided by signals rather than reconstructing them.
reason: Keeps normalization responsibility with the object-creating class so all callers (forms, signal handlers, batch creators) behave uniformly and avoids fragile temporary state changes to internal model fields or duplication in signal-handler helpers.
common_pattern: Wagtail redirect creation should centralize path handling: normalization lives with the object-creating class and entry points consume shared path data, distinct from cache-invalidation concerns, and with dedicated test coverage.

text: Do not reuse the cache-invalidation path method (`get_cached_paths`) for redirect generation; expose a dedicated `get_route_paths()` method that returns only the path-based URLs needed for redirects and can be overridden to customize redirect sources.
reason: `get_cached_paths()` is intended for cache invalidation and may include GET-parameter variants unsuitable for redirects; a separate method decouples redirect behavior from cache behavior and gives a clear extension point.
common_pattern: Wagtail redirect creation should centralize path handling: normalization lives with the object-creating class and entry points consume shared path data, distinct from cache-invalidation concerns, and with dedicated test coverage.

text: For StreamField blocks whose display label is derived from a child block, provide an option to specify which child field supplies the label instead of hardcoding the first child block.
reason: Hardcoding the first child reduces flexibility; different block structures may need a more meaningful or user-specific label field.
common_pattern: Handling display labels for Wagtail blocks/widgets: use the dedicated `label` API/name correctly, avoid semantic clashes with `description`, and make label derivation configurable for compound blocks.

text: When rendering admin edit links/buttons for model instances (including bulk lists), resolve the edit URL via AdminURLFinder keyed on object type/admin registration instead of hardcoding `wagtailadmin_pages:edit`, and reuse a single finder instance for the whole list. Only attach the edit affordance when the finder returns a valid admin edit URL; do not fall back to optional views (e.g., the snippet inspect view) that may not be enabled for a given model type, and omit the button/link otherwise.
reason: Pages, snippets, and other model types use different admin edit routes, so hardcoded page URLs are wrong for non-page objects; a shared finder avoids redundant lookup-table reconstruction per row. Additionally, some objects are not editable in the admin and optional views are opt-in, so fallback logic produces broken or misleading affordances.
common_pattern: In Wagtail admin code, edit URLs must be resolved dynamically by object type/admin registration (via AdminURLFinder) rather than hardcoded page routes, and edit affordances must be omitted when no valid admin edit URL exists.

text: In Wagtail admin chooser result items, do not wrap the item in an `<a>`/navigational link that triggers selection or navigation. Render the select action as a `<button>` (or non-interactive markup) instead, and only attach a URL to the title for single-selection choosers — in multiple-selection choosers, leave titles unlinked so a click cannot override the current checkbox selection or close the modal.
reason: Links imply navigation and expose browser-native link behaviours (right-click, middle-click, open-in-new-tab) that are inappropriate for a select action; in multi-select mode a linked item acts like a single-selection action that closes the modal and discards checkbox state.
scope: global / Wagtail admin chooser components and generic chooser column definitions (`wagtail/admin/views/generic/chooser.py`)
common_pattern: Wagtail admin chooser result items must not be rendered as navigational links; selection is a button-like action, and multi-select choosers must avoid any link-based interaction that could override checkbox state or close the modal.

text: When recursively traversing Django model relationships, resolve each nested field from the current related model's `_meta` (`child_field.related_model._meta`), not from the original root model's `_meta`.
reason: Referencing the original model metadata during recursion can accidentally resolve a same-named field or raise `FieldDoesNotExist` when deeper models use different field names.
common_pattern: Recursive Django model-relationship traversal must resolve fields relative to the current related model, and tests should use distinct field names across the model chain so incorrect model resolution cannot silently pass.

text: Workflow cancel/restart actions in the Wagtail page edit view should reuse the same comment-logging and notification logic as submit_action, and their messages should be handled consistently with other workflow states (placed in the corresponding is_cancelling_workflow branch while still permitting cancellation on a locked page).
reason: Keeps comment auditing and notifications consistent across page workflow states, and matches existing handling of other workflow states.
common_pattern: Consistency and accurate documentation of workflow-cancellation handling in Wagtail admin views: wherever a form can be invalid (validation errors OR lock), comments, tests, and cancellation code paths should reflect all reasons and reuse the same behavior as the normal submit/action flow.

text: Do not use Django model `Meta` options (in particular `Meta.abstract = True`) on non-model classes such as form widgets or Wagtail `Block` subclasses. These classes use non-model metaclasses (e.g. `MediaDefiningClass`) and will silently ignore `Meta`, producing dead, misleading code. For genuinely subclass-only classes, enforce abstraction with Python's `abc` module or `NotImplementedError` instead.
reason: Django's `Meta` options are handled only by the Django model metaclass, so applying them to widgets or blocks has no effect and misleads readers into thinking inheritance or abstraction is enforced.
common_pattern: Correct use of Django's `Meta` class in class hierarchies: `Meta` options (especially `abstract`) only apply to Django models, and shared `Meta` configuration belongs on abstract base models with subclasses inheriting via `Meta` subclassing.

text: On abstract Django base models, define shared `Meta` options (e.g. `indexes`, `ordering`) that do not depend on subclass-specific fields or relationships in the base model's `Meta`, and have concrete subclasses inherit them by subclassing `Meta` (e.g. `class Meta(Base.Meta)`). When an abstract subclass overrides an inherited field with less restrictive options, verify the subclass field definition is the one resolved for concrete models, since the base class's stricter constraints must not leak into derived models.
reason: Avoids duplicating configuration across concrete models (which risks divergence) while ensuring that unintended stricter constraints from a base abstract class do not leak into subclasses.
common_pattern: Correct use of Django's `Meta` class in class hierarchies: `Meta` options (especially `abstract`) only apply to Django models, and shared `Meta` configuration belongs on abstract base models with subclasses inheriting via `Meta` subclassing.

text: Treat component rendering methods (e.g., render/render_html) as side-effect-free and centralized: add new HTML-rendering variants or pieces to the existing render_html method rather than introducing parallel render_*_html methods, and do not add compatibility/fallback logic whose only justification is guarding against hypothetical side effects in overridden render methods.
reason: Render methods that mutate state are non-standard and should not drive core API design; guarding against hypothetical side effects adds complexity for an obscure case, and parallel rendering paths expand the rendering API surface and split HTML output across multiple places.
common_pattern: Rendering design and documentation conventions: keep rendering logic centralized in a single render method (treating it as side-effect-free) and document rendering contracts in terms of what the object produces rather than over-specifying the mechanism.

text: Registry classes should only collect and expose configuration; keep domain logic such as composing rewriters or performing conversion in the consuming module or converter class (e.g., `rich_text/__init__.py`), not in the registry itself.
reason: Maintains separation of concerns: the registry owns configuration collection, while conversion/rewriting remains the responsibility of consumers. This keeps the registry pattern consistent and avoids special-case logic inside registries.
common_pattern: Registry design conventions: use descriptive domain-specific registry names, define a single shared registry instance in a central module and import it, and keep registry classes limited to configuration collection rather than domain logic.

text: When adding `render_form` context variables or override hooks to a Wagtail block class, mirror the equivalent `StructBlock` interface and template-variable names so subclasses can override them consistently. In block `render_form` template contexts and constructor/meta options, name the form-rendering CSS class `form_classname` (matching `StructBlock.Meta.form_classname`) rather than a generic `classname`; reserve `classname` for established panel/admin attributes (e.g. `FieldPanel`, `Block.Meta`). A rendered block template may contain multiple elements with customizable classes, so a generic key is ambiguous.
reason: Consistency with the existing StructBlock Meta convention and disambiguation of context keys make template overrides predictable and prevent divergence between block types.
scope: Wagtail block render_form contexts, meta class-name options, and override hooks
common_pattern: Wagtail block form-rendering APIs must use the specific context/meta option name `form_classname` (matching `StructBlock.Meta.form_classname`) instead of the generic `classname`, and new block `render_form` context variables/hooks must mirror the existing StructBlock interface so subclasses can override them consistently.

text: Wagtail media Admin API endpoints and serializers should expose the fields required by the admin UI consistently across documents and images: include `created_at` for list ordering and the 'Uploaded' column and `filesize` for detail views; in admin image serializers (e.g., `AdminImageSerializer`), also expose the original image URL (`file`) and the rendition sizes consumed by admin UI features (notably `max-800x600` for focal point editing) so the admin UI can render those features correctly.
reason: The Admin API backs the admin UI; missing fields break list ordering/columns and detail rendering, while divergence between documents and images causes inconsistent admin behavior and incomplete image views.
scope: Wagtail media Admin API endpoints and admin image serializers
common_pattern: Wagtail media Admin API endpoints must expose the fields required by the admin UI, and parallel media endpoints (documents/images) must keep equivalent field coverage aligned.

text: When an admin image serializer must expose multiple renditions, model them as a list/object keyed by filter spec rather than as separate hard-coded top-level fields, and design it so callers can request only the rendition sizes needed for the current view.
reason: A keyed rendition collection keeps the API shape stable as new renditions are added and avoids returning every possible resolution when a view needs only a few.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin image API serializers should expose the image representations required by admin UI features (renditions and the original file URL) and should model multiple renditions as an extensible, client-selectable collection rather than hard-coded top-level fields.

text: In FilteredSelect / FilteredModelChoiceField, filter accessor parameters (e.g. filter_accessor) must accept either a string attribute/method name or a callable/queryset factory that receives the instance and returns the related value/queryset. get_filter_value must invoke callable accessors with the instance before normalizing the returned queryset to IDs.
reason: This allows filtering by reverse relations or arbitrary querysets not exposed as model attributes/methods, improving reuse without subclassing.
common_pattern: FilteredSelect / FilteredModelChoiceField should expose a flexible filter-accessor contract: accept either a string attribute/method name or a callable/queryset factory that receives the instance, invoke callable accessors when resolving filter values, and document the Python/JavaScript filtering contract.

text: When building field-copy/sync exclusion APIs, keep a separate default exclusion list for protected/internal fields (e.g., `latest_revision`) distinct from the public, user-configurable override (`exclude_fields_in_copy`); combine the default list, the instance override, and any caller-supplied exclusions before performing the copy; and document how the default and override combine and take precedence. When adding such a public override field to a mixin (e.g., `RevisionMixin`), mirror the naming used by the analogous existing field on the related class (e.g., `Page`'s `default_exclude_fields_in_copy`) rather than prefixing it as private with an underscore.
reason: Lets developers customize copy behavior freely while guaranteeing internal fields are never copied; makes the interaction/precedence of defaults vs. overrides explicit; and keeps copy/translation naming consistent across models, supporting a future generic copy action and avoiding surprising name variants.
scope: project-specific to Wagtail copy/translation helpers (wagtail/models/i18n.py, RevisionMixin, Page)
common_pattern: Design and naming of Wagtail's field-copy/sync exclusion APIs: how protected-internal default exclusions, user-configurable overrides, and caller-supplied exclusions are layered, named, and documented.

text: In `client/src/utils/actions`, action creator utilities must require a `type` argument and return an action object containing that `type`; parameterless action creation is not supported.
reason: Action objects need a type for dispatch/reducer handling, and unsupported API use cases should not be allowed or codified in tests/types.
common_pattern: Tests should exercise the real action-creator/reducer contract by supplying the required type, arguments, and payload fields rather than simplifying calls or using stale/minimal action objects.

text: For form-driven auto-updates, prefer native browser events (`change`, `keyup`, and validation events like `invalid`/`reportValidity`) over `MutationObserver` or custom DOM events. When programmatically adding form fields or panels, explicitly dispatch `change` on the inserted fields so existing change-based listeners stay in sync. When programmatically updating form inputs or hidden state fields (e.g., Django formset DELETE management inputs), compare the current value first and only assign and dispatch `change` when the value actually differs; likewise guard lifecycle/removal mutations by checking whether the element is already in the expected final state and bypass the logic if so.
reason: Native browser events integrate better and are less fragile than custom validity events, while `MutationObserver` is overkill for normal field edits and causes extra work. Programmatic additions do not naturally emit `change`, so an explicit dispatch is required to preserve the consistent event-driven update model. Comparing values first and guarding removal transitions keeps server/client state reconciliation idempotent, because server-rendered responses (e.g., POST error pages already containing deleted forms) can already reflect the target state; unconditional assignment fires spurious change events and duplicate custom events.
common_pattern: Client-side form state management should be driven by semantically correct DOM events: avoid redundant state writes/event dispatches when the target is already in the desired state, and prefer native browser events (change, keyup, invalid/reportValidity) over MutationObserver or custom event plumbing when syncing dependent UI.

text: Treat icons (and other template-tag-rendered assets) as sprite-rendered resources, not static files: store icons as individual source files for maintainability, override, and extension, but serve them as a single sprite, and do not register or expose individual icon files as static assets or rely on staticfiles features for icons. When documenting custom icon customization, explicitly state the exact directory the file must be saved in (a template directory such as `templates/`) and warn that placing it in a static directory will not work, because icons are rendered/served through a single sprite rather than as individual static files.
reason: The underlying principle is that icons are template-rendered sprite assets, not individual static files. Storing them as individual source files aids maintainability, while serving them as a sprite avoids redundant staticfiles features. Documenting the required template directory prevents users from placing icons in a static directory where they fail silently.
common_pattern: Icon assets in this project are stored as individual source files in TEMPLATE directories but rendered/served as a single sprite (not as individual static assets); this non-obvious distinction must be documented for users and respected in implementation.

text: Debounce `SwapController#patch` (formerly `request`) in addition to `swapLocation`, likely by creating a separate debounced function in `connect()`.
reason: DOM-patching Stimulus actions can also benefit from debouncing, and the reviewer expects this action to be debounced alongside `swapLocation`.
common_pattern: Improvements to the same SwapController method: clearer naming (patch instead of request) and consistent debouncing as a Stimulus action.

text: When a shared parsing/formatting helper is introduced for a form field (e.g., `format_choices`), route all parsing sites for that same data — including choices and default/initial value handling — through the shared logic instead of ad-hoc inline parsing. Ensure all related helpers split and strip on the same delimiters, including newlines, so multi-line values behave consistently. If a derived attribute needs a different output shape (e.g., a flat list of values instead of `(value, label)` pairs), add a companion helper that reuses the same parsing logic rather than reimplementing split/strip handling. Document any fallback normalization behavior in the docstring.
reason: Inconsistent delimiter handling across related helpers breaks default/initial values, especially multi-line values, while duplicated inline parsing causes mismatched behavior and makes fallback logic easy to miss.
common_pattern: Centralizing parsing/formatting logic for a field: when a shared helper (e.g., format_choices) exists, all other parsing sites of that field — including default/initial value handling — must route through shared logic rather than ad-hoc inline parsing; when the required output shape differs, add a companion helper instead of duplicating the parse.

text: Use secure temporary-file creation APIs such as `tempfile.mkstemp()` for files (and `tempfile.mkdtemp()` for directories) instead of `tempfile.mktemp()`.
reason: `tempfile.mktemp()` is insecure/deprecated and can introduce race conditions; `mkstemp()`/`mkdtemp()` create the temporary resource atomically.
common_pattern: Safe temporary-file handling: use atomic/secure creation APIs instead of insecure ones, and guarantee cleanup through try/finally scoping.

text: When rendering keyboard shortcut dialogs, detect the platform (`is_mac`/User-Agent) and use native key combinations and wording where needed (e.g. macOS Redo `Shift+⌘+Z`, Windows/Linux `Ctrl+Y`); if a neutral label such as 'Paste text only' works across OSes, prefer it over platform-specific wording.
reason: Shortcut bindings and action wording differ by OS, so modifier-only abstraction or generic labels can misinform users or conflict with browser/OS conventions. Neutral wording is acceptable when it avoids unnecessary per-OS branching.
common_pattern: Conventions for Wagtail admin keyboard shortcut UI: separate translatable labels from untranslated key combinations, abstract the platform modifier as `MOD`/`mod`, and render OS-native shortcut labels/key bindings via platform detection.

text: When code needs to query a specific database, always select the alias explicitly with Django's documented APIs (`QuerySet.using(db_alias)`, `Manager.db_manager(db_alias)`, or `router.db_for_read/db_for_write(Model)`) instead of relying on implicit or private connection state such as `django.db.connection.alias`, `transaction.atomic()` context internals (`Atomic.using`), or `instance._state.db`. For reloading an instance after a write — particularly under a custom database router that reads from a replica and writes to a primary — resolve the alias via `router.db_for_write(Model)` (which matches how treebeard determines the write database) and fetch with `Model.objects.using(alias).get(...)`; never assume the `default` connection, a transaction context's alias, or `instance._state.db`, since those can resolve to a read replica. For reloading based on an instance's own binding, use `instance._state.db`. Never mutate a shared manager's `db`/`_db` attribute to pick a database — use `db_manager()` (or `QuerySet.using()`), which is thread-safe and fails loudly (AttributeError) rather than silently misbehaving if the API changes.
reason: Shared/global and private connection state does not respect custom database routers or read/write replicas and is not thread-safe; only `router.db_for_write(Model)` guarantees a reload reads from the database where the write occurred, and the documented per-call APIs reliably target the same database the operation actually used. `db_manager()` also fails loudly (AttributeError) rather than silently misbehaving if the API changes.
common_pattern: In Django ORM code, selecting the correct database alias must be done explicitly via documented, per-instance/queryset APIs (`QuerySet.using()`, `Manager.db_manager()`, `router.db_for_write()`) instead of relying on implicit connection state (`django.db.connection.alias`), private transaction internals (`Atomic.using`), or mutating shared manager state (`Manager.db`). Generalizations 1–3 are a progressive refinement within one PR (the earlier `atomic_ctx.using`/`_state.db` proposals are corrected by the router-aware recommendation), and generalization 4 expresses the same principle for a different scenario (avoid shared/global state when binding a manager to an alias).

text: In Draftail entity decorators, read semantic document/link metadata (e.g. `filename`, `url`) from the entity's structured data via `contentState.getEntity(entityKey).getData()` rather than by parsing the entity URL. When a decorator needs a new metadata field, add it at the data-production points (the dbHTML->contentstate converter and the document chooser) so it is available in entity data.
reason: Entity URLs do not reliably follow a predictable path structure, so parsing them is fragile; centralising metadata extraction at the source keeps decorators independent of URL formats.
scope: Draftail entity decorators / document entity pipeline
common_pattern: Draftail entity decorators should treat the entity's structured data as the single source of truth for metadata (URLs, filenames) — never reconstruct it from the entity URL — and should represent absent metadata explicitly (null) rather than with arbitrary fallbacks.
