reason: Pattern matching improves readability and avoids repetitive comparisons; adopt it once Python 3.9 support is dropped.
common_pattern: Simplification of conditional branching: single-source the selected branch/default instead of duplicating it across if/else arms, and choose the broadest applicable default for the API.

text: In controller event handlers, delegate value transformation to the existing controller behavior/transform method instead of reimplementing the transformation with a utility function. When delegating, read the source value from event.detail.value, fall back to this.element.value, and return the transformed value.
reason: Keeps controller behavior consistent by reusing defined transformation logic and supports both event-driven and direct/programmatic invocation without forcing a DOM update.
common_pattern: Controller event handlers should delegate value transformation to existing controller behavior/transform methods rather than reimplementing the logic; the delegating handler must source input from event.detail.value with a this.element.value fallback and return the transformed value.

text: Centralize the cancelable pre-action dispatch sequence in a shared target-processing helper: dispatch the before event, skip or filter out targets when event.defaultPrevented is true, and have action methods rely on that helper instead of duplicating dispatch/cancel logic in each action.
reason: Provides consistent cancellation semantics across actions and avoids duplicated event-dispatch code paths.
scope: Stimulus controller helper design, especially target-processing helpers
common_pattern: Designing, centralizing, and testing cancelable custom-event behavior in Stimulus controllers: dispatch before side effects, honor event.defaultPrevented, centralize the dispatch/filter logic, and verify cancellation in tests.

text: Do not introduce thin wrapper or helper methods (including context managers) that are used only once or that merely delegate to an existing function/standard-library call; inline the call at its single use site unless the helper manages a non-trivial resource lifecycle or delivers clear reuse/readability benefit.
reason: Single-use indirection adds complexity and API surface without reuse benefit, can obscure resource-lifecycle handling (e.g. whether the underlying resource is ever closed), and can drift from the API it wraps; direct calls also keep important arguments (such as security-related flags on `hashlib`) explicit at the point of use.
common_pattern: Helper/wrapper hygiene: minimize redundant computation and unnecessary indirection around helper functions — reuse the results and encapsulation of existing helpers instead of re-calling or duplicating their logic, and avoid creating new single-use wrapper helpers that only delegate to an existing call.

text: In change/compare handlers such as `*ValueChanged` callbacks and controller guards, keep equality logic pure and explicit: derive plain values and compare with `===` instead of calling side-effecting methods; return early when `previous === current` or after updating reactive state that causes the handler to re-run; rely on the handler re-running rather than duplicating comparisons inline; and use the correct boolean polarity when gating sync or `preventDefault` behavior on equality.
reason: Prevents unintended side effects, stale reads, duplicate work, and inverted sync behavior in reactive value-change flows.
common_pattern: Reactive change/comparison handlers should keep equality logic pure and explicit, return early when there is nothing to do or when a state update will re-run the handler, and document non-obvious previous/current or re-entry control flow.

text: For deterministic, non-security-sensitive hashing in Wagtail (e.g., redirect URL hashes, namespace-based UUIDs), prefer a faster hash algorithm over SHA-1-based `uuid5`: use `uuid.uuid3()` (MD5) when a UUID format is required, or `hashlib.blake2b()` when a UUID format is not externally required. Only add a new third-party hash dependency (e.g., BLAKE3) if its benefits clearly outweigh the cost of the dependency. Cryptographic security properties are not needed for internal identifiers.
reason: MD5-based/`blake2b` hashing is cheaper than SHA-1, and the additional security of `uuid5` provides no benefit for internal, user-facing-but-not-security-sensitive lookups such as redirect hashes, where the database lookup is the real bottleneck.
scope: global (non-cryptographic hashing needs, e.g. wagtail/contrib/redirects get_redirect_hash)
common_pattern: Choosing hash algorithms for deterministic, non-security-sensitive internal hashing in Wagtail. Within the redirects PR review thread, sentiment converges on preferring cheaper/faster hashing (MD5-based `uuid3`, `hashlib.blake2b`) over SHA-1-based `uuid5` because cryptographic security is irrelevant for internal identifiers. A loosely-related second thread concerns DRY extraction of stdlib hashing compatibility helpers.

text: Extract duplicated standard-library compatibility fallbacks (e.g., handling `hashlib.md5`'s `usedforsecurity` argument across Python versions) into a shared utility in `wagtail.coreutils` (e.g., `safe_md5`) and update all affected call sites to use it.
reason: Centralizes Python version compatibility logic, avoids duplicated try/except blocks across modules, and ensures consistent handling of `usedforsecurity`.
common_pattern: Choosing hash algorithms for deterministic, non-security-sensitive internal hashing in Wagtail. Within the redirects PR review thread, sentiment converges on preferring cheaper/faster hashing (MD5-based `uuid3`, `hashlib.blake2b`) over SHA-1-based `uuid5` because cryptographic security is irrelevant for internal identifiers. A loosely-related second thread concerns DRY extraction of stdlib hashing compatibility helpers.

text: Represent a control's disabled state with the native `disabled` attribute/property (e.g. `.prop('disabled', boolean)`), not a `disabled` CSS class. Use that disabled state as the single source of truth for non-interactivity (e.g. don't add click-handler guards for an already-loading/disabled button). Keep disabled controls visible with muted disabled styling rather than `display: none`, and in component styles cover `.disabled`, `:disabled`, and `[disabled]` selectors so styling applies regardless of how the state is applied.
reason: A CSS class only affects styling and does not communicate state to assistive technology or change focus/interaction semantics; hiding disabled controls removes affordance. Covering all disabled selectors ensures consistent styling, and relying on the native disabled state avoids dead-code click guards since disabled controls can't receive clicks.
scope: frontend UI components and button/controller styling (e.g. `client/scss/components/_button.scss`)
common_pattern: Correct handling of the 'disabled' state on interactive controls — asserting it truthfully in tests and implementing/styling it via the native disabled mechanism so it stays accessible, visible, and is the single source of truth for non-interactivity.

text: Add a trailing comma to multi-line Python parameter/argument and collection literals (lists, dicts, etc.), and run the project formatter (`make format` / Black) before submitting so the formatter normalizes wrapping, indentation, and nesting.
reason: Black's magic trailing comma makes literals stay multi-line, keeps diffs minimal as entries are added/removed, and ensures changes match the project's automated style, reducing review churn and CI failures.
common_pattern: Use trailing commas and the project's Python formatter (Black/`make format`) to keep multi-line list/dict/parameter literals consistently wrapped and diff-friendly, per Wagtail style guidelines.

text: In project stylesheets (SCSS/CSS, including component styles under `client/scss/` and docs styles under `docs/_static/css/`), use CSS logical properties and values instead of physical directional properties: `margin-inline-start`/`margin-inline-end` (not `margin-left`/`margin-right`), `padding-inline-start`/`padding-inline-end` (not `padding-left`/`padding-right`), `inset-inline-start`/`inset-inline-end` (not `left`/`right`), `border-inline-start`/`border-inline-end` (not `border-left`/`border-right`), and `border-start-start-radius`/`border-start-end-radius` (not `border-top-left-radius`/`border-top-right-radius`).
reason: Logical properties automatically adapt to text direction and writing mode, giving correct RTL and internationalized layouts without duplicated direction-specific overrides, and they satisfy the project's Stylelint `property-disallowed-list` configuration (so physical directional properties fail frontend CI).
common_pattern: All generalizations converge on a single CSS authoring convention: use logical (direction-aware) CSS properties instead of physical directional properties in project stylesheets, so layouts adapt to writing mode and RTL, and so Stylelint's property-disallowed-list CI check passes.

text: Keep the element reference used across a controller's lifecycle hooks consistent — the same node destroyed/updated in `disconnect()`/`resize()` must be the one initialized in `connect()`.
reason: Mismatched element references between setup and teardown leak observers/instances or fail to clean up the initialized element.
common_pattern: Stimulus controller lifecycle discipline: `disconnect()` must symmetrically and completely undo what `connect()`/initialization set up, using shared cleanup rather than duplication, without relying on callbacks that don't fire during teardown, and without retaining live third-party widget instances across disconnects.

text: In Django templates, place `{% load %}` tags at the top of the file, load only the libraries whose tags/filters are actually used, and combine multiple loads into a single space-separated tag (e.g. `{% load i18n static %}`). Load tag lines must be syntactically valid with no extraneous characters after `%}`.
reason: Idiomatic placement, no unused or malformed loads, and consolidated single-line loads keep template dependencies accurate, concise, and free of syntax errors.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail template tag library conventions: how to register tags/filters in `templatetags/`, how to name and document the library, and how to write `{% load %}` tags in templates.

text: Express status and warning messages using the project's existing semantic status classes (e.g. `status-msg warning`) rather than hard-coded inline `style` color declarations, and only apply status-specific modifier classes (`w-status--*`) to actual status tags — not to generic buttons or unrelated UI elements.
reason: Centralizes theming in project CSS, avoids hard-coded color values, expresses semantic intent, and keeps the status-tag namespace limited to elements it actually represents.
common_pattern: Establishing a BEM-based CSS class naming and usage convention: correct `block__element--modifier` syntax, semantic modifier naming tied to the modified component's actual state/variant, minimal use of modifiers, and reuse of existing semantic status classes rather than ad-hoc styles.

text: In bulk-action selection state, track selected items by their stable data ID rather than a cached DOM element reference, and do not derive selection order from numeric object IDs — use actual DOM/selection order, since search, filtering, default sorting, and drag-and-drop can change or invalidate visible ordering and element references.
reason: DOM references can become stale when drag-and-drop or other DOM manipulation replaces/detaches elements, and numeric ID ordering is not equivalent to user-visible order once the list is searched, filtered, or sorted — both cause incorrect previous/next/range selection behavior.
scope: client admin bulk-action selection code (e.g. client/src/entrypoints/admin/)
common_pattern: Reliable management of bulk-action selection state: track selected items by stable data identifiers (not cached DOM references or numeric-ID-derived ordering), and centralize derived selection lists (e.g. non-disabled items) in reusable controller helpers.

text: In icon SVG/HTML assets and documentation examples, use `<!--! ... -->` (exclamation mark immediately after `<!--`) for licensing/attribution comments, and accurately state the exact Font Awesome license tier and version (e.g., "Font Awesome Free 6.5.1").
reason: Makes licensing conventions discoverable, prevents removal of the `!` marker, and ensures correct attribution for compliance.
scope: global (SVG/HTML licensing comments in icon assets and docs examples), including FontAwesome-based icons in this project
common_pattern: Licensing/attribution comments in icon SVG/HTML assets and docs must use the `<!--! ... -->` marker (exclamation immediately after `<!--`) and accurately state the exact license tier and version.

text: Helper logic that does not depend on class instance state should be defined as a standalone function rather than a static class method (exporting it when shared), and file-local helpers should be placed after the main exported class/entry point so the primary abstraction appears first.
reason: Extracting helpers as standalone functions reduces coupling to the class, makes them easier to import and test, and ordering them below the main export keeps implementation details out of the top of the file.
common_pattern: How to define and position standalone/helper logic: prefer standalone (non-instance-dependent) functions over static class methods, and keep the main export as the first abstraction in the file with helpers placed after it.

text: In JavaScript class methods, access class members through the correct receiver: instance fields as `this.<field>`, static members as `this.constructor.<member>` or `ClassName.<member>`; never use bare identifiers for instance fields or `this.<member>` for a static member.
reason: Static members live on the class constructor, not on instances, so `this.<member>` for a static field is undefined; similarly, bare identifiers do not resolve to instance state. These mistakes silently break inherited behavior and cause runtime errors. When converting a member to `static`, update all instance-side references accordingly; when a member is only accessed via `this`, declare it as an instance field rather than static.
common_pattern: Correct receiver qualification for JavaScript class members: instance state must be accessed via `this.<field>`, static members via `this.constructor.<member>` or `ClassName.<member>`, and bare identifiers or incorrect `this` access are bugs.

text: When restoring accidentally removed code, restore the complete original block, including export style, class names, static declarations, documentation, and compatibility/framework configuration lines, rather than a subset.
reason: Partial restoration can break the application, leave the module undocumented, or remove necessary backwards compatibility or framework behavior.
common_pattern: When restoring accidentally removed code, restore the complete original content rather than a subset, including exports, documentation, and configuration lines.

text: In sidebar/menu SCSS (e.g., `client/src/components/Sidebar/SidebarPanel.scss` and admin menu containers), do not use `overflow: hidden` on the container element because it clips nested submenus. Fix the underlying layout/scroll issue instead; handle label/footer text truncation by wrapping at the individual menu item level rather than imposing character limits; and ensure nested submenu panels use `inset-inline-start` with the full menu width variable (not the slim/collapsed variable) so they clear the parent menu.
reason: Container-level `overflow: hidden` prevents nested menu levels from rendering, while per-item overflow/wrapping styles provide truncation without restricting menu depth. Nested submenus also need correct full-width offset to avoid hiding behind the parent menu.
scope: component: sidebar menu styles (`SidebarPanel.scss`) and admin menu containers
common_pattern: Avoid container-level overflow clipping in sidebar/menu components so nested submenus and long text remain visible; handle overflow locally at the item level instead.

text: When a DOM element reference is needed—whether for existence validation, later event dispatch, or inside a returned closure—resolve it directly from the actual target element via an in-scope reference (e.g., the container/element parameter passed into the init/render function), rather than querying an associated control (like a panel's toggle) or referencing an undeclared identifier.
reason: Direct, in-scope references to the actual target element make the variable reusable beyond the initial guard check and avoid runtime ReferenceErrors from undeclared identifiers.
scope: global DOM initialization and closure patterns
common_pattern: When a DOM element reference is needed (for validation, event dispatch, or inside a returned closure), it must be resolved directly from the actual target element using an in-scope reference, rather than from an associated proxy control or an undeclared identifier.

text: In side panel components with shared show/hide handlers, dispatch hide events for all other panels before dispatching the show event for the newly selected panel, and dispatch show events outside any loops used for dispatching hide/close events (resolve reusable DOM references before such loops).
reason: Prevents shared hide handlers from clearing state (e.g., auto-update interval) just set by the new panel's show handler, and keeps show-event dispatch out of per-item loop scope, making event ordering and scope explicit.
scope: client/src/includes/sidePanel.js — side panel event dispatch / initSidePanel
common_pattern: Correct ordering and scoping of show/hide event dispatch in side panel components with shared handlers

text: Construct sets idiomatically: use set comprehensions (`{x for x in it}`) instead of `set(x for x in it)`, and pass a dict directly (`set(d)`) instead of `set(d.keys())`. In tests, assert with `assertSetEqual` rather than `assertEqual`.
reason: Set comprehensions are more concise and idiomatic, dicts iterate over keys by default so `.keys()` is redundant, and set-specific assertions give better failure diagnostics.
common_pattern: Python collection-type selection and idiomatic construction/use of sets — choosing the right container for membership/uniqueness needs, avoiding premature micro-optimizations, and constructing sets idiomatically.

text: In preview side-panel templates, render interactive controls that keyboard users need (e.g., preview mode selectors) before the preview iframe in DOM order so tab focus follows the visual top-to-bottom flow.
reason: Keyboard users would otherwise have to tab through the entire iframe before reaching controls, and focus would jump down then back up.
common_pattern: Wagtail preview side-panel iframe implementation conventions, covering accessibility/DOM order, background styling, responsive sizing, and stable iframe identification. The generalizations are related by the preview iframe context but represent distinct sub-patterns rather than one single rule.

text: In preview panel code, eliminate redundant and dead declarations: reuse existing preview SCSS classes (e.g., `w-preview-*`) instead of inline styles for generated elements, and remove dataset attributes/state that are not consumed by the preview logic.
reason: Generalizations 1 and 2 converge on using reusable `w-preview-*` classes rather than inline styles; generalization 3 adds the complementary concern of removing an unused `data-active-preview-size` attribute. Together they express a preview-panel code-hygiene rule spanning two PRs.
common_pattern: Preview panel code should avoid redundant styling and unused/dead DOM state by reusing existing preview SCSS classes and removing dataset attributes that are not consumed.

text: Each `{% hook_output '<hook_name>' %}` call must reference a distinct hook name; do not render the same hook name (e.g. `insert_editor_css`) more than once in a template.
reason: Duplicated hook outputs cause the CSS/JS registered to that hook to be injected twice, producing redundant payload and potential ordering/specificity bugs, and can cause plugins/features to load twice.
common_pattern: Correct semantics for Wagtail's `{% hook_output %}` template tag: avoid duplicate renders of the same hook name, and gate deprecation warnings on real hook output rather than hook-name queries. Two related but genuinely distinct sub-patterns (template duplication vs. deprecation-warning triggering).

text: Order version-comparison branches so that each branch is reachable and not shadowed by an earlier condition; typically order from most specific to least restrictive (e.g., for >= checks, higher version bounds before lower ones). Remove any elif whose condition is already covered by a preceding if.
reason: Unreachable branches silently become dead code and mislead readers into thinking version-specific behavior exists when it does not.
common_pattern: Ordering version-comparison branches to avoid unreachable code and shadowed conditions.

text: Compatibility shims or backported framework internals should be conditionally defined only for the framework versions that require them, rather than left active unconditionally.
reason: Avoids obsolete compatibility code and prevents conflicts with newer framework behavior on supported versions.
common_pattern: All four generalizations concern how to write and maintain framework/library version-compatibility branches: the shape of version comparisons, when compatibility shims should be active, and how to document non-obvious version-gated code.

text: In Django templates, when consuming structured context data such as lists of dicts, dict items, or dict keys that are tuples, use explicit key/index access or named unpacking to retrieve the intended value. Avoid generic filters like `|first`, single generic pair variables, or rendering the whole dictionary/tuple. Examples: use `items.0.item` for a list item dict, `{% for name, value in items %}` for dict items, and `category.0` / `category.1` for tuple-keyed dicts.
reason: Prevents templates from rendering unreadable Python representations and ensures the intended labels, values, and stable identifiers appear.
common_pattern: Django templates should access structured context data through explicit keys, indices, or named unpacking rather than generic filters, generic pair variables, or whole-object rendering.

text: Keep interactive-state selectors minimal and correct: do not add `:hover`/`:focus`/`:focus-within`/modifier selectors when an earlier condition already covers that state; for disabled exclusions use a single `:not(:disabled, .disabled, [disabled])` selector list rather than chained or comma-separated `:not()` selectors.
reason: Redundant state selectors bloat the stylesheet and can change specificity or exclusion semantics; chained `:not()` raises specificity, while comma-separated outer `:not()` selectors can unintentionally match disabled elements.
common_pattern: Interactive-state styling in component SCSS: hover/focus/active/disabled states should be token-driven, preserve default feedback, use correct selectors and grouping, and align with design specs.

text: Only include interaction state styles (e.g. hover backgrounds) when the current design spec explicitly defines that state; remove obsolete state rules rather than keeping legacy styling.
reason: Keeps component SCSS aligned with the design source of truth and avoids shipping unintended or unapproved hover/state behaviour.
common_pattern: Interactive-state styling in component SCSS: hover/focus/active/disabled states should be token-driven, preserve default feedback, use correct selectors and grouping, and align with design specs.

text: For DOM text reads/writes in client-side code and Jest/JSDOM tests, prefer `textContent` over `innerText` (JSDOM does not implement `innerText`, so `innerText` writes are invisible in tests); use `innerText` only when the rendered/visible text is actually required, and prefer these native properties over jQuery's `.text()`.
reason: `textContent` works natively in JSDOM without shims/mocks, while `innerText` reflects rendered text that JSDOM cannot produce. Choosing the right API avoids unnecessary test mocks and makes text assertions observable.
scope: client-side JavaScript / Stimulus controllers and their JSDOM tests
common_pattern: Choosing and using the correct DOM text API: preferring native DOM text properties over jQuery/coercion helpers, selecting `textContent` vs `innerText` based on whether layout-aware/rendered text is needed (notably in JSDOM tests), and assigning values directly.

text: When setting a DOM element's text property (e.g., `textContent`), assign the value directly rather than calling `.toString()`; the property setter already coerces to a string.
reason: Avoids redundant conversion calls and keeps DOM assignment code concise.
common_pattern: Choosing and using the correct DOM text API: preferring native DOM text properties over jQuery/coercion helpers, selecting `textContent` vs `innerText` based on whether layout-aware/rendered text is needed (notably in JSDOM tests), and assigning values directly.

text: Do not define `__ne__` on a class that defines `__eq__`; Python 3 derives `__ne__` as the inverse of `__eq__`. Only implement `__ne__` when inheriting from a type whose `__ne__` is not derived from `__eq__`.
reason: The default `object.__ne__` already negates `__eq__` in Python 3, so an explicit implementation is redundant and creates extra maintenance surface.
common_pattern: Implementation rules for Python rich comparison dunder methods: rely on Python 3 defaults where available, return NotImplemented for unsupported operands, and keep equality/comparison semantics type-consistent rather than coercive.

text: In JavaScript files linted by ESLint (including docs/_static/js/), access browser and third-party globals as properties on `window` (e.g. `window.docsearch`, `window.READTHEDOCS_DATA`, `window.location`, `window.alert`) instead of bare global identifiers, so `no-undef` passes without suppression. If a separate lint rule bans the API itself (e.g. `no-alert`), still qualify it with `window.` and add only a targeted `// eslint-disable-next-line no-alert`, not a `no-undef` suppression.
reason: Converges three PR comments across PR#8671 and PR#9224: qualify browser/third-party globals with `window.` to satisfy linting and make global dependency explicit; use targeted disables only for API-specific rules.
scope: JavaScript files linted by ESLint, especially docs/_static/js/
common_pattern: JavaScript global handling: make global access explicit (`window.`), avoid accidental redeclaration/module-scope assumptions in global contexts, and prefer intentional globals over incidental DOM or implicit global references.

text: In Wagtail admin templates, ensure every interactive control has a localized accessible name. For icon-only controls, use `aria-label` (e.g. `{% trans 'Clear' %}`) or the component's established accessible-label API; do not rely on `data-tippy-content` or a native `title` alone. If visible text already provides the control's name, do not add a redundant or conflicting `aria-label` (e.g. do not set both `toggle_label` and `toggle_aria_label`; use `toggle_describedby` when extra context is needed). For supplemental tooltips/toggletips, use the project's accessible pattern (`w-tooltip`, focusable trigger with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, or `w-sr-only`) instead of native `title` or hover-only markup.
reason: Icon-only controls otherwise have no accessible name; redundant/conflicting ARIA overrides visible labels and breaks voice-control users; native `title` and hover-only tooltips are not reliably announced or available on touch/keyboard.
common_pattern: Accessible labeling and tooltip semantics in Wagtail admin templates — ensuring icon-only controls have localized accessible names, avoiding redundant/conflicting labels, and not relying on native `title` or `data-tippy-content` alone.

text: Render grouped actions that must share state (e.g. selected item ids) as a `<form>` with submit buttons rather than individual anchors with per-link query parameters.
reason: Using a form provides a single submission path and native handling of shared state, avoiding per-link query-param wiring.
common_pattern: Both rules aim to decouple reusable Wagtail admin frontend code from view-specific wiring, using native form submission or caller-supplied options instead of ad hoc hardcoding.

text: Management commands should subclass `django.core.management.base.BaseCommand` directly and implement their logic in `handle()`. Do not alias `NoArgsCommand` as `BaseCommand`, add try/except compatibility imports, or retain a `handle_noargs()` shim — these belong to the deprecated NoArgsCommand API and are unnecessary across all supported Django versions.
reason: BaseCommand is available in every supported Django version, so version-specific fallbacks are dead weight and reliance on a deprecated interface. Using handle() keeps commands aligned with the modern API.
common_pattern: Django management command code structure — using the modern BaseCommand API directly and keeping command internals clean/testable (no deprecated compatibility shims, non-trivial resolution logic factored out).

text: In management command classes, move non-trivial template/path resolution logic out of `add_arguments()` and `handle()` into a named helper method (e.g. `get_default_template()`).
reason: Separates argument wiring from path/template resolution, improving readability and making the logic independently testable.
common_pattern: Django management command code structure — using the modern BaseCommand API directly and keeping command internals clean/testable (no deprecated compatibility shims, non-trivial resolution logic factored out).

text: When removing a method (public or internal) as part of a refactor, also remove the associated private helpers, manager classes, or companion methods that existed only to support it, so no orphaned dead code is left behind.
reason: Orphaned helpers create dead code and misleading public surface, making the module harder to understand and maintain after the refactor.
common_pattern: Deciding when to remove code versus preserve it: internal/dead code (only used by tests or removable legacy subsystems) should be deleted outright rather than shimmed, and removal of a method must sweep along its orphaned helpers; but genuine public API must be preserved for downstream consumers.

text: In JavaScript, declare variables with `const` by default and `let` only when reassignment is needed; do not use `var`, and declare at the point of first assignment rather than pre-declaring earlier.
reason: `const`/`let` give block scoping and make intended immutability explicit; keeping declaration and initialization together reduces scope, improves readability, and avoids stale uninitialized variables.
common_pattern: JavaScript local-variable hygiene: how variables should be declared (const/let over var, at first assignment), where they should live (minimal scope, only hoisting invocation-invariant values), and when an alias variable is justified (rarely — for lint-required param mutation, otherwise reference the source directly).

text: Do not create a local variable that only aliases a function parameter or an existing value; reference the original value directly, or rename the parameter if a more meaningful name is needed. The one exception is when a lint rule (e.g. `no-param-reassign` with `props: true`) forbids mutating a parameter — in that case assign the parameter to a local variable before mutation rather than disabling the rule.
reason: Redundant aliases add indirection and multiple names for the same value without improving clarity or safety; when mutation is genuinely required, a local copy satisfies the lint rule while making the intentional mutation explicit.
common_pattern: JavaScript local-variable hygiene: how variables should be declared (const/let over var, at first assignment), where they should live (minimal scope, only hoisting invocation-invariant values), and when an alias variable is justified (rarely — for lint-required param mutation, otherwise reference the source directly).

text: Place JavaScript local variables in the smallest scope where they are used: keep runtime-dependent values inside their consuming function, but hoist values that do not change per invocation (constants derived from the enclosing context) to the enclosing scope instead of recomputing them on every call.
reason: Hoisting runtime-dependent locals narrows their scope of validity and can change when the value is computed; conversely, recomputing invocation-invariant values inside a nested function is wasteful and hides a shared dependency.
common_pattern: JavaScript local-variable hygiene: how variables should be declared (const/let over var, at first assignment), where they should live (minimal scope, only hoisting invocation-invariant values), and when an alias variable is justified (rarely — for lint-required param mutation, otherwise reference the source directly).

text: Avoid inline styles in HTML, templates, Python render methods, tests, and documentation examples. Use CSS classes, utility classes, or the project stylesheet/SCSS sources instead; never embed raw CSS declarations in className.
reason: Inline styles violate CSP compatibility, bypass the styling pipeline, mix presentation with logic or markup, and make automated detection harder. Keeping styling in CSS classes or stylesheets improves maintainability, theming, and consistency.
common_pattern: Avoid inline styles across all code and documentation contexts; define presentation in CSS classes or stylesheets. A secondary documentation-specific pattern is to keep examples minimal by omitting unnecessary classes/styling arguments.

text: In Django template inheritance, ensure `{% extends %}` is the first template tag, place all rendered content inside `{% block %}` tags, and keep parent templates intended for extension structurally valid with balanced opening/closing HTML/template tags. Documentation should explain these tag-level and structural requirements rather than conflating them with template file location.
reason: These constraints determine whether template inheritance works: incorrect `{% extends %}` placement, content outside blocks, or unbalanced parent tags silently break rendering. Documenting the actual tag-level requirements prevents an incorrect mental model.
common_pattern: Correct usage and documentation of Django template inheritance constraints: tag placement, block-only content, and parent-template structural validity.

text: Remove obsolete presentational HTML attributes such as `valign` from templates and express alignment/layout in CSS instead (e.g., apply `vertical-align: top` to the corresponding cell/listing CSS rule) so the original alignment is preserved after the attribute is removed.
reason: Keeps templates semantic, separates structure from styling, and avoids silently breaking layout when a relied-upon obsolete attribute is dropped.
common_pattern: Table-cell styling should live in CSS rather than HTML presentational attributes, and cell styling must respect the table layout model (global cell rules, no layout-breaking display values, no redundant per-selector overrides).

text: Do not break the table layout model when styling cells: avoid setting layout-changing `display` values (e.g., `display: flex`) directly on `td`/`th` — wrap cell contents in a block-level element instead — and do not add per-selector padding/alignment overrides (e.g., on `td.title`) to compensate when a global rule (such as `vertical-align: middle` on `td`) already covers the cell.
reason: `display: flex` on a `td` removes its table-cell display and breaks adjacent row/column layout, while redundant per-selector overrides duplicate and conflict with the global cell rule, bloating SCSS.
common_pattern: Table-cell styling should live in CSS rather than HTML presentational attributes, and cell styling must respect the table layout model (global cell rules, no layout-breaking display values, no redundant per-selector overrides).

text: When replacing or introducing breadcrumb markup/classes (e.g. `.breadcrumb-link`, the locale breadcrumb in the page editor modal), ensure the new element or class is covered by the existing breadcrumb colour selectors (such as `.page-editor .modal .breadcrumb a`), or update those styles in the same change.
reason: Prevents visual regressions such as white-on-white text when users drill into breadcrumbs because the stylesheet skips the new class.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern the Wagtail admin shared breadcrumb component (`wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/shared/breadcrumb-next.html`) — its Tailwind utility-class width behavior, current-item visibility/data-attribute contract, test fixture markup, and CSS color-selector coverage. The cluster is topically coherent (one component) but contains several genuinely distinct sub-patterns that cannot be collapsed into a single rule.

text: Follow standard Python formatting for literals and their comments: keep simple literal assignments (e.g., empty lists) on one line without redundant parentheses or unnecessary multi-line formatting; for multi-line literals, place the closing brace on its own line aligned with the start of the assignment; place short explanatory comments inline on the same line as the dictionary entry or assignment they describe.
reason: Merges the three related Python style generalizations: closing bracket placement for multi-line literals, inline comments for dictionary entries, and avoiding needless multi-line formatting/parentheses for simple literal assignments.
common_pattern: Python literal formatting and comment placement: use conventional formatting for literals, keep simple literals concise, and attach short explanatory comments inline.

text: In Django/Wagtail templates, when displaying or conditioning on related model data, traverse existing related object attributes directly (e.g., `{{ obj.related.attr }}`) instead of adding Python-level convenience properties or separate annotated/helper attributes solely for template use, and ensure the same attribute path is used consistently in both the condition and the rendered value.
reason: Avoids redundant Python boilerplate, keeps the related object as the single source of truth, and prevents silent rendering failures caused by mismatched attribute paths between a condition and the value it renders.
common_pattern: In Django/Wagtail templates, related model data should be accessed directly through existing object attribute paths rather than via added Python-side convenience properties or separate annotated/helper attributes; the same attribute path must be used consistently in conditions and rendered values.

text: Only use ARIA relationship attributes that reference another element (e.g. `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`) when the referenced target element actually has a matching `id` present in the same template/DOM.
reason: Browsers and assistive technologies validate these relationships against an element `id`; without it the relationship is broken and screen readers cannot associate the two elements, so the ARIA enhancement must not precede correct base markup.
common_pattern: Correct and minimal ARIA usage in HTML templates and Stimulus controllers: use valid ARIA names/syntax, only reference existing IDs, keep validation messages precise and actionable, prefer standard ARIA over custom/data attributes and over ARIA-derived fallback logic, and access ARIA reliably in test environments.

text: In Wagtail admin templates, dynamically updated status or notification containers should use an ARIA live region, preferably role="status" with explicit aria-live="polite", so assistive technologies announce content updates; do not add ARIA live-region roles such as role="status" to static content.
reason: Screen readers do not reliably announce content that appears or changes after page load unless an explicit live region is declared. role="status" plus aria-live="polite" gives consistent, non-interruptive announcements, while applying live-region semantics to static content adds misleading or noisy accessibility behavior.
common_pattern: ARIA live-region semantics for dynamically updated notification/status content in Wagtail admin templates: use role="status" with explicit aria-live="polite" for dynamic announcements, and do not apply live-region roles to static content.

text: Use the project's shared focus utility (e.g., `forceFocus`) for programmatically focusing elements instead of ad-hoc `element.focus()` calls, and keep a single source of truth for focus — do not duplicate focus logic across controllers, components, or lifecycle methods.
reason: Centralizing focus makes the behavior robust for non-input/future targets and avoids confusing, duplicated, or divergent focus logic that is hard to reason about.
common_pattern: Programmatic focus management in UI components: how and where to trigger element focus, how to guard it, when in the lifecycle to run it, and how to centralize/test it.

text: Defer initial-focus logic in lifecycle methods until after all callbacks that may add DOM elements or listeners have fired, and separate always-executed behavior (scroll/focus) from conditionally-executed state mutations (e.g., setting/removing tabIndex) — gate only the mutation, not the primary action.
reason: Callbacks can create or mutate DOM and attach listeners, so focus code must run after them so the target exists; guarding the whole block on an attribute check silently skips intended behavior.
common_pattern: Programmatic focus management in UI components: how and where to trigger element focus, how to guard it, when in the lifecycle to run it, and how to centralize/test it.

text: Iterate collections directly (`for item in items:`); only materialize a snapshot copy when the collection may change during iteration. When a snapshot of a dict/mapping view (`items()`, `keys()`, `values()`) is required, use the idiomatic constructor (`list(view)` / `tuple(view)`) rather than an equivalent list comprehension.
reason: Avoids unnecessary allocation/copying and keeps loops simple, while retaining a copy only when mutation safety demands it. `list(...)`/`tuple(...)` also signal snapshot intent and avoid redundant-comprehension lint errors.
common_pattern: Idiomatic iteration over collection types (dicts/mappings and sequences): iterate directly rather than making unnecessary copies, materialize a snapshot only when mutation during iteration must be tolerated, and honor the standard iteration contract (Mapping.__iter__ yields keys).

text: Prefer idiomatic Python collection constructs: use list comprehensions (e.g. [x for x in xs if pred(x)]) to build filtered/transformed sequences instead of wrapping a generator in tuple(); use list(iterable) directly to materialize an existing iterable when a list is genuinely required, and remove the corresponding `# noqa: C416` suppression rather than disabling the rule; and use tuple literals for fixed, read-only sequences used only for membership testing or iteration. Reserve tuple()/tuple literals for cases that require immutability or hashability.
reason: List comprehensions and list(iterable) are the idiomatic, more readable forms for building sequences, and noqa suppressions should be reserved for cases where the linter is genuinely wrong; tuple() around a generator adds noise when no immutability/hashability is needed, while tuples correctly signal fixed read-only constants.
common_pattern: Python collection-construction idioms: choosing between list comprehensions, generators, and tuple()/list() wrapping, and when tuples are appropriate for fixed constants — all sharing the principle of using the most idiomatic construct for the actual use of the collection.

text: Use dict.setdefault(key, value) instead of a manual `if key not in d` check before assignment, and initialize a mapping whose values are always lists with collections.defaultdict(list) rather than repeated .setdefault(key, []) calls. However, do NOT use defaultdict for a pre-built lookup mapping that may be queried with unknown keys during normal matching — it silently inserts missing keys and grows unbounded; use a plain dict and non-mutating access (e.g. .get) instead.
reason: Covers the insertion/initialization side of the dict idiom while preserving the explicit complementary-half caveat: defaultdict is right when every accessed key should exist, wrong when misses are a normal non-mutating query path.
common_pattern: Idiomatic Python dictionary access and initialization: pick the lookup primitive (direct indexing, dict.get, try/except KeyError) based on whether the key is contractually required, optional, or exceptional, and use setdefault/defaultdict for conditional insertion while avoiding defaultdict for read-only pre-built mappings.

text: In Wagtail admin reports, use existing denormalized model fields (e.g., `Page.owner`, `Page.latest_revision_created_at`) and nested template attribute access (e.g., `page_type.last_edited_page.owner`) directly instead of deriving values via `PageLogEntry` subqueries or adding dedicated Python properties; ensure column headers match the field's actual meaning, and only include columns that are part of the report's intended data set.
reason: Reduces query cost (avoids correlated subqueries), eliminates redundant annotations and properties, and prevents misleading column labels by aligning them with the underlying field semantics. Keeps reports focused on their intended data.
common_pattern: In Wagtail admin reports, leverage existing direct model fields and nested template attributes instead of deriving data via PageLogEntry subqueries or adding dedicated properties/columns; keep column labels accurate and omit data not intended for the report.

text: Extract only stable, reusable data mappings (e.g. id-to-object lookups); keep surrounding branching and control-flow logic inline. Before collapsing or simplifying an existing mapping to direct indexing, verify whether it encodes fallback semantics (deleted records, missing values) and preserve them unless the producing source (e.g. an aggregation method) guarantees all keys are present — in which case remove the now-redundant missing-key fallbacks.
reason: Mappings in reports often encode null/deleted handling that is easy to lose when 'simplifying', while prematurely extracting single-use control flow adds indirection. Stable data mappings are safe to extract; fallback-aware lookups should only be collapsed once the source guarantees key presence.
common_pattern: When deciding whether to extract or simplify a mapping/lookup table, the key criterion is whether the indirection carries behavioral semantics (fallbacks for missing/deleted values, control flow) versus being a stable reusable data mapping.

text: In Django code, when only a foreign key's ID, presence, or identity is needed, use the foreign key's ID column/accessor (e.g. `<field>_id`, `get_<relation>_id()`) instead of dereferencing the related object (e.g. `field.pk`, `field`, `get_<relation>()`). This applies in ORM queries, templates, loops, queryset iteration, nullable checks, and Subquery annotations. Avoid relation traversal unless the relation has already been eagerly loaded via `select_related()`/prefetching. For Subquery annotations, select the FK's `_id` field and/or set `output_field` to the target field type so the annotation returns the expected model value.
reason: Django automatically stores foreign key IDs on the model instance and in the database. Reading those IDs directly avoids extra database queries, N+1 behavior, and unnecessary object materialization.
common_pattern: Django ORM: when only a foreign key's ID, presence, or identity is needed, prefer the FK ID column/accessor instead of dereferencing the related object, to avoid unnecessary queries and N+1 problems.

text: In Wagtail admin UI, avoid naming configurable external providers (e.g., Gravatar) in user-facing labels; use provider-agnostic wording such as 'Reset to default' so labels remain accurate when the provider is swapped or disabled via settings like WAGTAIL_GRAVATAR_PROVIDER_URL.
reason: Users do not need to know which external provider is used, and provider-specific labels become inaccurate when site owners replace or disable that provider through configuration.
scope: Wagtail admin templates and UI strings
common_pattern: Wagtail admin avatar handling: provider-neutral UI copy and explicit data passing in templates

text: Use `issubclass(model, BaseClass)` to test class inheritance instead of manually inspecting the MRO with `inspect.getmro()` or checking `_meta.parents`/`get_parent_list()`; when iterating over candidate models, pass the loop variable (not the base class constant) to any MRO check.
reason: `issubclass` is a built-in, clearer, and less error-prone way to test inheritance, and it covers both the equality and descendant cases without relying on Django internals; manual MRO checks are prone to subtle bugs like passing the wrong class.
common_pattern: Correct use of Python class-introspection predicates (`issubclass`/`isinstance`) in Django-style code: (a) they must be guarded against `None` inputs that raise `TypeError`, and (b) they should be preferred over manual MRO/parent-list inspection.

text: When removing a template block or context variable that is no longer used (including blocks whose only consumers were deleted templates), also delete its corresponding entry from the template's documentation comment so the docs stay in sync with the blocks/variables the template actually supports.
reason: Unused template blocks and variables are dead code, and leaving their documentation behind is misleading and makes future cleanup harder; template docs must reflect what the template actually supports.
common_pattern: Dead-code cleanup in shared templates: removing template blocks/variables that are no longer used (including those whose only consumers are deleted templates) must be paired with removing their corresponding entries from the template's documentation comment.

text: When a filter/context value is used only to affect a template message or link display in an admin view, derive just that specific value (from the object, or by checking whether the parameter is present in `request.GET`) instead of fetching the referenced object or forwarding all current GET parameters via `querystring`.
reason: Avoids unnecessary database queries and unintentionally preserving unrelated or unsafe query parameters; simpler and more future-proof.
scope: Wagtail admin chooser/listing views and templates where filter values are display-only
common_pattern: All generalizations concern how admin/chooser listing views handle filter state: keeping filter UI consistent (empty states, active-filter labels), keeping filtering logic consistent across sibling views, and avoiding over-fetching/over-forwarding when the filter value is only used for display.

text: Empty-state/no-results messages in generic chooser and listing UIs should use consistent, neutral, result-oriented wording (e.g. 'There are no results') and follow existing translatable-block/template conventions rather than one-off filter-specific or app-specific variants.
reason: Consistent and neutral empty-state copy avoids misleading creation-oriented or filter-specific messaging, keeps translations predictable, and prevents UI drift across admin chooser and listing templates.
common_pattern: Empty-state/no-results messaging in Wagtail generic chooser and listing UIs: keep user-facing copy consistent, neutral, and translatable, and expose message customization through overridable view methods rather than divergent templates or one-off filter-specific wording.

text: When writing custom form clean() methods in Django, keep validation logic explicit and consistent: add a brief comment for cross-field conditional requirements, use Django's standard required error message (e.g., 'This field is required.'), and remove redundant clean_<field> methods when field inclusion is already controlled by dynamic form construction and no additional validation is required.
reason: Improves maintainability, aligns with Django conventions, and prevents dead or duplicated validation code.
common_pattern: Ensuring correctness and consistency in Django form validation logic, particularly around field name references and clean method implementation.

text: Keep breadcrumb URL-resolution logic centralized in the shared breadcrumb template and keep it generic: use URL name references (e.g., `wagtailsnippets:index`) to link to parent index views instead of reusing another view's breadcrumb items, and avoid adding view-specific special cases (such as `page_to_move`) to the shared template.
reason: Centralizes breadcrumb construction, avoids duplication, and prevents specialized behavior from leaking into reusable components while keeping callers simple and consistent.
common_pattern: Centralize breadcrumb URL-resolution logic in a shared generic template, avoid view-specific special cases, and reference parent index views by URL name rather than reusing other views' breadcrumb items.

text: When refactoring date/time formatting helpers, preserve existing special-case branches in their original scope rather than relocating or broadening them to cover adjacent edge cases.
reason: Maintains the original behavior and avoids unintended semantic changes to edge-case handling such as midnight or same-date cases.
common_pattern: Use established, localized date/time formatting primitives in Wagtail/Django UI instead of ad-hoc raw, hard-coded, manually marked-up, or translated date rendering.

text: In component/global SCSS, apply layout and alignment styles (e.g. vertical alignment, positioning) to the container/pattern element rather than to the interactive link or button itself, and position action buttons independently of adjacent text flow so their alignment stays stable when nearby text wraps to multiple lines.
reason: Keeps alignment as a layout concern on the container, avoids coupling presentation to the interactive element, and prevents buttons from shifting when row text wraps — which is common and otherwise makes the layout look inconsistent or broken.
common_pattern: CSS layout/display decisions for interactive controls (buttons, links) should be made deliberately to match their layout context: alignment belongs on the container/pattern element, and the `display` value should reflect whether the control is intended to sit inline or as a block.

text: Choose the `display` value for interactive controls to match their intended layout: keep `display: inline-block` (or the browser default) for buttons/controls meant to sit inline with surrounding form content, and explicitly set `display: block` when an inline element such as a link is styled to appear as a block-level component so its focus outline matches the block layout.
reason: Forcing `block` on an inline-intended control pushes it onto its own line and causes layout regressions, while leaving a block-styled inline element as an inline box produces a mismatched focus outline. Matching `display` to the intended layout keeps controls aligned and their outlines correct.
common_pattern: CSS layout/display decisions for interactive controls (buttons, links) should be made deliberately to match their layout context: alignment belongs on the container/pattern element, and the `display` value should reflect whether the control is intended to sit inline or as a block.

text: Set line-height with unitless values (e.g. `1.5`) chosen for the element's own typography, and avoid explicit `line-height` declarations unless necessary — rely on inherited/default line heights where possible.
reason: Unitless line-height scales against the current element's font-size (respecting component typography and user font-size settings), while absolute units tied to the root font size produce oversized or inconsistent spacing. Avoiding unnecessary explicit line-height reduces cascade/inheritance complexity.
common_pattern: Typography in SCSS/CSS must be driven by the design system's central theme tokens (font-size scale, font-weight) rather than hardcoded values, with type classes keeping color inheritable and line spacing relative to the element's own font size.

text: In Python files, follow PEP 8/Black blank-line conventions: use two blank lines around top-level function and class definitions and between top-level definitions/classes; use one blank line between methods or definitions inside a class; use at most one blank line to separate logical sections inside function/method bodies; and do not add a blank line immediately after a class/function header before its body. Keep files compliant with flake8 blank-line checks when editing imports or cleaning up code.
reason: Consistent vertical whitespace matches PEP 8 and project formatting conventions, improves readability, avoids noisy diffs, and prevents style-checker/CI lint failures.
common_pattern: PEP 8 / Black blank-line conventions for Python files, including top-level definitions, class bodies, and function/method bodies.

text: When assembling a message via implicit string concatenation, end any segment that is followed by a segment beginning a new word or sentence with a trailing space so the resulting message reads correctly.
reason: Prevents adjacent words from running together in implicitly concatenated string literals.
common_pattern: String composition from optional/multiple fragments should be done linearly (list + join, or single f-string + strip) rather than via conditional branching per combination or via a dedicated helper method.

text: In `wagtailsettings/edit.html`, when a site-scoped setting is editable for only one site by the current user, render the site name as read-only context instead of rendering `SiteSwitchForm` as a `<select>`.
reason: A site selector with a single meaningful option implies a choice that does not exist, but the site name is still useful context for disambiguating which site the setting applies to.
common_pattern: Correctly preserving site context when editing Wagtail site-scoped settings: reusing the canonical edit-URL helper (with the site pk) for post-save redirects, and showing the site name rather than a single-option site switcher.

text: Wagtail admin dropdown behavior should live in the shared dropdown initializer in `client/src/entrypoints/admin/core.js` (`$('.dropdown').each(...)`) and be extended there, and should be applied narrowly to only the dropdowns that need it (e.g., the Tippy plugin only on the header dropdown, `hide_on_click=True` only for modal-launching buttons) rather than adding one-off scripts or applying behavior to all dropdowns.
reason: Centralizing avoids duplicated one-instance dropdown logic, and scoping narrowly avoids side effects that other controllers must work around and preserves dropdown accessibility behavior.
scope: Wagtail admin client JS / dropdown component
common_pattern: Wagtail admin dropdown behavior/maintenance conventions: keep behavior centralized in the shared dropdown code path and apply it narrowly to only the dropdowns that need it, rather than duplicating or over-applying; new component variants should be disambiguated in naming.

text: When defining `UniqueConstraint.fields` (or similar ordered constraint arguments), use an ordered sequence (tuple or list) rather than a set literal so migration autodetection sees deterministic ordering and does not generate spurious migrations.
reason: G15 identifies a distinct deterministic-ordering requirement for constraint definitions (PR#12983, single-PR but clearly distinct sub-pattern).
common_pattern: Managing Django constraint migration from legacy `Meta.unique_together` to modern `Meta.constraints`/`UniqueConstraint` — careful sequencing, backward compatibility, avoiding spurious migrations, and preferring the modern API.

text: For dropdown/popover components, implement closed-state hiding with transition-friendly CSS: avoid `visibility: hidden` as the closed-state mechanism because it prevents fade-out; prefer `opacity` plus `pointer-events: none`, and use `[hidden]`-based selectors (e.g. `:has(:not([hidden]) > ...)`) for end-of-transition styling instead of immediate `[data-state]` attributes to avoid flashes/layout shifts.
reason: `visibility: hidden` toggles rendering immediately and cuts off opacity transitions, while `[hidden]` is applied after the exit transition and more closely matches stable end-of-transition behavior.
common_pattern: Dropdown/popover visibility behavior should preserve transitions and remain accessible, rather than using abrupt hiding mechanisms or pointer-only dismissal.

text: Remove translatable strings that are no longer consumed — e.g. obsolete `_()` entries in i18n lists or unused `_()`/default strings on components (such as `aria-label` defaults) — rather than leaving dead translatable entries.
reason: Unused translatable strings add translation maintenance overhead and i18n debt without providing runtime value.
common_pattern: i18n/translation hygiene in Wagtail: translatable strings and their generated catalogs must be kept in sync with source, and dead translation entries should be pruned.

text: Keep SVG icon `<path>` attributes on a single line rather than wrapping each attribute onto its own line.
reason: Matches existing formatting conventions of the icon set, keeps icon files compact, consistent, and easy to diff.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns concern SVG `<path>` elements: one about correct data serialization for the `d` attribute, the other about compact markup formatting.

text: When adding or maintaining multiple rendering implementations of a component (e.g., a custom icon branch, or a server-rendered template alongside its JavaScript counterpart), preserve existing accessibility attributes and conditional wrappers (such as aria-hidden or visually hidden title text) across all variants.
reason: Alternate rendering paths can silently drop accessibility markup, causing regressions or divergent screen-reader behavior between implementations.
common_pattern: Accessibility consistency across component rendering variants: when a component has multiple rendering paths or implementations, they must preserve the same accessible markup and conditional wrappers.

text: When serializing query parameters with `urlencode` (including when round-tripping values from `parse_qs()`), pass `doseq=True` so sequence/multi-valued parameters are emitted as repeated keys instead of being rendered as a bracketed array string. Do not manually collapse parsed lists to scalars first.
reason: `parse_qs()` returns values as lists; plain `urlencode()` corrupts them into `['value']`-style strings. `doseq=True` preserves repeated-parameter semantics, avoids lossy manual list handling, and keeps the code simpler.
common_pattern: Use the standard library's encoding helpers (urlencode with doseq=True, QueryDict.urlencode()) to serialize/round-trip multi-valued query data, rather than manually reducing sequences to scalars or hand-rebuilding dict-of-lists structures.

text: For session-backed Django `QueryDict` data, serialize with `QueryDict.urlencode()` and deserialize by constructing a `QueryDict` from that encoded string, instead of converting to a plain dict of lists and rebuilding with `setlist()`.
reason: URL-encoded strings are more compact in session storage, faster to serialize/deserialize, and avoid brittle manual reconstruction code.
common_pattern: Use the standard library's encoding helpers (urlencode with doseq=True, QueryDict.urlencode()) to serialize/round-trip multi-valued query data, rather than manually reducing sequences to scalars or hand-rebuilding dict-of-lists structures.

text: In Wagtail admin templates, apply `|unlocalize` to any numeric value that will be machine-consumed (IDs, primary keys, hidden form field values, checkbox `id`/`value` attributes). Do not use locale-aware formatting filters such as `|intcomma`, which would render IDs above 1000 as `1,234` and break round-tripped submissions or programmatic comparisons.
reason: Locale-specific number formatting inserts group/decimal separators and other characters, corrupting values that are submitted back to the server, compared programmatically, or used as DOM identifiers. `|unlocalize` emits the raw, unformatted value at the template boundary.
common_pattern: Machine-consumed numeric values (IDs, primary keys, hidden form field values) rendered into Wagtail admin templates must not pass through locale-aware number formatting; the non-localization guard should be applied once, at the template boundary, via the `|unlocalize` filter.

text: Apply the non-localization guard exactly once: prefer `|unlocalize` in the template and remove the now-redundant `str()` cast on the same value in the Python context builder (e.g. chooser/editing-session modules).
reason: Duplicating the guard in both Python and the template obscures where non-localization is enforced and can cause redundant or inconsistent behavior (e.g. when both survive a merge). The template filter is the canonical enforcement point because it also covers values that reach the template by other paths.
common_pattern: Machine-consumed numeric values (IDs, primary keys, hidden form field values) rendered into Wagtail admin templates must not pass through locale-aware number formatting; the non-localization guard should be applied once, at the template boundary, via the `|unlocalize` filter.

text: When multiple `PageLogEntry.objects.log_action()` calls differ only by their `action` value, compute `action` conditionally and make a single `log_action()` call instead of duplicating the full call.
reason: Reduces duplicated logging logic, keeps the shared payload in one place, and makes future changes to the log event less error-prone.
common_pattern: Design conventions for Wagtail's audit-log action taxonomy and logging behavior: how actions are named (hierarchical dotted identifiers reflecting the true operation), when to emit separate log entries, when to reuse existing action identifiers rather than spawn parallel variants, and keeping the action reference documentation in sync.

text: Use the project's established breakpoint scale (avoid one-off breakpoints) and keep breakpoint tokens in sync with canonical values; validate responsive changes that mix ratio-based and fixed units across viewports from the relevant breakpoint upward.
reason: Mixed proportional and fixed calculations can behave unexpectedly at viewport extremes, and using non-standard breakpoints or diverging token definitions causes responsive inconsistencies and token drift.
common_pattern: Maintaining consistency in responsive breakpoints and their token definitions across the codebase.

text: When removing a file or module, complete the cleanup: delete the file if it becomes empty, orphaned, or unused, and remove all lingering references to removed files from configuration and ignore files, including hidden files (e.g., .eslintrc.js) and sibling ignore files (e.g., .eslintignore).
reason: Partial removals leave dead code, stale lint/ignore exemptions, and misleading references that confuse developers and tooling.
common_pattern: Complete repository cleanup after file/module removal: eliminate orphaned or empty files and remove all stale references to deleted files from configuration, lint, and ignore files.

text: Scope SCSS layout/width overrides for side-panel/minimap states to the relevant UI state classes (e.g., `.side-panel-open`, `.minimap-open`) and the `.content` ancestor/descendant pattern (e.g., `.side-panel-open .content .tab-content`, `.minimap-open .content .tab-content`) instead of global selectors or malformed selectors like `.content.tab-content`; use breakpoint mixins for responsive overrides and compound state selectors (e.g., `.side-panel-open.minimap-open`) when multiple states can apply.
reason: Generalizations 1 and 4 establish state-scoped responsive layout rules and simultaneous-state handling; generalizations 2 and 3 establish consistent `.content` ancestor/descendant scoping in the same file so layout compensation matches surrounding selectors and only applies inside the main content region. These are complementary halves of one selector-scoping principle.
common_pattern: SCSS layout/width overrides for side-panel/minimap UI states must be scoped correctly using state classes and DOM ancestry, rather than global selectors, malformed compound selectors, or component-only selectors.

text: Prefer standard unprefixed CSS properties and keyframes over vendor-prefixed or non-standard variants; do not hand-author vendor-prefixed duplicates for browsers outside the project's support matrix—rely on autoprefixing/build tooling for prefixes that are actually needed.
reason: Standard names are more maintainable and cross-browser; obsolete manual vendor prefixes add dead code and should be generated only when required by the supported browser set.
scope: CSS in templates and static styles
common_pattern: CSS compatibility and standardization: use standard/custom-property-aware CSS, avoid unnecessary or obsolete vendor-specific code and JS indirection, and document browser-specific behavior precisely.

text: Use CSS custom properties directly and sparingly: reference them in CSS rather than reading them through getComputedStyle(...).getPropertyValue(...) in JS solely to consume their values, reserve color/derivation helpers for runtime manipulation needs, and verify against the project's supported browsers with fallbacks where custom-property support is absent.
reason: CSS custom properties are for CSS styling; reading them in JS duplicates styling logic, runtime derivation should be limited to dynamic cases, and unsupported browsers such as IE11 need literal or compile-time fallbacks.
scope: CSS custom properties and client-side browser compatibility
common_pattern: CSS compatibility and standardization: use standard/custom-property-aware CSS, avoid unnecessary or obsolete vendor-specific code and JS indirection, and document browser-specific behavior precisely.

text: Prefer regex literals for static patterns; when a regex must be constructed dynamically, use the language's constructor idiom (e.g. `new RegExp(...)` in JavaScript). For regexes used in repeatedly executed code paths, define/compile them once at module level instead of recreating or recompiling them per call.
reason: Avoids unnecessary regex construction/recompilation overhead and lint suppressions; especially important in hot loops where per-call compilation/cache misses are costly.
common_pattern: Regex definition and usage hygiene: avoid unnecessary regex construction/recompilation and redundant capturing constructs, while keeping related regex definitions consistent.

text: Avoid whole-pattern capturing groups by default; use the full-match group (e.g. `match.group(0)`) or the original matched string when no real subgroup extraction is needed. However, when several related regexes live in the same module/ruleset, favor consistency with their shared syntax over local micro-optimizations that remove redundant characters.
reason: Redundant whole-pattern groups add overhead and mislead readers; consistent regex syntax makes related patterns easier to scan, compare, and maintain. The consistency exception handles the apparent tension between removing redundant groups and preserving a shared regex style.
scope: module-level for related regex definitions; otherwise global
common_pattern: Regex definition and usage hygiene: avoid unnecessary regex construction/recompilation and redundant capturing constructs, while keeping related regex definitions consistent.

text: In JavaScript, for own-property checks and object iteration, prefer modern prototype-safe constructs: use `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` instead of `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, key)` or `obj.hasOwnProperty(key)`, and use `Object.entries()`/`Object.keys()` with `for...of` or array methods instead of `for...in` with a `hasOwnProperty` guard. Do not add file-level `eslint-disable` comments to keep the legacy pattern; rewrite the code.
reason: Prototype-safe modern APIs avoid inherited-property bugs, verbose manual guards, and lint suppressions while improving readability and aligning with existing codebase patterns.
common_pattern: Use modern, prototype-safe JavaScript APIs for object own-property checks and property iteration instead of legacy `for...in`/`hasOwnProperty` patterns or lint suppressions.

text: In generated HTML/static markup, place block closing tags (e.g. `</tr>`) on their own line rather than trailing the preceding cell, matching the surrounding file format and keeping regenerated diffs clean.
reason: Consistency with existing markup formatting improves readability and avoids noise in diffs of generated output.
common_pattern: Valid HTML/XML template tag syntax: non-void elements require explicit closing tags, closing tags must not repeat attributes, every opening tag must be closed, and XHTML/ePub templates must self-close void elements.

text: When refactoring or reusing code that contains conditional logic or guards, ensure the conditions are appropriate for the new context: reuse existing guard helpers instead of duplicating checks, preserve required guard clauses (e.g., None checks) when extracting logic, and remove conditionals that are unreachable or were only context-specific optimizations.
reason: Dropping necessary guards can introduce runtime errors, while keeping unnecessary ones adds dead code and misleading behavior; aligning conditionals with the new context maintains correctness and clarity.
common_pattern: Correct handling of conditional logic (guards, checks) when refactoring, extracting, or reusing code across contexts: reuse existing checks, preserve necessary guards, and remove unreachable or context-specific conditions.

text: When building a dictionary in Python, prefer a dictionary comprehension (`{k: v for ...}`) or a dict literal (`{...}`) over the `dict(...)` constructor wrapping a generator and over an explicit `for` loop with an accumulator. This applies whether mapping from a predefined list of keys or filtering/mapping an iterable.
reason: Comprehensions and literals are more concise, declarative, idiomatic, and often faster than imperative loops or `dict()` constructor wrapping.
common_pattern: Preferring idiomatic, purpose-specific dictionary idioms in Python (dict comprehensions, dict literals, `.copy()`, and direct keyword arguments) over the general-purpose `dict(...)` constructor and manual accumulator loops.

text: When you already have a dict, make a shallow copy with `.copy()` rather than wrapping it in `dict(...)`. Reserve `dict(...)` for converting a non-mapping iterable of key/value pairs. Likewise, when constructing an object from another instance's fields, pass the fields directly as keyword arguments to the constructor instead of building a temporary dictionary solely to unpack with `**`.
reason: `.copy()` explicitly expresses copy intent and is faster, while passing fields directly avoids pointless indirection and allocation for temporary dictionaries.
common_pattern: Preferring idiomatic, purpose-specific dictionary idioms in Python (dict comprehensions, dict literals, `.copy()`, and direct keyword arguments) over the general-purpose `dict(...)` constructor and manual accumulator loops.

text: In HTML templates, when an element has both an `aria-label` and a `class` attribute, place `aria-label` before `class` and keep the opening tag on one line when it fits within the project's line-length limits.
reason: Maintains consistent attribute ordering, makes accessibility metadata prominent, and avoids unnecessary line breaks in template elements.
common_pattern: Best practices for handling accessibility attributes (e.g., `aria-label`, `id` on labels) in HTML/Django templates, covering documentation of non-obvious attributes, ensuring valid (non-empty) values in reusable partials, and consistent attribute ordering.

text: In class bodies, place class-level configuration attributes/properties (including `static` members) together near the top before method definitions, rather than interleaving them between methods, and insert a blank line between the static configuration block and the following documented instance property declarations (`declare`/typed fields).
reason: Keeps class configuration discoverable and predictable, and visually distinguishes static configuration from instance state.
common_pattern: Class-body organization: keep class-level/static configuration grouped near the top of the class and visually separate it from instance property declarations.

text: Never nest `<form>` elements: invalid HTML5 causes browsers to silently drop or reparent the inner form. When a component must appear inside a parent form (e.g. page editor footer actions) or pulls in a partial containing its own `<form>` (e.g. via `{% include %}`), wrap it in a non-form container such as `<div>` or move the include outside the surrounding `<form>`.
reason: Nested `<form>` tags are not permitted by the HTML5 spec; browsers silently drop the inner form, producing broken markup, incorrect submissions, and accessibility/output issues.
common_pattern: Avoiding nested `<form>` elements because they are invalid HTML5 and browsers drop/reparent them; use a non-form wrapper instead.

text: In the Wagtail admin UI, when adding or modifying message/notification/dialog panels—including new variants such as upgrade notifications—reuse the existing message styling conventions: apply a state class on the container (e.g., `.w-dialog` when `message_heading`/`message_icon_name` is present) to override close-button/icon colours to grey-600, and include forced-colors mode styling such as a bottom border matching existing success/warning/error messages.
reason: Ensures consistent visual appearance and accessibility behavior across all Wagtail admin message panel variants, including Windows High Contrast mode, and avoids ad-hoc styling that fails to target the correct element.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin UI message/notification/dialog panels must reuse existing styling conventions across variants and accessibility modes, including state-class-based color overrides and forced-colors mode borders.

text: Use modern CSS selectors (e.g. :has(), :focus-visible) only with confirmed fallbacks or when graceful degradation is non-critical; avoid relying on them for critical layout or functionality.
reason: Unsupported browsers may silently drop these selectors, breaking critical behavior unless fallbacks or safe degradation are verified.
common_pattern: CSS selector compatibility and modern-syntax conventions: ensuring selectors work across the supported range of browsers/test environments (fallbacks for modern selectors like :has()/:focus-visible), respecting test-runner (nwsapi) selector limitations, and using standard modern CSS syntax (::before/::after).

text: Use double-colon syntax (::before, ::after) rather than single-colon (:before, :after) for CSS pseudo-elements.
reason: Double-colon is the modern CSS3 standard and distinguishes pseudo-elements from pseudo-classes.
