common_pattern: CSS selector compatibility and modern-syntax conventions: ensuring selectors work across the supported range of browsers/test environments (fallbacks for modern selectors like :has()/:focus-visible), respecting test-runner (nwsapi) selector limitations, and using standard modern CSS syntax (::before/::after).

text: When removing or relocating code from a file, also clean up artifacts left behind — including orphaned section headers/comment blocks that become empty, and leftover blank lines — rather than leaving dead documentation or visual noise.
reason: Residual headers and blank lines are dead documentation and visual noise; removing them keeps files clean, accurate, and diffs readable after cleanup.
scope: global (with specific relevance to settings/variable files, e.g. SCSS, where section headers can become orphaned)
common_pattern: When removing code from a file, also clean up residual artifacts that the removal leaves behind (orphaned section headers/comments, leftover blank lines) so the file stays tidy and accurate.

text: Derive count badges and their visual state from the same stable count value they display, not from indirect collection lengths or by scanning DOM elements/Stimulus targets — third-party UI libraries (e.g., Tippy) may detach or hide closed content, making those sources unreliable.
reason: When the displayed number and the state class come from different sources, or when the source is DOM that a library may clear, badges can silently disappear or show inconsistent state.
common_pattern: Deriving UI counts and state from a single stable source of truth — reusing an existing controller's built-in state/label features rather than ad-hoc templates, indirect collection lengths, or DOM scans that third-party libraries may invalidate.

text: In HTML table templates, structure-preserving markup is required: do not add duplicate or empty cell elements for layout (remove duplicated `<th>` headers; use `colspan` on the remaining content cell instead of empty `<td>` placeholders so content aligns with the table's left edge). When a cell must exist purely for visual alignment, mark it `aria-hidden="true"` and include an inline template comment explaining that the blank cell is intentional.
reason: Duplicate headers and empty placeholder cells misrepresent the table structure and confuse both assistive-technology and sighted users, while intentional layout-only cells must be explicitly documented and hidden from assistive technologies.
common_pattern: HTML table cell markup should faithfully represent the real table structure: redundant or empty structural cells (duplicate <th>, placeholder <td>) should be removed or replaced with colspan, and any cell that exists solely for visual alignment must be marked aria-hidden with an explanatory comment.

text: Before changing or reintroducing code, check git history (blame, commit messages, related tests) to understand the original intent and avoid regressions.
reason: Existing code often encodes undocumented rationale; changing it without understanding intent can silently break assumptions or reintroduce previously fixed bugs.
common_pattern: PR hygiene and deliberate code changes: keep changes minimal and scoped, verify historical context before modifying or reintroducing code, avoid PR-specific artifacts in comments, and ensure abandoned conventions are fully removed.

text: When abandoning a proposed convention, remove its introduced instances from all affected files in the same PR instead of leaving partial adoption.
reason: Prevents inconsistent conventions and accidental leftovers across related files.
common_pattern: PR hygiene and deliberate code changes: keep changes minimal and scoped, verify historical context before modifying or reintroducing code, avoid PR-specific artifacts in comments, and ensure abandoned conventions are fully removed.

text: Keep model/tree persistence explicit and isolated: preparation helpers that set insertion/move fields such as `path`, `depth`, or `numchild` must not call `save()`; `save_instance()` implementations should be self-contained with a clear ordered sequence of save steps and avoid cross-class or conditional indirection; document any conditional that depends on a non-obvious save/tree-state assumption, such as `path` being unset before the final save.
reason: Separating preparation from persistence avoids hidden database writes, makes save timing explicit, and keeps save-related logic self-contained and understandable. Documenting non-obvious lifecycle assumptions prevents future maintainers from moving logic too early or reintroducing unnecessary lookups.
common_pattern: Model persistence code should be explicit about when saves happen and how save-related state is prepared: keep preparation separate from persistence, keep save sequences self-contained and ordered, and document non-obvious save/tree-state assumptions.

text: When a single behavior applies to multiple form controls or selectors, define the selectors in an array and use event delegation with `event.target.matches(selector)` instead of binding each selector individually (and prefer this over adding new jQuery usage in touched code).
reason: Array-based delegation handles multiple similar controls consistently with one handler and supports the project goal of removing jQuery from touched code.
common_pattern: Choosing the right selector scope for front-end JS behaviors: bind to the semantic container/element that owns the behavior — precise enough to avoid affecting unrelated widgets (headers, other icons, other instances), yet anchored to a stable container class rather than an incidental tag — so the behavior is both safe and reusable.

text: Define constant lookup tables and mapping dictionaries (e.g., theme/option maps, operator mappings) as class-level constants — preferably `static` class properties declared with `as const` — rather than rebuilding them inside method bodies or per instance. Reference them from instance code via `(this.constructor as typeof ClassName).xOptions[key]` when TypeScript does not infer the concrete class for `this.constructor`.
reason: Centralizes constant configuration on the class, avoids per-call/per-instance object allocation, preserves literal types via `as const`, and keeps related constants grouped alongside existing class-level constants (e.g., `DEFAULT_OPERATOR`).
common_pattern: Constant lookup maps/dictionaries used for configuration (themes, operator mappings) should be hoisted to class-level constants (preferably `static` class properties) instead of being reallocated per instance or rebuilt inside each method call.

text: Do not render empty structural/optional elements (e.g., `<caption>`, `<col>`, `<td>`, subtitle/description blocks) as placeholders. Guard each such element with a conditional so it is only emitted when it carries content or when the underlying data is non-empty.
reason: Empty elements are semantically incorrect and add DOM noise, causing unexpected spacing, layout, and accessibility issues; conditionally rendering keeps output clean and aligned with view-layer logic.
common_pattern: Optional/structurally-conditional markup should be guarded by a conditional so empty elements (captions, columns, cells, descriptions, etc.) are never emitted into the DOM.

text: Choose the array iteration construct that matches intent: use `map` when building a new collection from each element; use `some`/`every`/`find` when the original loop used `return` to short-circuit or exit the enclosing function; use `forEach` or `for...of` only for pure side-effect iteration that must visit every element. Never rely on `forEach` to return a value or exit the outer function — it ignores callback return values.
reason: `map` expresses transformation and collects results; `some`/`every`/`find` preserve short-circuit and return semantics; `forEach` ignores callback returns and always visits every element, so using it where a result or early exit is needed silently changes control flow and produces incorrect behavior.
common_pattern: Selecting the appropriate array iteration construct based on intent (transformation vs. short-circuit result vs. pure side effect vs. property mutation), because each construct has distinct control-flow and linting semantics.

text: When iterating an array to mutate properties of its elements (e.g., DOM objects), prefer `for...of` or a plain `for` loop over `Array.prototype.forEach()`, because the `forEach` callback makes the mutated element look like a reassigned parameter to `no-param-reassign` and forces unnecessary `eslint-disable` comments.
reason: Avoids false positives from `no-param-reassign` and unnecessary lint suppressions when mutating element properties inside the iteration.
common_pattern: Selecting the appropriate array iteration construct based on intent (transformation vs. short-circuit result vs. pure side effect vs. property mutation), because each construct has distinct control-flow and linting semantics.

text: In test and Storybook example files that render anchors (including custom Link components), do not hardcode a dummy `href="#"` to satisfy `jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid`. Either bind a real URL (e.g. pass it through story args such as `args.url`, or use a shared URL variable / in-page fragment that matches an existing section `id`), or—when the custom link intentionally deviates from plain anchor semantics—suppress the rule with a file-level `/* eslint-disable jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid */` comment instead of adding a fake `href` or changing component behavior.
reason: Bare `#` hrefs fail anchor-validity linting and produce non-functional, ambiguous links; forcing `href` onto a component that intentionally handles navigation differently misrepresents its behavior and only superficially satisfies the linter.
scope: test files and Storybook `.stories.tsx` files rendering links
common_pattern: Handling anchor links in test/Storybook example files: never hardcode a dummy `href="#"` merely to satisfy `jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid`; instead either supply a real URL (e.g. via story args / shared variable) or explicitly suppress the lint rule with justification when the custom link intentionally deviates from plain anchor semantics.

text: Do not copy, unpack-and-rebuild, or re-iterate a list when no transformation is needed; pass the original iterable (or rely on `+` concatenation, which already returns a new list) directly to the downstream API, and remove no-op branches.
reason: Avoids unnecessary allocations and redundant passes over the same data, prevents divergence between a copy and its source, and removes dead code, keeping data flow clearer.
common_pattern: Avoid redundant list copying, unpacking-and-reconstructing, or re-passing when passing the original iterable (or using `+` concatenation) already suffices — eliminates allocations and dead code.

text: Order operands in compound boolean conditions deliberately: place the cheapest, most-selective, or gating check (in-memory lookup, feature-flag/global gate, bound-state check) first so short-circuit evaluation avoids expensive database/cache/subscript operations and reduces the chance of raising on later operands.
reason: Boolean operators short-circuit, so evaluating a cheap or gating condition first skips unnecessary expensive lookups and makes the intent (e.g. feature disabled → shortcut disabled) clearer.
common_pattern: Deliberate ordering of operands within compound boolean conditions — ordering cheap/gating checks first to exploit short-circuit evaluation, and keeping flag order consistent across related expressions for readability

text: When a guard clause checks multiple boolean flags and reuses those flags to build an error/message array, keep the flags in the same order across the declarations, the guard condition, and the message array.
reason: Consistent ordering reduces cognitive load and makes each error message easier to match to its corresponding condition.
common_pattern: Deliberate ordering of operands within compound boolean conditions — ordering cheap/gating checks first to exploit short-circuit evaluation, and keeping flag order consistent across related expressions for readability

text: When overriding a Django CBV lifecycle method such as `form_valid`, delegate to `super().form_valid(form)` and augment its returned response rather than re-implementing the parent's login/redirect/success logic inline. Call `super()` before mutating session state (e.g., setting expiry for 'remember me'), because the parent login flow resets the session and calling `super()` afterwards discards the customization.
reason: Reusing the parent avoids duplicated logic and imports, keeps behaviour consistent with upstream, and makes overrides resilient. Ordering `super()` first is required when the parent resets session state; otherwise the custom session logic is overwritten.
common_pattern: Django class-based view (CBV) conventions: when converting function-based views to class-based views or extending framework CBVs, follow the framework's idioms (use generic base classes, conform to expected method signatures/`self.request`, override only needed hooks, delegate to `super()` and keep overrides minimal).

text: Do not use regex or format-sniffing to detect special value types (e.g., UUIDs); instead normalize values by converting both sides of a comparison or lookup to the same canonical type (e.g., `str()`), so format variations (uppercase, braces, urn prefixes, non-canonical forms) cannot cause mismatches.
reason: Format-based type checks are fragile and must anticipate every valid representation of a value, whereas normalizing to a single canonical type is simpler, more robust, and eliminates classification logic and type-coercion surprises.
common_pattern: Both generalizations come from the same review comment and express the same principle: instead of inspecting/classifying the shape of a value (e.g., regex-based UUID detection), normalize values to a common canonical type (e.g., `str()`) so that comparisons and lookups are like-for-like and robust.

text: In client SCSS, constrain form/component width using `max-width` on the canonical component class (e.g. `.w-form-width`, `.w-field`) rather than `width: 100%` or selectors scoped to DOM structure (e.g. `.content .tab-content`), so fields keep their intrinsic sizing until a limit is reached and the rule applies in all contexts.
reason: `width: 100%` forces every matching field to fill its parent and `.content .tab-content`-style selectors couple width control to DOM structure, causing unintended layouts in contexts like snippets or modals.
common_pattern: CSS/SCSS width handling for form components: constrain sizing with `max-width` on the canonical component class rather than `width: 100%` or DOM-structure-scoped selectors, and apply such fixes as minimal, additive declarations.

text: In CSS/SCSS, write selectors to be clear, consistent, and minimally specific: use the correct combinator for the intended element relationship, split selectors that target unrelated elements, apply readability simplifications uniformly across similar selectors, and move component-part rules outside parent container selectors to reduce unnecessary nesting/specificity.
reason: Unclear or inconsistent selectors are error-prone and harder to maintain; precise combinators, split selectors, consistent simplifications, and lower specificity make styles easier to understand, override, and evolve.
common_pattern: CSS/SCSS selector authoring should prioritize clarity, consistency, and minimal specificity by using correct combinators, splitting unrelated selectors, uniformly applying selector simplifications, and avoiding unnecessary nesting.

text: In `wagtailadmin_tags.py`, define keyboard shortcut entries as positional `(label, shortcut)` tuples (e.g. `(_("Save changes"), f"{KEYS.MOD} + s")`) rather than dicts with `label`/`shortcut` keys, and render the label in `keyboard_shortcuts_dialog.html` via `{{ category.1 }}`.
reason: Tuples reduce visual noise in long shortcut lists, and matching the template to the tuple-indexed structure prevents the rendered category label from being broken.
scope: Wagtail admin keyboard shortcuts dialog and its template tag data structure
common_pattern: Wagtail admin keyboard shortcut dialog conventions in `wagtailadmin_tags.py`/`keyboard_shortcuts_dialog.html` — covering data structure (tuple entries), completeness (preserve/no-duplicate), and grouping/ordering by scope and user intent.

text: Group keyboard shortcuts by user-facing purpose/scope rather than implementation details: put admin-wide/global actions (e.g. sidebar toggle, modal close, the `?` shortcuts trigger) under the common `actions-common` section and keep `actions-model` for model-specific actions only; order broad/common categories before more context-specific groups (e.g. 'Page editing actions'), and within a group order entries by UI prominence (most relevant first, navigation toggles last).
reason: Users look for shortcuts by intent and frequency, so grouping by scope/purpose and ordering by prominence improves discoverability and reduces cognitive load, avoiding confusing splits like separating link insertion from text formatting.
scope: Wagtail admin keyboard shortcut dialog grouping and ordering
common_pattern: Wagtail admin keyboard shortcut dialog conventions in `wagtailadmin_tags.py`/`keyboard_shortcuts_dialog.html` — covering data structure (tuple entries), completeness (preserve/no-duplicate), and grouping/ordering by scope and user intent.

text: Combine nested `with` statements that manage independent context managers into a single comma-separated `with` statement (e.g., `with a() as x, b() as y:`) instead of nesting separate `with` blocks.
reason: Reduces indentation levels, improves readability, and keeps the resulting diff smaller and easier to review, while preserving context-manager exit semantics.
common_pattern: Both generalizations prescribe collapsing nested `with` statements that enter independent context managers into a single comma-separated `with` statement to reduce indentation and shrink the diff.

text: In Wagtail SCSS, give form/action controls an explicit height using the shared `$text-input-height` variable when they render alongside text inputs, instead of relying on another control's default height; conversely, do not enforce identical dimensions between form controls (e.g., switches and checkboxes/radios) unless they appear together in the same form context.
reason: Explicit token-based sizing prevents controls from collapsing or shifting when optional adjacent controls change, while avoiding shared dimensions for controls that are never used side-by-side prevents unnecessary coupling and conflicts with control-specific DOM or design constraints.
common_pattern: Form control sizing in SCSS should be explicit and tied to shared design tokens when controls are rendered together, while avoiding implicit dimension coupling between controls that do not share a form context.

text: For icon-only buttons, use an icon whose action glyph is enclosed in a solid circle or square (e.g. a solid circle-arrow) rather than a bare arrow/action glyph.
reason: The enclosure signals an interactive button affordance rather than a static indicator or decorative arrow.
common_pattern: Visual consistency and design-hierarchy conventions for action buttons — sizing must be stable regardless of optional icons, shared utility classes should be reused, the primary action should be visually emphasized, and icon-only actions should read as interactive affordances.

text: When defining `data-w-kbd-key-value` shortcut bindings, use the modifier convention consistent with the rest of the project's bindings (e.g., `alt+]` rather than `mod+]`) so that no two features claim the same key combination.
reason: Shortcut bindings must not collide across the app; a single agreed modifier convention avoids conflicting registrations and keeps bindings predictable for users.
common_pattern: Keyboard-shortcut declarations in this project's controller/component system should expose shortcuts through the standard ARIA attribute `aria-keyshortcuts` on the interactive element that triggers them (as the single source of truth), with conditional element targeting instead of global scoping, and consistent modifier conventions to avoid collisions.

text: Keep admin client entrypoint files minimal and centralized: place required `window`/global registrations in `client/src/entrypoints/admin/core.js`, extract cohesive feature logic into dedicated modules instead of growing `page-editor.js`, avoid unnecessary `window` exposures, remove redundant entrypoint files after their globals are consolidated, and audit sibling admin entrypoints for duplicated code when removing shared behavior.
reason: This consolidates the repeated review guidance around admin entrypoints: avoiding redundant entrypoint files, preventing `page-editor.js` from becoming an oversized catch-all, eliminating dead global exports, and ensuring shared behavior is removed consistently across sibling entrypoints.
common_pattern: Admin client entrypoint organization: keep entrypoint files minimal and centralized, manage window/global registrations explicitly, and remove duplicate or unnecessary entrypoint code.

text: Put shared history/revision view UI (such as action columns and revision URL configuration) on the generic `HistoryView` rather than duplicating it in app-specific `HistoryView` subclasses, so generic models, pages, and snippets share one implementation.
reason: Reduces duplication, keeps behavior consistent across view types, and makes revision support automatically available for future mixin and ModelViewSet combinations.
common_pattern: Correct behavior and implementation of admin history/revision views: these views must reflect the *current* context (current page state, applicability of actions) rather than stale or irrelevant revision data, and shared revision UI should be centralized rather than duplicated.

text: For range filter widgets/adapters, label each bound explicitly: when inputs are stacked vertically avoid the default `RangeWidget` dash and use a `SuffixedMultiWidget` subclass with min/max placeholders (mirroring the existing date-range widget in `wagtail/admin/filters.py`), and when a bound is missing render an explicit neutral placeholder (not an empty string, and not error-like labels such as `N/A`; prefer conditional `from {start}` / `until {end}` labels when only one bound exists).
reason: Empty strings or a stray dash produce ambiguous displays like `42 -` or `- 1000`, obscuring which bounds are active; explicit placeholders keep range widgets consistent with existing date-range filters.
scope: Wagtail admin range filter widgets and adapters
common_pattern: Consistency rules for Wagtail admin range filters and their widgets/adapters: naming bounds to reflect inclusive/general range semantics, matching the filter class to the underlying field granularity, and rendering/labeling bounds explicitly rather than ambiguously.

text: In Wagtail admin UI editor code, required-field indicators (e.g., an asterisk next to a field label) must be consistent across all editor variants that render the same field. For the shared alt text field, either fix the required asterisk indicator in both the rich-text editor and `ImageBlockDefinition` in `image-chooser-modified.js`, or remove the broken rich-text asterisk code.
reason: The alt text field is shared between image chooser and rich text editors, so its required-state UI should behave identically in both contexts; this prevents inconsistent user cues and avoids leaving broken or partial UI code.
scope: Wagtail admin UI editor components and entrypoints, especially the alt text field in the rich-text editor and image chooser
common_pattern: Required-field indicators for shared fields must be rendered consistently across all editor variants; if an indicator is broken, either fix it in all relevant places or remove it.

text: For string-based model fields (CharField/TextField) in Django/Wagtail, avoid `null=True`; use `blank=True` (and `default=""`) so the empty string is the single representation of "no data". Detect unpopulated values by comparing against the empty/sentinel value (`field=''`) rather than `__isnull=True`, and when a field can legitimately be blank, fall back to a related non-empty value. Exception: a CharField that is both `unique=True` and `blank=True` still needs `null=True` to avoid unique-constraint violations on multiple blanks.
reason: Django's documented convention; avoids two ambiguous "no data" states (NULL vs empty string) and prevents incorrect detection of unpopulated values.
common_pattern: Choosing the correct sentinel for empty/missing values in Django/Wagtail code — the codebase consistently prefers explicit, unambiguous representations (empty string for string model fields and user-facing output; None only where a value is genuinely optional/absent).

text: Handle datetimes consistently by using timezone-aware values and ISO-8601 representations: normalize to aware datetimes before comparison, never compare naive and timezone-aware datetimes, prefer `.isoformat()` over manual `strftime()` for serialization/comparison, and in `freeze_time` tests encode the offset in the timestamp string (e.g., `"2020-07-01 12:00:00+09:00"`) rather than using `tz_offset`.
reason: Mixing naive and aware datetimes can silently evaluate False and cause logic to fall through to incorrect fallback output; manual `strftime()` formats are less canonical and error-prone; `tz_offset` is less intuitive and not portable to time-machine.
common_pattern: Consistent timezone-aware, ISO-8601 datetime handling: avoid mixing naive and aware datetimes, prefer canonical `isoformat()` serialization over manual format strings, and make test timezone offsets explicit in timestamp strings.

text: Avoid adding `z-index` or `isolation` unless explicit stacking-order control is required; if required, do not hard-code numeric values—define semantic z-index tokens centrally (e.g. in `client/tailwind.config.js` under `zIndex` and consume with `theme('zIndex.<token>')`, or shared Sass variables where applicable), preserve any intended derivation, and comment non-obvious uses.
reason: Unnecessary stacking contexts add complexity and unexpected layering. Centralizing required z-index values as semantic tokens or variables avoids magic numbers, keeps stacking order discoverable, and prevents values from drifting from related layer definitions.
scope: project-specific SCSS/Tailwind config in the Wagtail client
common_pattern: Deliberate z-index / stacking-context hygiene: avoid unnecessary z-index or isolation, and when stacking control is genuinely needed, use centralized semantic tokens or shared variables instead of hard-coded numeric values; document non-obvious cases.

text: In inline panel JS, access child data through an explicit contract exposed by the child (a dedicated marker such as `data-inline-panel-child`, a public method, or an event) and always scope DOM queries to the current child element (e.g., `currentChild.find(...)`) instead of using broad/negative selectors. Filter, count, or order child forms only via that marker so auxiliary elements (error messages, etc.) rendered in the same container are never mistaken for real children, and keep the marker accurate when children are deleted.
reason: Broad or negative selectors can accidentally match nested/descendant panels or auxiliary elements, causing the wrong panel's controls to be moved, updated, or deleted; wrapping the traversal in a shared, marker-based helper on InlinePanel keeps this contract in one place instead of leaking into subclasses like MultipleChooserPanel.
scope: wagtail/admin/static_src/wagtailadmin/js/page-editor.js and related inline panel controllers (InlinePanel, MultipleChooserPanel)
common_pattern: InlinePanel/chooser JS must treat the child-panel DOM as an encapsulated boundary: scope queries to the current child, address children through explicit contracts/markers rather than reaching into internals, and explicitly test the nested-panel edge case that exposes over-broad selectors.

text: When interpolating boolean context values into JavaScript (e.g., in an object literal), render them as unquoted JS boolean literals (`true`/`false`) instead of quoted strings. Acceptable idioms include a conditional block (`{% if value %}true{% else %}false{% endif %}`) or Django's `yesno` filter (`{{ value|yesno:'true,false' }}`).
reason: Avoids string-vs-boolean type mismatches in JavaScript consumers and prevents fragile comparisons like `opts.allowDuplicates === 'True'`. This ensures type correctness and cleaner client-side code.
common_pattern: Passing boolean values from server-side templates into JavaScript as unquoted boolean literals rather than quoted strings, using either conditional blocks or the yesno filter.

text: When flushing a batch based on a size threshold, compare with `len(batch) >= threshold` instead of `len(batch) == threshold`. An entry can add more than one unit (e.g. a page contributing multiple URLs), so an exact-equality check may never be true, letting the batch grow unbounded or never flush.
reason: Accumulated collections can grow by more than one element per iteration, so equality against the chunk size may be skipped entirely, leading to unbounded batches and backend rejections.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the identical correctness principle: when flushing an accumulator against a size threshold, use an inequality (`>=`) instead of exact equality (`==`) because entries can add more than one unit at a time and skip the trigger point.

text: Log only significant, actionable events: omit routine operational/progress messages or log them at DEBUG, and do not add log entries for derived or redundant data that is already captured elsewhere.
reason: Keeps production logs useful and low-noise by avoiding routine progress output and duplicate/derivable information.
common_pattern: Logging discipline: production logs should contain only meaningful, non-redundant events; routine/progress output and derived data should be omitted or lowered to DEBUG.

text: In `SiteManager`, use a single `SITE_CACHE` keyed by host+port that stores `Site` objects directly (removing any secondary ID-only cache and its indirection), and when caching the default `Site` store it under both the default key and its hostname+port key so subsequent host+port lookups hit the cache.
reason: Simplifies site lookup and cache invalidation (only one cache to clear) and avoids extra SQL queries when the default site is later fetched by host+port.
common_pattern: Wagtail `Site` resolution from a hostname: prefer the shared helper, validate that the resolved site actually matches the requested hostname (rather than silently accepting the default-site fallback), and cache site lookups under a single host+port key.

text: When embedding a regex pattern in a string literal, ensure backslashes survive the string-literal layer: use raw string literals in Python (e.g., r"\W+") or double backslashes in languages without raw strings (e.g., JavaScript `'\\d'` to produce pattern `\d`). Escape only regex metacharacters that need escaping; for example, `?` inside a character class like `[?&]` does not need a backslash. Escape literal dots as `\.` when the intent is to match a literal dot.
reason: Regex engines receive the string after string-literal escaping has already been processed. Missing or excessive escaping silently changes the pattern, while raw strings/doubled backslashes preserve intent and avoid invalid escape warnings.
common_pattern: Correctly escaping regex patterns when they are embedded in string literals: ensure backslashes survive the string-literal layer (Python raw strings or doubled backslashes in JS/other languages) and escape only the regex metacharacters that actually need it.

text: For border-radius in Wagtail admin SCSS, reuse existing `theme('borderRadius.*')` design tokens (e.g. `borderRadius.xl` for pills, `borderRadius.full` for circles) instead of hardcoded pixel values or newly added tokens.
reason: Keeps rounded/circular corner styling consistent with existing patterns and avoids arbitrary or duplicated values.
common_pattern: Border-radius styling in Wagtail admin SCSS should reuse existing design-token values (theme('borderRadius.*')) for consistency, rather than hardcoding pixel values or introducing new one-off tokens; shared shape styling belongs on base classes.

text: Place shared shape styling such as `border-radius` on the base indicator class, and reserve modifier classes for variant-specific properties like color and shadow.
reason: Shared shape behavior applies across all variants and avoids duplicating the same styling in each modifier.
common_pattern: Border-radius styling in Wagtail admin SCSS should reuse existing design-token values (theme('borderRadius.*')) for consistency, rather than hardcoding pixel values or introducing new one-off tokens; shared shape styling belongs on base classes.

text: Ancestor privacy dialog templates must not render their own `header`/`h1`; the dialog wrapper already provides the heading. Tests for these dialogs should assert the correct ancestor privacy template/message, the absence of a duplicate `header`/`h1` in the dialog HTML, and a link to the restricting ancestor's edit page.
reason: Prevents duplicate headings in ancestor privacy dialogs and ensures tests protect the intended dialog behavior.
common_pattern: Ancestor privacy dialog templates should not duplicate the dialog wrapper's heading, and tests should verify that no duplicate heading is rendered while also checking the expected privacy message and ancestor link.

text: For temporary file-like buffers that may contain large binary data, such as image or rendition processing, use tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile instead of io.BytesIO to avoid loading the entire content into memory.
reason: BytesIO keeps all data in memory, while SpooledTemporaryFile spills data to disk after a configurable threshold, reducing memory pressure for large files and matching existing rendition-resizing patterns.
common_pattern: Prefer tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile over io.BytesIO for temporary buffers that may contain large binary data, to avoid holding the entire content in memory.

text: Do not paper over unintended scrolling bugs with workarounds. Avoid forcing scroll position (e.g., calling `window.scrollTo` from component/init code on page load) and avoid capturing-then-restoring scroll position after a bug occurs; instead rely on native anchor scrolling and fix the underlying cause of the scroll.
reason: Forced scroll calls and capture/restore hacks conflict with native anchor/deep-link behavior and mask the real bug, producing fragile, hard-to-maintain code with unexpected side effects.
common_pattern: Handling browser scroll behavior without fragile workarounds: rely on native scrolling mechanisms or fix root causes, rather than forcing scroll positions or masking bugs, with any deferred scrolling using a reliably-tested timeout.

text: When deferring DOM scrolling after page load (e.g., `scrollIntoView` for `contentpath` targets), use a timeout of around 100ms; no timeout or smaller values proved unreliable for letting JS-rendered content resolve.
reason: Gives JS-rendered content time to finish rendering before scrolling to it; empirically, only ~100ms worked consistently.
common_pattern: Handling browser scroll behavior without fragile workarounds: rely on native scrolling mechanisms or fix root causes, rather than forcing scroll positions or masking bugs, with any deferred scrolling using a reliably-tested timeout.

text: When resolving `window.location.hash` (or any URL fragment) to a DOM element, prefer `document.getElementById()` over `document.querySelector()`. URL fragments are arbitrary strings that may not be valid CSS selectors (e.g. IDs starting with a digit), so `querySelector` can throw; `getElementById` performs a direct ID lookup and simply returns `null` when nothing matches, so only the leading `#` needs stripping and no character sanitization is required. If `querySelector` must be used (e.g. for generic HTMLElement typing), guard against the empty-and-invalid-selector case first, since `querySelector('#')` throws while `getElementById('')` safely returns `null`.
reason: Two PRs surfaced the same failure mode — `querySelector` parsing arbitrary fragments as CSS selectors — while the third comment established the exception (typed selection) and the exact failure it must guard against (empty hash producing `querySelector('#')`). The rule captures both the safe default and the compensating condition when the alternative API is chosen.
common_pattern: Resolving `window.location.hash`/URL fragments to DOM elements requires an API choice that is robust against arbitrary (possibly CSS-invalid or empty) fragment strings — `getElementById` is the safe default; `querySelector` requires extra guarding.

text: Use explicit escape sequences (e.g. `\0`, `\u00A0`) for invisible, non-printable, or non-ASCII characters in source string literals instead of embedding the literal characters, so the intent remains visible and robust against encoding, copy, merge, or editor issues.
reason: Literal invisible/control characters are hard to see, easy to lose or mangle in diffs and merges, and can cause encoding or editor problems. Explicit escapes are self-documenting and safer.
common_pattern: Use explicit escape sequences for invisible, non-printable, or non-ASCII characters in source string literals rather than embedding the literal characters.

text: Read `document.currentScript` at the top level of a browser entrypoint script during synchronous execution, never inside `DOMContentLoaded` or other later callbacks.
reason: The browser only exposes `document.currentScript` while the script is actively executing; by the time a deferred callback fires the value is `null`.
common_pattern: How browser entrypoint/page scripts should hook into DOM readiness: use a DOMContentLoaded-style ready listener (not window.onload/load), keep initialization code and helpers scoped inside the ready callback to avoid globals, and respect the synchronous-only availability of APIs like document.currentScript.

text: Keep component state lifecycle-clean: perform cleanup tied to a state transition in the state-change callback that deactivates the state (e.g., clear timers when `loading` becomes `false`), and remove state variables and associated error-state handling once no behavior references them.
reason: Prevents stale timers, misleading dead state, and contradictory async-operation logic, reducing maintenance burden.
common_pattern: State/lifecycle hygiene: avoid stale or dead component state by tying cleanup to the relevant state transition and removing state that no longer drives behavior.

text: Use a directional back-arrow icon rather than a cross/close icon for controls that navigate back from a nested submenu.
reason: A back arrow communicates returning to the parent menu, while a cross implies dismissing or closing the menu, which is misleading for nested navigation.
scope: UI convention for sidebar/menu components; conditional on nested submenu support.
common_pattern: Improving accessibility and UX of nested menu navigation controls by avoiding portalization that disrupts tab order, centralizing state to prevent duplicate controls, and using appropriate iconography for navigation semantics.

text: When a controller problem has already been solved by another controller, reuse or adapt that established implementation instead of introducing a new ad-hoc approach, and add a brief code comment referencing the existing implementation and clarifying any boundary or related behavior kept elsewhere.
reason: Preserves design intent, ensures consistency with existing project patterns, relies on proven implementations, and helps reviewers/maintainers understand where related functionality lives.
common_pattern: Reusing existing controller implementations and documenting the reference to avoid ad-hoc solutions.

text: When querying for the latest record(s) from the database, use efficient constructs: for a single latest record, order by descending timestamp and fetch one result (e.g., `.order_by('-created_at').first()`) instead of retrieving and iterating over all matching records; for the latest record per group, prefer window functions (e.g., Django's `Window` and `RowNumber`) over correlated subqueries with `OuterRef`.
reason: Prevents unbounded query work as data grows, avoids unnecessary processing, and improves readability and performance by using efficient database operations.
common_pattern: Efficient retrieval of latest database records, avoiding inefficient queries

text: In user-facing, translatable strings, use the Unicode ellipsis character (…) instead of three periods (...) and avoid hard-coded directional symbols like →; prefer RTL-aware, translatable representations such as icons or translatable strings.
reason: This merges the complementary requirements from the cluster: proper typography for ellipses and internationalization/RTL safety for directional symbols. Both principles apply to the same context (user-facing, translatable UI strings) and together form a consistent rule for string formatting.
common_pattern: Use typographically correct and localization-safe representations in user-facing, translatable strings (e.g., proper Unicode characters instead of ASCII approximations; avoid hard-coded directional glyphs).

text: In JavaScript, use strict equality operators (`===` and `!==`) instead of loose equality operators (`==` and `!=`) to avoid unintended type coercion.
reason: Strict equality avoids type coercion, making comparisons more predictable and reducing subtle bugs.
common_pattern: Improving readability and correctness of comparison expressions in boolean conditions.

text: In QuerySet proxy methods (and similar methods that clone/copy an object before returning), perform cheap argument validation and early-return/guard checks before calling `self._chain()` (or other cloning/copying), so invalid or no-op calls don't pay the cost of an unused clone.
reason: Cloning the queryset is only useful when the method actually returns a modified clone; if a preceding guard raises or returns early, the clone is wasted work. Ordering validation before cloning avoids unnecessary allocations on error and no-op paths.
common_pattern: In QuerySet proxy methods, guard/validation checks (e.g., `if not lookups`) should run before `self._chain()` so the queryset is only cloned on paths where the clone is actually used, avoiding wasted allocation on error/no-op paths.

text: When accumulating tuple-valued attributes in QuerySet helper methods (e.g. on a `_chain()` clone, such as `_specific_prefetch_related_lookups`), prefer explicit concatenation (`attr = attr + values`) over augmented assignment (`attr += values`), because the operands may be tuples where `+=` fails.
reason: Augmented assignment reads naturally and matches the clone pattern, but it breaks for tuple operands; explicit concatenation keeps tuple handling correct across the supported argument types.
common_pattern: How to accumulate tuple-valued attributes (e.g., `_specific_prefetch_related_lookups`) on a cloned QuerySet within helper methods — augmented assignment vs. explicit concatenation.

text: When opening files, use the file mode that matches the content type: open text files in text mode and do not call `.decode()` on read results, because text mode already returns decoded `str`; open binary data such as images/renditions in binary mode (`'rb'`/`'wb'`) rather than text mode, because text mode may perform newline translation or encoding handling and corrupt binary output.
reason: Choosing the wrong file mode causes redundant or erroneous decoding and can corrupt binary data on platforms that translate newlines, such as Windows.
common_pattern: Correct use of Python file modes: match the mode to the content type and avoid redundant codec calls that text mode already handles.

text: Implement forced-colors / high-contrast accessibility styling at the correct scope: place forced-colors-only fixes inside `@media (forced-colors: active)` rather than in base styles. Inside that block, use system color keywords (e.g., `Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `ButtonText`, `Highlight`) for color properties, use `currentColor` for borders on non-interactive elements, and use `transparent` borders/outlines to preserve component boundaries, active/selected states, and silhouettes. Do not use `forced-color-adjust: none` unless you also explicitly provide appropriate system colors for every affected color property, and do not rely on custom color variables in forced-colors blocks unless `forced-color-adjust: none` is set. For non-focusable elements, prefer `outline` over `border` for transparent indicators to avoid layout shifts. Add high-contrast overrides only when the contrast difference clearly justifies them and when active/selected states remain distinguishable; if elements already use a shared token such as `border-furniture`, update the shared token rather than adding a component-scoped high-contrast override and a new token.
reason: Ensures UI remains usable and legible in Windows High Contrast Mode without breaking normal rendering or creating unnecessary design-token branches.
common_pattern: Forced-colors / Windows High Contrast Mode accessibility styling for UI components: scope overrides correctly, use system colors or transparent borders/outlines to preserve visibility, states, and shapes, and avoid fragile overrides such as forced-color-adjust:none or custom color variables without system-color fallback.

text: When matching a list of requested keys against a prefetched or related collection, build a lookup dictionary keyed by the match field before the loop (or split into two passes: first narrow to plausible matches, then do expensive per-item work like cache-key generation) instead of iterating the collection inside the loop.
reason: Avoids nested iteration and redundant expensive work (e.g., cache-key generation for items that cannot match), and makes the lookup logic clearer.
common_pattern: Performance-conscious iteration over collections in hot paths: build keyed lookups instead of nested loops, narrow before doing expensive per-item work, and prioritize these optimizations on user-facing/high-frequency code paths.

text: Prioritize hash and performance optimizations based on whether the code path is user-facing and high-frequency: optimize hot paths like redirect lookups even if the model seems small or internal, while lower-priority internal-only paths (e.g., the reference index) may not need the same optimization.
reason: User-facing paths can be exercised far more often than internal-only code, so the cost of hash conversion and similar operations has greater real-world impact there.
common_pattern: Performance-conscious iteration over collections in hot paths: build keyed lookups instead of nested loops, narrow before doing expensive per-item work, and prioritize these optimizations on user-facing/high-frequency code paths.

text: Verify spacing, padding, and offset changes in component SCSS at small/mobile viewport widths (and re-check padding after font-size increases), since tight viewports expose crowding that is not visible on larger screens; adjust with small spacing increments when components start to feel cramped.
reason: Spacing that looks correct on desktop can appear too tight on small devices or after larger fonts shrink perceived spacing; checking narrow viewports avoids shipping cramped layouts.
common_pattern: Responsive CSS spacing/alignment in component SCSS: verify spacing at small viewports and prefer intrinsic layout techniques over adding new breakpoints/media queries.

text: Interactive controls (buttons, bulk-action footer actions, filter/dropdown menu items) must be visually identifiable as interactive controls: give them a border or other non-color affordance, and use borders/colors with sufficient contrast (avoid low-opacity neutral borders like `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25)` and do not rely on text color alone). Dropdown/action-menu items should not use low-contrast tokens merely to de-emphasize secondary or destructive actions.
reason: Low-contrast borders and color-only differentiation weaken affordance, are inaccessible to colorblind users, and fail color-contrast requirements; confirmation flows (not visual de-emphasis) provide the safety for destructive actions. Distinct controls (e.g., filters vs. sort chevrons) need distinct styling so users can predict the action.
scope: global/component styling; buttons, listings, table headers, bulk-action footers, dropdown/action menus
common_pattern: Two related but distinct SCSS/style sub-patterns for interactive-control affordance: (a) buttons/actions in listing, table-header, and menu UI must remain visually identifiable as interactive controls — via sufficient-contrast borders or non-color affordances rather than low-contrast or color-only styling; (b) disabled button borders should adopt existing grey design tokens to signal the disabled state.

text: For disabled button icon-wrapper borders, use existing grey design tokens (e.g., `$color-grey-4`) instead of leaving the enabled border color unchanged, so the disabled state is visually clear using the established token palette.
reason: A muted token-based border makes the disabled state visually clear with minimal custom styling and keeps styling consistent with the design system's color tokens.
common_pattern: Two related but distinct SCSS/style sub-patterns for interactive-control affordance: (a) buttons/actions in listing, table-header, and menu UI must remain visually identifiable as interactive controls — via sufficient-contrast borders or non-color affordances rather than low-contrast or color-only styling; (b) disabled button borders should adopt existing grey design tokens to signal the disabled state.

text: When rendering option lists in compact controls, ensure the UI prevents overflow and truncation: for small fixed sets, prefer radio buttons over dropdown/select controls; for dynamic or variable-length lists, update the component CSS to handle overflow through wrapping, scrolling, or container constraints.
reason: Both generalizations address the same UX risk—option lists overflowing or requiring painful scrolling—and provide complementary solutions: control selection for small fixed sets, and defensive CSS for growable lists. Merging them yields a single actionable rule.
common_pattern: Defensive UI control design for option lists: choose the right control type and CSS handling based on option-set size to prevent overflow, truncation, and awkward scrolling.

text: Use native DOM/form-control state (e.g. `checked`, `selected`, or jQuery `:checked`) as the source of truth for selection/UI state; do not duplicate it in custom `data-*` attributes or parallel JavaScript state objects. When tracking selected elements, store the DOM element reference rather than a parsed dataset value.
reason: Native form state and DOM references stay in sync with the actual rendered controls, while duplicated custom data attributes or parallel JS state can drift, especially when defaults change or the browser restores form state during back/forward navigation.
common_pattern: Use native DOM/form-control state as the single source of truth for selection and UI state, avoiding duplicate state in custom data attributes, parallel JavaScript objects, or parsed dataset values.

text: Prefer color inheritance over redeclaring text colors: apply the color once on the common ancestor (e.g. `w-text-current` / `color: inherit` / `color: currentColor`) and let descendants inherit it, instead of repeating fixed color values or utilities on each child. When a component relies on inherited color, still explicitly set `color` in hover/focus/active states whose background contrast differs from the inherited context.
reason: Inherited colors stay consistent across a subtree, adapt automatically to light/dark mode, avoid redundant declarations that mask inheritance, and centralize theming changes. The exception for state backgrounds prevents unreadable interactive feedback where an inherited color would not contrast with a state-specific background.
scope: global; SCSS/CSS component styling (utilities like `w-text-*`, `color: inherit`/`currentColor`)
common_pattern: Styling rules governing how text/foreground colors relate to backgrounds in SCSS/CSS: prefer inheritance over redeclaration of colors, and keep contrasting foreground/background declarations co-located and conventionally consistent.

text: In flex layouts, set vertical alignment according to the content: use `align-items: center` to vertically center single-line content against a fixed-height sibling such as a button or dialog header, and use `align-items: flex-start` when a fixed-size icon/preview sits next to text that can wrap so the icon stays aligned with the first line. Remove child margins (e.g., title/subtitle `margin-bottom`) or set `height: 100%` on the centered item when needed so default spacing/height does not break the intended alignment.
reason: Flex vertical alignment depends on the item's box height, child margins, and whether adjacent text wraps. Centering works for single-line content, but wrapped text requires top alignment to keep icons/previews visually anchored; stale margins or missing height can leave items looking off-center.
common_pattern: Choosing and enforcing flex vertical alignment based on content shape: center single-line content against fixed-height siblings, but top-align fixed-size icons/previews when adjacent text can wrap; child margins/height must be adjusted to avoid breaking intended alignment.

text: Keep code and documentation examples CSP-compliant by avoiding `eval`, inline event handlers, and `javascript:` URLs; use external event listeners, data attributes, or nonce-friendly patterns instead.
reason: Inline and eval-based JavaScript can be blocked by Content Security Policy, and the project has deliberately removed such patterns to remain CSP-compatible. Documentation examples should model secure, modern implementation patterns so copied code works under a CSP.
common_pattern: Content Security Policy (CSP) compliance: avoid JavaScript execution patterns that CSP blocks, in both source code and documentation examples.

text: When writing raw HTML (test fixtures, code examples, docs), use the HTML `class` attribute — never `className`, which is JSX/DOM-only syntax and will be ignored by an HTML parser.
reason: Ensures class attributes actually apply when HTML strings are parsed, and keeps HTML examples valid, copy-pasteable HTML rather than JSX-specific syntax.
common_pattern: Correct attribute syntax when writing markup: use the right attribute name/syntax for the target language (HTML `class` vs JSX `className`) and avoid unnecessary expression syntax for static values in JSX.

text: In JSX, write static string props as string literals (e.g. `className="foo"`), not wrapped in expression containers (e.g. `className={'foo'}`).
reason: String literals are idiomatic JSX, avoid unnecessary expression syntax, and keep attribute values easier to read.
common_pattern: Correct attribute syntax when writing markup: use the right attribute name/syntax for the target language (HTML `class` vs JSX `className`) and avoid unnecessary expression syntax for static values in JSX.

text: Gate controller lifecycle methods that must not run until initialization is complete with an explicit readiness boolean (e.g., `isReady` / `this.ready`) set at the appropriate lifecycle point and an early-return guard, rather than using call-count-based wrappers such as `after(fn, n)`.
reason: Explicit readiness flags express intent directly, are more readable, avoid fragile reliance on invocation count/order, and match the codebase's established style; call-count-based helpers are obscure and harder to reason about if call sites change.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same principle: use an explicit readiness boolean flag (set at the appropriate lifecycle point) with an early-return guard to gate method execution after initialization, instead of relying on call-count/order-based helpers like `after(fn, n)`.

text: When a limit is specified in human units (e.g. "1MB"), express the constant in matching units (e.g. `1024 * 1024` or a named byte helper) rather than a bare number that encodes a different magnitude.
reason: Bare numeric size constants are easy to mis-scale (1KB vs 1MB); stating the unit explicitly prevents off-by-1000 errors.
common_pattern: Non-obvious numeric literals, limits, and thresholds must be self-documenting: either annotated with an inline comment explaining the rationale and stating the exact value in use, or expressed in units/named helpers that make the magnitude unambiguous.

text: In `TabsController` panel switching, preserve the original double-delay sequence: wait for the incoming panel's unhide transition before applying active animation classes, then wait again after applying them before completing the transition.
reason: The original tabs implementation intentionally applied the delay twice; skipping the first wait can change the animation behavior of the incoming panel.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin tab panel visibility and animation must be derived from the component's actual state (configured active class, ARIA attributes, or JS transition sequence) rather than static utility classes or generic transition attributes.

text: Pagination previous/next button labels must use the same text styling as the pagination page-number buttons, without extra span/b tags.
reason: Maintains typography consistency across related controls within the pagination component.
common_pattern: Pagination display behavior (number of visible page buttons/ellipses, hits per page, and text styling of controls) should be an intentional, explicit, and ideally configurable choice rather than hardcoded magic numbers or ad-hoc markup.

text: When an element can be conditionally hidden or omitted, keep its layout and spacing styling on a stable surrounding wrapper (or explicitly reset inherited spacing utilities such as `space-y-*` on the hidden child) so that toggling visibility does not introduce unwanted gaps or lost styling.
reason: Styling utilities like `space-y-*` still apply to `display: none` children, and classes placed on a conditionally rendered form disappear with it; anchoring the styling to a persistent wrapper (or neutralizing it on hidden children) keeps layout stable in both states.
common_pattern: Conditional visibility/rendering of content must not distort layout: styling utilities (spacing, layout, indicators) belong on a stable wrapper or must be explicitly reset so that hiding or omitting the inner element leaves surrounding layout intact.

text: Do not use `functools.partial` to wrap a call that is invoked immediately or whose arguments/method reference can be resolved at the call site; call the target directly instead.
reason: `functools.partial` is for deferring calls or reusing partially-applied callables. Wrapping an immediate or easily-resolved call adds indirection and obscures control flow without benefit.
common_pattern: Misuse of `functools.partial` as unnecessary indirection or as an inextensible wrapper; prefer direct calls when arguments are available and subclassable classes when downstream extension is required.

text: When adding a new declaration or block of code that parallels or relates to existing code, place it next to the related existing declaration/section and mirror the neighboring formatting, doc-comment, and section-comment conventions.
reason: Maintains internal consistency and keeps related code grouped, making symmetry and organization obvious to readers.
common_pattern: New code should follow the local structure of related existing code: place it adjacent to the related declaration/section and mirror the neighboring formatting and comment conventions.

text: Group related controller declarations into contiguous, ordered blocks by logical category (e.g., by declaration kind such as values/CSS classes/targets, or by mutability with readonly/immutable values first and mutable values separate), and refactor the whole block rather than editing individual lines.
reason: Consistent grouping and ordering makes controller declaration sections easier to review, understand, and maintain, while block-level cleanup avoids piecemeal edits.
common_pattern: Controller declarations should be organized into coherent, ordered blocks by logical category (such as declaration kind or mutability) to improve readability and maintainability.

text: In Wagtail admin templates, derive the document's `lang` and `dir` attributes from the active language (`{% get_current_language as LANGUAGE_CODE %}` and `{% get_current_language_bidi as LANGUAGE_BIDI %}`, after `{% load i18n %}`) instead of hardcoding `lang="en"` or adding a hardcoded `|default` fallback; `get_current_language` already falls back to `settings.LANGUAGE_CODE`.
reason: Hardcoded English locale/direction breaks localization and RTL rendering for non-English admin users, and redundant defaults like `en-gb` can diverge from the project's configured `LANGUAGE_CODE`.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin internationalization (i18n) patterns: how the admin derives/displays language and direction, how the permitted-language set is configured, and how language-related settings/thresholds must be documented and tested.

text: In multi-branch UI state handlers, keep each state's user-facing message/notification logic inside the if/elif branch that processes that state. If side-effect timing prevents this, refactor the message handling out so it can live with the corresponding state branch.
reason: Keeps state-specific behavior consistent and centralized, making control flow easier to follow and avoiding hidden coupling.
common_pattern: UI state-handling code should be disciplined: branches should exist only for states users can actually reach, and handling for each reachable state should be colocated in the branch that processes that state.

text: When a component exposes a helper that synchronizes field values to the current DOM order, all order-changing operations (move up, move down, drag reorder, etc.) must call that helper instead of reimplementing the order-sync logic. Refactor existing reorder operations (e.g. in `InlinePanel`, `client/src/components/InlinePanel/index.js`) to use it as the single source of truth.
reason: Prevents duplicated order-update logic, keeps behavior consistent across all reordering paths, and reduces maintenance burden.
scope: global for reorderable form/list components (e.g. InlinePanel)
common_pattern: Both sub-groups concern reordering operations and sort-order consistency, but they describe distinct aspects: (a) reusing an existing order-sync helper across client-side reorder paths instead of duplicating logic, and (b) correctly handling null/unset sort_order values in server-side reordering views so persistence is not skipped and duplicate sort_order values cannot occur.

text: Use `http.HTTPStatus` enum members (e.g. `HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST` instead of `400`, `HTTPStatus.GONE` instead of `410`) when returning or checking HTTP status codes in Python/Django view responses. Do not use `HTTPStatus` members for non-HTTP values such as domain identifiers or arbitrary integers (for example, image IDs in signatures) — use plain integers or domain-specific constants there instead.
reason: Enum constants are self-documenting and avoid magic numbers in HTTP response handling, improving readability and reducing errors. Conversely, reusing `HTTPStatus.OK` for a value that is not an HTTP status is semantically misleading and confuses readers about what the argument represents.
common_pattern: Appropriate use of the `HTTPStatus` enum for HTTP status codes in Python/Django code — using enum members instead of numeric literals, and restricting their use to genuine HTTP status semantics.

text: In the ComboBox component, use `-1` as the sentinel value for clearing `previewedIndex` (instead of `undefined`), and reset `previewedIndex` to `-1` whenever the search value becomes empty, not only during filtering.
reason: Maintains a consistent numeric index-sentinel convention, avoids invalid `undefined` assignments, and ensures any active preview is hidden when the search box is cleared.
common_pattern: Use a consistent numeric sentinel (-1) for ComboBox's previewedIndex and reset it to -1 in all conditions that clear the preview, including when the search value becomes empty.

text: In `Table` subclasses, only set attributes specific to that subclass; rely on the base class or mixin for shared attributes (e.g. orderable item identifiers) to avoid redundant assignments that duplicate and can drift from mixin behavior. For one-off variation such as a fixed `classname`, set it as a class-level attribute on the subclass instead of adding a single-use parameter to `Table.__init__`, reserving base constructor parameters for options that are broadly useful across multiple tables.
reason: Redundant overrides and single-use base constructor parameters add duplication, invite drift from mixin handling, and make the base class API harder to understand.
common_pattern: Design Wagtail admin table classes for maximum reusability: keep the base `Table` class lean and reusable, compose optional/conditional behavior via mixins applied at runtime (selected by the viewset), name and place classes by their true reusable scope rather than by viewset coupling, and keep subclasses limited to only their subclass-specific additions.

text: When refactoring component styles (extracting/renaming classes, adopting new naming conventions, or changing breakpoints), preserve the existing rendered dimensions, spacing, and responsive breakpoint rules; if a deliberate change is intended (e.g., a sm-to-md breakpoint shift), apply it consistently across all affected component style files rather than only the one in the diff.
reason: Prevents visual regressions and layout inconsistencies at responsive breakpoints during style refactors, and avoids reviewers having to flag dropped-but-still-required styles.
scope: component styles (SCSS partials under client/src/components and client/scss/components)
common_pattern: When refactoring component styles (extraction, renaming, breakpoint changes), preserve existing visual characteristics — spacing/dimensions and responsive breakpoints — and propagate deliberate changes consistently across all affected component files rather than only the file in the diff.

text: Before adding a new config entry or utility class, search the codebase for an existing equivalent; if an existing utility is close enough for the requirement, reuse it instead of introducing a new one.
reason: Avoids duplicate functionality, prevents CSS bloat, and keeps styling consistent with utilities already present in the codebase.
common_pattern: Reuse existing utility classes or config entries instead of adding redundant or near-duplicate definitions.

text: When composing Wagtail model mixins, use the canonical order: `WorkflowMixin`, `LockableMixin`, `DraftStateMixin`, `RevisionMixin`. This reflects the order in which they were introduced and ensures `get_lock()` precedence behaves as intended.
reason: Mixin order affects method resolution, especially for `get_lock()`, and the canonical order keeps Wagtail model composition consistent.
common_pattern: Wagtail model API/class conventions, with two distinct sub-patterns: preserving public re-exports from `wagtail.models` and maintaining canonical mixin ordering for model classes.

text: For simple, one-off request-header checks (e.g. `request.headers.get("X-Requested-With") == "XMLHttpRequest"`), inline the check at the point of use rather than introducing a dedicated helper, property, or function. Extract an abstraction only when the same check is reused in multiple places, and keep the inline form consistent with existing similar implementations in the codebase.
reason: Inlining a single-use request-header check avoids unnecessary indirection and premature abstraction, keeps view methods self-contained, and matches established project conventions (important during function-to-class view migrations).
common_pattern: Handling of request-header checks: three generalizations converge on avoiding premature abstraction of header checks in views (inline simple, one-off checks; extract a helper/property only when reused), while a fourth addresses test coverage for standalone header/user-agent parsing utilities. The dominant pattern is 'keep single-use request-header logic inline and consistent with existing conventions', with a related sub-pattern about testing the fallback path of header-parsing utilities.

text: In tox.ini, indent entries within configuration sections (e.g. under `deps =`) using 4 spaces rather than tabs.
reason: Maintains consistent indentation in the tox configuration and avoids mixed whitespace.
common_pattern: Two weakly-related sub-themes: (a) where and whether tool/test-runner configuration belongs in pyproject.toml vs an external INI file — containing a genuine contradiction between 'move config out of pyproject.toml to save package bytes' (G1/G2) and 'prefer centralizing in pyproject.toml, do not split solely to reduce size' (G4), with G3 (only keep documented/supported config) as the orthogonal safe consensus; and (b) a narrow whitespace convention for tox.ini (G5). The cluster does not converge on a single principle.

text: When copying or translating model instances, detect and exclude all `GenericRelation` fields from model metadata instead of hardcoding individual relation names, so newly added generic relations are handled automatically and generic relations are never duplicated onto the copy.
reason: Hardcoding a single relation name (e.g. `index_entries`) misses other relations such as `postgres_index_entries` and any future generic relations added to the model; metadata-driven detection keeps the exclusion complete and self-maintaining.
common_pattern: Proper handling of Django `GenericRelation` fields: define them only when ORM reverse filtering/prefetching is needed, keep internally-motivated relations private (via omitted `related_query_name` or `_` prefix) so they don't pollute the public query API, and manipulate them generically via model metadata rather than hardcoded field names.

text: In Python 3-only code, use cooperative `super()` for method overrides: prefer zero-argument `super()` over `super(ClassName, self)`; pass through all arguments the method received (e.g., `super().method(**kwargs)`); and when intentionally skipping an intermediate class in the MRO, use `super(IntermediateClass, self).method(...)` instead of hard-coding a later ancestor class. Apply this consistently project-wide after dropping Python 2 support.
reason: Zero-argument `super()` is the idiomatic Python 3 form, reduces coupling to base-class names, respects cooperative inheritance/MRO, and remains correct if class hierarchies change. Explicit `super(IntermediateClass, self)` is the correct exception when deliberately skipping an intermediate class, because hard-coding a later ancestor creates brittle dependencies on third-party MROs. Forwarding arguments preserves parent-class contracts, and project-wide cleanup avoids mixed legacy Python 2 idioms.
common_pattern: Python 3 cooperative `super()` usage in method overrides: prefer zero-argument `super()` in normal cases, forward arguments, and use explicit class arguments only to skip an intermediate MRO class rather than hard-coding an ancestor.

text: For mutually exclusive option groups, use the WAI-ARIA radio group pattern: prefer native `<input type="radio">`, otherwise use `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`. Do not use `aria-current` on `<button>` elements to represent the selected option.
reason: Radio group semantics provide expected keyboard behavior and correct selection state for assistive technology; `aria-current` on button roles is not intended for this purpose.
common_pattern: Use ARIA state attributes as the semantic source of truth for current/selected UI state: place the correct attribute on the interactive element, style from that attribute instead of parallel presentational classes, and choose the ARIA/control pattern that matches the interaction type.

text: In HTML templates, any `<button>` that is not intended to submit a form must explicitly declare `type="button"`; do not rely on the browser default, which is `type="submit"`.
reason: A `<button>` without an explicit `type` defaults to `type="submit"`. Inside or near a form this causes unintended form submissions (including Enter-key submissions triggering the first such button), forcing click handlers to call `preventDefault()`.
common_pattern: HTML `<button>` element semantics in templates: buttons must declare an explicit `type` to avoid the browser's implicit `type="submit"` default, and submit controls should use `<button type="submit">` rather than `<input type="submit">`. The dominant pattern (≈30 of 33 generalizations across ~21 PRs) is the explicit `type="button"` requirement; a smaller, clearly distinct sub-pattern covers the `<button>` vs `<input type="submit">` preference.

text: In documentation code-example comments, write guidance directly (e.g. `# To add a caption field:`) without redundant lead-in phrases like 'for example' — the surrounding example already establishes the illustrative context.
reason: Keeps example comments concise and grammatically consistent (avoids constructions like 'for example To').
common_pattern: Guidelines for writing high-quality documentation code examples: (1) include concrete examples when introducing schema fields/annotations, and (2) keep examples that build on existing definitions incremental and accurate.

text: Overlay controls (e.g., dialog close buttons) must be styled to remain visible and legible when positioned over arbitrary content: give them a z-index above the dialog content's z-index, and define an explicit background color using the project's theme tokens.
reason: This combines complementary requirements—layering (z-index) and contrast (background color)—to ensure overlay controls are not obscured or illegible when anchored to edges or overlapping other UI.
common_pattern: Overlay controls (like dialog close buttons) must be styled to remain visible and legible when positioned over arbitrary content, addressing both stacking order and background contrast.

text: When a rendering routine may run multiple times, or when several DOM mutations are performed in sequence, avoid duplicate, stale, or dead DOM content: remove or replace any previously-appended element (using a stable `data-*` selector for reliable lookup) before appending a new one, do not perform a DOM mutation that is immediately discarded by a following `innerHTML`/`.html()` overwrite, and use `.replaceWith(fragment)` (not `.html(fragment)`) when the fragment includes the target node's own root element.
reason: Repeated invocations otherwise stack duplicate badges/elements or leave outdated content, and redundant or mis-targeted mutations create dead code, duplicated wrapper nodes, and confusion about what actually renders.
common_pattern: DOM-update correctness: rendering code that may run more than once (or that has multiple sequential mutations) must avoid duplicate, stale, or dead DOM content — clean up or replace existing nodes rather than appending/overwriting blindly.

text: When implementing focus-trap/readiness checks, detect the focused element or target with selector-based DOM APIs (`document.activeElement.closest(containerSelector)`, `container.matches('<parent-selector> [data-focus-target="true"]')`) instead of assuming anchors or checking attributes directly on the container; if the target is already present, proceed immediately, and fall back to a timeout only when it is absent.
reason: This supports nested focus targets and non-anchor focusable elements, while avoiding unnecessary animation delays when the element has already rendered.
common_pattern: Robust focus detection/readiness in UI components: use selector-based DOM checks for nested/non-anchor focus targets, and avoid fixed delays when the target is already available.

text: When converting arrays to strings, use explicit .join(separator) with a deliberate, collision-safe separator rather than relying on implicit toString() or join() without a separator; for equality checks, prefer element-by-element comparison when serialization could create false matches.
reason: Implicit array-to-string coercion obscures formatting and can cause incorrect equality checks because concatenated elements without separators can produce identical strings for different arrays.
common_pattern: Array-to-string conversion should be explicit and safe: avoid implicit coercion or separator-less joining, and choose comparison/display strategies deliberately.

text: In admin table cell templates, render linked preview images with minimal markup — avoid unnecessary semantic wrappers such as `<figure>` — and ensure the focus outline wraps the image's rendered dimensions rather than a larger containing element.
reason: Extra wrappers add markup and cause focus/hover outlines to mismatch the visible image area; matching the outline to the image improves keyboard navigation accessibility.
scope: admin table cell templates and related styles
common_pattern: Minimal, accessible markup for linked preview images in admin table cells: avoid unnecessary semantic wrappers and ensure the focus outline matches the image's rendered dimensions.

text: When a UI widget/controller synchronizes DOM/form state or has symmetric paired controls, keep the synchronization convention consistent: use a `sync*` prefix for reconciling controller methods, declare sync communication params (e.g., `data-w-sync-bubbles-param`) consistently with other forms, and apply attribute/ARIA updates to paired controls together.
reason: The cluster spans distinct sync-related concerns—method naming, data-attribute configuration, and symmetric control updates—that all enforce predictable synchronization behavior across UI components.
common_pattern: Synchronization behavior in UI controllers/widgets should be expressed consistently across naming, configuration, and paired-control updates.

text: In admin UI, implement toggles and interactive controls with semantically correct native HTML elements rather than links or styled spans. Use a checkbox input, typically inside its dedicated toggle template and label, for toggles that affect listing results and can participate in form/AJAX submission; use a <button> for controls that trigger an action. Avoid using <a> elements, styled status-tag spans, or hidden `view` inputs for these controls. When AJAX reloads must keep the control state in sync, re-render it via the established teleport/controller pattern or use CSS such as `:has(input:checked)` for simple visual state changes.
reason: Native form controls and buttons are accessible, semantically correct, keyboard-operable, and integrate with existing form/AJAX behavior. This merges the complementary checkbox-vs-button cases by context.
