common_pattern: Admin toggles and interactive controls should be implemented as semantically correct native HTML controls (checkbox inputs or buttons) instead of anchors, styled spans, or hidden state inputs, with JS/CSS only used to keep state synchronized.

text: Prefer function components over class components, and share behavior through composition (rendering other components, hooks, extracted logic) rather than component inheritance; do not create bespoke class-based abstractions that imitate a framework API (e.g., a `props` + `render()` pair mimicking React).
reason: Hand-rolled component abstractions duplicate framework behavior, add indirection, and inherit tightly coupled props/state/lifecycle that are hard to reason about; function components and composition are the modern React convention.
common_pattern: React component design conventions: prefer function components and composition over class components and bespoke abstractions that reinvent framework APIs, with an explicit carve-out for non-React (Telepath-driven) definition classes.

text: Only add or retain a module-level logger when it is actually referenced by logging calls in the file; remove unused logger assignments.
reason: Unused module-level definitions are dead code, can trigger lint warnings, and add unnecessary maintenance noise.
common_pattern: Python module-level logging conventions: how loggers should be named (default `__name__` vs. explicit public-namespace names), kept only when used, and documented so they are discoverable.

text: When spacing flex or grid children, use the CSS `gap` property (or Tailwind `gap-*` / `w-gap-*` utilities) with design-system spacing tokens (e.g., `theme('spacing.N')`, `w-gap-*`) instead of child margins or relying solely on `justify-content: space-between`. Use the shorthand `gap` when row and column gaps are equal; use separate `gap-x`/`gap-y` (or `w-gap-x-*`/`w-gap-y-*`) when they differ — especially for flex containers with a variable number of items, where combining `w-flex-wrap` with distinct x/y gaps lets content wrap cleanly. Verify browser support for `gap` and provide a fallback when compatibility is not guaranteed.
reason: Using `gap` with theme tokens enforces consistent spacing from the design system and avoids collapsed or inconsistent gaps. The shorthand is concise and avoids implying per-axis differences; separate x/y gaps are necessary when axes genuinely differ (e.g., wrapping flex items). Compatibility checks prevent layout breakage on older browsers.
scope: Wagtail admin templates and general CSS layout code
common_pattern: Guidelines for using the CSS `gap` property (or Tailwind gap utilities) in flex/grid layouts: prefer the property over margins/space-between, use theme spacing tokens, choose shorthand vs longhand based on whether axes differ, and consider browser support.

text: When retrieving the first or last element from a collection, prefer concise built-in approaches over manual loops or index arithmetic: use `array.at(-1)` instead of `array[array.length - 1]` for the last array element, and use `Object.values(obj)` rather than a manual loop that tracks first/last values.
reason: Reduces error-prone length arithmetic and unnecessary loop state, making the intent clearer.
common_pattern: Simplify retrieval of first/last collection elements by using concise built-in methods instead of manual loops or length arithmetic.

text: Tune the maxLength used to truncate UI labels to the available layout space rather than defaulting to a conservative value — e.g. desktop views can support longer labels.
reason: Better use of horizontal space and improved readability at no functional cost.
common_pattern: Truncation of UI labels via a maxLength parameter — where the truncation responsibility belongs (raw label callbacks vs callers vs child blocks) and how the limit should be chosen for the available layout space.

text: Action buttons rendered inside admin messages should reuse the existing message button component/style and be placed adjacent to the main message, before any nested error list such as `ul.errorlist`.
reason: Existing message button styles clearly communicate interactivity and affordance, while placing buttons after a nested error list causes them to fall to the bottom of the list and breaks visual consistency with the styleguide.
common_pattern: Rendering action controls inside admin messages should follow the established message UI conventions: reuse existing button styles and place buttons in the conventional position relative to the main message and nested error lists.

text: When interpolating a model method into a string, call it (`obj.get_username()`) rather than referencing the bound method object.
reason: Referencing the method without calling it outputs a method repr instead of the intended value.
common_pattern: Correct use of a Django model's string representation when formatting/interpolating model instances into messages, logs, and diagnostics — preferring `str(obj)` (which respects `__str__` overrides), ensuring models define `__str__`, and not mis-referencing attributes/methods during interpolation.

text: In Storybook stories for React components, render `<textarea>` initial content via the `defaultValue` prop (uncontrolled) or the `value` prop (controlled) rather than passing it as JSX children; if a story arg no longer represents React children, rename it to match the DOM prop it feeds (e.g. `defaultValue` or `value`) in both `argTypes` and the template component signature.
reason: React warns when `<textarea>` receives children because its content should be managed through `defaultValue` or `value`; keeping a `children` arg name for non-child content is misleading and conflicts with React semantics.
common_pattern: Correct handling of React `<textarea>` content props and corresponding Storybook story arg naming in story templates.

text: Decorate classes that define `__str__` with Django's `@python_2_unicode_compatible` (from `django.utils.encoding`) whenever the code must remain Python 2 compatible.
reason: The decorator provides a Python 2-compatible `__unicode__` method automatically, ensuring correct Unicode string behavior and following the established Django convention for Python 2 support.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same rule: classes defining `__str__` in Python 2-compatible Django/Wagtail code must be decorated with `@python_2_unicode_compatible` to preserve correct Unicode string behavior. They are direct rephrasings of the same principle across two PRs.

text: When `:hover` reveals hidden interactive elements (e.g. chooser actions, checkboxes), pair it with `:focus-within` so keyboard users see the currently focused control, and attach the hover/focus-within state to the component root class (e.g. `.chooser`) rather than a generic field wrapper (e.g. `.w-field__input`) so nested component instances are not all activated at once.
reason: Well-hidden tab-order elements lose their focus indicator without a matching focus state, and a generic wrapper's focus-within matches every descendant component, causing nested instances to reveal simultaneously.
common_pattern: Accessible CSS/SCSS focus-state styling: preserve or correctly target the focus indicator so keyboard users get visible focus without leaking outlines to pointer users, and pair hover-revealed interactions with focus-within so keyboard users can see the revealed control.

text: In the welcome-page project template CSS, prefer `:has(:checked)` on a suitable ancestor/container to style checkbox-state descendants instead of long `#id:checked ~ ...` selector chains when it materially improves readability; however, in normalize/base CSS, check for existing widget-specific checkbox styles and modify those instead of adding or changing generic checkbox styling.
reason: Combines the two checkbox-styling concerns: selector readability in a self-contained template and avoiding broad side effects in shared/base CSS.
scope: CSS checkbox styling; welcome-page project template styles and normalize/base styles
common_pattern: Checkbox styling should be applied in the most specific, readable context: use modern state selectors in self-contained template CSS, but keep shared/normalize CSS generic by modifying existing widget-specific styles first.

text: In code that must support both Python 2 and 3, use `six.text_type(value)` (or `six.text_type` as the text type) instead of `str(value)`, `unicode`, or bare `u'...'` string literals whenever a text/unicode value is required.
reason: `six.text_type` maps to `unicode` on Python 2 and `str` on Python 3, providing consistent cross-version text handling. Using `str()` on a Python 2 unicode value with non-ASCII characters raises `UnicodeEncodeError`, and `unicode` is undefined on Python 3 (causing flake8/Travis failures).
common_pattern: Python 2/3 compatibility handling of text/unicode values via the `six` compatibility library: use `six.text_type` for text-type conversions and cross-version type checks, and exercise such code paths with non-ASCII input to catch Python 2 encoding regressions.

text: When rendering a set of sibling status indicators for a timeline (e.g., `wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/workflows/workflow_status.html`), keep the icon style a cohesive family: map each status to a circle-shaped FontAwesome icon, and pair filled icons with filled icons (e.g., `circle-check` for approved with `error` for rejected) rather than mixing filled and outline variants. For statuses lacking a distinct circled variant (e.g., `skipped`), reuse an existing circular icon such as `radio-full` instead of a non-circular or semantically misleading one; use `circle-xmark` for `cancelled` to distinguish it.
reason: All the icons in the timeline appear together, so mixed filled/outline or non-circular shapes look inconsistent and ambiguous; matching visual weight and shape makes the status set read as one recognizable family.
common_pattern: Both sub-groups concern how to present workflow/state statuses consistently to users — one about visual (icon) consistency across a set of sibling statuses, the other about textual (label) consistency when a state is a variant of a parent state. They share only a loose theme ('status representation'), so they should be split into two distinct rules.

text: Reuse a function's existing class-matching/validation logic instead of writing a parallel inline condition. If a new call site needs different matching semantics (e.g. exact class vs isinstance/subclass match), expose that as an explicit keyword argument on the shared check rather than duplicating the condition or hard-coding one behavior.
reason: Avoids duplicated class-matching logic, keeps validation consistent across branches, and makes differing semantics explicit and testable instead of hidden in separate code paths.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern Python class/type membership checks: how to test whether an object belongs to a type (or family of types) in a robust, idiomatic, and extensible way. The cluster has three distinct sub-patterns: (1) prefer isinstance() over type()/duck-typing checks, (2) avoid hardcoded isinstance class lists for feature selection in favor of extensible base-class opt-in, and (3) avoid duplicating class-matching logic.

text: When resolving a configured field name against a default, compute the final value explicitly or via one canonical helper/property (e.g., `self.to_field_name or instance.pk`, or a shared `pk_quoted` property) instead of passing a boolean-style `or` expression as the attribute-name argument to `getattr()` or duplicating `kwargs.get(..., default)` fallback logic in multiple places.
reason: An `or` expression inside `getattr()` selects between attribute names rather than producing the intended value, and duplicated fallback logic can drift out of sync. Resolving the fallback explicitly and centrally makes intent clear and keeps lookup behavior consistent.
common_pattern: Fallback/default resolution should be explicit and centralized, not embedded inline in attribute lookup or duplicated across code paths.

text: Arrange DOM markup in the intended visual and keyboard-focus order rather than using CSS `order` or other visual reordering; place focusable/interactive controls at the structural position where users should encounter them so tab order matches the visual reading order.
reason: Screen readers and keyboard navigation follow DOM order, so CSS visual reordering creates confusing mismatches between visual order and announced/focus order.
common_pattern: Ensure DOM/structural order matches the intended visual and keyboard-focus/tab order for accessibility; avoid CSS-based visual reordering. Generalizations 1-5 clearly converge on this pattern. Generalization 6 is an accessibility-adjacent outlier about ARIA table descriptions rather than DOM order.

text: In custom decorators that wrap a function or view, apply `@functools.wraps(original_func)` to the inner wrapper function to preserve the wrapped callable's metadata (`__name__`, `__doc__`, `__module__`, annotations).
reason: Preserves the original function's name, docstring, module, and annotations, improving introspection, debugging, documentation generation, and consistency with Django decorator behavior.
scope: global for custom decorator implementations (e.g., `permission_required` in `wagtail/wagtailadmin/utils.py`)
common_pattern: Custom decorators that wrap a function or view must apply `@functools.wraps` to the inner wrapper to preserve the wrapped callable's metadata.

text: Use 4-space indentation consistently across all code and all languages in the project, and configure linting/formatting rules to enforce it (do not use 2-space indentation).
reason: The project treats 4-space indentation as a sensible cross-language consistency standard; 2-space indentation is considered harder to read and breaks visual consistency across languages.
common_pattern: The project standardizes on 4-space indentation across all languages, both as a code style convention and as a linting/formatting configuration to enforce it.

text: When detecting the presence of a numeric `col#` CSS class token, use an unanchored word-boundary regex like `re.search(r'\bcol\d+\b', classname)` instead of a regex that enumerates the currently valid column range (e.g. `col1`–`col12`). The generic token shape is simpler, avoids brittle range validation, and stays correct if the number of available columns changes.
reason: Encoding the current grid width into the detection regex couples the check to a value that may change; matching the generic `col<number>` shape keeps the code readable and resilient.
common_pattern: Detecting CSS grid column classes by matching the generic token shape rather than enumerating a hard-coded valid range

text: In Python source, use a consistent quote convention that follows the file/project's established style. If both single and double quotes are used, give them a clear, consistent semantic role (e.g., double quotes for human-readable/translatable strings and single quotes for internal identifiers or machine-readable keys) rather than mixing them arbitrarily.
reason: This reconciles the reviewer's concern about arbitrary quote mixing with the author's intentional convention for distinguishing translatable/user-facing strings from internal identifiers. It keeps the codebase visually consistent and makes diffs and tooling easier to manage.
common_pattern: Python string quote style consistency, with intentional use of single vs. double quotes when both appear in the same file or data structure.

text: Plain-text notification templates (`wagtailadmin/notifications/*.txt`) require formatting that differs from their HTML counterparts: apply the `|safe` filter to `{% blocktrans ... asvar %}` output (e.g. `{{ message|capfirst|safe }}`) so Django autoescaping does not emit HTML entities such as `"` into the email body. This filter is unnecessary in the paired `.html` templates, which intentionally escape.
reason: Plaintext emails do not render HTML entities, so escaped characters appear verbatim to the recipient; HTML templates render them correctly and do not need the filter.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern the organization and formatting of Wagtail admin notification templates — chiefly that shared structure, copy, and context should live in common base templates (both HTML and plain-text variants), with plain-text templates requiring their own specific handling distinct from HTML.

text: When order matters — deduplicating a sequence, iterating generated key/value pairs, or producing ordered output — use order-preserving constructs (e.g. `dict.fromkeys(seq)` for dedup, a list of tuples instead of a dict + `.items()` when older Python must be supported) rather than `set()` or dependency on unordered iteration.
reason: `set()` and/or pre-3.7 dict iteration do not guarantee order, so they can silently reorder caller-supplied inputs and produce nondeterministic output. Order-preserving constructs remove duplicates and render output in a stable, predictable order in one pass.
common_pattern: Python data-structure ordering: be deliberate about whether insertion/iteration order is preserved, and choose constructs (dict.fromkeys, list of tuples) that preserve order when it matters, rather than relying on set() or unordered iteration. A secondary, contradictory sub-pattern concerns whether OrderedDict is worth using for JSON-serialized dicts.

text: When retrieving the first key from a dict/OrderedDict in code that must run on Python 2 and Python 3, do not index `.keys()`, `.values()`, or `.items()` directly; use `next(iter(d))`/`next(iter(d.keys()))` when only the first key is needed, or wrap the view in `list(...)` when a list is required.
reason: Python 3 dict views (`odict_keys`, `dict_keys`, etc.) do not support indexing, so direct indexing raises `TypeError`. Using `next(iter(...))` avoids unnecessary list construction when only the first key is needed; `list(...)` preserves compatibility when an actual list is required.
common_pattern: Python dictionary access pitfalls: dict views are not subscriptable in Python 3, and bare `in` checks are unsafe when the iterated value may be a non-dict such as a string.

text: When filtering a heterogeneous iterable for dictionaries containing a specific key, guard with `isinstance(v, dict) and key in v` rather than `key in v` alone, because `in` on a string performs substring matching instead of dictionary-key membership and can cause false positives or later `TypeError`.
reason: A bare `key in v` check may match strings that contain the key name as a substring. Requiring `isinstance(v, dict)` first preserves the intended meaning: the value must be a dictionary that contains that key.
common_pattern: Python dictionary access pitfalls: dict views are not subscriptable in Python 3, and bare `in` checks are unsafe when the iterated value may be a non-dict such as a string.

text: When a data migration only needs a subset of fields from each row, restrict the queryset with `.only(...)` to exactly those fields.
reason: Minimizes data transferred and memory/network overhead when iterating over large tables in production.
common_pattern: Performance-oriented Django data migrations: avoid per-row Python iteration and N+1 lookups by pushing work into bulk database operations (UPDATE/bulk_update/Subquery), and restrict fetched data to only the needed fields.

text: Recalculate derived UI state (e.g., visibility, enabled, and action states) inside the page-load/initialization handler so that browser-restored form values are reflected in the rendered interface.
reason: Browsers can restore form control state on navigation (including the back button) without firing change events, which leaves dependent UI controls stale unless the update logic runs on load.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same principle: derived/dependent UI state must be recomputed during page load/initialization because browsers can restore form control state (e.g., via back/forward cache) without firing change events, leaving the UI stale.

text: When generating form-submission email/display content for Wagtail forms (`wagtail/wagtailforms/models.py` `send_mail`), iterate over form fields and read submitted values with `field.value()` instead of raw `form.data`; normalize list-valued fields by joining them with `', '` and replace an empty joined result with a non-empty placeholder such as `'None'`; build the body with an explicit loop that appends `'{label}: {value}'` lines and joins them with newlines rather than using nested comprehensions.
reason: Uses Django/Wagtail's BoundField value semantics, correctly handles multi-value and empty fields, keeps tests passing, and makes conditional normalization readable and explicit.
scope: file: wagtail/wagtailforms/models.py, method: send_mail; applicable to Django/Wagtail form-value serialization for emails or display output
common_pattern: Formatting submitted form values into Wagtail form-submission email/display content: use the BoundField API, normalize list and empty values, and build output with an explicit loop.

text: When code paths branch on object/render state (e.g. populated vs empty/placeholder, changed vs new vs deleted), handle every state explicitly: order conditional checks from the most general condition (e.g. `has_changed`) before narrower ones (`is_new`, `is_deleted`) so null/empty values aren't misclassified, and verify layout or output changes against each rendered state before committing.
reason: Shared wrapper markup and unguarded condition ordering cause regressions: a CSS tweak that fixes the populated listing breaks the empty-state message, and checking new/deleted before changed misclassifies null or empty values as additions or deletions.
common_pattern: State-conditional rendering logic must account for ALL possible states — both the order of condition checks and the visual/behavioral outcome in each state (populated vs empty, changed vs new/deleted).

text: Do not re-declare a property inside a media-query ruleset when the same property/value is already declared on the same selector in the base (non-media-query) ruleset; media queries should only contain properties that actually change at that breakpoint.
reason: Redundant declarations add noise, make it harder to see which rules are truly breakpoint-specific, risk future inconsistencies, and can introduce cascade/order issues since base rules already apply at all viewport sizes.
common_pattern: SCSS media-query authoring conventions: how responsive/feature-query styles and breakpoints should be written, scoped, de-duplicated, and sourced from shared variables/mixins.

text: Manage script inclusion mechanics deliberately: bundle multiple contiguous JavaScript assets into a single `{% compress js %}` block instead of separate `<script>` tags, and place a library's inline initialization immediately after the script/library it configures, before unrelated shared scripts.
reason: Concatenation/minification reduces HTTP requests and improves load performance, while pairing an inclusion with its initialization makes the dependency explicit and avoids script-ordering problems.
common_pattern: JavaScript asset organization: keep JS out of HTML/template markup and in dedicated external static files, extract shared logic into reusable modules rather than duplicating or inlining, and scope/bundle inclusions deliberately. All generalizations address how client-side JavaScript should be structured and included relative to templates.

text: For CSS centering/layout, prefer size-agnostic techniques—flexbox, CSS Grid, or `transform: translate()`—over `position: fixed` or hard-coded offsets. Reserve `position: fixed` for elements that truly need viewport anchoring; when a fixed full-viewport container already exists, position its child decorative elements with `position: absolute`. Small visual offsets (e.g., 1px) are acceptable only when exact centering is geometrically impossible (e.g., even-width elements in odd-width containers).
reason: These techniques are more predictable, reusable, and resilient to content-size changes than viewport-fixed positioning or brittle pixel math.
common_pattern: Use resilient, size-agnostic CSS centering/positioning techniques (flexbox, CSS Grid, transform) and scope positioning to containers instead of relying on viewport-fixed positioning or hard-coded offsets.

text: Validate CSS/SCSS syntax manually before submitting: spell property names correctly, use values valid for the target property, and terminate every declaration with a semicolon; do not rely solely on the linter to catch these errors.
reason: Misspelled properties, invalid values, and missing semicolons produce invalid CSS that browsers may silently ignore, causing styling to fail without obvious errors.
common_pattern: CSS/SCSS declaration syntax correctness: property names must be valid, values must be valid for the target property, and declarations must be terminated with semicolons. These errors often fail silently in browsers, so manual verification is needed beyond relying on the linter. The JavaScript duplicate-semicolon generalization is a separate punctuation-hygiene outlier and is not merged into this CSS/SCSS rule.

text: For links with a custom underline in SCSS component styles, use the longhand `text-decoration-*` properties (e.g., `text-decoration-line`, `text-decoration-thickness`) instead of the `text-decoration` shorthand when Safari support is required, and reset the underline on hover (e.g., `&:hover { text-decoration: none; }`) to provide clear interactive feedback.
reason: Safari ignores some values in the `text-decoration` shorthand, so the intended underline styling silently fails; hover feedback also requires explicitly clearing the custom underline.
common_pattern: SCSS/code-style hygiene in component styles: (a) comments must stay attached to the rule they describe, and (b) link underline styling must handle hover state and Safari compatibility via longhand text-decoration properties.

text: When stripping a known leading character from a string, use an explicit removal method (e.g., `str.lstrip(char)` in Python, `.replace(char, '')` in JavaScript) instead of fixed-index slicing like `[1:]` or `.substring(1)`, because slicing assumes the character is present and can silently truncate valid data.
reason: Fixed-index slicing assumes the leading character is always present; if it is omitted, the first real character of the remainder is silently removed, producing hard-to-debug errors. Explicit methods are also clearer about intent.
common_pattern: Avoid fixed-index slicing (e.g., `[1:]`, `.substring(1)`) when stripping a known leading character from a string; instead use an explicit removal method (e.g., `lstrip`, `replace`) that expresses intent and is safe when the character is absent.

text: When applying an optimization or formatting change to assets of a given type (e.g., SVGs, images), apply it consistently to all existing assets in the affected directory/set; when updating an existing asset referenced from docs or other files, modify the file in place rather than creating a new file with a modified name and updating references.
reason: Keeps existing assets consistent with the new standard, avoids orphaned or stale asset files, keeps references stable, and reduces repository clutter.
common_pattern: Consistent management of repository assets: apply changes to all relevant existing assets and update files in place rather than adding duplicates.

text: Do not set `width: 100%` on block-level elements (`display: block`, e.g. `<div>`). Block elements already fill their containing block, so the declaration is redundant and adds noise or confusing override chains (particularly when more specific mode/class rules set the width anyway). Use `max-width` or other constraints only when a genuinely narrower layout is required.
reason: Block-level elements natively expand to the width of their containing block, so `width: 100%` is a no-op that clutters stylesheets and obscures real layout intent / override behavior.
common_pattern: CSS stylesheet hygiene: eliminating redundant or inconsistently applied CSS declarations so that stylesheets stay minimal and layout behavior remains predictable. Three generalizations converge on the concrete case of removing redundant `width: 100%` on block-level elements; a fourth addresses a related-but-distinct concern (global vs. selective `box-sizing`).

text: When defining page-wide `box-sizing` behavior, use a global reset — `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: inherit; }` plus `box-sizing: border-box` on the root/body element — rather than applying `box-sizing` to only a few selected elements.
reason: A global reset guarantees consistent sizing behavior across all elements and pseudo-elements, preventing layout inconsistencies when new elements are added.
common_pattern: CSS stylesheet hygiene: eliminating redundant or inconsistently applied CSS declarations so that stylesheets stay minimal and layout behavior remains predictable. Three generalizations converge on the concrete case of removing redundant `width: 100%` on block-level elements; a fourth addresses a related-but-distinct concern (global vs. selective `box-sizing`).

text: In Wagtail admin SCSS, style icon-only or icon-optional control buttons so the icon is centered within the clickable area and button/label alignment does not depend on whether the `::before` icon pseudo-element is present. Use layout techniques such as flexbox (`display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;`) or symmetric padding/spacing rather than asymmetric padding.
reason: Centered icons improve visual alignment and ensure the clickable target matches the visual target; making alignment independent of optional icons prevents no-icon buttons from being misaligned, improving scanability and usability.
scope: Wagtail admin SCSS, especially streamfield controls and block picker buttons
common_pattern: Wagtail admin SCSS buttons with optional icons must keep icons centered in the clickable area and maintain consistent alignment whether or not the icon pseudo-element is rendered.

text: When changing an element's tag or semantic role (including replacing a semantic element with a role-carrying <div>, or relocating styles onto an existing semantic element), update the associated CSS: adapt selectors to target the replacement (e.g., [role="main"] or a dedicated class) rather than the raw element selector, and verify the layout and appearance remain correct.
reason: Element selectors and browser default styles silently break when the underlying tag or role changes; explicit selectors/classes keep styling preserved and intent clear.
common_pattern: When changing an element's tag, semantic role, or relocating styles between elements, associated CSS must be updated (selectors adapted or a dedicated class added) and styling verified, so appearance and layout are preserved.

text: For user-facing strings that interpolate a count, use Django/Wagtail i18n pluralization (`{% blocktrans count counter=... %}{% plural %}...` or `ngettext`) instead of hardcoding plural nouns, concatenating counts, or using f-strings. Ensure the singular branch is grammatical for `count == 1`, keep the `count counter` variable name consistent between assignment and interpolation, and when a message contains multiple independent counts, use only one count per `{% blocktrans %}` block and split/nest the message into separate blocks or keep other counts as ordinary placeholders.
reason: Count-dependent user-facing text must pluralize correctly across languages and count values. Django supports only one pluralization count per `blocktrans` block, so multiple independent counts require splitting or careful placeholder use. This applies to templates, Wagtail admin UI, and management-command output.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail internationalization: user-facing strings that interpolate a count must use proper pluralization rather than hardcoded plural nouns, and template-level pluralization must be structured correctly around `{% blocktrans count %}`/`{% plural %}`.

text: Declare Python classes without a base class as `class Foo:` — omit the empty parentheses and do not explicitly inherit from `object`. Reserve a base-class list for classes that actually inherit from another class.
reason: In Python 3 the parentheses and `object` base are redundant, add visual noise, and trigger lint warnings; omitting them keeps class declarations clean, idiomatic, and consistent.
common_pattern: Python class-declaration hygiene: keep class headers minimal — no redundant empty parentheses or explicit `object` base when there is no base class, and reference a real base class by its directly imported name rather than a redundant syntactic form.

text: Generate cache keys through a single shared helper method rather than repeating inline key formatting such as `"{hostname}:{port}"` at each call site.
reason: Keeps cache-key formatting consistent, reduces duplication, and makes future changes to key construction easier and safer.
common_pattern: Cache-key handling should be centralized and safe: avoid collisions with user-provided values and avoid duplicating key-generation logic across call sites.

text: When building up a parameter or filter dictionary across conditional branches, assign or update keys on the existing dictionary rather than reassigning the variable to a new dictionary in each branch.
reason: Reassigning creates unnecessary dictionaries and can silently discard entries added by earlier branches or by future extensions, making the code wasteful and error-prone.
common_pattern: These two generalizations come from the same PR and both concern the `filter` variable used to build request parameters, but they express two genuinely distinct Python coding principles: (1) avoiding shadowing of built-in names in naming, and (2) mutating an existing dictionary in conditional branches rather than reassigning it. They share context but not a single underlying pattern.

reason: The generalizations converge on the same semantic-HTML principle from complementary angles: list elements must be used for real lists, non-list content must not be forced into list markup, and list semantics must remain valid and meaningful.
common_pattern: Match HTML list semantics to actual content: use `<ul>`/`<li>` only for genuine lists with valid nesting, and use non-list semantic/block elements for standalone messages, layout containers, and other non-list content.

text: For text or links rendered on dark backgrounds, ensure legibility by applying font smoothing (e.g., `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale;`) to light text and by using the project's standard link styles with verified color contrast at all breakpoints, rather than ad-hoc color overrides.
reason: Light-on-dark text can appear heavier or blurrier without font smoothing, and low-contrast or custom-colored links can be difficult to read and may bypass established accessible link styling.
common_pattern: Ensuring legibility and accessibility of text and links rendered on dark backgrounds.

text: When specifying entity or link type values in rich-text conversion rules, use the project's `ENTITY_TYPES` constants (e.g. `ENTITY_TYPES.DOCUMENT`, `ENTITY_TYPES.EMBED`) instead of bare string literals.
reason: Centralizing entity-type identifiers avoids typos, keeps values consistent across multiple references, and makes future renames/refactors safer.
common_pattern: Design of reusable inline-entity handlers in rich-text converters: keep handlers generic by parameterizing entity metadata, avoid magic entity-type strings via central constants, and keep the cross-language (Python↔JS) attribute contract tolerant of missing values.

text: Make selector matching explicit and precise: define selector types so supported selector shapes are explicitly enumerated, prefer exact-match selectors (e.g., [attr="full-value"]) over suffix/broad matches when the full attribute value is known, and audit related selectors in the same module for the same tightening.
reason: Explicit selector shapes and exact matches make supported syntax discoverable and avoid ambiguous or unintended element matches.
common_pattern: Selector matching should be explicit and precise: enumerate supported selector shapes and prefer exact-match selectors over broad/suffix matches when the full value is known, auditing related selectors for consistency.

text: In `wagtail/admin/rich_text/converters/html_to_contentstate.py`, whitespace normalization must collapse all whitespace sequences to a single space (`' '`) using a `+` quantifier rather than `{2,}`, so downstream `content == ' '` sentinel checks continue to identify whitespace-only text nodes and single line breaks between paragraph blocks are stripped instead of becoming empty paragraphs.
reason: Using `{2,}` leaves single whitespace characters unnormalized; inconsistent whitespace replacement makes `content == ' '` false and causes single line breaks between paragraph blocks to become empty paragraphs instead of being stripped.
common_pattern: Normalization/edge-case handling in content processing: avoid ad hoc normalization unless justified, and when normalization is required, implement it consistently so downstream assumptions hold.

text: Use semantic HTML elements (`<strong>` for importance/bold intent, `<em>` for emphasis) instead of generic `<span>` elements styled with CSS `font-weight` or presentational utility classes like `w-font-bold`. Target the semantic element in CSS selectors and omit redundant font-weight utilities the semantic element already conveys.
reason: Semantic elements expose emphasis/importance to assistive technology and keep document meaning separate from presentation, so visual styling can change without losing semantics.
common_pattern: All four generalizations converge on the same principle: emphasis/importance should be expressed with semantic HTML (<strong>, <em>) rather than simulated visually via CSS font-weight or presentational utility classes on generic <span> elements.

text: When writing regex patterns that match whitespace and must work across database backends, do not rely on a single portable pattern; add explicit backend-specific handling for engines like MySQL that interpret backslash escapes (e.g., \s, \n inside character classes) differently from SQLite/Python.
reason: MySQL treats backslashed character classes literally, so a shared whitespace pattern can silently fail on that backend.
common_pattern: Regex whitespace matching must account for environment-specific differences: database backend regex engine quirks (e.g., MySQL) and OS line-ending conventions (\r vs \n).

text: When defining an explicit whitespace character class in a regex (e.g., replacing a broader \s), include \r in addition to \n to match both Windows and Unix line breaks.
reason: Avoids missing Windows-style \r\n line endings, especially when replacing a broader \s pattern with a narrower explicit character class.
common_pattern: Regex whitespace matching must account for environment-specific differences: database backend regex engine quirks (e.g., MySQL) and OS line-ending conventions (\r vs \n).

text: For page footers, prefer a Flexbox sticky footer pattern (e.g., flex column layout with a min-height on the page container) over `position: fixed` so the footer adapts when content height changes or when the viewport scrolls.
reason: A Flexbox sticky footer keeps the footer at the bottom of the viewport for short pages while allowing it to flow naturally after content on longer pages, avoiding overlap and layout breakage as content grows or screen sizes vary.
common_pattern: Footer styling best practices: footers should be resilient to layout changes and remain visually accessible across rendering modes.

text: Reusable footer styles should define a border or equivalent visible separation so the footer remains distinguishable from its background in high-contrast mode.
reason: Without visible separation, the footer can blend into its background in high-contrast mode, making the UI harder to perceive for users relying on high-contrast settings.
common_pattern: Footer styling best practices: footers should be resilient to layout changes and remain visually accessible across rendering modes.

text: In recursive traversals that carry a parent/context variable across iterations (e.g. `parent_use` in `Use.from_nested_list` in `wagtail/core/collectors.py`), explicitly reset that variable to its default (usually `None`) in branches where the current item must not become the parent of subsequent items. Do not rely on implicit ordering or undocumented invariants of the input data (such as Django `NestedObjects.nested()` output order) to make a stale value harmless.
reason: Explicit resets make the control flow and intent clear, avoid hidden dependencies on upstream ordering assumptions, and prevent subtle correctness bugs if those assumptions ever change. The original code was described as hard to reason about precisely because the carried state was left at its previous value.
scope: module/locality: recursive collector logic in `wagtail/core/collectors.py`; generalizable to other recursive traversals carrying parent state
common_pattern: All three generalizations describe the same principle: in recursive traversals/iterators that carry a parent/context state variable across iterations (e.g. `parent_use`), the state must be explicitly reset (typically to `None`) in branches where the current item should not act as the parent of subsequent items, instead of relying on implicit input ordering/invariants (e.g. `NestedObjects.nested()` order) to make a stale value harmless.

text: In CSS, when a hard-coded value (such as a hex color) corresponds to a design token/variable, keep an inline trailing comment naming that variable (e.g. `color: #333; /*$color-grey-1*/`). If the referenced variable name has become obsolete, update the comment to the current variable name rather than deleting it.
reason: Preserves traceability between literal CSS values and the design-token system, keeping future token-based refactors and consistency checks possible; deleting or leaving stale comments loses that link or misleads.
scope: CSS files, including docs CSS such as `docs/_static/css/custom.css`
common_pattern: All four generalizations address the same practice in CSS: when a hard-coded value (e.g. a hex color) corresponds to a design-token/variable, retain the inline comment naming that variable, and when the referenced variable name has become stale, update it to the current equivalent instead of deleting the comment. They are complementary halves (preserve the link + keep the reference accurate) of one principle.

text: When the same object or value is constructed in multiple branches within a loop iteration, hoist the construction to the top of the iteration and reuse the resulting variable. If the code instead deliberately repeats work that could be hoisted (e.g., clearing and re-populating a container each time it is opened), add an inline comment explaining the reason so reviewers and maintainers do not treat it as accidental redundancy.
reason: Reduces duplication and repeated work while keeping branch-specific logic focused on control flow; documenting deliberate repetition prevents repeated review questions and accidental 'optimizations' that break behavior.
common_pattern: Handling repeated/duplicated work: hoist construction out of branches (or loop iterations) to reuse a single value, but when the repetition is intentional, document the reason inline instead of silently duplicating.

text: In SCSS, when composing selectors with the parent selector `&`, avoid concatenation that changes selector meaning: keep class separators (`.`) directly attached to interpolated class names, and use `@at-root #{selector-unify('element', &)}` to combine an element type with the parent selector instead of `&element`, which produces an unintended class selector (e.g., `.bicolorbutton` instead of `button.bicolor`).
reason: Whitespace and `&` placement change selector meaning or produce invalid CSS; string concatenation with `&` (e.g., `&button`) yields an unexpected class selector rather than an element.class combination.
scope: SCSS stylesheets, especially component styles under client/scss/components/
common_pattern: Correct composition of SCSS selectors using the parent selector `&`, avoiding accidental concatenation or malformed selectors.

text: For StreamField widgets, initialize each widget inline at its render/definition point rather than emitting a `data-streamfield` JSON payload and bulk-initializing all widgets after page load.
reason: Direct initialization avoids showing StreamFields in an uninitialized state and eliminates the noticeable 1–2s perceived page-load delay caused by a delayed global setup phase.
common_pattern: Wagtail StreamField handling conventions — the cluster shares the StreamField/JSONField entity but splits into three distinct concerns: (a) when/how widgets are initialized client-side, (b) canonical discovery/serialization helpers for StreamFields, and (c) internal API-shape details of the StreamField class itself.

text: In client-side JavaScript, iterate the result of `document.querySelectorAll()` directly with `.forEach()`: do not spread it into an array (`[...nodeList]`, `Array.from(...)`, `[].slice.call(...)`) and do not guard it with an `if (collection)` check. `querySelectorAll` always returns a NodeList (empty if no matches), and the project's current browser baseline implements `NodeList.prototype.forEach`, so the array cast and null guard are unnecessary.
reason: The earlier NodeList-to-array conversion and compatibility utility existed only to work around IE11, which lacked `NodeList.prototype.forEach`. With the supported browser baseline no longer including IE11, the direct NodeList + `.forEach()` form is simpler and idiomatic, avoids a redundant array allocation, and avoids a misleading guard (an empty NodeList is truthy, so an `if (tabs)` check is pointless). Use `.forEach()` rather than `for...of` for consistent, idiomatic style across frontend code.
common_pattern: Idiomatic iteration of DOM query results (`document.querySelectorAll`) in client-side JavaScript, including whether to convert the returned NodeList to an array, which iteration method to use, and whether a null/empty guard is needed.

text: Wrap dynamic/interpolated values (e.g. entity titles) in quotes inside accessible labels, icon `title` attributes, and aria text (e.g. `Edit '{title}'`, `View child pages of '{title}'`) so screen readers announce them as a distinct value rather than running them into the surrounding label text.
reason: Without delimiters, assistive technologies can read the interpolated value and the static label as one continuous phrase, harming comprehension; quoting makes the dynamic content a distinct entity.
common_pattern: All three generalizations state the same accessibility convention: dynamic/interpolated values (entity titles, names, etc.) embedded in accessible labels, `title` attributes, or aria text must be wrapped in quotes so screen readers announce them as distinct from surrounding static text.

text: When replacing an element with a component tag, check whether the component's base styles already provide the needed display behavior (e.g. a `.status-tag` that already sets `inline-block`) before adding utility classes like `w-block` to override display.
reason: Avoids redundant utility classes and keeps markup aligned with the component's intended display behavior instead of overriding it.
common_pattern: Choosing (and cleaning up) HTML/template elements so that element semantics, rendered block/inline behavior, and default styles all align with the content's purpose — and removing wrappers/utilities that serve no purpose.

text: Keyboard activation handlers for toggle/button-like elements should treat both Space and Enter as activation keys.
reason: Native buttons activate on both Space and Enter; custom handlers should match this behavior for consistent keyboard accessibility.
common_pattern: Best practices for handling keyboard events: use modern standard properties and shared constants instead of deprecated or hard-coded values, drop legacy browser-specific aliases, and ensure accessible activation keys.

text: Remove markup identifiers and hooks — `id` attributes, `data-*` attributes, their `dataset.*` assignments, and script-only classes — when nothing references them (implementation, CSS, JS, ARIA, or tests). This includes auto-generated/editor-inserted ids in static SVG assets and hooks orphaned after their consuming script is deleted.
reason: Unreferenced ids and data attributes are dead code: they add noise, can go stale or collide (e.g. tool-generated SVG ids like `Oval`/`Path` when inlined), trigger unnecessary DOM mutations, and mislead future maintainers into believing the element is still consumed.
common_pattern: All four generalizations express the same principle: markup identifiers and hooks (id attributes, data-* attributes, dataset.* assignments) that are not referenced by implementation, CSS, JS, ARIA, or tests are dead code and should be removed before merge.

text: When temporarily activating a language for a request or a block of code, use `django.utils.translation.override()` as a context manager instead of manually saving and restoring the active language with `get_language()`/`activate()`. Apply this idiom consistently wherever temporary language switching is needed.
reason: Django's context manager is cleaner, correctly handles edge cases such as exceptions raised inside a view, and consistency avoids divergent hand-rolled implementations. This is the established pattern in the project's `language_preferences` view.
common_pattern: Idiomatic Django handling of request/locale-scoped language state — using framework-provided mechanisms (translation.override, request.LANGUAGE_CODE) instead of ad-hoc save/restore, query-param tricks, or premature utility extraction.

text: When copying or adapting code from a sibling module or similar feature, update every entity-specific reference to match the target context: rename identifiers and context variables, rewrite comments and docstrings to name the correct entity, and strip remnants of the source feature (commented-out calls, TODOs, stale names) so no trace of the source domain remains.
reason: Leftover references from the source module — in docstrings, comments, variable names, or dead code — are misleading, become stale documentation, and confuse readers about which entity or operation the code actually concerns.
common_pattern: When code is copied or adapted from a sibling/parallel module or feature, all entity-specific remnants of the source (identifiers, variable/context-variable names, comments, docstrings, commented-out calls, TODOs) must be updated or removed to reflect the target module's domain.

text: In HTML templates, represent dates in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) for data attributes rather than JavaScript numeric month values.
reason: ISO dates avoid JavaScript Date month-indexing ambiguity and are easier to read.
common_pattern: Date/time handling best practices: minimize dependency weight and use standard, unambiguous formats.

text: When a Django ORM queryset expression is too long for one line, wrap it in parentheses and break chained method calls (`filter`, `exclude`, `order_by`, `first`, etc.) and multi-condition `Q()` filters onto separate indented lines. Place binary operators (`|`, `&`, `and`, `or`) at the beginning of continuation lines, not at the end of the preceding line.
reason: Multi-line formatting makes query structure and condition grouping easier to read and review, and beginning-of-line operators satisfy flake8 W504 so the formatting stays lint-compliant.
common_pattern: Multi-line formatting of long Django ORM queryset expressions: wrap in parentheses and break chained calls / `Q` conditions onto separate indented continuation lines, with binary operators placed at the start of continuation lines for lint compliance.

text: When the (type_name, value, id) tuple shape is constructed in multiple places to build StreamValue in stream_block.py, define a named tuple or small class for it instead of repeating anonymous raw tuples.
reason: Makes tuple field meanings explicit and improves readability and maintainability.
common_pattern: Make StreamValue/stream_data representations in stream_block.py explicit and self-documenting: document every supported input form and make repeated tuple structure self-describing.

text: When guarding against a missing, unset, or unusable value (selector/store lookups, dynamic config-map keys, browser feature detection), check the value's usability rather than its identity: use a falsy/truthiness check for lookups and mappings, and for feature detection combine an `in` property check with `typeof x !== 'undefined'` instead of comparing against `null` or `undefined`.
reason: Narrow comparisons (`=== undefined`, `=== null`) and bare `in` existence checks only answer part of the question — they miss null/empty values, prototype-chain matches, or properties that exist but are unset, so they are more fragile than reading and testing the value itself.
common_pattern: Defensive presence/validity checks for values that may be missing or empty: prefer checks that widen coverage (truthiness, `typeof` guards, combined existence+value checks) over narrow identity comparisons (`=== undefined`, `=== null`) or bare existence checks (`in` alone).

text: Avoid using direct `.innerHTML`/`ref.current.innerHTML` to embed SVG or HTML. Render static SVG/HTML declaratively, such as with JSX in React; for raw HTML strings use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. When embedding server-rendered SVG/sprite via `.innerHTML`, serve it with `Content-Type: text/html` to match the HTML parsing context, or embed it with an `` tag instead.
reason: Declarative rendering and content-type-appropriate embedding are more idiomatic, predictable, and avoid mismatches between how content is declared and how the browser parses or executes it.
common_pattern: Avoid direct/imperative `.innerHTML` injection for SVG/HTML markup; instead use the rendering or embedding mechanism that matches the framework or content type.

text: When adding new markup, leave pre-existing legacy structural/accessibility issues unchanged; apply the correct pattern only to newly added code.
reason: Avoids scope creep and breaking existing layouts while still improving new code.
common_pattern: Scope discipline in accessibility-related changes: keep documentation focused and separated, and avoid modifying legacy markup beyond the task.

text: When a cached value would be immediately regenerated and stored again, don't delete the cache entry to mark it invalid; instead treat the invalid value as a cache miss by folding the staleness check into the existing recompute guard (e.g. `if result is None or <stale_check>:`) so regeneration overwrites the entry uniformly.
reason: Avoids redundant cache deletion and duplicated invalidation logic, keeps validation side-effect free, and leaves cache state changes in a single place.
common_pattern: Both generalizations express the same principle: when a cached value will be regenerated and stored immediately afterward, staleness detection should be folded into the existing cache-miss/recompute condition rather than performing a separate cache deletion — avoiding redundant invalidation and keeping cache state mutation in one place.

text: Apply the same state/value-setting convention consistently across all render paths of a widget (e.g. use the same mechanism in `renderState` and `renderEmptyState` rather than mixing `.val()` and `setAttribute('value', ...)`).
reason: Mixing value-setting mechanisms across render methods for the same input produces inconsistent behavior between populated and empty states.
common_pattern: Conventions for how widgets receive and mutate state through render/setState APIs: keep initial state separate from mutable state, make mutation optional/real rather than faked, and apply the same state-setting convention across all render paths.

text: When rendering form-bound model collections in Wagtail admin edit handlers/panels (e.g. `CommentPanel.comments`), avoid per-instance `.user` lookups by batch-prefetching related users and nested replies on the existing in-memory instances (e.g. `prefetch_related_objects(self.comments, 'user', 'replies__user')`), with a bulk user-ID `in_bulk()` fallback where needed. Do not re-query the collection by PK, because form-bound collections may contain unsaved edits.
reason: This prevents N+1 queries when resolving comment/reply authors while preserving unsaved form state in the Wagtail admin comments UI.
scope: Wagtail admin edit handlers / form-bound model collections
common_pattern: Avoid N+1 queries when rendering collections of model instances with related users in Wagtail admin panels/edit handlers by batch-prefetching related objects, while preserving form-bound in-memory instances instead of re-querying them from the database.

text: For multi-line Python calls and context managers, indent continuation arguments one level (4 spaces) and align the closing bracket/`])` with the statement start (e.g. the `with` keyword or opening line). Apply this consistently in tests and documentation Python examples, matching flake8/black, and do not add `# noqa` to silence style or line-length warnings caused by non-standard indentation.
reason: Consistent multi-line formatting improves readability, avoids lint failures, matches the project formatter, and prevents unnecessary warning suppressions.
scope: global; especially Python tests and documentation code examples
common_pattern: Consistent formatting of multi-line Python calls and context managers: indent continuation arguments one level, align the closing delimiter with the statement start, and avoid `# noqa` suppressions when reformatting can satisfy flake8/black.

text: Use a robust statistic (e.g., median) rather than a mean when aggregating element positions/sizes, so a single extreme outlier does not skew the result.
reason: Averages are sensitive to outliers; for placement calculations a robust central value better represents the data.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern how to compute and communicate an aggregation of element positions/sizes: one addresses the readability of the aggregation expression, the other addresses the statistical robustness of the aggregation method. They are complementary concerns about the same computation rather than restatements of one principle.

text: Keep comment storage concerns (parsing/serialising comment data such as `position`, and styles filtering) inside the `wagtail-comment-frontend` module rather than in editor components like `CommentableEditor`. Where editor variants (commentable vs non-commentable) would otherwise duplicate save/filtering logic, extract a shared helper used by both so behaviour changes are made in one place.
reason: Centralising comment serialisation and shared save/filtering logic in the frontend storage module avoids divergence between editor variants and ensures future schema or behaviour changes are handled in a single location.
common_pattern: Separation of concerns in the Draftail commentable editor: comment storage/serialisation logic and shared save/filtering behaviour should be centralized (in `wagtail-comment-frontend`) rather than duplicated or embedded inside editor components like `CommentableEditor`.

text: Use `<input type="search">` instead of `<input type="text">` for search input fields to convey semantic search behavior and enable native search UI, accessibility, and mobile keyboard affordances.
reason: Semantic HTML provides better accessibility, browser search-specific UI/behavior, and appropriate autocomplete hints.
common_pattern: Use semantic HTML input types for search fields, specifically replacing generic text inputs with `<input type="search">` to gain accessibility and native browser search behavior.

text: Construct Draft.js `SelectionState` objects atomically with `new SelectionState({ anchorKey, anchorOffset, focusKey, focusOffset })`, passing all fields in a single call and ordering them as the anchor pair followed by the focus pair; avoid `SelectionState.createEmpty()` followed by repeated `.set()` calls, and if immutable `.set()` calls are used elsewhere, group related anchor/focus properties together rather than interleaving start/end fields.
reason: Makes selection state creation atomic, avoids intermediate mutations, and makes the start/end boundaries of a selection easier to read and verify at a glance.
common_pattern: Draft.js `SelectionState` construction style: prefer an atomic constructor call over repeated immutable `.set()` calls, and order/group fields by anchor/focus pairs for readability.

text: For UI components injected into arbitrary host pages, such as the Wagtail userbar, ensure style isolation from the host page. Prefer neutral containers like `div` with ARIA roles unless semantic elements are genuinely required. If semantic elements such as `ul`/`li` or interactive elements like `button` are used, start their style declarations with `all: initial !important;` (or equivalent reset) to prevent inherited host-page and user-agent styles from leaking into the component.
reason: Injected UI is rendered inside pages the project does not control. Host pages may apply styles to common elements such as `ul`, `li`, and `button`, causing visual regressions. Explicit style resets and careful element choice keep the component consistent and accessible.
scope: Wagtail userbar / UI components injected into arbitrary host pages
common_pattern: Style isolation for UI components injected into arbitrary host pages: avoid or defend against host-page CSS inheritance, especially for commonly styled elements like ul/li/button, using neutral containers with ARIA roles and/or explicit CSS resets such as `all: initial !important;`.

text: For model fields that track a workflow state or lifecycle transition in Django, use a nullable DateTimeField named `{state}_at` (e.g., `resolved_at`) instead of a BooleanField.
reason: A timestamp records when the state was reached, supports future audit or display features, and preserves temporal information that a boolean flag discards.
scope: Django model design / project-wide model fields
common_pattern: Django model timestamp field design: use DateTimeField (not BooleanField) with `_at` naming for state/lifecycle tracking, and apply correct `auto_now_add` / `auto_now` options for creation vs modification timestamps.

text: In Django models, name timestamp fields according to their behavior: use `created_at` with `auto_now_add=True` for creation timestamps, and `updated_at` / `modified_at` with `auto_now=True` for last modification timestamps.
reason: Consistent naming and correct Django field options make timestamp semantics clear and prevent accidental misuse such as a `created_at` field that changes on update.
common_pattern: Django model timestamp field design: use DateTimeField (not BooleanField) with `_at` naming for state/lifecycle tracking, and apply correct `auto_now_add` / `auto_now` options for creation vs modification timestamps.

text: When computing layout or positioning for tabbed content, resolve positions only for the currently visible tab rather than iterating over all tabs.
reason: Avoids unnecessary computation for off-screen tabs and improves layout performance.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern tab-component layout handling, but they are distinct sub-patterns: one is about scoping position computation for performance, and the other is about validating tab styling in an embedded modal context to prevent overflow.

text: When initializing tabs inside a modal (e.g., via `initTabs()`), verify the tab layout in the modal context and adjust tab container styles or options to prevent horizontal overflow/scrolling.
reason: Tabs initialized in a modal can inherit or collide with modal styles and overflow, causing broken layout and horizontal scrolling that degrades usability.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern tab-component layout handling, but they are distinct sub-patterns: one is about scoping position computation for performance, and the other is about validating tab styling in an embedded modal context to prevent overflow.

text: When a React component needs to know whether it actually received children, test `React.Children.count(children) > 0` (or an equivalent guarded non-empty check). Do not compare `children` against `null`, and do not rely on `children?.length > 0`: React `children` may be an empty array (`[] !== null` is true), and `ReactNode` does not guarantee a `.length` property (single element, string, boolean, number), so `children?.length` can be a type error (TS2339) or a wrong result.
reason: Null checks produce false positives for empty arrays, so components render or enter logic paths for children that do not exist. `.length` is not defined across all ReactNode forms, so the optional-chained length check is both type-unsafe and unreliable for a single non-array child. `React.Children.count` handles undefined, empty arrays, and single nodes consistently.
scope: React components (e.g. reusable components under client/src/components/)
common_pattern: React/JSX rendering-correctness idioms: primarily (a) how to correctly test whether `children` are present (a converging 4-generalization pattern), plus (b) the idiomatic shape of no-else conditional JSX. A fifth generalization (Python/Wagtail panel container visibility) is a different domain and appears in only one PR, so it is treated as an unrelated outlier rather than part of the shared React pattern.

text: When conditionally rendering JSX with no fallback branch, use `{condition && (<Element />)}` rather than a ternary whose else-branch is `null`.
reason: Logical AND is the concise, idiomatic form for no-else conditional rendering in React/JSX and avoids a redundant `null` else branch.
common_pattern: React/JSX rendering-correctness idioms: primarily (a) how to correctly test whether `children` are present (a converging 4-generalization pattern), plus (b) the idiomatic shape of no-else conditional JSX. A fifth generalization (Python/Wagtail panel container visibility) is a different domain and appears in only one PR, so it is treated as an unrelated outlier rather than part of the shared React pattern.

text: Do not coerce DOM `data-*`/`dataset` values used as identifiers (object IDs, primary keys) with `Number()`. Keep them as raw strings for storage and comparison unless numeric behavior is explicitly required and the data contract guarantees numeric values.
reason: Dataset attributes are always strings and identifiers may be non-numeric (e.g. UUIDs); numeric coercion can produce `NaN` or silently change valid string identifiers, breaking selection state and identity comparisons.
common_pattern: DOM `dataset` / `data-*` values are always strings, so identifier-like values (object IDs, primary keys) must be kept as raw strings and not coerced with `Number()`, because IDs may be non-numeric (UUIDs) and coercion can yield `NaN`, collapse distinct IDs, or silently alter identity. The lone outlier (comment #676063909, PR#7340) argues only about the *form* of coercion (`Number()` vs unary `+`) if coercion is done at all.

text: When numeric coercion of a dataset-derived value actually is required, use an explicit conversion such as `Number()` rather than the unary `+` operator.
reason: Unary `+` is easy to overlook or mistake for a typo or arithmetic operator, whereas `Number()` makes the numeric-coercion intent explicit.
common_pattern: DOM `dataset` / `data-*` values are always strings, so identifier-like values (object IDs, primary keys) must be kept as raw strings and not coerced with `Number()`, because IDs may be non-numeric (UUIDs) and coercion can yield `NaN`, collapse distinct IDs, or silently alter identity. The lone outlier (comment #676063909, PR#7340) argues only about the *form* of coercion (`Number()` vs unary `+`) if coercion is done at all.

text: Keep UI animations fast and subtle: use short durations (e.g., 0.1s) and avoid long delays for transitions; avoid scale/transform hover animations on frequently used controls, and omit animations on small affordances, preferring color/underline changes or no animation.
reason: Frequent or small UI interactions should not be slowed or made distracting by motion; short or omitted animations provide immediate feedback and reduce visual noise.
common_pattern: UI animations should be minimized (short, subtle, or omitted) to keep interfaces responsive and non-distracting.

text: When styling a mobile bulk-action bar, mirror the existing edit-form action bar's mobile layout and styling rather than introducing a new pattern.
reason: Keeps action-bar layout and behavior consistent across the UI and reduces mobile-specific regressions.
common_pattern: Styles for the bulk-actions-choices UI component should be encapsulated under its own component namespace/SCSS partial and should reuse existing action-bar patterns instead of leaking into shared selectors or creating new layouts.

text: Losslessly compress image assets (e.g., under `docs/_static/images/`) before committing or uploading them.
reason: Lossless compression reduces repository size and bandwidth usage without degrading image quality.
common_pattern: Managing image/animated assets to minimize repository weight and maintenance burden: prefer static, non-animated formats over animated ones (SVG animation, GIF), and losslessly compress image assets before committing them.

text: Write zero values without units (e.g., CSS/SCSS `padding: 0`, not `0px`/`0rem`); for SVG `x`/`y` attributes, omit the attribute entirely when it is `0`, since SVG defaults omitted position values to `0`.
reason: Reduces redundant markup and follows standard CSS/SVG conventions; unitless zero also avoids stylelint/CI errors.
common_pattern: Zero values should be expressed without redundant units or attributes, using the shortest idiomatic form that preserves default behavior.

text: Extract helper functions that have grown large from admin entrypoint files (client/src/entrypoints/admin/**/*.js) into dedicated modules under the sibling `includes/` directory. In the new module, `export default` the function and `import` it back into the entrypoint, keeping the function body and call sites otherwise unchanged.
reason: Keeps entrypoint files focused on initialization/wiring, gives the helper a clear module boundary, and preserves existing behavior during extraction.
common_pattern: Extract large helper functions from admin entrypoints into dedicated includes/ modules using a default export/import convention, preserving the function body and call sites unchanged.

text: Use robust CSS sizing units for UI controls and inline graphic elements: prefer em/rem over hardcoded px for form-control padding/heights, and use em rather than percentage widths for icons/spinners. This keeps sizes stable across zoom, font-size changes, and parent-width changes.
reason: Sizing choices should be intentional: px padding can break under zoom/font-size changes, while percentage widths make icons/spinners scale with the parent container. Using em/rem keeps related form-control dimensions consistent and prevents distortion.
common_pattern: CSS sizing unit selection for UI components: avoid units that make intrinsic element sizes depend on unrelated factors such as hardcoded pixel assumptions (zoom/font-size) or parent width (percentage), and instead use robust relative/fixed units like em/rem consistently.

text: For literal text inside SVG icons (e.g. under `wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/icons/`), prefer a `<text>` element over converting glyphs into a `<path>` — path lettering becomes blurry when the SVG is resized and is less crisp at normal size; when using `<text>`, explicitly position it against the icon's `viewBox` via `transform`/`x`/`y` so it stays aligned after size or viewBox changes.
reason: Path-based lettering degrades visually on scaling, while `<text>` renders more consistently; however text elements need explicit coordinates to remain correctly positioned when the viewBox or icon size changes.
common_pattern: SVG icon authoring in wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/icons/: choosing and positioning text/path primitives so icons render crisply and at consistent visual weight

text: When modifying or replacing elements in an icon SVG, verify the result preserves the original's visual weight and apparent size — adjust stroke thickness and/or icon dimensions (viewBox/scale) as needed so the icon stays consistent with the surrounding admin icons.
reason: Element substitutions (e.g. text→path or path→text) can render too thin or too small, producing visual inconsistency with the original rendering and other icons in the set.
common_pattern: SVG icon authoring in wagtail/admin/templates/wagtailadmin/icons/: choosing and positioning text/path primitives so icons render crisply and at consistent visual weight

text: Mount dialogs at a predictable document root — either append to `document.body` or move `<template>` content to the end of the DOM when the dialog opens — rather than rendering them inline in place. Only insert a dialog adjacent to its triggering template/container when the dialog is intentionally scoped to that surrounding panel.
reason: Inline dialogs can inherit ancestor container styles (layout, positioning, typography, z-index) and end up nested in unintended DOM locations, producing inconsistent appearance or trapping whole-page dialogs inside local panels.
scope: global UI pattern; specific file: client/src/includes/dialog.js
common_pattern: Dialog mounting target (root vs inline) and its documentation in dialog.js

text: In the Wagtail admin form submissions listing (wagtail/contrib/forms/templates/wagtailforms/index_submissions.html), derive table columns and headers from the form's fields/submission data rather than hard-coding field names (except fixed metadata such as submission date), and wrap the table in a horizontally scrollable container to handle long/wide tables.
reason: Form fields are user-defined and vary per form, so hard-coded columns cannot correctly represent arbitrary forms; long/wide tables need horizontal scrolling in the admin UI.
common_pattern: Rendering the Wagtail admin form submissions index template: dynamically derive table columns from form fields and ensure wide tables are horizontally scrollable.

text: In chooser/widget code, access and mutate DOM attributes and input values using native DOM APIs such as `getAttribute()` and `setAttribute()` rather than jQuery methods like `.attr()` or `.val()`. When updating an input's value, set the DOM `value` attribute so the attribute and value property remain in sync.
reason: Using native DOM APIs keeps attribute access explicit and avoids jQuery's value abstraction; setting the `value` attribute also keeps live widget state consistent with serialized/re-rendered markup.
scope: local to chooser/widget component render and input-manipulation code
common_pattern: Within chooser/widget code, prefer native DOM APIs for reading and writing element attributes and input values instead of jQuery's `.attr()`/`.val()`, including setting the `value` attribute to keep attribute and property state synchronized.

text: In Storybook documentation stories (e.g. `client/src/**/*.stories.tsx`), style tables by adding shared CSS such as row/cell padding via `border-spacing` to the existing `<style>` block that injects `:root` variables — do not use the `.docutils` class (it adds unwanted alternate row coloring) and do not repeat inline padding styles on each cell.
reason: Keeps tabular documentation readable and scannable while reducing duplicated inline styles and preserving copy-pasteable markup for external documentation.
common_pattern: Styling tables in Storybook documentation stories: apply shared CSS (e.g. cell padding via `border-spacing`) in the existing `<style>` block that injects `:root` variables, rather than using the `.docutils` class or repeating inline styles on each cell, so tables render readably and remain copy-pasteable into external docs.

text: When styling reusable form input components, target the native input elements directly and include native state pseudo-classes such as `:invalid`, `:checked`, and `:disabled` in state-dependent styling. Do not rely solely on wrapper elements or class/ARIA-based markers like `.error` or `[aria-invalid='true']` to represent input state.
reason: Native inputs carry browser-provided state and form semantics directly; styling them directly keeps visual states consistent without requiring JavaScript-added classes or ARIA attributes, and avoids wrappers that may not exist or may not receive the same native states.
common_pattern: State-dependent form styling should target native input elements and their native state selectors/pseudo-classes rather than relying only on wrapper elements or JavaScript/ARIA-managed state markers.

text: Wrap non-essential CSS animations in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so they only run for users who have not requested reduced motion.
reason: Respects the `prefers-reduced-motion` accessibility preference, improving accessibility for users with vestibular disorders or reduced-motion settings.
common_pattern: Use the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` media query to guard non-essential CSS animations, ensuring they're disabled for users who request reduced motion.

text: When parsing CSS color values (e.g. `hsl()`) with regex, match the full syntax permitted by the underlying CSS data types (e.g. hue uses `<angle>`, which allows an optional leading `+`/`-` sign and decimal fractions, so use `[+-]?\d+(\.\d+)?` rather than bare `\d+`). Conversely, do not include optional-syntax matching for constructs the spec does not permit.
reason: Values valid per the CSS spec may be user-supplied or overridable (e.g. customized token colors), so a regex that is too loose or too strict can accept malformed input or fail on spec-valid input, silently producing wrong derivations.
scope: shared CSS color token parsing utilities, e.g. `client/src/tokens/colorVariables.js`
common_pattern: Regex patterns for parsing CSS color/token values must match the exact syntax permitted by the underlying CSS data type spec, rather than a looser or tighter ad-hoc pattern.

text: When a controller temporarily replaces a DOM element's text to show a loading/active state, cache the original text in an instance property before mutating the element. Initialize the cache only if it is empty and do not overwrite it on subsequent state changes. When deactivating the state, restore the text from that saved original value, guarded by the saved value and the target's existence.
reason: The four generalizations are complementary parts of the same state-preservation pattern: save before mutation, avoid overwriting the saved original, and restore safely from the saved value rather than from the transient active state.
scope: client/src/controllers (Stimulus controllers that toggle transient UI state content)
